text: 4 stars on the Reno scale. I wasn't really expecting much from this place but it wasn't bad. Full steak dinner, including salad and sides, for the price of a steak alone at any other fine steakhouse. I wouldn't call this a "fine" steakhouse as steakhouses go, but the price was pleasantly reasonable for what was delivered. Choice of soup or salad included with dinner. I got salad which was decent enough. I got the balsamic vinaigrette dressing. It came on the side in like a tiny like jug. It had all kinds of herbs in the bottom flavoring the vinegar and oil. I had never seen that before, nice touch I thought. The steak came with vegetables and a choice of potato, I chose baked. The waiter brings the food on a cart and dresses the potato at the table, another nice touch. I don't normally get sucked in by that kind of thing but here I just fell for it. The veg was haricot vert and carrots, steamed I think, with some butter maybe. That was the only weak link in my meal. The steak was very good, very tender and cooked just the way I wanted. The potato was huge and satisfying. The GF had clam chowder instead of salad. I found it way too thick for my taste. She had mashed potatoes instead of baked. Those were not good. They were piped onto the plate with star-shaped piping tip and set up like a mound of spackle. They tasted OK, but the texture was awful. Overall I have to say that I was very happy with the meal here. The wine list had enough selections by the glass. The staff was incredibly welcoming, helpful and friendly. That 4 stars is on the Reno scale. Lots of casino restaurants have awful food and this place seems to being doing their best to buck that trend. In the bay area I would give them 3 stars. If I ever go back to Reno and stay in one of those 3 hotels, I'll be eating here again.

text: It's really bordering 2.5 stars, but I will be generous. This particular Maggiano's was quite entertaining for me. You sure will find every single group of people here from... a) teeny boppers going on their first real date b) groups of families c) group of teenagers hanging out but trying to act grown d) older couples (anywhere from 40s-50s to grandma & grandpa's age) e) local couples in their late 20s to mid 30s having date night The portions are good, but the food is the quality of Olive Garden, maybe a skosh better. Either way, when you order from their BOGO section (buy one and take one home), I have to give it up to Maggiano's sales & marketing team - it's a clever and cheap way to entice the customer and make like they are giving you a deal. But really folks, let's think about this for a second. They use Barilla pasta and sauce . So in fact, they are upcharging you for what you will buy at the supermarket for a fraction of the price of what they are charging you...granted it's prepared and served to you with a lot more oil and toss-ins as well as an extra serving to take home, but I hope you are catching my drift here. All in all, it's a chain restaurant. It is what it is. Portions are generous. The dishes swimming in oil and butter - the standard. A place to kick back and wind down the night after you went shopping all day at the mall. The service was horrible though. It was probably our particular server and not a reflection of the entire wait staff, but she simply sucked. How hard can it be to tell you the specials before we order or offer a dessert menu at the end? We had to ask for both. I know I'm not eating at Le Bec Fin, but put a little effort into it lady. Honestly, I'd only come back to hang out with friends for drinks and dessert after I ate at any of the other handful of restaurants you will find that perimeters the mall. Location - somewhere around the mall Parking - ample, big private lot Pics to come...
label: NEG

text: What a profoundly disappointing experience! Recently I watched a Biography show about Paul Prudhomme and was taken with his story of struggle, how he came up out of poverty, his love of cooking, his love affair and sad story of loss of the love of his life to Cancer and the incredible popularity of his food and iconic restaurant K-Pauls in New Orleans. So when I found myself alone in New Orleans at 11:45 on a Thursday and free for lunch I immediately grabbed the opportunity to run to K-Pauls! I was a bit surprised but thrilled when I turned the corner and found no line. I went into the fairly quiet restaurant and learned that lunchtime means a "deli lunch" at K Pauls. i.e. you order and pay at the counter, leave your name, help yourself to plastic utensils and condiments, take a seat and they bring your food out. Perhaps a tad more casual then I expected given that the prices reflected a more traditional restaurant set up, but I was game. Still though I thought, man, this food must be great! The food came out fairly quickly. I ordered chicken étouffée -figured it was a classic. I was delivered on a plastic plate, mediumish portion, with a side of sweet potato fries. It was mediocre at best. The fries were decent but the étouffée had little to no flavor..definitely no spice.. and the chicken pieces were small and simply bland. BORING. What a disappointment. Based on the reputation I was expecting so much more. Given the prices I am sad to say its a tourist trap and I'd defintely avoid in the future. :-(

text: So. I'm not quite sure what a "utilitarian bar" exactly means but I can tell you that I like it. A lot. A couple of months ago, some friends of mine mentioned that a snazzy new establishment was prepping to open next to Dino's Bar + Grill. I was a little shocked by the locale but curious and thrilled that the East Side would home another independent biz. Fast forward to Tuesday evening, my friend let me know that she was at a "soft opening" and suggested that we have our planned "girls night" at No. 308 in lieu of our original plan to head to Holland House. Sure, why not? I knew that I was in for a treat as soon as I walked into the dark yet spunky retreat. The retro furniture and booths were perfectly appointed but not overly staged. Even the striped walls stood out yet didn't take away from the overall tone of the space. I absolutely loved the bar. The contrast of wood and metal pipes masterfully showcased character. Bottoms up! Our group nestled into a massive tufted booth and started ordering the "goods". The drink menu boasted imaginative cocktails with interesting names such as the "Writer's Block Shots" section ($5) that included the William Burroughs and Charles Bukowski! Smitten. I opted for a gin laced cocktail named the Suffering Bastard ($8) which nearly knocked me on my arse. Delish but potent! Our whole table enjoyed the libations and a few even ordered some food. The Sweet Potato Soup was on point and comforting! My friend knew the owners well and made the intro. I really enjoyed meeting Alexis and her staff. She proposed to the other owner in a Manhattan hotel room...guess what room number they were in? No. 308 Witty right? The owners and staff were casually dressed in tee shirts and jeans and was actually a refreshing contrast to what some may expect. It further drives the message home that this is going to be a fantastic destination place for some but still manage to be a cozy neighborhood bar for me. No. 308 is a real bargain due to crafty cocktails and interesting space. I am sure that I will be "checking in" a ton moving forward! TIP: The playlist was a fun mix of Johnny Cash, Top 40 R&B, and Indie Rock...gotta love it.

text: rittenhouse is my favorite of the CC parks. it's my absolute favorite people-watching perch and is perfect for passing the time in warm weather. i have a really great work schedule that allows me the opportunity to enjoy sitting in the park in the early afternoon as most people are finishing up a late lunch break in the park or just passing through on their way somewhere. there's a really diverse crowd that filters in and out of the park that really adds to the flavor of the city. i have many fond memories of the white noise of the city rising up in symphony all around me as i sit on my picnic blanket reading a book or doing a crossword puzzle while feeding cheez-its to the abnormally tame sparrows. even writing this review is making me long for the warm weather to get here faster so i can return to the park! the arts festival in the summer is a great draw to the park, as are the impromptu as well as sanctioned musical performances that can be found fairly regularly. and if you're a fan of dogs, there's plenty that come through for you to say hi to! :) if you're just wandering around the city some afternoon, i'd encourage you to stop by and grab a bench if you can. and sit on the side. i guarantee that someone interesting will sit next to you and will be more than happy to chat you up. there's a special place in my heart for rittenhouse, and not just for all if its intrinsic qualities. it's the place where i've had the strangest pickup line asked of me: "are you foreign?" really? that's your line? followed, after my laugh and "no" response, with "ohhh, you just have a very european air." heh. nice try buddy. but hey, added bonus to the single ladies out there i suppose. if you're having a bad day and need an ego boost, just go sit in the park for a bit and wait for a stranger to walk by and give you a compliment. take it from me, i'm not the kind of girl that gets randomly hit on, with cheesy lines or otherwise!

text: Short Version: The food is great, IF you ever get it! Be prepared to WAIT and maybe not get exactly what you ordered... Long Version: My first experience there was a Sat. afternoon, got a sandwich for lunch, no big deal, no incident. My opinion of the place was blown on my second visit. I went with a big group who had made a reservation. We were seated on the deck where we could only order from a small bar menu, not the regular dinner menu (the kitchen was about 10 feet away and no different from the other deck on the other side of the walkway). The entire deck had only one server, not one for our group, but one for everyone. I got a "wait one minute" from the server when I had been there at least 10 minutes with no acknowledgment at all! So, I finally got to order a drink and that came out as expected. Later, some friends and I ordered food, which was really only finger food... I ordered a Caesar salad and a shrimp cocktail. Exactly the same thing as the people I was with. I waited and waited... Their food came out and somehow I was left out of the order. The waitress continued to apologize, saying she would check on the salad, my order got lost. The next time out, the excuse was there were a bunch of new interns in the kitchen that weren't familiar with the menu (On a Friday night?!?). Next time, she was shocked that someone else hadn't delivered my salad to me yet and decided to go make it herself. I know none of this is the server's fault, except that she did not ask for help. At this point, the rest of the deck was filling up with people that were not with our club, and she had served most of the people that I was sitting with already. My friends, after they were done with their meal, kept asking on my behalf when I would be getting my food! So, after my friends had finished eating, and were up and about being social, I had to ask once again for my shrimp cocktail. Keep in mind, this is what they had ordered and had already finished eating. I ordered the exact same thing at the exact same time! Shrimp cocktail finally came out, and for $9.99 it was 6 medium sized shrimp on some fancy-swirled sauce! It tasted good, but for the wait and the price I was not really impressed.( It is a fancy menu with gourmet food served to patio tables and vinyl chairs!) After all of that, everyone was leaving and I got my check with no mention from the server about a half-off or any kind of deal at all. Working in hospitality, that was all I would hope for and what I would do for someone in that situation, at the very least. So, I asked since I waited so long if I could get a break on the check. They must have thought I wanted all the food for free, because after yet another wait to have the manager and a snooty chef come out looking down their noses at me thinking I'm trying to cause trouble. The chef explained that on a Friday night the meals take up to :45 minutes and I should have expected a wait. I explained that it was only a salad and shrimp cocktail that the other people I was with had ordered the same thing and finished before I even got my salad!!! His exact words were, "I'm only willing to give you a free dessert!" I was appalled! I don't want a dessert! I only wanted $5- half off the shrimp... some acknowledgment that they screwed up. Take the price of the dessert and subtract it off my tab! So, after waiting, they waited once again to get me my free dessert, and I paid my $40 tab and left... alone, after all my friends were up, paid and gone! In short, like I said above, go for drinks. If you get food, it's good, be prepared to wait, and for poor management.

Plus, there is a cafe that serves sandwich and salads and BOOZE. Definitely beer and wine, but I think there is a full bar too. Our server was very attentive and the manager comped us Kir Royales (it pays to be part of bridal party). If you are staying at the Biltmore, you need to head over here for a few hours. text: We visit White Dog Cafe only about once a year, but have been a fan for more than two decades. But our recent visit will be the last unless I hear that significant changes have been made. First, I was surprised by a couple of items on the menu. Knowing Ms. Wicks' commitment to healthy and sustainable food, wild striped bass appears to be an inappropriate contradiction. The DEP warns that consumption of this fish should be limited to a maximum of 4 servings per year for most people while pregnant women and other high risk individuals should avoid eating this fish altogether. Wild striper is heavily contaminated with cancer-causing dioxin and PCBs. Considering the ready supply of healthy and sustainable farm-raised striped bass as a suitable alternative, why would any knowledgeable diner want to pay for the wild toxin-laden fish? Food that comes with a safety warning is simply not something I would expect at White Dog Café. The same comments apply to the tuna appetizer. Environmentally conscious diners simply do not eat tuna anymore, especially the ahi type, because it is an unsustainable food under severe environmental pressure. Health concerns about mercury levels in tuna are also well documented. (I suggest the book Bottomfeeder and the NJ DEP Web site for more information on seafood safety. One bad mussel in the appetizer undetected by the kitchen gave the entire dish an unpleasant smell and unfortunately I did not detect the bad one until I bit into it and had to spit it out. (Anyone who has eaten a bad mussel knows what I mean). The sauce was the most bland I have ever had on this dish. A restaurant serving mussels, especially in the summer when more shellfish die in transit, needs to be more careful about inspecting each mussel before cooking. My wife's broiled scallops were delicious, but the vegetables on the dish were completely bland. It doesn't take much effort to make vegetables taste great, but these just didn't make the grade. Most disappointing was the $7 bacon & cheese risotto. The bacon and cheese completely overpowered the dish so that I couldn't even finish. Again, it is not difficult to create a great taste with these basic ingredients, so it is surprising that the kitchen managed to find a way to make it almost inedible. The best dish this night was the beet salad. The beets were well prepared with a great dressing and the portion was generous. We opted for glasses of wine because the bottles were a bit over our budget. Given the $120 price for dinner for two, I expected more.

text: I've had lots of mediocre sushi in Tampa. From SB in Ybor City to CB near the stadium, there's a lot of just average... or restaurants trying too hard to be fusion. I grew up near Tampa, and every time I come back, there's only one requirement as far as dining -- I have to get in to see Ryo at Kaisen Sushi. Kaisen is a little known secret that Tampa has been hiding for years. Ryo initially opened over by Harpos, further south on Dale Mabry than their current location. I went in for the first time in 1999, and have been a repeat customer ever since, dining there sometimes twice a week. In all my years of eating at Kaisen, I've never once been disappointed. In fact, they know me by name now and I get that personal of service that keeps me coming back. Here are my highlights: Appetizer: Calamari -- I can't say enough about this stuff. It's not your typical frozen rings, this stuff is FRESH. They saute large chunks octopus, not just rings or tentacles, in a delicious sauce that has a mild tangy flavor to it. It's then topped with bonito flake, green onion, and a lemon. I could eat calamari appetizers as a meal and walk away satisfied... Stuffed Mushrooms -- Forget everything you know about stuffed mushrooms. Ryo takes large mushrooms, stuffs them with crab meat, tempura batters, and deep fries them. They're then coated with what I think is ponzu sauce for a delicious creation. Nigiri: One of my personal favorites is the zuke tuna. Ryo takes the best cuts of Tuna and marinates them in what I believe to be sesame oil, rice vinegar, and soy sauce, for about three days. The fish changes consistency and flavor, and becomes just ridiculously good. You have to try it. Ryo's fish selection and cuts are the absolute best in Tampa, in my opinion. He hand-selects everything, and he's committed to culinary excellence. You really can't go wrong. Rolls: My personal favorite, although not containing raw fish, is the Cynthia's Vegetable Tempura roll. The kitchen takes asparagus and sweet potatoes, tempura batters, then deep fries them. These scrumptious veggies are then rolled up and served with a side of ponzu sauce. It's HEAVENLY. The spicy tuna is by far the best I've ever had as well. Most restaurants pulverize the tuna or use shoddier quality of fish. Ryo takes his sushi tuna, cubes it, and mixes it with spicy sauce. You don't feel like you're eating some strange mush -- it has consistency, texture, and above all, great flavor. Dessert: I love the green tea ice cream. It's that simple. They also carry "Red Bean" ice cream, but I tend to stay away from that. It's a little too weird for me. For all you non-sushi lovers, they do a delicious cooked salmon and chicken teriyaki. I can't recommend Kaisen Sushi enough, that's plain and simple. If you're a first time sushi-er, or a seasoned expert, stop into Kaisen and prepare to be wowed. They also organize a yearly fishing trip, and I hear a lot of people have had a really good time on these excursions. You'll always see Ryo making sushi, and his Dad and sometimes his wife are there working to keep the place running smoothly. GO! NOW (unless it's Sunday or Monday)! DO IT! :-)

text: Little Fish, BIG FLAVOR! Little Fish lived up to all our expectations for great seafood in a quaint environment. By scoring a reservation for their $28 Sunday prix-fixe, we were able to sample several of their dishes. Fresh out of the oven bread w/ a dipping sauce of garlic, herbs and olive oil was amazing. We could have lapped up the dipping sauce like stray cats looking for milk. 1. Baby frisee salad w/ oranges, radishes, & goat cheese - The salad was good, except that mine didn't have any oranges. 2. Blue Bay mussels w/ wild mushrooms, butternut squash, & pastina - This was delicious, my wife thought so as well and she doesn't even like mussels. The wild mushrooms were the perfect undertone to this dish. The broth alone was heavenly. 3. Suzuki (Japanese black bass) w/ grapefruit, fennel, & fingerling potatoes - This was the best dish of the night. The crust on the fish was perfectly crispy and seasoned. The grapefruit provided a sweet & sour contrast to the saltiness of the fish. The potatoes were very good as well. 4. Mahi-mahi w/ sweet potato puree, Madras curry, pear, & watercress - The sweet potato puree was creamy and delicious. The pear also provided a nice sweetness. My wife felt that her fish was underseasoned. 5. Spiced apple bread pudding w/ whipped cream - a nice finish to a delicious meal. I wish that the bread pudding was warmed though instead of being served at room temperature. Overall, Little Fish has great food and the Sunday prix-fixe is an exceptional deal. The courses were the right size and timed perfectly to leave you satisfied by the end of the night. One word of wisdom - arrive early to get the best table, otherwise you might be stuck at a table that is only inches away from the next table. Don't bother trying to get reservations for a weekend in the next few months, they're booked through April. Bon Appetit!

text: On any given weekend, you will find me and a few of my friends having brunch at some local haunt. A few weekends ago, a friend mentioned this little place Downtown called "Rooster". Being a city-kind-of-guy, and wanting to support Downtown, I was all in. Off we went for brunch. The decor of "Rooster" is perfect for that urbanite wanting to feel hip and trendy for an hour of their life. Pictures are clever or handmade by local children, seating is unique, windows are large, etc. Upon sitting down, we immediately asked to move tables, though. Two big gentleman do not work well at a small table for two. We were moved to a table for four without issue, although the waiter seemed very perplexed by the whole experience. This was just the beginning. The restaurant offers an extensive menu of mimosas and bloody marys, for which, again, I was all in. The drinks were better than ordinary, but the celebration at lunch quickly ended there. Breakfast was marginal, at best. The eggs/omeletes ordered were greasy and the presentation was awful. I could do better myself. The ingredients didn't live up to expectations. (Note: If you are going to say something is spicy in the menu, back it up.) Menu selections ranged from the typical to the original, but the food was just so-so. We ordered potatoes as a side. Seriously, how can you mess up breakfast potatoes? For an answer to that question, head to "Rooster". Under-cooked, sloppy, greasy, blech. Awful. Two strikes. On to the toast, which was fantastic. Homemade with nice jam...scrumptuous. While the toast was certainly the highlight of the meal, as a brunch place, that is the LAST thing you want to be remembered for as the "highlight of the meal" in all honesty. Good toast will not fill seats -- eggs and atmosphere do that. All in all, it wasn't a wasted trip, but I do not intend to go back whatsoever. There are much better places closer to me and most likely cheaper. I'll only return if I want a good bloody mary, some good bread to soak it up, and that is it.

text: 3.75 stars. Some years ago, when the great love of my life was still a sapling, I stopped at Half Moon with my companion for an unexpected late dinner. I remember relaxing by the windows, gazing at an old clock's alabaster face glowing against the chilly night sky, admiring the light dusting of snow on the streets, and enjoying a comforting meal. With a dose of anticipation and glee, I stepped into Half Moon over the weekend with my companion, and prepared to indulge in its storied menu of game dishes. Unfortunately, our hostess was quite rude, and left us feeling unwelcome as we slid into a half booth close to the back. Shaking her memory from our minds, we studied the cocktail and dinner menus, deciding on a French Orchid (Grey Goose, Chambord, and a splash of pineapple), brown IPA, crab nachos, gator gumbo with chorizo, and the game sampler. Then, our faces relaxed into lazy smiles in the low candlelight, and we giggled as absurd conversations from the bar floated across the room. Hungry from an earlier bike ride in Philadelphia, we were pleased when the gumbo and nachos soon arrived. The crab nachos presentation was elegant and gorgeous. The blue corn chips and warm crab salad were layered so that the chips appeared to be lotus petals lightly cloaked in toppings, the avocado salsa's green and red colors interspersed with lumps of crab and a snowfall of grated cheese. The dish was also quite tasty, particularly the buttery, citrus-infused salsa and pungent cheese, but it was difficult to distinguish the taste of crab from the other flavors on the plate. As my companion remarked, we could have had shredded chicken and the taste would have been the same. I greatly enjoyed the comforting quality of the gumbo, but had the impression that pureed beans formed part of the soup's base. The soup's richness was nicely offset by a lingering heat, and the alligator meat's flavor was a welcome addition to the dish, but I wished that more generous portions of alligator, chorizo, and the holy trinity were added to the soup, as it sometimes felt like I was eating separate dishes when scooping from different areas of the bowl. After several bites, the soup became less interesting, and I slid the bowl across the table. The wild game sampler arrived last, showcasing filets of kangaroo, ostrich, and wild boar accented with a tart cherry sauce and a gougere. The ostrich was deeply flavorful, and perfectly cooked until it was firm but moist. It provided the night's outstanding culinary moment, and my fork locked tangs with my companion's utensils as we struggled to get the last bite. The tart cherry ver jus completely captured my palate and imagination, and I greedily dragged my spoon across the plate to discern its cinnamon, pink peppercorn, and offal flavors. The kangaroo and wild boar both had interesting flavors but were a bit chewier than we preferred. By this time we were stuffed, and it seemed a challenge to continue. If you order slightly differently (try the local goat cheese appetizer, any of the numerous local brews on tap, and an ostrich dish with cherries), I think your meal at Half Moon can be phenomenal. Our server was a sweet, spunky girl who understood our leisurely mood, and eagerly answered our questions about the chef and restaurant. The restaurant's setting was comforting and fun, with live music that started soon after we arrived. And the upstairs section, with its wrought iron tables and chairs, hanging plants, and large windows, would be perfect for a summer or winter party. Recommended.

text: Mercer Café is a neighborhood gem, serving up creative dishes with quality ingredients, but located just a little bit off the beaten path. One thing that I liked was that they go the extra mile with La Columbe coffee and LeBus bread, for instance, but the restaurant has an utterly low key, unpretentious atmosphere. The location is in Philadelphia's Port Richmond neighborhood, not far from the Castor Ave/Alleghany I-95 exit. Our party of 6 stopped by for lunch on Saturday, and the entire group left the Mercer Café happy and satisfied! The restaurant is not a large space; while we were there, they were able to accommodate 2 groups of 6, plus several other tables seating 2 or 4 people, mostly families. There is also a lunch counter. Service was friendly and attentive, with the owner pitching in and also checking in with each table. It seemed like there was a lot of familiarity in the greetings. The only downside was that we were seated near the door and the alarm kept on beeping. I hope that is a glitch that was acting up that day, because it was pretty irritating before we eventually were able to tune it out. The menu has a lot of variety, including specials, and I found it hard to choose since it all looked really good. Some of the items that we ordered included: bacon, lettuce, tomato, shrimp, and avocado sandwich (on LeBus multigrain); grilled vegetable panini; house salad; salad plate of tomato, mozzarella, and tuna in olive oil; roasted turkey sandwich; freshly made potato chips. Our portion sizes were more than adequate, but we saw some hoagies delivered to another table that were absolutely gigantic! If my lunch experience is any indication of what the Mercer Café is capable of, I definitely look forward to stopping back for breakfast or dinner!

text: I had a fantastic experience working with Carl Alan for the flowers for my wedding. When I went in for my first meeting with him, his staff was in the middle of assembling an order for a wedding that night. When I saw the literally hundreds of urns of black magic roses and expensive-looking lilies swarming all around me, I decided to be upfront with Carl about my teeny tiny floral budget to make sure we wouldn't be wasting each others' time if his business was focused on high-end projects. He laughed heartily and told me that while this particular bride was spending over $50,000 on flowers, he worked with all price ranges. We got down to business as I revealed my ignorance about flowers. He took one look at the peridot green bridesmaid dress I brought with me and said "Aha - we must do cymbidium orchids!" I said "Huh?" and he showed me the coolest looking green flowers I had ever seen. He worked them into bouquets amongst more cost-efficient neutral flowers, made them into solo boutonierres for the guys, and floated them in candle-lit bowls of water for the centerpieces. The final result was spectacular and it looked like I spent WAY more then $1,500 on flowers. He also provided extra flowers for the cake and display tables at no extra charge. The service was also fantastic. I could easily get in touch with Carl himself if I had any questions. He was far more concerned than I was when some peach lilies arrived in a too-bright shade, and instead ended up dying white ones (at no extra charge) so they would look perfect. His staff was also able to get all of the flowers delivered to the correct four separate locations on the morning of my wedding, which was in the middle of a sleet storm with 6 inches of snow on the ground.

text: We were in Santa Barbara for the weekend to celebrate my wife's birthday. We arrived around 2P and walked around the pier and a bit on State Street. Then off to check into our motel and get settled. As we had brought our laptop I decided to check Yelp for a good place to eat dinner that night. Right away at the top of the list came up the The Palace Grill with 71 reviews and 4 1/2 stars. I looked at a few reviews and clicked on the link to their website. Everything checked out and I was quite enthused about going there for dinner that evening. We arrived about 5:45 and was seated immediately. The hostess was really friendly and everything was off to a good start. Next our waitress arrived, again another sweet and friendly person. We got our drinks and the buss boy brought us a basket of muffins and butter. There was quite a variety and all very, very good. It was now time to order and I decided on the house specialty, stuffed blackened filet mignon, and my wife got divers scallops. I added a bowl of seafood gumbo and my wife got a Creole Caesar salad. Oh, let's not forget that if you want their famous bread pudding for desert, you have to order it at the same time you order your meal. They have to prepare it and then bake it, all taking about 30 minutes. The soup and salad came promptly. I was looking forward to the gumbo as I am a fan of soups and spicy food . It looked good and I was ready to dig in. As I spooned through the soup looking for signs of shrimp and crayfish I saw none. But what was in abundance was pieces of Ahi tuna and loads of rice. There was also a bit of oil or grease that collected on the top so I mixed it around. Now, I'm not really a big fan of tuna in such a soup, and would prefer to have only shrimp and crayfish, that's just me, but I was going to let my taste buds decide. I tried the first spoonful and to me it was not at all what I expected. It was very bland and tasteless and had no kick to it at all, and as I said there was no shrimp or crayfish in sight, just tuna and rice. I was not impressed at all. Campbell's soup makes a thick and chunky variety called Grilled Chicken Sausage Gumbo that has the Palace's gumbo beat hands down! As for my wife's salad... she said it was OK, but nothing special. I also noticed her moving some big un-edible pieces of romaine hearts to the side of her dish. While waiting for our main course to come I was checking out the decor of the room. There are playing cards stuck on the ceiling, really! There is also a huge painting on the west wall of a black trumpet player dressed in a white suit. Not bad, it added to the room and gave it a feel of down south. But what I didn't expect to see next to the painting crawling down the wall was a cockroach, and on the shelf below it several other dead ones. May wife saw the look of surprise on my face and had a look. I almost wish she hadn't because no one wants to see such a thing. In fact, the young women sitting at the table next to the wall called one of the waitresses over and showed her the dead cockroaches. She promptly got a wet cloth and whisked them away. But still.... this was not a good sign and sort of set the mood for dinner. After about 20 minutes I was wondering if our dinner was ever coming. At that point our waitress came by and said our food would be out shortly. It really made me wonder if she had put the order in promptly or just forgot. I say this because the people next to us got their food about the same time as we did, and they arrived 10 minutes after us .Oh well, that's life. The food came and I dug in. It was nicely presenter and looked good, but didn't have much flavor. The stuffed filet was cold and tasteless. When I think of something blackened it brings forth memories of robust flavors and heat, but this had none. The scoop of mashed potatoes and fresh vegetables looked nice, but lacked flavor just like the filet. As for my wife's scallops... they were extremely salty and had an odd grilled flavor to them. Again, not a good experience. The owner's wife stopped by the table to chat a while. She was so nice I didn't have in me to tell her what I really thought of the dinner. I just told here everything was fine and left it at that. I know, I probably should have.... but I didn't. I hate any confrontation, that's just me. Well, we finally made it to desert and for what it's worth it was probably the only half way decent part of the meal. The waitress brought the bread pudding out and separated the center with two spoons and pored the whiskey cream sauce all over it. As the pudding was a bit dry on it's own, the sauce moistened it up nicely and made it quite tasty. I enjoyed it. All in all I was disappointed with our dinner. When you go out and spend well over 100 dollars for a meal you expect it to be good. I can understand an unlucky experience with the meal, but one live cockroach crawling around and two dead ones visible is inexcusable!

text: Aunt Annie flew in a couple of weeks ago and we decided to grab a dog on our way back from the airport. We choose Foxy's over Woofy's due to some other reviews for the gyros and I'm always looking for a great chile dog. Ms T had the gyro and thought it was very good. It was loaded with meat that was very well seasoned and flavorful. She ordered no onion, so enjoyed it with tomato only. The bread was very nice and soft. The tzatziki sauce was very good. She likes lettuce on hers and will ask for it next time. Aunt Annie had the Italian beef and said it was also good. Plenty of meat, very tasty. I am skeptical of Italian beef since all I have had is Portillo's in the Chicago area. I have found it pretty boring and unremarkable. Anne said this was better than that. I had two chile dogs. Again, being a "no-raw onion" guy simply had chile and yellow mustard. Sorry but these did not make it. The dog (Vienna beef) was devoid of salt. I find the places that feature Vienna dogs to be pretty formulaic. It is just a guarantee of commercial mediocrity. They are much like the takeover of the Schnuck's Delis by Boar's Head products. They make about a thousand different products, none of them much good. It just makes it that much harder to find good, old fashioned cold cuts and sausages with real character. So I thought perhaps they may have some good chile. Again, I was disappointed. The chile lacked depth and flavor. It was pretty boring and again, lacking salt. The beans were a mealy texture. They don't make a coney dog sauce, they just put their chile that you would get in a bowl, on the dog. Coney dog sauces should have their own character. So if you go here, stick with the gyro. I'll keep looking for a good chile dog. The rating is for my chile dogs.

text: I have shopped at Forever XXI (the larger store version of the US' Forever 21 stores) ever since it opened inside West Edmonton Mall. This is my ultimate dream shopping destination! The place is huge and I can easily spend an hour plus inside going through all the racks upon racks of female clothing. Although about a year ago, they put in a section for guys that takes up about a corner of the store as well. Prices for a shirt ranges from $10 to $20. Dresses from $20 to $35. Now and again they have their "brilliant buys" where a tank top is as cheap as $2.50, dresses go for $15. They specialize in having the latest trends in fashion for cheap. The store carries everything from hip to girly to business-y to more casual and sports/sweats type clothing. As well they carry accessories such as purses, scarfs, jewelery and shoes. They get weekly shipments of merchandise so the staff practically put out new stuff everyday! I found myself going almost every other week in the summer just to grab up the hot items. Because unlike other stores, once an item is out of stock at Forever XXI they rarely get it back in again. Since the city only has one location, I am finding myself shopping more and more on their Canadian website: canada.forever21.com, I still enjoy shopping in store to avoid the online shipping fee, although its free with $75+ CDN purchase. I am finding the store becoming increasingly disorganized. I was told when the store first opened, the clothing was organized by same colors, so the same shirt in different colors could be found in several areas of the store. But you never knew whether a shirt was available in another color since the same styles were not placed all together. Now apparently the clothes are organized according to themes. Ex. Urban Chic, Business Attire, Girly Wear, etc. but it is often difficult to distinguish between the different areas. The fitting rooms have full-length mirrors inside with a curtain. But I don't like how the curtains go all the way from the floor all the way up to the ceiling. This makes it really hard to pull to close it all the way and tends to flutter whenever somebody walks by. But other than these peeves, the place is amazing with their everchanging fashions and cheap prices!

Sure, I was hammered, and didn't think to wait for it to cool, and it totally burned my lips, but I ate it all anyway. And it was only $2 and change. Works for me.
label: POS

text: In town for a convention. Went for lunch on St. Patrick's Day. Had a very tasty short rib sandwich with pretty good fries. Sandwich was tender, came with onions and jack cheese on a ciabatta roll. Guinness was nice and cold. Sat at the bar and the service was good, but there was a noticeable swarm of fruit flies all around the bar. Not cool. Went back later in the night with a group of about 10 people and tried my hardest to get plastered but apparently there was no Jack in my $7 Jack and Cokes. I stopped in Friday afternoon hoping to grab a stool and catch some of the tourney but the stools were filled with people saving them for their friends. Bartenders should have stepped up and told the people to give up the stools. Ordered a Guinness but they were out so I got a Sam Adams Noble Pils that cost $6 for a pint. In sum: Good food, bad drinks, high prices, needs a bleaching.
label: NEG

text: This is my first Wahoo's experience and I am glad to report that it was a good one! I had the fish taco combo plate with both kinds of rice and beans. It's really cool that they let you do that... most places would charge extra for this type of thing. I chose the blackened, spicy fish for the tacos and it was delicious! None of that battered fried mess here! The salsa was just right and I love that little bit that they put on top of the beans and rice. The cajun white beans were so flavorful. The black beans with the white rice went well together too. The brown rice was a little dry for my taste. Prices weren't bad either! I think my combo plate was $5.99.
label: POS

text: Amazingly fast drive through... But wow... They have managed to obliterate all semblance of customer service in the process. text: Stopped off at this Jimmy John's for some quick refueling while cycling around town. I was greeted by a smiling face as I walked in the door. The service was very friendly and quick. text: I had looked at the menu when I saw Jen on Top Chef but the menu didn't seem interesting. Then my friend from NYC wanted to go to this restaurant because he and his wife were excited to see what the top chef contestant has to offer in her restaurant. As appetizers we had the heirloom tomato salad, grilled octopus, cobb salad, and calamari. The grilled octopus was the best thing here but still not as good as the one from Raddichio. The calamari could be easily confused with the one from Olive Garden and the heirloom salad looks like something my year-old niece could put together. Okay...so I held my reservation until the dinner. We had the Striped Bass with "Baby Bok Choi", Short Ribs, Roast Chicken, and Salmon. The Striped Bass was unflavorful and the bok choi wasn't bok choi at all...they was scallions (gasp). Short ribs were okay but have had better at other places. Roast chicken was cooked nicely but too much salt (I rarely complain about too much salt as I like things slightly over-salted). The salmon was just plain at best. So it's between 1 and 2 stars. I feel like giving 1 star but the meal wasn't atrocious...just very very forgettable. But I had to try it once, I guess.
label: NEG

text: This place is great. I wanted to make use of my newly aquired dental insurance a year or so ago so I found this place on yelp and decided to give it a go. They did a great job on my cavities, And hows this for a first- I slept in and missed my last appointment and they never charged me. They just set up another appointment. Good Peeps here at Gilbert Dental.

text: I don't go to Reading Terminal nearly enough. I just got off the chinatown bus and would you believe it, but I missed the 48. I hadn't eaten lunch, so why not stop in. This time I went to 12th St. because I was in the mood for fish tacos and the line was short. It was quite tasty, and the fish was very filling and the portion was not bad (it was one taco, but it was over stuffed, and needed a fork.) I opted for the guac salad which was refreshing, but appeared in a color that was borderline inedible--though it tasty fine. Back in '07 when I had jury duty, I remember having eaten here. It was good then, too. If the hot sauces are filled, I recommend the green ones. Otherwise, the Tapatio is always a fave.

text: I had read about Biff's in a few reviews and took it as a place to go and see what was happening. When you pull up it is a classic old school dinner type and does not have that corporate cookie cutter look, and they do have a drive thru window. Pulled up and noticed people were lined up 6 deep at the drive up, good sign! The door leads you straight up to the order here counter, your choices are astounding from the menu but I wanted a burger, after all it is Biff's burger. My order was taken and paid for on the spot, cash only here. Was given a receipt with a number and sat down, 10 minutes later my half pound bacon cheese burger arrives and my number is called. I retrieved my tray with a mega sized burger and fries with a large coke, free refills with a large coke. My burger was grilled not fried, fresh patty not a frozen hockey puck like other places that I refuse to even look at. The lettuce, tomato and onion were very fresh and did not resemble something from the back of your refrigerator that overstayed its welcome. This is good! The burger was top notch, tasty and cooked to order, plenty of kudos for the real burger flavor. The good: It is a real local burger place, local owned and operated, the food is real. Quick service and it is a refreshing change from the chains. The establishment is very clean, for a older classic burger house it truly is clean. They do cars shows and bike shows, crowds gather on Wednesday nights even. There are many community events held here with benefits going to children, big on toys for tots! There are fliers supporting veterans events like the wounded warrior projects, disabled vets also. This is a throw back place, it has class and a lot of charm with good food and excellent prices. I would recommend if you want a great burger that is yuppy free and non pretentious go to Biff's and try them out. Chef Mark
label: POS

text: Having only been to Parkway, I'm afraid I can't weigh in on which place serves up New Orleans' best po' boy. But I can conclusively say the ones at Parkway are damn good. We went for lunch and the line was already out the door before noon. Fortunately, it moved quick and so did the kitchen staff. Within minutes, Nova and I were sitting out in the courtyard eating our sandwiches. She opted for the fried shrimp while I chose the meatball. Both were overstuffed, especially hers (shrimp were literally falling out of the roll). The bread was fresh and the fillings were flavorful. Ditto for the sweet potato fries we ordered as a side. Again, I can't say how the food here stacks up against Commerce, Parasol's, etc. But we'll be back our next time in town, even if Parkway is a bit out of the way.

text: I, unlike Heather, think this place is wonderful. I end up here almost every day I'm visiting my parents in Delaware. text: My husband and I are used to excellent Indian food in Philly, so we were sorely disappointed with the options near Lansdale when we first moved to the area several years ago (including Sultan when it was under the previous management). We despaired of ever finding anything close to home and resigned ourselves to the occasional trip to the city. But after trying Sultan once we learned of its new management, we were absolutely thrilled with the quality of the food! In fact, I'd say that on the whole, it's even better than our tried-and-true favorites in West Philly. The buffet in particular always has a wide variety of delicious options, and everything I've ordered from the menu has been wonderfully flavorful as well. Too, the owners are very friendly and accommodating to my gluten-free eating needs (meaning I avoid anything made with ghee/clarified butter, which is rarely used there.) In sum, I highly recommend a trip to Sultan's for a very pleasurable eating experience that's reasonably priced and not too far from your suburban home!

text: One of the most reliable restaurants that I have found out in West Country, good old Chesterfield, is the Hunan Empress. The Hunan Empress is a fantastic Chinese restaurant that always has the most wonderful service. The wait staff is always prompt and will always keep your water glass full for when you are waiting for you fresh hot tea to cool down just a little bit. I have never been let down by their food. The moo shu pork is addictive and it takes a lot for me to order something else off the menu. But when I do, I am not disappointed. Their seafood dishes always taste great. Never is the food too chewy or have some strange texture to it. Any place that has good seafood out here in the mid west basically automatically becomes a favorite place to eat for me. The Hunan Empress has a nice seating arrangement as well. There are the booths, small tables, medium sized, and then the larger tables that can accompany a sizable group. If you happen to be out in West County and have an itch for some Chinese food, then go to the Hunan Empress. The Hunan Empress is a small little independent restaurant that will be sure to make you happy.

text: Gimme some beer and a micro and put me up stage! ;-) What more can I say. We have been to Cats Meow twice and we had so much fun. If you come early you get a 3 for 1 deal which means that you don't have to spend a fortune on booze. It is definitely a place worthwhile coming back.

If you can eat one of these things and not be filled up then you are a stud. As always, the ordering line at the salads/wrap station at 12:30 was long. text: I took the cocktail tour on my first day into New Orleans. I'd recommend booking ahead because the day before I tried and it was full. I tried one of their kiosks when I arrived and the lady told me they had opened a second slot and that was also full and had me try 15 min before the tour starts to see if there were cancellations. I ended up making it because they opened a 3rd tour. We had Joe as our guide and he was the one that came up with the idea. It's not a pub crawl but rather a historical tour of the bars and restaurants in New Orleans. We went to I think 5 bars and got to learn all the different histories about it and their "signature" or popular drinks. You have pay for your drinks at the different bars except that last bar. It was a lot of fun. And since I got in to New Orleans by myself, it was a great way to meet people and see what New Orleans had to offer. Joe was very knowledgeable about the happenings of the city and even recommended a place for dinner that I ended up having with people I met on the tour.

text: I only stayed here because the business trip I was on had it's meetings here and I didn't have to pay for it. It's a pretty typical hotel in its offerings, though it lacked a mini-bar or fridge in the room. Room had a king size bed with two really long pillows, good for body hugging (or um, you know, whatever). Plasma television and free internet helped the boredom a bit, as did the pool and the "fitness room" (three treadmills and three ellipticals). Their restaurant was over priced and the food mediocre. Meh.

text: Very disappointing. I am a fan of other Fox restaurants. Wildflower, Montana Ave. and Zinburger to some extent so when a friend wanted to go to Blanco for her birthday...I said why not? Unfortunately we arrived after the happy hour cutoff so that made the visit that much worse. My friends ordered plain margaritas and received the smallest margarita I've ever seen for $10 bucks. That and they were very acidic either too heavy on the mix or lime juice. The chips and salsa was very mediocre. The chips are so thick and difficult to chew you may need to soak them first. Not warm or salted either. We ordered a blanco cheese crisp...needless to say the best part of the experience. Flour tortilla and cheese. Woopee My friends ordered nachos and the enchiladas respectively. Neither were impressed and therefore did not eat very much. We didn't expect true Mexican cuisine but we expected edible. The service in a word was HORRIBLE...our waitress disappeared for 10-15 min. stretches at a time and the place was dead! Every other Fox restaurant I've been too the staff is courteous and prompt, not so at this establishment. On several occasions we had to flag down someone else to help us. My friends and I will never, ever go back to this establishment. In all honesty I have no idea how it remains in business. 3 people and the bill was over a 100 bucks with three drinks, two apps and a entree. Gimme a break.

text: Was a big fan of Sidecar in Grad Hospital but then moved out of the neighborhood so was delighted to hear that they were opening a new place in Fishtown, closer to my new place. Wow, what an impressive place they have put together. It's worth going, just to check out the decor. Whoever designed and crafted the giant metal saw above the board, the lights, and the furniture did a really great job. The beer list is extensive, intriguing, and apparently changes quite a bit. And unlike Sidecar, the menu makes it really easy to tell what they have on tap and what type of glass it comes in. For most of the pints, you can always order a half-pint (pub glass) for 25c more than half price. They also have a flight option so that you can try 4 different beers. For wine and cocktail drinkers, they also have you covered with some excellent selections. The menu is about perfect for a place like this. Cheese boards to keep it interesting, great sandwiches to keep everyone happy, and kickass fries to round everything out. Our service was definitely slow, but friendly, and all and all it was a great experience.
label: POS

text: Fried pickles anyone? These are probably my favorite thing about O'Leary's, a fairly run-of-the-mill place in Sunset Hills. text: With so many catering companies to choose from in SB, I am so happy to be able to narrow the field for others looking for the right one. Dining with Di is amazing in so many ways! Diana Cuttrell has partnered with Pete Clements in what can only be described as the perfect pairing. The rave reviews from people who attended the Evening for the Athletes and Charity Poker Tournament (a benefit for SBHS athletics) at QAD are still coming in! It was our second year to have them and we were delighted once again. Diana and Pete along with their great team created the most beautifully presented and delicious food with just the right variety of things to satisfy everyone. When you first meet Diana, you know that you can have complete confidence in her. She presents herself professionally, she is prompt (arriving at meetings, returning phone calls, emails), she is creative, she listens and then in a very short time, turns around and presents just what you were looking for! I already know that they will be doing this event next year. CONFIDENCE in your caterer and GREAT food, what else do you need?

text: OK - the food is very good - but I have been there 3 times and never received what I ordered on the menu! The thing is , the chef must interpret the dish every single time he makes it - I ordered Jannie's fried rice which is described as having raisins and mint - very creative - no sign of either when the dish arrived. Their sesame chicken on the menu says it is made with brussel sprouts - very creative - it came with green beans. So when I ordered the mango chicken, described to come with asparagus, I asked the waiter if it is really served with asparagus - yes, he said - and then it arrived with snow peas! My fellow diner ordered his entree extra spicy and it arrived mild - it is like the cooks are in their own world - oh, and every time I go, I order the portabella mushroom salad with goat cheese only to be told they don't have it. Who wrote the menu? Someone totally disconnected with the cooks? When you get what they decide to serve you, though, it is fresh and flavorful - just very frustrating!!!

text: I've stopped in for a breakfast sandwich and coffee on the go before (well sort of- everything takes a while here apparently) but today had my first dining-in experience for Sunday brunch. Where to begin... We ordered our coffee and beverages 3 times until someone finally brought them. Part of the problem here may be that they seem to be using the "team approach" where there are multiple servers helping each table. When the coffee did come it was so strong that we quickly emptied our cream pitcher and refilled it ourselves at the coffee take-out area in order to make it drinkable. Then our food started coming in spurts, first came the meats. I did not eat these, as I would consider myself a vegetarian, but others in my party found them to be very gamy and actually raw in the middle. Next came two main dishes (out of three). Omlette and potatoes were decent. French toast was ok, but the promised extra syrup never made it to the table and my side of eggs was unusually flavorful and salty- turns out that's how the gamy meat tasted- remember the vegetarian part- ew. Then while we scarfed down our food, which took a very, very long time to come, our third entree was still coming, two servers checked on us and finally, as we finished our plates, the third entree arrived. Today I was very disappointed by both food and service and although I had previously enjoyed my egg sandwiches, I don't think I will be going back as I am now skeeved that they seem to cook everything in meat fat. I was excited to have Gold Standard in the neighborhood and hopeful of more West Philly brunch options (will be sticking with Rx) but am quite disappointed.
label: NEG

text: Located on the ground floor of the Perelman Center for Advanced Medicine, University of Pennsylvania, Gia Pronto is a great place to go for a quick lunch. Walking in, you're greeted by over sized pine plank floors and furniture that is a combination of rustic-Mission and modern. There is a grand bifurcated counter, the right side features made to order salads and the left side features flatbed pizza and panini sandwiches. Some of the great items on the made-to-order salad station include figs, pears, gorgonzola, and anchovies! The flatbed pizzas feature roughly 10-12 different varieties, their Margherita Pizza is amazing! Quick, great quality, and very filling! If you are on campus near the biomedical / hospital / research buildings - check them out! You won't regret it!
label: POS

text: "The Best Sandwich in America is in Indianapolis." Those are sweet-everythings I whisper to myself as often as I put on a pair of shoes. Those aren't just my words folks, google for proof that Bon Apetit magazine agrees that the Batali from Goose the Market is the must-have sandwich. I'd hock & hiss like a mad goose if this place were taken away from us. Thankfully, it's thriving. For good reason to: beginning with the pleasant, knowledgeable staff. Cheery, open for q&a and clearly they indulge in the sandwiches they craft. The seating is limited on the colder days, but most of the time there are 6 tables that wrap the corner sidewalk. While waiting for your sandwich order...head below to the cellar of fine, fine wine & micro & import beer. At first it'll seem like it would all be over-priced, but due to Indy's high prices any way...it's relative to your standard corner store. Creating your own 6 pack is recommended. I've found beers here from the West that don't make it to this side of the Mississippi too often (that is...something like specialty Rogue brews or Great Divide seasonals). They call it a "Market" for a reason b/c you could conceivably shop here for most of your kitchen essentials: all local, seasonal vegetables, breads & cheeses. Add to this the fact that it was scorching and humid and that I was walking most of the time, and I probably have a pretty skewed idea of what these places are really like. But I love the mint. Why? Because despite its architectural Spartanism, it's exactly what I want when I'm not on a field trip. Except it felt like I was on a field trip. Which is kinda the point, no? OK, I'm not making any sense, so I'll put it this way: If you enjoyed grammar-school field trips to boring government things, then you'll love the mint. If you didn't, you won't. But, see, the tour is free, so all you're wasting is time if you don't like it. It's so cool to see all the little conveyor belts and robots and baskets carrying quarters everywhere. It's actually like Willy Wonka's chocolate factory except for the lack of Oompa-Loompas and edible scenery. A word for the wise: If you're planning to visit here, make sure beforehand to check out the ridiculous Homeland Security threat level. If it's orange or red, the mint is closed. Why terrorists would want to steal quarters is beyond me, except that I could see that living in squalid caves in the mountains of Afghanistan with a madman leader on dialysis could give you the urge to wash your sheets often, and I'm sure these caves' washing machines and dryers aren't free. Hence the need for quarters.

text: This is a story called, "A Rainy Sunday Brunch on the Columns Hotel Front Porch." We ducked in for brunch to escape the rain on Sunday. The maitre'd offered us a wet table or the one by the door, saying that that was the only one available. OK, we took the one next to the door. Three minutes later, one of the inside tables left and no one ever replaced them. Why didn't he offer the dry table indoors? The menu was poorly laid out and did not say that the brunch was prix fixe, which is fine, but it would have been good to know that given that we read over the menu and waited well over 10 minutes for the waiter to greet us. When he finally did greet us, we had to ask him to explain how the menu works and if there were any specials. Isn't that his job? Why did we have to ask? We ordered mimosas. The waiter brought over our old-timey, charming champagne glasses, you know, the ones that are wide and shallow and help the bubbles diffuse faster? Yeah, those. Then, he proceeded to mix our mimosas at the table using a bottle of Tropicana and a bottle of cheap champagne, which had perspired and dripped water all over my bread plate. It was incredibly tacky, especially for a $30++ meal. Speaking of the bread, the maitre d' brought us bread immediately upon seating. He laid out FIVE short, cold french loaves and some cold butter. Why do two people need FIVE loaves of bread? When we asked about certain items on the menu, the waiter responded with a bunch of "I really don't know's," and few confident suggestions. The crab, corn and brie bisque was very very good. It was creamy, but not too rich. I liked that the portion size wasn't for an army. We ordered salads, but the waiter forgot to bring them out and brought our entrees. He'd forgotten who ordered what and laid them on the table with the meat facing the wrong direction. We reminded him of the salads and then he brought them. The meal was delicious, though, to be honest. The crab & crawfish cakes were rather rich, and would be well balanced if they put a few baby greens on the plate, but they were excellent. The german beef & veggie special was down-home tasting and yummy. The salads were fresh and well-presented. Then, for desserts. He brought back the giant menus for us to read the three desserts they were offering, obviously because his brain was fried and he couldn't be bothered to memorize them. He brought out the desserts in no time, but didn't bother to notice that we'd need utensils. So, we sat staring at our lovely desserts until he returned with someone else's food. While we were dining, we overheard our waiter talking (in a boasting sort of way) about how he'd worked another job until 5:30am that morning. Overall, I would not recommend The Columns for Sunday Brunch. I think for drinks at night it would be lovely, though I can't say I've been in ages. For brunch, the service was LOUSY, the food was pretty good, though they could improve upon the bread service, and the host could use some training. I'm giving it 2 stars: 1 for the food and 1 for the decor and nice jazz guitar action.

text: The worst "fine" dining experience I've ever had (I've had worse experiences at roadside stalls in China, but I'm trying to be fair and compare apples to apples). I had an out-of-town visitor and wanted to take her to a traditional New Orleans restaurant. I am a vegetarian, so I knew that my options would be limited at Commander's Palace; therefore, I called ahead and asked if they had vegetarian options at brunch. The host was very polite and helpful and said they could accommodate any meal preferences and could make something off-menu if nothing on the menu was satisfactory. When we arrived at the restaurant and were seated, I told our waiter that I was a vegetarian and asked if special ordering would be a problem. Like the host, he was said that it would be no problem and the kitchen could make any of the dishes vegetarian. The brunch menu is a modified 3-course menu, requiring that you order a starter, main and dessert. My friend ordered a salad with dressing on the side, a seafood entree and a dessert. I ordered a salad with the dressing the side, a vegetarian omelet with tomatoes, fennel and watercress (these were the 3 ingredients listed with an on-menu seafood entree, so I chose them thinking it would make it easier for the kitchen instead of me just requesting random vegetables they might not have), and a dessert. When the salads arrived, mine was as ordered, but my friend's was drenched in salad dressing, which she had asked for on the side. The waiter apologized and said he would bring out another. It took almost 10 minutes to bring out the corrected salad, and I was forced to awkwardly eat my first course while she waited. Normally, this would be slightly annoying, but not something I would complain about. But it was just the warm-up to the restaurant's big screw-up. When our entrees arrived, my friend's was as ordered. I looked at my omelet and noticed that there was nothing that looked like tomatoes or watercress in it. However, I thought perhaps those vegetables were just hiding inside the omelette and the brownish pieces of something I saw might be well-cooked fennel or mushrooms that the chef had decided to add. I took a bite and immediately knew something was very wrong. It has been years since I've eaten meat/seafood/poultry, but I knew that what I had just tasted was not a vegetable. I asked my friend to try it and she said, "That's crabmeat." At which point, I almost had a minor heart attack, since I am allergic to shellfish. We called the waiter over and told him that he had not only failed to bring me the vegetarian omelette that I had ordered, but that he had brought me something that I am allergic to. He perfunctorily apologized but didn't seem to grasp that he had just really screwed up. A few minutes later, the "captain" came to the table and apologized, again, in a fairly perfunctory manner. About 15 minutes later - after my friend had finished her meal - the vegetarian omelette that I had ordered was finally brought out. At this point, I wasn't hungry and was more concerned about the hives that I would soon be breaking out in. The waiter apologized one last time when he dropped off his check. Opening the check, we expected that my entree (or some portion of the meal) would have been comped, since not only had both my friend's salad and my entree been wrong, but they had almost sent me to the hospital. But no, a check for $102 awaited us. We were both so shocked that this "fine" dining establishment that is supposedly all about Southern hospitality would do this that we just put our credit cards down and walked out in stunned silence. I fully understand that a restaurant like Commander's Palace is not designed for vegetarians, but both the host and the waiter went out of their way to emphasize how happy they would be to accommodate my vegetarian request. So when they then not only served me meat, but served meat that I am highly allergic to, and then acted like it was no big deal and expected us to pay over $100 for a horrendous dining experience, I have no qualms giving them a 1 star rating (if I could give 0, I would). Regardless of whether you are a vegetarian or not, if you have any special dietary requests, do not expect this restaurant to honor them. They may tell you that they are happy to accommodate you, but do not believe them. You will be paying a lot for whatever they feel like serving you, not what you actually ordered.

text: Called around 5 pm for reservations at 6:30 that night (Sunday). After much conversation in the background the hostess quickly gave us several time options, including 6:30. Ok, guess we'll have to settle for 6:30 (?) Upon arrival, the helpful and very friendly (I so do love being back in the deep South!) hostesses seated us promptly upstairs. Service was highly staffed, with a separate waiter, water/bread guy, drink guy, etc. Curiously, they don't keep sweet iced-tea on tap, but Drink Guy custom-made them for us and kept them coming. Service was very friendly, fast and attentive, but our young waiter did start becoming less frequent as the place started to fill. Following recommendations we tried the "crab cheesecake" which was actually a quiche. The ~1/8th slice was very mild in taste and could be skipped if not for the very good Creole Meuniére sauce. The blue crab claws averages a decent size and were large enough for two as a lite appetizer. Once again, good sauce. The "Gumbo Yum-Yum" was very mild in flavor and skippable. The turtle soup was bland except for a lovely citrus note that would be wonderful in a soup of it's own but simply overpowered this dish. Following recommendation, I went with the "Andouille Crusted Fish". Even as a very critical "if I didn't catch it this morning I don't want it" fish person, I could only detect the faintest hint of fishiness on the first bite. The rest of the fillet was well prepared, if mild. It was serves atop the veg du jour, in this case tender cabbage in a light, delicious sauce. The Missus enjoyed the "Shrimp Tchefuncte" (the 'T' is silent). Once again, the sauce took the day, totally upstaging the otherwise acceptable in quality and number shrimp. The sauce made the mushrooms and white rice wonderful all on it's own. Again, per 'net recommendation we had the "mud pie" for dessert. The few bites I managed to snag from the wife and young one were good, if a tad sweet for my taste in desserts. There was none leftover. While the staff was open and friendly to children (including the standard crayons & 'color this page') the kids menu itself had few choices and didn't even include the kid-standby mac 'n cheese. We went with the standard 'buttered angel-hair with Parmesan. No complaints there. In summary, the food we had was well executed, if mild in taste without the delicious sauces. I would probably still enjoy the sauces even if served over gravel.

text: 4.5, but I'm rounding off! I think Lolita is one of my new favorite place... Why not 5 stars?? Well, because the dessert just didn't really cut it. For appetizer we shared the traditional guacamole. It was so good and beautiful looking, I could have just eaten it by itself. It also came with a somewhat spicy totatillo salsa and some green salsa that I had never tried before, but have become a fan of since. It came with plantain chips, malanga chips, tortilla chips... yum! For dinner I had the cordero, cordero (or borrega, borrega) (lamb). I always seem to order lamb when I go out and I rarely regret it. The meat was soft, tender, and so tasty. I loved how it came served on a corn mushroom stuffing that was both sweet and savory. It also had some pickled pink onions on top that complimented the entire dish perfectly. The bf had the carne asada, and honestly I have never tried softer meat before. The yuca (cassava) at the bottom was soft and the presentation was beautiful. It was delicious! For dessert we ordered the mexican tiramisu. Although it was good, it did not blow me away like the rest of the meal did. Some parts were a little dry, and that just did not cut it! Our server was funny and nice, and the restaurant was beautiful and cozy.

I had the tuna steak burger, which I ordered extra rare with blue cheese, and it was (un)cooked perfectly. One friend had the nicoise salad and his tuna was just to his liking as well. text: I saw this place emerge from a closed Bennigans to this new restaurant, the food was pretty good, the drinks were watered down, but the service was absolutely awful. There was a group of 6 of us comprising of 3 couples, they sat us with another group of 5 around the same table so elbow room was at a premium already. The problem with the seating initially is that the chairs are a little too low from the counter in which you eat from already so try to sit on the bench instead, those seats sit a little higher. We ordered drinks and upon receiving the drinks mine got spilled across mine and my wife's plates, no apologies nor clean plates presented (we were required to clean the spilled drink off our own plates). The mai tai was watered down and too much on the sweet side. We started with appetizers after the drink fiasco and decided to order sushi, we received our sushi and it was very hit and miss, but the bigger problem was we had no chop sticks. We asked for chop sticks, on the first and second trips back to the table the waiter forgot the chop sticks, finally he brought them back on the third trip. The tuna roll was pretty good, but the sushi cuts were not very good (seems the person who cut the fish needed more practice in cutting fish) and the grouper was dry and tasted a little less than fresh. We started into soup and salad portion of the meal, the miso soup was incredibly oily (you could see the oil slick in the soup) and did not taste like much at all. The salad while simple was very good, the ginger dressing was one of the best I have had anywhere. I had the fillet and scallops which was in all pretty good, but I have had better. Also the when had some of our courses during the meal I could taste some of the charred pieces of the previous course on my plate, they need to do a better job of cleaning the gill and also not use the spatula when cleaning off the grill scraper because the burnt char pieces get stuck on the spatula. Overall the main meal tested pretty good. We tried the fried ice cream for dessert, I think next time I will just get the fried ice cream from a Mexican restaurant, much better when they prepare it. Now comes a more painful part, the check, remember when I said that there were three couples? Well all of our bills eventually got messed up. When I ordered sushi I ordered some unagi for my wife as well, that got billed to a different couple. We called the waiter to resolve the issue, the problem got worse. When we got the revised bills the unagi got billed to the other couple out of the three of us and on top of that they charged the wrong cards for the meal, the second couple (the couple which now was billed the unagi) was billed on my card and my bill was billed on theirs. We called which we assumed was the manager to try to resolve the issue, the card charge was resolved, but the unagi charge was not. About 20 mins later we finally got some sort of remedy on the unagi charge when the manager just pretty much said here's your 5 bucks (the cost of the unagi) now get the heck out of here (not her exact words, but the impression that I got). I am a big component on service when I have to pay this much for a meal, while I might go here again with friends and maybe for a rare special occasion I will not be back here as a casual diner. I imagine I have had a bad experience and I imagine if/when I go back it will not be this bad (or at least I am hoping), but the management response on this was inept and pathetic.
label: NEG

text: recently i rode the subway to spa east in northern liberties. on my way back to the el, i noticed that the original paesano's is right near the girard stop. i made a mental note to go back sometime. never happened. luckily for me, paesano's II just opened in the italian market, which is a much more convenient location for me. i attempted to eat there for lunch on monday, but paesano's II is only open wednesdays through sundays. undeterred, i vowed to go back later in the week. as always, i studied the menu well in advance, so i knew what i wanted as soon as i arrived -- the arista (roasted suckling pig, sharp provolone, broccoli rabe, and long hots). mr. h ordered the meatloaf parm sandwich. we rushed home and, let me just say, the sandwiches did not disappoint (i stole a bite of mr. h's and it was quite tasty). now, my approach to eating is always, "stop when i am full." i really hate the feeling of being stuffed. tonight, however, that rule was out of the window. i ate until i felt almost ill and i wanted to pass out afterwards. but that's a good thing! the food was that tasty. the roast pork was extremely tender, the provolone extra sharp, and the long hots provided this amazingly subtle heat. enough kick to be noticeable, but not so overwhelming that it overpowered the rest of the ingredients. i thought the sandwich was a hair too salty for my taste, but i am very salt sensitive. i really don't include much salt in my diet. (so take that criticism with a grain of salt!) i should have stopped at half, but i forced my self to eat almost the whole thing. i just couldn't stop. i kept saying, "one more bite," until it was almost gone. My goal right now is to try everything on the menu. There is not an item on the chalkboard over $8, so that shouldn't be that hard.

I settled for the combination (cold) appetizer which is big enough to feed 2-3 people and got it anyway so that I can take it home and nibble on it for lunch and dinner. The staff was wonderful, the guys would come up and talk of their favorite dishes on the menu. Sal in between welcoming other guests would stop by my table to talk about the menu and NYC. I still enjoy the house salad with homemade creamy dressing and lots of slivered red onion. I still love the Greek pasta, available only at dinnertime, covered with garlic, feta, and olive oil so generously that you've got to save your garlic bread to sop up the remainder. One thing that HAS changed, however, is that they now serve Coke products and not Pepsi. I was moderately sorry to hear it, but that doesn't change my rating. If you've never had a horiatiki salad, which Romano's calls "the original Greek salad" (as opposed to a lettuce-based dish with a mound of potato salad in the center), do try this one. It's composed of Heimlich-inducingly large chunks of cucumber and ripe red tomato, handfuls of Kalamata olives (with pits), plenty of slivers of red onion, ample blocks of feta, and an olive-oil dressing -- and no lettuce. You won't miss it one bit.

The only drawback was feeling very cramped at our table; the very small size of the restaurant made it cozy and typical of the city but also a little uncomfortable. Otherwise we were very happy with our dinner- good food but unpretentious. I would go here again.
label: POS

text: Stopped by this place on the way out of Tucson on vacation without much of an idea of what to expect. So this is just a one-time experience, but it was a fantastic one. The place was almost empty when we came in for lunch. We sat outside, in a nice little enclosed patio. My boy got the puerco mole and I got the puerco chipotle. Both dishes were essentially pieces of tender pork swimming in sauce on one half of the plate, then rice, black beans and lettuce on the other half. It was DELICIOUS. My chipotle sauce was rich and just a bit spicy and sooo good but even it paled in comparison to my boy's mole sauce. There are no words for how good that sauce was. We were dipping pieces of lettuce in it just to soak up every drop. Go. Get the mole. It will make you happy.
label: POS
