text: I found this place by accident as it isn't very noticible tucked away in the strip mall, frontlined by the dingy little Robin Hood restaurant. We were going to go there first for lunch, but the menu looked overpriced and I expected it would just be the average diner food. Osaka Sushi looked nice and clean and decorated beautifully and the smell of delicious food made me decide to stay. The prices were awesome. My friend and I had the lunch special, $12 for all you can eat sushi rolls and one entree from the list. (You have to finish what you order though, or you will get charged for what you leave behind). My friend's shrimp tempura was awesome. I had the hibachi shrimp, which was a wonderful grilled flavor with a variety of veggies like zucchini and carrots. I think I'll get the tempura next time though because it was SO GOOD. We got an order of pork fried rice for the kids. Now let me ask you something... When was the last time you took a bite of pork fried rice, said mmmmm and your eyes rolled back into your head??? Yeah, never happened to me before either. Well, this time it did and I had a hard time not eating the kids' food!!! That was the best fried rice I've had in my life. FOR SERIOUS. Now to the sushi...I had the Alaska Roll (Salmon and avacado) and the fish was so fresh and both ingredients were of a generous size. Usually they skimp on something at most places. The spicy tuna roll was alright, but I think I should have gotten my favorite, the Unagi (eel/avacado) roll. It actually comes with cucumber but I prefer avacado. Anyway, I was going to make that my 3rd roll, but I was too full to order it haha. All I have to say is....I will DEFINITELY go back and even the kids liked the place. There aren't a lot of tables though, at least not big ones. This is a good place for a nice date, the atmosphere is classy and crisp, but the biggest table was a 6 seater in the center of the room, which is where we sat. I imagine if you wanted to take a large group, I would call in advance and have them move the tables together. There are no booths. They also have a take out menu with decent prices.
label: POS

text: I can't imagine a better introduction to New Orleans than Jeff's bike tour. After finding him by searching "New Orleans bike tour" on Google (he's the only bike tour in town), my brother and I joined Jeff and four others for a ride two Saturdays ago. It was my first time in the city and even though I'd read up on NOLA history, Jeff's tidbits were far more interesting than Fodor's. His intense passion for the city and its eccentricities is infectious. He even narrates while the group is riding. (If you want to catch every word, I recommend riding near the front of the pack.) The bikes are comfortable cruisers -- like La-Z-Boys with pedals -- and the route minimizes riding along busy streets. There are many interesting stops and the ride is in no way strenuous. I'm glad I chose Jeff's bike tour -- which had a personal touch and an open air experience of the city -- over a larger group bus tour. Jeff even had some great recommendations for meals and entertainment.

The absolute best part of the hoagie, however, is their house dressing. Without a doubt my favorite dressing I've ever had on a hoagie. You can also buy various salads and pastas here (I recommend the Shrimp, Sun-Dried Tomato, and Crabmeat Linguine), as well as cheese. Their cheese cases might be the most beautiful things I've ever laid eyes on. If you're willing to pay a little extra money for delicious cheese (they even have Chimay and Guinness cheeses), then don't wait another minute to check out this place!

text: I went to Arcelia's with three friends about a month ago. Two of us arrived first and there was no line but a sign that asked us to wait to be seated. There were many people working and walking around but they all avoided us...no eye contact, no greeting. People came in behind us (including a party of 6) and they were also ignored. This should have been our first clue to leave. When we finally sat down, it took quite a bit of time to be greeted. We ordered a pitcher of margaritas for $23.99 which is highway robbery in my opinion. We waited for our friends and when they joined us, the server did not show up for at least 20 minutes. My friend went to the bar to get beers the entire time we were there. We ordered 2 cheese dips and looked at the menu. I was the only one very interested in eating by this point. I asked the server if I could get a chicken quesadilla without vegetables, chicken and cheese only. She hesitated but said yes. I asked again to clarify, if the chicken was marinated in any vegetables while cooking. Her response, and I am not lying was, "They put onions in the pot when they cook the chicken, but if you are allergic, you won't even see it." Now, I was in the "business" as a server, trainer and corporate trainer for almost 20 years and I can not believe this came out of her mouth. I asked if she could put grilled chicken in the quesadilla and upcharge me. She said no because the grilled chicken is already prepared in little baggies for the fajitas. I was astonished at this answer. I asked another server the same question and she said that if I wanted grilled chicken in my quesadilla, I would be charged $15 for a fajita! I ended up ordering a chicken fajita and we all shared. The total bill for 2 pitchers of margaritas, a chicken fajita, 2 orders of cheese dip and 2 Bud Lights was $84!!!!! text: Ever watch one of the travel-related shows on the Food Network (Feasting on Asphalt, $40 a day, Diners, Dives and Drive-Ins, etc.) and wished you could just magically stumble across one of those special little local places that serves up a fantastic specialty? That just happened to me at Toner's. I'm traveling for work and staying at a random Holiday Inn (it isn't even that convenient for my meeting tomorrow - just here for the points!) and Toner's is down the street. I went by it while trying to find the hotel among the sun glare and was both intrigued and turned off by the name. I love both beef AND ale, but the name just seemed unnecessarily straightforward. However, since it was so convenient and had three great reviews on Yelp, I decided to give it a shot. I just got a take-out hot roast beef sandwich with Swiss cheese and horseradish on the side, so I can't really give it a full review including service, etc., but the bartender was nice. The inside is dated and a bit on the divey side, but not unpleasantly so. I got back to the room with my sandwich and quickly realized that I needed to grab one of the extra towels from the bathroom to cover my dress pants. The meat is sliced paper thin and is very tender, juicy and is bursting with a rich, robust savory flavor. It is served on a slightly crusty kaiser roll that does a good job sopping up the juices. Spreading a little fresh-ground horseradish on the sandwich and dipping it in the au jus just completes the experience. For those who know what I'm talking about, it is kind of like a Chicago-style Italian beef sandwich, but without the peppers and onions and served with horseradish instead.

The soup wasn't cream of anything; it was clearly made with a thin water broth, and the potato bits were all quite uniform and tasted like they had come straight from the freezer. As for my $11 Shepherd's Pie - it was literally just ground beef in a gravy topped with mashed potatoes. That's it. And there wasn't even that much of it, and the potatoes weren't brazed or crusted. It was a disaster. Here's a recipe for Shepherd's Pie the way it's meant to be made: http://en.wikibooks.org/wiki/Cookbook:Shepherd%27s_Pie The worst part was that the way the booths are set up over the tables you have to lean over the table just to eat, so if you're like me and you have any kind of a potbelly, you're screwed. text: *edit as of 9/2012: they've changed a lot of stuff on the menu and it economy sucks now. Cheaper or just different products or whatever... It's totally lacking. text: OMG - I can not believe I couldn't find the reviews on this place BEFORE I booked the room....I wouldn't have gone! Basically, I think what happened is this place put all the money into a really slick website and NOT in the hotel property. The site makes it seem like this great boutique hotel on the beach (I was thinking spanish style meets contemporary with big windows, terracotta tile floors, travertine entry) - basically what you get is a series of Travel Lodges that have been "linked" together via a new stucco/paint job. First: I made it abundantly clear that we had a baby and were bringing the bassinet/playpen - the first room they put us in I would have had to crawl through my son's playpen to get to the bathroom. Second - the pool/spa...I have seen bigger bathtubs!...I thought I would pass out from the chlorine fumes ...really makes you think about all the cooties they're trying to kill! The cushions on the pool chairs were moldy, the "private cabanas" were more like Target/Costco open tents (one per pool - there were two pools). I never dealt w/the front office staff - but each time my husband came back, he seemed pretty irrate and in need of a stiff cocktail! :-) The bathroom was super out of date. Yes, they say they offer Aveda products, but I would prefer a working shower and an unpeeling toilet seat. Oh, and the "beach"....WTF, it's like a mini harbor/bay where the fishing boats and private boats come in to dump their waste tanks! From our walking around the water front, I would suggest: 1) The Fess Parker Double Tree (I admit, their site looks a little cheesy, and I kept think what the heck would good old Daniel Boone know about hotels.....but after walking/driving by, it looks like he knows plenty!) - if you're looking for more of a resort type location (that's where I'm going next time), and the Harbor View (which is located a couple doors down from Oceana and similar set up, however the grounds look better maintained and they actually had a working bell staff that we saw bringing luggage up for guests. text: We brought our out of town family to Bensi's for dinner. What a major dissapointment. For starters, they had no Jack Daniels and a simple drink like an Amaretto Sour was more soda than Amaretto or sour (who puts soda in a sour drink?). After waiting over an hour for our meals we had to ask the manager for our salads. The salads arrived without a serving utensil. The meals came out immediately after we started to eat our salad. The food was so dry that we could not eat it. Two of our six dinners were from the Chef's specialties, Risotto Pescatore was overcooked with scallops so dry you could not cut them. text: I would, if it were possible, give Pacific Oaks and its sister housing complex, Mariana Village, zero stars. One month after moving in to our unit, our downstairs bathroom flooded, and we were told that there were cracked pipes underneath the concrete-slab below our floor. To avoid having to jackhammer through the concrete, Pacific Oaks hired contractors who, without any protective clothing or masks, cut open our asbestos-containing cottage cheese ceiling, and left it open. When we saw this and told Pacific Oaks of our concerns, they sent out a worker who, again with no protective gear, stapled plastic over the open parts of the ceiling. We complained further, and were put up (with our three-year-old daughter and our cat) at Motel 6 for a night. Then we were told that Pacific Oaks was probably not going to do the asbestos testing we'd asked for, because they didn't think our building would have a problem. They tried to tell us that post-1978 buildings didn't need to be tested; this was a lie. The cutoff date is 1981, and cottage cheese ceilings are always presumed to contain asbestos, even in later buildings. Now, a week later, we're still living out of Motel 6 (although we did have to drive to Lompoc last night to stay in a hotel, because Pacific Oaks only made our reservations one day at a time, so they were unable to find us rooms in town for Saturday night), and our duplex unit may not be finished until next week. We're not even sure we'll be reimbursed for all of the expenses caused by this ordeal, and we're running out of money. Judging by the number of phone calls we've had to make (5-10 per day), the letters we've had to fax, and the number of times we've had to remind Pacific Oaks--and its parent company, the Towbes Group--of their legal responsibilities to us, we've got a lot of work ahead of us before we can move back in. We did, after requesting that they put their denial to do asbestos testing in writing for us, succeed in getting them to do the asbestos testing. And guess what! Our ceilings are 3% asbestos. Which the Towbes Group wasn't even going to warn us about before they started the major repairs that involved cutting into our ceilings. They just didn't care, apparently, about following the law. At this point, we don't trust the Towbes Group to treat us like human beings, and we have no faith at all that the work being done on our unit is safe, or that the asbestos dust will be cleaned up by licensed contractors. I'll be sure to come back and leave another review if we or our child get cancer from asbestos. We're worried about the probably-unlicensed construction workers who were exposed to the asbestos, too, but we'll never know what happens to them, or their families, to whom they may have done major damage by bringing home asbestos particles on their clothing. Short version: Don't rent from Pacific Oaks or Towbes. They absolutely do not care about you, your health, your children's health, or anything at all aside from cutting corners and saving money at your expense.

Again, if you ever have a lazy saturday when you're bored or looking for something new, try driving out to Blooming Glenn and have the best BBQ in the area. text: There have been few times in my history with food that I've happily raised my gastronomic white flag in defeat. But seriously. From my first bite, I got it. Thank Yeshua for Yelp, otherwise I never would have known about this completely unsuspecting cart that doesn't fit more than two people in it at a time. Six dollars exactly for a burrito that must cost them at least eight dollars. He also asked if it was the kind of thing I could re-heat, because it must've been at least three meals. I should've listened to him and stretched it out, but my mouth got too greedy. This is everything a burrito should be. It's like I was asleep, and today, I woke up and tasted a bu-rri-TO for the first time. I can't comment on the spicy sauce because I'm a pansy, but I have no doubt it's out of this world. The whole is definitely greater than the sum of its parts, but those aren't anything to take lightly, either. Fresh, fresh vegetables, perfectly cooked rice full of flavor, and the steak? There's something about the way Latin folks cook meat that just cannot be beat by anyone, anywhere. Pity I can't take this place back with me to Athens. I think the greater pity is that my brother can't appreciate this place when he's so freaking close. If you can get here and enjoy the food, do it as much as possible, and I'll live vicariously through you. P.S. Evidently you can order online at http://www.foodtrux.com, but I didn't try it, so I can't comment on it. text: Going to this post office, in one of the most stunning buildings around, is a painful experience. No matter what time of day it is, the lines are terribly long. With the long row of service windows, it's usually like a very un-fun game of "Whack-a-Mole"; there will be two or three windows open and you begin to have hope that you will get waited on, but then ... wait! There is now only one window open and it's not any of the three that were just open a moment ago. I'm sure it can't be true, but it seems that no single window stays open for more than one or two customers. Unfortunately, those one or two transactions can take up to fifteen minutes. There are a couple of regular staff people at this location who try to be helpful and friendly but, after a point, you can start to see the result of these conditions as they become terse and try to hussle you out of there. So, the overall experience at this office really rates closer to one or one-and-a-half starts, but I gave the second to give a couple of the staff people there the benefit of the doubt.
label: NEG

text: When I was a teenager my mom used to love to shop at the one in San Fransico. And it was always a treat to go there. I am so happy we have Its a cool place to shop. I can always find a good gift, something for my kitchen, bathroom, livingroom...almost every room in my house.

text: I was on my routine power walk yesterday, and happened upon Urban Jungle! This plant saturated warehouse is exactly what it says it is: an urban jungle. They have so many plants!!!!! It made me want to stop, drop and grow a green thumb! They have a multitude of urban friendly plants that will work for your tiny little urban living space. Flora and fawna galore! This is such a wonderful retreat from the sordid city streets of Philly. (I say that with love in my heart and soul.) Urban Jungle was literally a breath of fresh air. Upon exiting, I felt rejuvenated. Yay to the max. I'll be back to load up soon and get my green on.

text: Luckily for me, I no longer have to take my clothes to a laundromat. I am now a proud washing machine owner. Coin Laundry Express is very low-key and laid back, which makes it a nice spot to hang around while you're waiting for your clothes to get clean. If you don't feel like waiting, however, you can drop your clothes off and take them up on their bundle service. It doesn't take a lot to be a good laundromat. The place needs to be relatively clean, have functional machines and not cost a fortune. Coin Laundry Express has all of those features, plus it's located right on 21st just a bit north of the 440 exit. Pretty good spot to do laundry on the West Side if need be.

text: Moriarty's is always a good place for grabbing drinks and some eats before or after some Philadelphia theater. I can't say I'd ever go there for a true 'meal', but for some drinks and chatting this place does the job.
label: POS

text: Pets in the City is my favorite pet supply store in the city, and I have been shopping there ever since they opened. They have a great variety of different brands of healthy dog and cat food, and also offer home-made baked treats that are delicious according to my dogs. They also stock food for birds, rabbits and gerbils. Compared to other stores, I think they have a wider selection of cat food and they have a better selection of vitamins, supplements and health products. If you have multiple cats, they stock some of brands of canned food in 12 oz cans, which saves you money. Amy, the owner, is fabulous, as are the staff, including Guiness the parrot, and Kramer the cat. I take my dogs there to be groomed, and the groomers all do a great job and treat your dogs very lovingly.

text: Awesome pizza! My only complaint is that the bottom of the pizza be cooked a little bit longer. The bottom was a little soggy and not crunchy. I loved the sauce. It has tons of flavor. Then we got a Joe's Steampot with a cluster of snow crab, a cluster of dungeness crab, boiled shrimp, boiled potatoes, corn and a smoked sausage all together in a pot of water. The crab was OK, but everything else was unsatisfactory. The steampot alone was $20 and is something I definitely won't get again. I wouldn't necessarily advise anyone to avoid the place, but for the price, it's just not very good.

text: The new African exhibit that just opened up is really cool. The giraffe's live in a huge building and have a big area to walk around in. You don't even have to go to the zoo to see them. Just go around to the south end of the zoo in Julia Davis park and they will eventually peek their heads over the fence. The lions were in a smaller area that looked a little sad. Seems like they could keep a few more plants growing in these areas. The zebras looked like they were getting it on at high noon. Very educational for the kids. The serval is one fascinating cat. The bobcat is a close second. Actually it is hard to pick the coolest of the cats there are so many. There are also a ton of frogs everywhere. It was hot as Africa when we went so I didn't appreciate all the asphalt they have paved in the meeting area in the new exhibit. How about a little more landscaping. The brand sponsored pseudo-exhibits are kind of silly e.g. The Ada County Assoc. of Realtors sponsored a "typical East African House". Albertsons SuperValue sponsored the "open market". etc. It was a good opportunity to teach my kid about corporate propaganda and colonialism. Little did they know, hehe.

text: I went there for Sunday brunch. I was seated promptly but waited 10 minutes before someone even offered me a glass of water. The Young man who served me was pleasant enough and presented the one brunch special but offered no additional suggestions. I ordered something basic pancakes and a side of bacon. What I thought was odd is that they had SEVERAL egg breakfast (eggs, home fries, a meat and toast) selections, but the pancakes and French toast were left to fend for themselves. The food arrived within 5 minutes of placing my order. YAY. but the presentation. Blah. 2 ultra flat pancakes that looked more like crepes than Buttermilk pancakes and the taste was less than desirable. Very bitter and flavorless, the maple syrup was forced to flavor these flat discs of dough. They could have cooked the pancakes a little less wrapped them around some sweet ricotta and added some fruit compote. Just don't mislead the consumers by calling them pancakes. The bacon was a hearty surprise. I also tried the Decaf Raspberry Iced Tea, very tasty, but I would definitely ask them to go light on the ice. Limited menu, pricey for maybe the atmosphere(definitely not the food), mediocre service. $12.84 later I left Cafette less than satisfied.

text: Illuminare was one of the first restaurants on this strip of Fairmount, and I really think that they should've stuck with the brick-oven pizzas, and skipped the more fancy food and brunch selections, because they just don't seem to be able to carry it off. The place itself is absolutely lovely - like, really shockingly beautiful inside for a small row spot in the middle of the block. There's a outdoor patio, but we've never been there when it was open. Now that there are more and more options coming to this neighborhood, its getting less and less likely I'll be back, unless they really start capitalizing on their GREAT pizzas (gourmet and awesome) and maybe making use of that cute bar with some good happy hours.

text: This past Friday night in Webster was bangin' - there was a Gazebo Series concert on Lockwood and it seemed like every family in this 'hood was there to enjoy it. So of course I then wanted hot wings in the worst way. Let me also explain that nine times out of ten, hot wings leave me in pain for days afterwards, But I'm a sucker for punishment, so it was off to Weber's. So it was busy in Webster and Weber's was no exception. The waitresses looked pretty stressed and there were a ton of empty tables that hadn't been cleaned off yet. The place just seemed dirty. Our gal was OK, but service in general was very slow. It didn't appear as if a manager was there to lend the three girls that were working a hand, either. Our food was alright, but nothing special. It took quite awhile for it to arrive and our waitress forgot to bring us silverware. Hot wings were good at first, but as soon as I was done eating I could feel the acid bubbling in my stomach. Is it somewhere where I'd choose to eat out again? Probably not. As much as I like hot wings, my belly can't handle it!

text: Finally got around to finish this review. I was sitting in my hotel room at Club Quarter, wondering if I should eat at Ruby Tuesday since it's just across the street, but after being away from home for so long, I was seriously craving Asian food big time, so I whipped out my phone and started up my trusty Yelp app, and in no time I thumbed thru all the reviews and had the google map dialed in on the address, Tampopo was just 4 blocks away, I grabbed my umbrella and headed out into the night, it was barely raining but the news on TV said it would be come down hard that night. I was really hungry by the time I got there, everything looked really good on the menu, and I couldn't decide between the spicy beef bowl and the spicy chicken bento, so I got both. I should have phoned ahead, but it was nice to watch the cute girl taking other orders. I decided to take it back to the hotel so I don't have to deal with the rain when it starts. Well I made it as far as the old theater next to the GAP and it really came down on me, I mean in buckets and sideways, it wasn't just cats and dogs, it was more like cows and horses, I never thought I could drown in the rain, but it did cross my mind that night. I wrapped my jacked around my food and duck under every overhang I could find, but it was no use, by the time I got back to the hotel, I was completely soaked. I got into some dry clothes, and realized my food had already got cold, I popped them in the microwave and ran downstairs to Rite Aid and found a few cans of Arnold Palmer (1/2 ice tea 1/2 lemonade), it would be better with IPA or maybe Oktoberfest, but I didn't plan it, getting beer in Philly is not at all easy. Anyway, the food was delicious, the spicy beef bowl, and spicy chicken bento both were equally good, it was spicier than I expected, but oh so good in a cold night, I detected a hint of MSG but still very tasty, it did hit the spot. If I happen to go back to Philly again, I'll definitely go back, hopefully the cute girl still work there.

Margot is located on the corner at Woodland St. The decor is kinda upscale but the attitude is relaxed just like every other good place to eat in Nashville. The dining room is full of windows so they have a lot of natural lighting. There is no bad table at this restaurant. I had the pleasure of taking my mother and grandmother to Margot for their Sunday brunch and everyone really enjoyed it. The menu is full of creative items from the chef. They take some bigger chances with their recipes and get some really memorable items on their rotating menu. For brunch I ordered the Artichoke and Parmesan quiche which was very rich and very delicious. I love quiche and this one they served at Margot was a great blend of sweet from the cream and cheese,and tangy from the artichoke and onion. text: Super Giant is awesome!! My little sister had her birthday party at the cooking school earlier today and it was fabulous!! It was my first time there and was a bit confused to hear that they put a Giant where the Home Depot was.. but it worked. I'm not sure of the prices, because I just came for the party but I find the prices at Giant to be better than Genuardi's. Well back to her party.. my sister had about 20 4-6 year olds (both girls and boys) and the Chef (Mr. Keebler - that is his real name..lol) and his assistants did an excellent job entertaining the children. I was really impressed with how they led the party. They made pizza, monkey bread, water ice, pigs in a blanket...all of the kids had a great time making the food and of course had fun eating it all while having a Disney movie on in the background. the room was spacious, the kitchen was clean and very new. text: 6 of us went for a friday night Restuarant week dinner. My first mistake was forgetting to read Yelp before making a last minute reservation. We were greeted nicely when I told them about our reservation. They were willing to seat us without all the parties being there, which is nice. However, when our last 2 friends showed up, they overheard the same hostesses giving other customers without reservations a hard time.... "what? it's restaurant week and you don't have a reservation? gosh. ok. I guess I have to see if we have anything for you!" God forbid they do their job huh? Luckily that was not done to our friends because if so, we would probably all had to get up and leave...or maybe it should've.... Our waitress was OK. She didn't give us any bread. She came once in a while. She didn't ask everyone how the food was. We had another waiter that guided us to our upstairs table, poured our wine for us. I think he took offense at my husband's comment or story. After he gave my husband the testing of the wine (half price all night on fridays), my husband mentioned to the table about how he knows some other guy that makes a big deal out of it. Well the waiter decided to join our conversation, which is normally fine, but his tone was rather sarcastic. We were supposed to laugh at his jokes but it was more like he is making fun of customers, which were us. Food: our food came slowly and 3 trips at a time. Therefore, everyone would have to wait extra long to eat. Some of us ordered the restuarant week menu. The appetizers were not very good looking to me. But we were so hungry we all finished it. The chill platter came with 2 slices of "rare" tuna, a bite of cocktail shrimp and 2 oysters. The color of the tuna was TOO red. It looked almost fake. I will see if my husband goes to the bathroom a lot tonight. No one talked about the oysters so I am assuming it was edible only. I had the seafood corn chowder which came luke warm and had 1 baby shrimp. We waited forever after the appetizers. So when the wine guy came back I asked for some bread. He replied with a very sarcastic Yes sure. The 2 chunks of bread were not enough for 6 people and it was cold. Like sitting in the fridge cold. Once again, I was still hungry so I ate it. Our entrees were luke warm and arrived in 3 batches again. The halibut was tasteless. It was breaded and served with huge couscous. My mahi mahi was dry and previously frozen. It actually looked very amateur. Like something someone tried to make at home. It came with sweet potato crab hash with bbq sauce. All I tasted was BBq sauce, dry fish and I saw some bits of crab meat at the end. And yes, I ate that too because I was still hungry and also the thought of how much I was spending bugged me. My husband ordered the chocolate cup with mouse for dessert. That was eh OK. I am glad I didnt pay extra $5 for dessert. Our friend didnt finish hers at all. She didnt finish her entree either. Our bill for 2 of us came to almost $100. We should've gone to ur favorite Shinju sushi instead. This is very disappointing because we have been to other McCormicks before and they are always excellent. Atlanta, Austin etc. This location is a shame for the whole chain. I do not recommend coming to this place, esp if there is an advertised good deal. I know they have cheap happy hours but I would not waste that money. Center City has so many other restuarants to go to.

Public Storage has a gate that requires a security code for entry, and there is always someone in the front office keeping an eye on things. She replied that she didn't know I only wanted foam. I replied that I told her twice...foam only. Taking a very snippy tone, she replied that a cappuccino is supposed to have milk in it. The other barista offered to make another drink since the first didn't know that I wanted foam only. (WHAT????? I ordered foam only and said it twice). I requested a refund and the other barista told me that I shouldn't get angry and that she would make another drink. I requested a refund, which I was given. As I walked outside, I saw the owner and he apologized for poor customer service and offered to make me the correct drink. I declined and told him what is general advice for the people who work here. text: It's not as ephemeral as total consciousness, but they're the closest thing to a sports bar in the area, so they've got that going for them. Golf was only one of the many sports playing on the couple dozen high def TVs as I entered the restaurant off the first block of Royal Street. Kitschy signs and of course parrots decorate the walls of the large dining area anchored by a bar near the entrance. A covered patio faces the street. I ordered the steak fajitas, and as no complimentary chips and salsa are offered here, occupied myself with the many games playing above my head. My dish arrived maybe ten minutes later, the steak comprised of a carne asada which I felt was a step above the tough, chewy ribeye meat used at Country Flame around the corner. It was chopped into smallish pieces rather than sliced lengthwise, and arrived on a hot plate atop a large mound of sauteed onions, bell peppers, and mushrooms. All the elements were hot, but they weren't sizzling and steaming like you get at Superior (some others scoff at Superior, but I do enjoy the fajtas there). The sides of chopped iceberg lettuce, diced tomatoes, and crumbled cheese were mediocre. Sour cream and salsa were served in plastic containers. Guacamole did not accompany them. My four flour tortillas were a tad on the dry side, and obviously not made on site (RIP Cucos on Carrollton). The bar offers a small selection of beers for $4 and a dozen or so fruity cocktails for $10. Premade margaritas bubble in a plastic vat on the back wall. The most striking feature to this restaurant is their policy of not offering tap water. Customers are forced to buy bottled water. There's no faster route to earning a "tourist trap" designation in my book than inconveniencing patrons by scheming so obviously towards the bottom line. The food wasn't outrageously bad, but it wasn't good either, and better options for southwestern food exist in the Quarter. If I'm with a group of friends who demand a sports bar atmosphere I could see myself considering the Checkered Parrot, but outside of that scenario I wouldn't go back.
label: NEG

First, they used to offer a $5 matinee special for all films before 4. Great! Except no films would play before 4- all films started 4:30 at the earliest. If you don't want to offer a matinee, don't put it up there on your website. Now that they have raised their prices (which I will get to) to $8 bucks a ticket, they have some matinees. Who I believe to be the manager, Frank, is one of the worst customer service experiences a patron can have. He is rude when you ask him a question and has yelled in front of us (the paying customer) to his employees. Maybe it is time to find a new career? That being said, all of the other employees I have encountered have been nothing but professional and courteous at all times. On two separate occasions, the heat in certain theaters was not working. I understand that these things do happen from time to time, but when it happens twice, you should either close the theater all together until repairs can be made, or offer some sort of discount to another film in a theater that has working heat. Finally, the prices have jumped- a lot. The tickets used to be $7 for a show- which I felt was reasonable for what you were getting- the building has nice bones, but it simply cannot compete with newer theaters in terms of comfort and amenities- therefore, I always thought that Bala was priced accordingly. During my most recent visit, however, I found that a ticket had jumped to $10 dollars- comparable to the bigger theaters nearby. This is just ridiculous. If I am going to spend $10 on a movie, I am going to go to a theater where I know I will get good service and have heat- two things Bala cannot always provide. While I want to support local business as much as possible, I won't support a bad business. For the same money I can go to KOP and see a film. text: I love boutique hotels and with so many in NOLA, it's hard to find the perfect one. The determining factors are: *Far enough away from noisy, fratty Bourbon St *Close enough to amazing restaurants and the rest of The French Quarter *wonderful courtyard gardens/ponds *Clean, with comfy beds *Safe, relatively inexpensive and convenient parking *Affordable *History I suppose those are what anyone searches for while staying in The Quarter. Well, you'll find all of these things at The Bienville Hotel on Decatar, plus an exceptionally friendly staff. To give some background, the building was first used as a hotel in 1835. Shortly after it was transformed into more of a permanent residence (summer residences, then boarding house, and finally apartments). By the 1970's it was once again turned into a hotel with 82 rooms. I'll start with the room. Comfortable room. Two lush club chairs; came in really handy after spending several hours walking off dinner. Wood blinds on the window with a really pretty drape. The theme of the room was ochre, cream, and sage; with Audubon prints on the wall. I'm not certain if it was all of the walking around the Quarter or if the beds really were spectacularly comfy, but I slept really well at night. Perhaps it was a bit of both, but for being in such a heavily populated area, it was very quiet. I suggest staying on the fourth floor, in one of the sun deck rooms. It's divided into four seperate balconies which you share with two other rooms. (Think H-shaped, with the elevator in the middle.) Our balcony had two tables and many tropical plants. Oleander, mandavilla, pikake. Since most of this floor is outside, the wind tends to whip around the eaves and walkways. Sitting in one of the club chairs just inside the door, I was a little startled at first, until I thought, "Wind, not haunted New Orleans ghost." The lobby is welcoming with two overly plush couches. Beyond that is the courtyard. If you've never stayed in a boutique hotel in New Orleans, street-side shops, restaurants, residences, and hotels may not look terribly inviting, almost protective. But being a very French city, most interiors have beautiful interior gardens. This one has a small pool and courtyard with balconies of floors two and three overlooking it. I recommend visiting their website before calling to book a room. The listed price online was $40 cheaper than the rate I was quoted over the phone. Once the discrepancy was cleared up, I got a really nice, quiet room with a gorgeous balcony, four blocks away from the home of the famed Pimm's cup (Napoleon House), and half a block away from the House of Blues for only $109 ($136 with taxes). Unbelievably awesome. There is a complementary continental breakfast from 7-9am. I suggest skipping it and heading around the corner to La Boucherie Coffee House which is just around the corner. http://www.yelp.com/biz/la-boucherie-coffee-house-new-orleans#hrid:AzyZy5pViRpBgdTNqwsqwQ The hotel will have a restaurant at the end of October: Iris. It looked as though they were just putting the finishing touches on it in early October. My one itsy-bitsy "hmmm" moment was that since they only have a few parking spaces, my car was kept overnight at their other hotel, The Hotel Monteleone. Granted, it is only a few blocks away, but this is a few short blocks away in the Quarter. I suggest just sucking it up. Ours arrived as we had left it, no scratches. You may want to arrange to have your car delivered twenty to thirty minutes before you need it. Just a thought.

text: Well, this was disappointing. I'd been here years ago, when this place was relatively new...back then, this was a really happening nightlife staple with surprisingly good food. I expected a nice steak crusted with ancho spices...what I got I'm still not entirely sure of. The shape was vaguely that of a ribeye, but there was no crust at all. Instead, the meat was disconcertingly soft and soggy throughout its entire thickness. I concluded that it had to be a leftover piece of prime-rib from the weekend that they had sprinkled ancho powder over. Unfortunately, the meat was of low quality...it was poorly marbled and loaded with gristle. It was also less than a half inch thick. The mashed potatoes were gloppy with vague chunks of tasteless blue cheese. Nevertheless, the haricots verts were delicious...perfectly crisp and vibrantly green. In all, dinner was quite disappointling...the kicker was that the "special" was $34!! I would only return here for drinks at night and for the view.

text: Being a huge stand-up comedy fan, Zanies is my favorite place in Nashville to spend an evening. I try my best to make it to at least one show a month. It is, in fact, the only true comedy club in town but that's not the only reason I love it. It's an intimate little club with a handful of really standout headliners each month. The service is typically very good. Sometimes it can take a bit longer than you'd like to get a drink but you can always tell the wait staff are busting their butts so that's easily forgivable. They have a lot of tables to cover after all. The food is about what you'd expect from a comedy club, your typical bar selection. Nothing on the menu is exceptional. Everything is merely average or slightly above average. But you don't come here for the cuisine so I don't consider this very much of a negative. If you want fine dining grab dinner elsewhere before the show. If you do plan to eat there I recommend sticking with the chicken strips as they are rather tasty and difficult to screw up. Now, on to more legitimate gripes. Parking can be a pain at times. They have very limited space in their parking lot so you have to arrive rather early in order to find a spot there. If you aren't lucky enough to snag a spot in the lot you are pretty much left to fend for yourself. I have never had a problem finding a place to park. But several times the area I was forced to park in was a bit shadier than I would've preferred (Zanies isn't located in the greatest of neighborhoods). But I haven't had a problem yet, so it is what it is. All in all, parking is only a very minor complaint of mine. As I said, you can make it a non-issue simply by arriving early. The only thing that really bothers me about the place is that sold out shows are very, very crowded. You expect a certain level of overcrowding at a comedy club. And it's hard to blame club owners for wanting to pack in as many people as they can. Still, it seems like Zanies pushes their capacity just a BIT too much. There are certain spots that are extremely uncomfortable to sit in when they are sold out. But again this problem can be remedied, for the most part, by arriving early. Seating is on a first come, first serve basis so the earlier you get there the better the seat you will get. Despite the parking and seating problems, I really can't recommend Zanies enough. It's a great departure from the norm in Nashville and everyone should check it out at least once. If you have even a mild interest in stand-up comedy you will no doubt get hooked. By the way, it really is worthwhile to sign up for their mailing list and/or follow them on Twitter (@zaniesnashville). You will be informed of discounted and BOGO tickets when available.

text: What a difference a year makes. *** (see response after the review) I sent the following letter to the owner of Yalda because our recent experience was so bad. It's been a month, and I have yet to receive a reply, so I'm posting it. ***************** I want to tell you how disappointed we were with our dinner at Yalda last night. Because we have had great experiences here in the past, my daughter specifically requested that we take her here on her birthday. Coming with her, were her mother and father-in-law, and her husband's grandparents; neither of those couples had been to Yalda and were anxious to try your restaurant, based on our recommendation. We ended up being embarrassed hosts. I called for a reservation the day before, and therefore thought you would be prepared for a party of 8. It didn't seem that you were. The bread/chutney came out quickly, but after that, service just disappeared. The appetizers were wonderful, but took forever to come out. The salads, torn lettuce on a plate with dressing, also took forever. What takes so long to plate up lettuce and dressing? And the entrees? We had to ask several times where they were. Then only 6 of the 8 were served. The other two took an additional 20 minutes, and multiple inquiries to our server. The guest of honor had to sit at the table, watching everyone else eat, while she waited for hers. By the time she finally got her entrée, everyone else was finished their meal, and she didn't have much of an appetite to eat while everyone else watched her. She just packed her dinner up to take home. Inexcusable. I had called earlier that day to ask about doing a special dessert for the birthday. I spoke to you again when we arrived at the restaurant. It was surprising, then, when it took so long for our server to even ask if we wanted dessert - we foolishly thought that the delay was his waiting for "something special" to be plated in the kitchen. Not so. We skipped dessert and left, fearing that the additional course would not get us out of your restaurant until after 10 pm. I don't know if you were understaffed, if the fact that we were using a Restaurant.com certificate made a difference, or what the problem was, but it was certainly not the celebration we anticipated. Not once during the entire meal did anyone - either the server or you - apologize or even acknowledge that the service was terrible or that there was a delay. Not once. Even though my husband had to get up out of his seat numerous times to ask where out food was. Was the food good? Yes it was, but the terrible service overshadowed everything else. Well, we probably won't be back. Neither will any of the people who were with us. We had gotten them all excited about a great place, with wonderful food, and all left with a bad taste in their mouths. No, I'm not going to write a bad review on those sites where I originally posted glowing ones, unless of course you choose not to acknowledge my letter. I just won't be able to continue recommending Yalda to others. Or if I do, I will let them know up front that they will have to put up with some real service issues. Probably the most upsetting thing to us was that we, as the hosts, expected to be part of a special experience, and to show those who hadn't been to Yalda what we had been raving about. Instead we looked like fools with very poor taste in restaurants. I came in the door being a very vocal fan of your restaurant. I didn't leave that way. ********************************************* I received a very nice letter of apoplogy from Laila, who is the daughter of the owner. She had seen my updated review on Yelp & apologized profusely for the poor service we received and and said that she never received my original letter of complaint (it was sent to the email address posted on their website). She even offered to reimburse half of our bill. I sent her a reply, thanking her for her response, and declining her offer of the rebate on our bill. My intent was never to solicit a comp, but rather to let people know that a place I had vociferously raved about in the past had fallen way short. I was hoping that the complaint would reach the owners and that it might cause a change in their service so others wouldn't go through the same thing we did. It looks as though the posting had it effect. Am I ready to go back to Yalda? I really really love their food. Yeah, I WILL go back, just not right away. And I probably won't go with a group. I commeneded Laila for replying to my posting on Yelp. It shows she cares about her customers and her restaurant's reputation. Just based on that, Yalda is worth another shot.

The cookie I gave away to a coworker (in hindsight, I should have kept the cookie for myself) but ate the bear claw and the other pastry. text: We got married at the Oasis at Wild Horse Ranch on 9/26/09 and had a wonderful experience! The entire staff, including Raynu, was awesome. Planning the perfect wedding is very difficult. I worried for the entire year of our engagement that our special day would not turn out exactly as I had expected. Thanks to the staff at Wild Horse, our wedding day was perfect. Rehearsal, the day before - We had a wedding party of 16 including myself and my husband. With that many people plus parents that attended it got a bit out of control. Everyone was talking and not paying any attention. I was getting frustrated. Thankfully, Judy was very understanding and made things run smoothly. She ensured that everyone did their party and it went well. Judy also allowed us to run through it twice. She even mentioned that if people forgot what they were supposed to do, she'd be there to help the day of the wedding. There was no need to remember anything since we'd have her to guide us. She is an awesome coordinator. Day of wedding - Raynu allowed the girls to arrive early to the dressing room (being 8 of us my hair sytlist needed all day). Thanks Raynu!! While getting ready, we were served champaigne, water, and juices. Every hour a member of the staff checked in to make sure there was not anything additional we needed. We had purchased many favors, guest book, card box, table and other things to make our wedding day beautiful. All we had to do was bring it the day of the wedding. A staff member came and picked it up from my dressing room. It was displayed exactly as we had wished and looked great! We didn't have to do any setup. It was all done exactly as we had wanted. We were very pleased. When it came time for the ceremony. Judy was there to coordinate and ensure everything went exactly as we planned and wanted. She was on top of everything, down to the minutes, and made sure the ceremony was perfect. We were very impressed with the excellent work she did. It such a relief to have someone leading my entire wedding party and guests. We are thankful we didn't have to do it all on my own. We couldn't imagine it any other way. Dinner Reception - Our head table was served by Shannon. She was awesome too! Everything we asked for was done. She was very quick and efficient at attending to us. As I looked around at all the tables, I could see the favors, rose petals, disposable cameras, and diamonds laid out exactly as we wanted them. The centerpieces the Ranch displayed were beautiful. There were also several other staff members that attended to all the guests tables. We only heard wonderful things from our guests about the service they received. There were so many moments at the Ranch that I thought to myself, "I can't believe they are doing all of this for us. They are treating us like a king and queen." It was the best experience we've ever had. To top it off..,Shannon came up to me at the end of the night and asked for our car keys. She was going to load all of of our gifts into our cars. I was very impressed. When I first walked into the room where the gifts were, I was shocked. My husband and I thought we would have to have someone help us load them up...there were so many of them. Shannon was awesome!! Overall our experience at the Oasis at Wild Horse Ranch was the best we could have imagined. We couldn't have asked for anything better. Our wedding day was beautiful and I am so thankful we picked this venue for our special day. I would definately recommend all couples to check this place out. You won't regret it!!!

text: This place is one of the most over-hyped joints in Boise. It has been voted "Best of Boise" in the local events mag. They claim to have "world famous" milkshakes. You had better have one kick-ass milkshake to make that kind of boast. Let's start off by saying their milkshakes are OK, nothing special. My wife didn't even finish it. Wife and I went here twice and had breakfast. The food is about a C+ and we had to wait a little while to get it. I thought about trying a hamburger the second time, but noticed the obligatory frozen pre-formed patties visible in the freezer. No thanks. Second time I got the pot roast. The meat was good and plentiful, but the potatoes and gravy were lackluster. Not much to say about the breakfasts, C+ like I said before. The decor is charming (unique?) the first time you go in, and maybe for guests you might take here to visit the city. But what you really get is a 50 year old diner, literally, everything is cheap, beat up, dirty and grease-laden, and half-ass constructed. Seems like it's out of pure laziness, than some effort to present 50's style or charm. And the bathroom? There is no 50's charm to that awful festering sore of a room. Absolutely no excuse to have such a filthy rotting corpse of a horror. Almost unusable. There was a dude playing guitar both times, but after a while every song just sounded the same, a drone of strumming chords. If you check out their website it says, "You're invited to our NEW and IMPROVED gift shop." Now that is a hilarious joke. They are in fact closing down the gift shop, a gift shop that consists of piles of WAY WAY overpriced useless bric-a-brac, curios, junk and cheap, unappealing novelties. Conclusion: Go here once just to see what all the fuss is about. But if you want excellent breakfasts in a great atmosphere, clean environment and great prices, visit La Vie En Rose or Goldy's.

text: We stumbled upon Bommar's one weekend after making a visit to PetSmart. There are no signs from the street and it's well hidden behind some car lots and a strip mall. We were surprised to see something back there and decided to check it out. Bommar's is a typical sports bar and grill. They have large flat screen TVs (at least 6), darts (a whole wall of them), skee ball, shuffleboard, silverstrike, etc. They also have Club Keno. No pool table though (minus points). The food is actually pretty good. And word is they haven't finished the kitchen yet, so look forward to an even better menu soon. We've tried the roast beef on garlic cheese bread, southwestern chicken wrap, BLT wrap, and the cheeseburger quesadilla. All their meals come with chips and your choice of slaw (vinegar based) or cottage cheese. Plus, the chips are from The Billy Goat Chip Company. Nom nom nom! We've been to Bommar's about 3-4 times now and every time has been pretty empty. The crowd gets a little rowdy later in the evening, but they all seem fairly laid back. If you live in the neighborhood, check it out the next time you're in the mood for something different.

text: Basically the worst hotel I have ever stayed in, in my entire life. - Filthy dirty - Bed was old, stained and tattered. The bed frame was made out of slats of wood screwed together. The box spring looked like someone had spilled something (please don't make me guess what) and then beaten it with a bat. I didn't know they still made spring mattresses with no padding what so ever. It was horribly uncomfortable. - Road Noise was atrocious! I couldn't sleep at all because I was so worried about people breaking in (there is no top lock). All the rooms face out to the busy street. - The bathtub had about a half inch gap between the tub and the tile. That gap was full of mold. The bath mat they provided had mold rings all over it...eating up through the top of the mat. When we walked in, we knew something was wrong. The light hardly came on, it was low and dingy- we had to turn every light in the place on. There was an odor ionizing machine out in the middle of the room, sitting on a trashcan that had been turned sideways. There was also no shower curtain. The irony of the whole situation was when I called down to ask why there was no shower curtain and a machine in our room, they responded "we were doing a deep cleaning". No you weren't. I saw your housekeeping cart & it didn't have a vacuum. The floors were absolutely disgusting & covered with dirt and hair. There was a portion of the room (between the bed and the wall) where a vacuum cleaner couldn't have fit--it looked as if no one had ever cleaned there. I had the biggest panic attack because of this place and I am not even a germaphobe. I had just spent a week camping at Bonnaroo with 70k other people, using portapoties & public restrooms and there is no way I would ever get 5 feet within this hotel room. Absolutely the most disgusting place I have ever stayed in. When I got home I took the hottest shower I could & scrubbed 3 times. I feel violated. Price: $95 dollars through Expedia. They need to be put out of business. Pros: the man and woman who run the place seem nice...enough... I guess? There are no pros.

text: I have had great success at Corrieri's. Their selection of fine cheeses is extensive, as is their selection of "other" fine imports such as truffle oils, olive oils, pasta etc. However on a visit many of these packaged items were past their expiration date. Then on a different visit, the items had been made current. I'm very surprised to hear about the non-personal service other reviewers have received at this cheese shop. I have had experiences with two different cheese... mongers?? Both were very friendly and helpful and allowed me to taste as many cheese as I wanted. I'm a stinkier-the-better cheese lover, I like it when it's so bad it's good. I've also had a great toasted sandwich here along with a cup of soup (which was good until I spilled it on the floor, then received help cleaning it up from the person working ). The only negative experience I've had here is a wine tasting. On Saturdays, the free Vinea wine shop's tasting takes place at Corrieri's. I had been to one which I enjoyed, so I returned to Corrieri's for another. The person working this particular day was rather unpleasant. Perhaps this is the worker who everybody else is writing about!
label: POS

text: Very cool! Tons of Pinball games to choose from and play as much as you want (small hourly fee)! I love the old school games the most, great fun to be able to play them again. Lots of fun for young and old.

text: When it opened, what set Noble apart were the chef's inventiveness and insistence on fresh, locally-sourced ingredients. While the top-shelf ingredients remain, the inventiveness has given way to massive overcomplication and loss of attention to details. The chilled white asparagus soup I ordered tonight was lovely, but the risotto came out bathing in some appetite-destroying green liquid. (My overly-familiar server tried to pass this off as the way it is supposed to be, which was patent nonsense considering another person at my table had none of the Hulk juice around his risotto.) This place badly needs to get back to basics.

text: I cannot say enough good things about this store. I had the day to myself and had VV on my list of places to go. I've worked in boutiques and while I love them....I could never really shop at them b/c they were not accomodating to a plus size girl. I do most of my shopping online and had been eyeing this cute top on the Kiyonna website.... So here I find myself walking into VV and what do I see? The same top I had been eyeing onine for weeks! Ack! So.excited! It was so nice to be able to try the top on before purchasing it as oppossed to ordering it online & taking your chances. I found a million other things to try on and Erin was so attentive & accomodating. Seriously, I never felt so pampered and cared for...ever. I spent a pretty penny I will admit....but you know what? it was totally worth it. It was seriously THE BEST shopping experience of my life. I bought 2 tops and 2 dresses...and also got a bit of a discount....again...the best shopping experience of my life. Erin, my midwestern friend...I'm coming back in April and am already tucking away some extra dough b/c I know my trip to NOLA will not be complete without coming here. Fair warning...get ready! Side note: I was searching for stores that catered to women of all sizes so when I discovered this place online...I was hesitant. The name made me giggle and I thought...this place is either going to be super trashy....or super cute. I was so excited to find that it was a super cute place that carried familar brands that you can't always find in a store to touch and try on....Kiyonna, Karen Kane, B&Lu, Anna Scholtz...so on and so on. Ladies, if you are looking for a way to treat yourself - V.V is it!

text: A Full Plate Catered my sons wedding with 66 meals on 10-30-10. Our guests raved about the food. No one but the Bride & Groom were vegetarian, and everybody loved it! The food was great quality, set up was fast and on time. I would use them again without hesitation!

text: Like that it's a local, family joint, don't mind the soup-nazi ordering style, hate the hours. But, honestly, this review is about the food. And I have to sum it up with a simple, "Meh". I didn't try the cheesesteak and instead went for their roast pork and roast beef. The pork was dry and way over-seasoned. The salt and spices were beating me over the head, not complimenting the pork. The roast beef, on the other hand, was completely tasteless. I went with mild prov, so as to enjoy the taste of the beef, but was instead left with no flavor. If I'd got sharp prov, that's probably all I would have tasted. I've definitely tried more places than I've reviewed here, but for favorites, I have to go with Nick's for beef and DeNic's for pork. John's just didn't impress me in any way, and the hours make it hard to accommodate a revisit.

So if you just can't bear the drive thru one more night, and even Steak & Shake is getting old, steer on over to The Steer-In, have a seat and enjoy the food, and the people watching, there's plenty of both to go around.

text: Budget my ass. I needed a car rental this week at the last minute. My usual car rental places were sold out. I had no idea who else to turn to, but Budget ended up being the cheapest. And by "cheapest" I mean for a measly 28 hours I paid over $200 for a compact car. W to the T to the F. Price aside, I wasn't impressed. I'm so used to Alamo's painless renting (you can prepay online, then go straight to the car class, pick your own car, and drive off), that I guess I'm spoiled. The shuttle picked myself and a couple other passengers up at the airport quickly. Except the driver drove like a maniac. Another renter and I sat in the back of the shuttle, in the 5 seats that go across the back. Our driver flew over a pothole so fast we both flew up in the air and slammed back down. Normally this would just suck, but considering I had taken a bad spill that landed me in the ER 48 hours prior to this, my entire body was already sore. The pothole slam dance did not help matters at all. I was not pleased. We arrived to the car lot, and though I had already prepaid, I still had to go inside. AND WAIT IN LINE. They had 3 employees working the counter for both Budget and Avis. One woman was working two computers at once in what seemed like an effort to make things go more quickly, but I actually think she just slowed things down. As I waited I looked around for computer screens like they have at other rental places (*cough* Alamo *cough*) that allow you to check yourself in. Budget/Avis has no such thing. Lame. I finally made it up the counter thirty minutes later. That's right - half an hour. I was already in a foul mood because of the reason I was in St. Louis, their crazy shuttle driver, and if you know me at all, you know my feelings on standing in line. The woman was nice and I smiled politely and handed her my credit card and license. Then the sales pitch began. Oh, THIS is why you force your customers to stand in line - to hear a sales pitch! I politely declined all of the things she tried to tack on to my already ridiculously priced car rental. Then she asked me a second time. No. No no no no no. I said no the first time. Asking again isn't going to change my answer. While I wasn't a bitch to her (god, I should win an award for that restraint), she should have read the look on my face that I wasn't in the mood. It's called "reading your customer" and can be found on page one in your Sales 101 manual, folks. While she processed my paperwork, a man came in saying he needed to switch cars because he was too tall for the one they assigned him. You would have thought you asked them to find a cure for cancer. Surely this situation has happened before, but that situation required 3 employees and an act of congress. Seriously, oh my god. Bad customer service. Luckily I am vertically challenged and I fit into my assigned car just fine. I finally drove off and had no problems with the car while I had it. When I returned the car the next day it was late afternoon, which seemed to be a busy time for returns. And yet, they only had ONE employee checking people back in. I saw other employees milling about, and even asked one if I was in the right place to check in. He assured me I was and motioned to the guy 5 or 6 cars ahead of me. Sigh. I finally checked it back in, he printed my receipt, and I reluctantly got on the shuttle again. Luckily this driver drove a little less psycho. Overall, I don't think I'll be using Budget again, especially at this location. I'm so used to the way Alamo makes everything a breeze to get you in and out, and Budget is the complete opposite of that. While I do think the fact that they are severely understaffed was part of the issue, the fact that they make no effort to make things speedy for the customer isn't helping - oh sure, they have the 'preferred' club or whatever they call it, but I watched those people in line and their service wasn't any quicker than mine. There is zero efficiency in the way they run their business, and I don't like doing business with places that aren't efficient. Never again, Budget.
label: NEG

text: Hubby and I had breakfast here before our flight. Most food in airports is by the big chains and is mediocre at best. But this was no chain and I was surprised at how decent the food was. I had a scramble which (if I remember correctly) had sausage, bell peppers, tomatoes and maybe onion and cheese. It came with hash browns. The eggs were perfectly cooked (not too dry and not too wet) and the ingredients in the scramble seemed good quality. The hash browns were also perfectly cooked with that yummy brown, crispy outside and soft potato inside. Hubby had the breakfast burrito which looked pretty darn good. The service was good and the food came out fairly quickly so there was no anxiety about having to gobble the food to make the flight. The server was nice, too. Although this restaurant is upstairs and outside security, I'm not sure I'd make this a destination place to eat (other than for taking a flight out). Although if you like to watch small aircraft taking off and landing it might be fun. I noticed that they also had a bar and a small patio, so there you go! The next time we visit SB, I will definitely plan to eat here before our flight out.
label: POS

text: I came here while killing time at BayWalk before my step-sisters graduation. That place has really become a ghost own, especially during the day...but this little sushi restaurant is like the gem hidden in a barren town. We started off with miso soup, which was decent but nothing special. The sushi was fresh and flavorful. The waitress was very attentive and helped us customize our orders to our liking, my nephew hit his head because we sat on the high chairs and she was was quick to run to us and pat him on the head and try to make him feel better. Their California Roll was pretty tasty, but more expensive than the average. I had them make me a crab special which was alright, but not my favorite. The eel was tasty, and I had them put the sauces on the side which was a good choice since I'm not a huge fan of sauces on my rolls. The Salmon was pretty good, but a little too salty for my liking. They have all you can eat sushi for $25, but since I was with my nephew we just ordered by roll, not a bad deal though. The sushi also came out quick.

text: Perfect date spot for those who like stiff/classic cocktails, good meat and an authentic/retro ambiance. I enjoyed the fillet and my date's prime rib was on par (pun intended) with other steakhouses I've visited. Meals come with the traditional-- soup, salad, side (potatoes, pilaf, etc) choices. The wait staff is straight out of the 70s and awesome. Dimly lit, big leather booths-- perfect way to go if you're looking for something fun, good food and eclectic atmosphere.

text: After not getting into Brennan's we waited about a half hour for this very average place. Unfortunately after we sat down we realized it was the same owners as the Bayou where we had dinner the night before and hated. We ordered two mimosas at the bar and they were like large dixie cups for $8 each. We sat down at the table and I ordered the "hearty" three New Orleans specialties. This included: Gumbo, red beans and rice and Jambalaya. She brought out the plate and it was three small bowls filled with each. I was a bit shocked but dug in. The red beans and rice was fine but really how could you mess that up. I then tried the gumbo because I didn't want it to get cold. I took a mouthful and the "shrimp" (at least that's what i think it was) was frozen. I refused to eat the rest. The Jambalaya was ok but nothing special- I was starving so I ate it. Word to the wise- make and keep all reservations in New Orleans- especially during special events.

text: Had lunch here with my family this past Saturday. We sat outside and were immediately greeted by our perky waitress, whose name I wish I remembered - she did have neon fingernails, though! She was great - totally on it with our orders and super friendly. The food was much, much better than expected; I generally don't expect too much from sports bars, but Ricky T's, apparently, is a restaurant first and a place with TVs second. My brother had the prime rib sandwich and we were all amazed at the size of the cut. My dad had the Florida Chef's Salad and my mom and I had the portabello sandwiches. My mom and I were both vegetarians for 20 years, so we have pretty high standards for our mushrooms. The sandwich was unbelievably good - a real, meaty, non-watery mushroom. And the fries! text: I was really excited to stay at the Windsor Court for a recent weekend trip to NOLA with my wife. Unfortunately, we were both extremely disappointed. First, no rooms were available upon check-in, even though we had arrived at the check-in time of 3PM. No big deal for us as we would just walk around the French Quarter until a room was ready. The front desk took our cell phone number and promised to call when a room was ready. Three hours later, no call. When we got back, they had assigned us a room, but left our bags sitting out next to the front desk, despite having promised to deliver them when the room was available. When we got to the room, we were again disappointed. The room was a nice size, but the furnishings and decor were tired and dated. The bed was as hard as a rock and was uneven. We inquired about another room with the front desk, but were told they were sold out that night. After adjusting our expectations downward, we settled in to get ready for dinner out. When my wife went to take a shower, she discovered the removable shower head only pointed straight down. We called engineering and they improvised a fix, but it was such a hassle. The water pressure was terrible. Water from the bathroom faucet shot out sideways and squeeled when the cold water was turned on. The lights in the hall near the closet didn't work so you couldn't see into the closet. There was no garbage can in the main room (only in the bathroom). Housekeeping didn't replace hand towels or washcloths after our first night. When we called to request more towels, they only brought bath size towels and no hand towels or wash cloths. At least one of the additional towels they did bring was dirty. When we informed the front desk manager of our disappointment and a list of the problems we encountered, he responded with a terse "uh, sorry." Are any of these things huge issues? Not really - we're usually pretty easy going travellers. But all of these annoyances built up into a bad experience. Sure, the common areas are lovely and elegant, but unfortunately we weren't staying in the lobby. The Ritz-Carlton is about the same price at the time we booked, and given a second chance, we would've stayed at the Ritz, no doubt about it.
label: NEG

text: I've been to this location twice within the past 2 months, and I wasn't too thrilled either time. My most recent trip was Sunday night. I was not impressed at all. The cheesesteak was mediocre, and I couldn't even taste the CHEESE in it. I love when the cheese gets 'chopped in' to the cheesesteak, so that every bite is full of cheesy goodness. I guess this is a place you could hit up if you were really in dire need of a cheesesteak in the suburbs. The onion rings are very tasty , as is their dipping sauce. I want to try out their hoagies too, they look yummy. However, I will not be eating their cheesesteaks again.

text: Sadly, Hobbs the Liger has passed away. Which leaves the bird display (sponsored by a local bird-fancier group) as the best attraction: the birds looked happy and entertained, sitting on their perches under the trees. As for the rest of the zoo....well, it's a roadside zoo. Small enclosures, some of them empty (maybe those animals died), some designed so it's hard to see the animals, missing, incorrect, and illegible informational signs, etc. I wish they had more information on the animals: where did they come from? How did the zoo acquire them? That said, the kids appeared to be enjoying the petting zoo, and I was pleased to see so many happy-looking teen-aged volunteers.
label: NEG

text: Extra star for the staff and volunteers who were SO friendly, helpful, and knowledgeable. They really seemed like they enjoyed what they were doing and enjoyed talking to the visitors. Oh, and these volunteers were about 13 years old. How cute to have these kids pulling up plankton and placing it in microscopes for us, ringing us up in the gift shop, and pulling sharks out of tanks so we can pet them. You didn't have to ask them much, they would offer information just as you needed it. They really knew their stuff. There isn't a whole lot here, so don't expect Sea World or the Long Beach Aquarium, but there is enough to entertain you for an hour and a half or so. And if you are going to be strolling along Stearn's wharf, why not stop in and pet a shark, hold a star fish, or let some hermit crabs crawl in the palm of your hand. It's about 8 bucks for adults and it all goes to a worthy cause. Highlights: Petting the little sharks, holding the crabs and starfish, the actual shark eggs with living embryos inside (they are weird!! They look like transparent envelopes, not actual eggs), the octopus that was trying to open a jar with his snack inside, and pregnant the dolphin corpse. Eeesh, what a stench. It has a lot of interactive stuff to do, mainly geared for kids. But we adults enjoyed ourselves and even bought trinkets for the well stocked gift shop. I find it hard to beleive this is not reviewed yet. If its posted someone where else, let me know.
label: POS

text: I have to admit that it makes me sad to pen this review. I am (was) a fan of Savona, particularly Bar Savona. Thus, when I had colleagues in from abroad this week it was my first choice. The good news- spectacular wine list and lovely service. The not-so-good...the place was really noisy- to the extent that we couldn't chat in a normal voice. The fish was unseasoned and the artichoke puree was heavy, grasssy and did not match the fish's texture. The grilled artichokes certainly were well-cooked (charred). I ate about half and gave up. My wife's lamb was fatty and inedible. But- the wine was outstanding. I don't know, for this kind of tab I expect more. I am not sure whether to try again...the restaurant business on the Main Line has so much else to offer. Maybe it was because it was Monday?

text: This restaurant wasn't very good, although I did get delivery, I'm not sure how it would be in the actual restaurant. The Naan was soggy, the basmati rice didn't look or taste right, and the dish I got was mushy and not as flavorful as I was used to.
