text: Before getting rid of my car and joining carshare, I had the displeasure of taking my car to this Pep Boys for an oil change. I had made an appointment, and was confirmed for a Saturday morning at 10am... I arrived around 9:45am, and was informed that it would be about a 30 minute wait. Which was fine. The first attendant took my keys and filled out a little tag, noting the oil change and the time that I handed them over. I went into the waiting room, which was adjacent to the garage. There were 5 slips for car repair work, and 8 grease-monkeys shuffling around. I felt content. But then, the garage receptionist (for lack of a better term) left and some nasty minimum wage, middle aged, Napoleon complex, catty woman took over. Somehow my reservation was lost, and I was put into the "walk-in" pile. At 10:30am I inquired about my ETA, and was told that since I didn't have a reservation I'd have to wait. And since I hadn't checked in with Ghengis the Skank, I was now at the bottom of the pile. I had written down my confirmation number from the day before and also had the name of the person who confirmed it - so I gave Ms. Demeanor the information. All of which ended in a verbal parry and counter-parry, culminating in me demanding to speak with the manager. Oh but it wasn't that easy, because there was no manager there on a Saturday morning. I was told I could wait until 1pm when the assistant manager would be coming to work. I said fine, and walked around the corner to the Chinese restaurant - diluting my anger and annoyance in General Tsao's chicken... It did little to quell my agitation. I returned at Noon to find yet another garage maitre de; this one more insufferable than the last. I again explained the situation and politely asked if my reservation could be restored. I was greeted with a nasty retort about being on time and since I wasn't there at 10am my reservation was cancelled. I calmly tried to explain that I had been here since 9:45am, I asked her to check the time indicated on my key tag, and gave the names of the first person to check me in and the last person who was just at the desk. To which I received a "I wasn't here so I don't know what happened, if you want you can have a seat and we'll call you when there's an open space." I was furious by this time, but had about 40 minutes to contemplate and strategically plan out my argument for the assistant manager. 1pm came and went... 1:30pm came and went... 2pm came and I inquired about the assistant manager. The latest maitre de replied "he won't be in until 3pm". I lost it! I demanded that she get some kind of supervisor over to the podium, and also demanded that my keys get returned. I was told it was the supervisors lunch break and if I got my keys I'd lose my place in line. I was also told that I was 2nd in line now and it should be done within 20 minutes. I took a deep breath and walked back to the waiting room. I looked out at the garage and noticed that there were no mechanics working... What happened to the 8 that I had seen all morning?! I had a view of the parking lot and didn't see any of them wandering around out there. I returned to the podium and asked where they were. "At lunch, they'll be back in about an hour". I asked how would my car be done in 20 minutes if the mechanics were not there and would not be back for an hour?! "Oh, I meant 20 minutes after their lunch is over". As a good anthropologist, I know that if things can be solved at the local level you need to lobby to the next highest level to effect change. I decided it was time to call corporate... I explained the whole situation, including the fact that a manager had not been present since the store opened. The woman on the phone said my reservation was valid and she would look into getting me a free oil change. I agreed to wait for to call back before making any decisions. I went back to the waiting room... Fast forward 60 minutes, and the mechanics still had not returned; 75 minutes no return and no phone call; 80 minutes and no return, no phone call, and no manager; 90 minutes... I had all I could take and demanded my keys back. The woman had the nerve to give me a comment card and ask if I'd like to take a survey on my experience at Pep Boys! ARE YOU FREAKIN KIDDING ME?! I got my keys and the survey (a nasty-gram would soon be sent)! I got in my car and called Jiffy Lube who told me to come on in... My oil change was done in 30 minutes. At 6pm that night the customer service woman from Pep Boys corporate called me back. She had informed the manager of everything that had happened and my free oil change was waiting for me. I told her that I had gotten great service at Jiffy Lube and that she could shove her free oil change up Ghengis the Skanks ass! Don't ever go to PEP BOYS! THEY ROYALLY SUCK!

text: Twelve thirty rolls around in the office of Son of Veggie Girl and I suddenly realize that I am very hungry. Something that I realized much longer ago, however, is that I am also very lazy. Being that I am hungry, lazy and a long-time vegetarian (Mom is so proud!), my options for an afternoon meal are somewhat limited. Lucky for me, Zivaz Mexican Bistro is spitting distance from my desk. One of my favorite things about Zivaz is the wide-array of options they offer for the carnivorously disinclined and my choice today was the milanesa de berenjena; a lightly breaded eggplant cutlet is topped with a layer of queso freso and a mild tomatillo salsa. That layer is then topped with more delicious white cheese and fresh chopped squash. As I wait for my meal to arrive, the polite and unobtrusive server brings a bowl of tortilla chips and two kinds of salsa. Both are tasty but not nearly spicy enough for my palette. The milanesa arrives and I dig in: the first thing I notice is that the lime in the tomatillo salsa is slightly overpowering, something that I personally enjoyed but might be a turn-off for others. The eggplant is, to my surprise, well-prepared and not too mushy or firm. The squash is also well prepared and tastes like it was picked fresh from a garden right before my meal. All in all, a delectable dish rounded out by a black bean paste and hand-made tortillas. The inexpensive and well-prepared vegetarian plates combined with their rare ability to make a proper mojito make Zivaz an easy choice to make. Though watch out for the rice, fellow lettuce heads, as they prepare it in chicken broth. Just let the server know that you 'd prefer no rice and they'll substitute a double portion of spring green salad topped with an enchanting vinaigrette.

text: Marly B's extremely negative review of PCS got my attention today so I wanted to write my own review, since I have had the exact opposite experience with this company. I absolutely love this company. I moved to Philly 2 years ago, and before I came here, I sold my car. One of the reasons I knew I'd be able to live car-free was that I knew PCS existed, and that I would have relatively convenient access to a car whenever I needed it. Well, that's exactly what I've gotten. We're still just in the infant stages of what I think will become a very large car sharing industry. And even at this early stage, car sharing programs demonstrate their unbelievable value. My annual transportation costs are FAR lower than they would be if I was a car owner. The true value of PCS is in the minimal annual expense. Sure, they've got an annual fee now. That has apparently annoyed a lot of people. What is it? $120? That's a couple gas refills if you're a car owner. Give them a break. Jeez. I was actually very happy when they instituted the annual membership fee. I WANT this company to succeed, and I recognize that they need a somewhat stable revenue stream, and I also recognize that having a membership fee will tend to eliminate from the program members of inferior quality - deadbeats. The kind of people who are more likely to damage the car, steal shit, etc. It adds just a small bit of exclusivity to the program, which I like. So people don't like the annual membership fee? Okay, well do they like not having to pay over 1000 bucks for car insurance every year? I mean, come on. I'll take that trade any day. Speaking of the annual fee, it used to be a monthly charge to your credit card. I like that they now automatically charge my credit card just once a year. Because I don't like seeing a charge on my credit card every month. It just irritates me. I prefer one annual charge. A few more points about PCS: *Some have complained that the cars are unclean on the inside. Generally speaking, I've always found them to be fairly clean on the inside. Do members really want PCS to vacuum the cars after EVERY use? If so, expect higher hourly charges. Personally, I'd rather have lower hourly charges and the occasional crumb on my seat. *Many of the complaints I've seen are along the lines of "I did something stupid and irresponsible and PCS penalized me for it." Well, ya know, ya might want to stop doing stupid and irresponsible things. If you're relatively intelligent and responsible, you won't have too much trouble. I've never gotten any kind of penalty in the two years I've been a member. *In two years, I've only had trouble with one reservation - I couldn't get into my car. On this particular day, I also had a broken cellphone, which complicated things. Had my cellphone worked, I could have called them and I'm fairly confident they could have helped. Regardless, they refunded my money for this reservation. The folks on the phone are always really nice.
label: POS

text: I want to give this place a better rating but I just can't. Here's a pro/con comparison. The pro: DVD's at dirt cheap. Seriously, anywhere from 50 cents to around $5.00, lots of TV boxed sets for $10-15. The con: If you want to trade in your own DVD's for cash or store credit, you will get jack squat. The pro: A young, alternative staff (goths, punks and nerds galore!) who usually have a good, if sarcastic, attitude. I've found them fun to be around, and I even stopped in and dropped off Xmas presents for them this year. The con: A lot of fooling around and a casual attitude can lead to some customer service neglect and very long wait times if you are trading something in and waiting for it to be evaluated. The pro: They buy a huge variety of items, from phones and mp3 players to TV's, video games and systems, DVDs and so on and so on...if it is in working order and of a reasonable value to people, they will buy it. The con: Everyone and their mother brings in stuff to sell, and it seems like business isn't really booming. This means that if you go in to sell your item, they may tell you point blank that they can't do it that day because they don't have the cash available. *AND*, you can't call them up before going in to find out if they CAN buy your item that day, because they have absolutely no phone number listed. (The staff claims they literally don't have a store phone.) The pro: You can pre-shop on their website (www.webuy.com) to get an idea of whether they will buy in your item and how much they will give you for it; and also what items they have in the store. The con: The quotes on the website wildly vary from the quotes in the store. Items are generally ranked in condition from A-E, but the quote on the website is generally for an "A" item, meaning pristine condition. Thus your ipod that has some very mild wear and tear might fetch you $30 less because an employee deemed it a 'C". Of course, this is kind of moot as I'm writing this because the American version of their website has been down for over a week. The pro: If your item is not already in their system, they can contact an appraiser via email with the specs and get a quote for you in or around an hour. The con: The appraiser lowballs - every time. Also, often times if your specific item brand/model isn't listed in their system, they will offer you the system trade-in value of a 'generic' similar item, which is usually extremely low. No one wants to get a Dynex price quote for an LG flat screen TV... The pro: They offer a warranty for a year on electronics. The con: There is virtually no return/exchange policy. You can bring something back within 48 hours to exchange it for an identical item - no refunds. Otherwise you have to fork over your item and have them ship it to God Knows Where for repair. Good luck with that... One thing I've noticed that is a definite con is that items that are 'boxed' are more expensive than items that are not, often dramatically so. To give you an example, an old GameCube system unboxed costs $20, but boxed is $40. You would THINK that this would mean the boxed version comes in the original packaging with manuals and such. But it doesn't. In my case, they put a GameCube console in a box for a totally different version of the console, with no manuals - so that lovely piece of cardboard cost me an additional $20. And also, as I'm writing this, it just dawned on me that they sold me an Xbox at the boxed price and didn't even give me a box... Which literally made me drop my rating to 2 stars. Well crap. Now I'm pissed off. Follow-up review to come in the next 24 hours...

text: We recently went to Emerald City after not having been there in YEARS. It seems like a lot has changed. If I remember correctly they used to be geared much more toward the pastry type stuff they sold, and sandwiches, in addition to their coffees, teas, and other drinks. I ended up going for breakfast and boyfriend went for a lunch sandwich. I got the french toast and boyfriend got a sandwich (caughlin club I believe) with tomato soup. I can defiantly say that since Lisa R's review I think they decided to do away with the microwave concept because my french toast was defiantly freshly made. It took far too long to be something that was just nuked. I also made an extra effort to listen to kitchen sounds because I had read Lisa's review a while back and remembered when I walked in that she had mentioned that they have a cook come in to prepare things ahead of time. I heard lots of food making noises lol - on the stove etc. So maybe they decided to hire a full time cook now! My french toast came with a wonderful fruit salad. I had anticipated a blah fruit salad consisting of cut fruit in a little cup - but this was cut fruit with sliced almonds and yogurt on top, very tasty. And it had pineapple and strawberries in it to, not just the crappy grape and melon fruit salads you get at other places. My french toast was thick, and yummy. A very nice breakfast for me! Much more filling than I had planned on - I thought it was still the same little coffee place where all I ever got was a bagel... Now I'm getting full-on meals! My boyfriend got his sandwich with cheese jalapeno bread and it was big and he said delicious. The best part was his tomato soup - another surprise! We thought it would just be like canned tomato soup, but it actually had big tomato chunks in it and everything. My boyfriend hates everything, and he said "next time we want a big plate of delicious food, we have to remember to go here." Yay! Boyfriend likes something I like! Oh, and I almost forgot... they DO carry grape juice here (which is something boyfriend must always have). The inside is pretty much the same, with the quotes and all on the walls and the seating near the fireplace - and outdoor seating. I was sad they didn't offer the pot of tea anymore :( The girl at the register informed me that they switched to new teas since I had last been in too - so I'm assuming that's why they don't do the pot of tea to share anymore. That was always fun though, to get a big pot for you and whoever at your table and just share it. Their Jasmine tea was my favorite, but they still do have a Jasmine Flower tea available.

The dishes at least are LARGE, probably better to share if you're a girl like me; manly men could probably finish off the entrees easily enough, although the entrees seem to be primarily the rice and beans that accompany every dish. I got the Ensalada Mixta with sauteed shrimp - not very many shrimp, but boy was that salad huge. And not that great. Neither, from the looks of it, were the other dishes we ordered. It was just okay, and for prices like that I'd like a little better than 'okay.' But its clear from the other patrons there that the draw of this place are the drinks. Mixto seems like a good place for a group of friends to sit, drink, joke and share the massive dishes - being too buzzed to care at the quality of the food consumed. So, if that sort of place is your thing, you'll probably love Mixto. For me and my bf's family, when we decide to eat out we want food that we wouldn't normally prepare, and we want it to taste like effort went into it.

text: We went to Murrieta's 10/16/2010. I have been wanting to go there ever sine I saw them with Sam Shad cooking those seafood enchilada's. So I finally persuaded my husband to go Chips and salsa at the beginning on the meal: the standard Pico de Gallo and then a smokey creation. The Pico de Gallo was my favorite however the smokey creation tasted more like something that would accent a taco rather then a chip. We ordered the pork half ribs and the seafood enchiladas with the cheese and salsa sauce as a n appetizer. Cheese and salsa dipping sauce: Not what I was expecting. The cheese tastes of a cheaper quality then Velveeta? Slightly sour, slightly plastic... if they change their cheese product-- great! Chips: A good standard chip however they need to make sure they don't mix the stale with the new-- we can taste the difference... The pork halk rack: A thick well sauced slab of pork ribs served on crispy onions with a corn on the cob as well as black beans. The Pork Half rack: It is not slow cooked, it tasted as though it was steamed or baked with fluid to cook it quickly, then slathered with a chipotle BBQ sauce. I would recommend them to at least bake their ribs and then paint on the sauce in the last 10 minutes so it cooks and caramelizes-- this tasted as if it was spooned on after coming out of a hot water pan.... The corn? ugh-- old, very old. There were brown mushy kernels mixed in with the yellow-- and the corn cob was drying out-- when preparing to offer fresh corn, please ensure and keep your corn in a warm bath so it wont dry out... and check its age before you serve! The crispy onion strings: they came served under the huge slab of pork and when found, no longer were crispy but a mushy greasy memory of what could have been.. please serve those on the side so they can be experienced in their full glory... and a little salt would help too.... The black beans: black beans should be cooked with a few cloves of garlic and a lot of white onion and salted to perfection to truly bring out their flavor... these were just beans and water.... The seafood enchilada: After seeing the chef make them for Sam Shad , I thought they were going to be a spectacular cousin of what the chef used to make in Andeoti's of Harrah's. Wow, no way. barely any crab or lobster, the seafood is not fresh-- freshness is king for a good flavor to last the entire meal-- fresh garlic sautéed with the seafood in olive oil then mixed with the other ingredients would slap some life into this creation. The way he prepared it on TV was divine- his chefs need to be retrained and not skimp on the ingredients. Beans and rice were of course totally bland-- making a authentic Mex rice from a good chicken stock and the normal medley of ingredients will do wonders for your plates... and dont serve refried can beans--- make a good pot of pinto beans and they last for 5 days...... But then again folks I have worked and tasted the best food out there and also been served the absolute most authentic home cooked Mexican food and Mom will always do better then food commercialized.... I will not be coming back, because I have had and worked with better food then this....

text: We stayed at this hotel a few times in winter. It's location is very convenient for hiking and going out. It is a somewhat run down resort from the 70s. Make sure you get a room NOT facing the freeway (I-10), which wraps around the property on the outside. This side is quite noisy. The amazing thing is that the freeway noise is not penetrating the courtyard very much, i.e. the rooms on that side are not much affected by traffic noise (the train can be heard quite intensely, though, when it passes through town. Over the years the place saw some improvement. When we stayed there the first time, it was quite a mess. Then year after year things improved...some paint here, new furniture there, new tiles in the bathroom etc... Sadly, not everything improved: One of the latest 'achievements' was to blanket the courtyard with quite loud music all day from 7 am to 10 pm (management seems to prefer a ghastly advertisement riddled oldies station playing top 40s from the late 60's to the early 90's-how utterly boring and annoying!). This can make quite unhappy, especially if you prefer to sleep with the window open. They appear to be quite convinced that this nuisance is necessary to improve their appeal. Repeat calls to the front desk to turn down the music a notch in the morning (it is clearly noticeable with closed windows-quite sad when trying to sleep in a bit!) did not yield any action. So, make sure to bring a set of heavy duty ear plugs (I recommend 3M) if you must stay at this place. I am actually thinking this may be the last time we stay here due to this unfortunate development. I also have to agree with William P.'s review that the service can be sloppy at times, and that they skimp on the shampoo (they will give you more at the front desk if the maid forgets to replenish it...). In summary, this place could be o.k., but the recent musical onslaught makes it difficult to like it. Think of second hand smoke-you cannot stop breathing-same thing with noise: No off switch for your ears!-So, show some mercy with your customers, InnSuites management!

text: One of the mysterious things about eating out for me is how out of an entire table of people, each individual has a completely different experience. Cue in the invention of Yelp to express those diverse experiences. Like the reviews before me, I went to Mosaic with a group of 6 for Downtown Restaurant Week. We had reservations and were very quickly seated. If my experienced ended here I would have given them 5 starts. Sadly, this is where I buckled my seat belt as everything went steeply downhill. We waited 30 minutes to order drinks and another 15 to order food. Our server had 2 other tables. Sangria was good, not amazing but not terrible. Average. Amuse Bouche was good, mix it all together to get a nice crab salad. Too bad someone at our table was allergic to shellfish. Did the server ask this or mention that there was shellfish on the menu? Nope. From what I've read here the butternut squash soup is hands down love it or hate it. If it were snowing out and I was at home wrapped in Snuggie I would have loved this soup. Yes, there is easily a pound of sugar in each bowl, but I liked it. Was it the proper menu choice for August? No. Even worse, I'm reading that there was a loaded baked potato option last night, our server extraordinaire did not mention this. Not a whisper or a hint. Make sure your seat belt is securely fastened because things are about to get really bumpy. Salad comes. I had the baby arugula, which had such great potential. Server man tells us the egg is soft boiled so that the yolk will mix with the speck and create this creamy dressing. Well, my cold egg did nothing of the sort. It just made for a messy and someone unsavory yolk drenched dish. The speck though was fantastic and I think as a concept it was good. Just missing points on execution, like using a warm egg where the yolk would drizzle out and create this dressing. And then the steak... I know better than to order a steak outside of s teak house so I lowered my expectations, but I didn't throw them out the window. It was rare, or pan seared, when I asked for medium rare. Half of it was fat. HALF! It was ice cold. I had about 3 bites. Waiter asked how everything was, I said I didn't like it. He gazed at me blankly before asking if he could bring anything else and walked away. Even if I were to say I wanted something else he would have been long gone. I wouldn't serve a steak cut like this at my own house, let alone at a restaurant. But, I did try a bite of the chicken and it was wonderful. Food envy to the max. Desert saved them a little. I liked the Manchengo cheesecake, although I would have whipped it a bit more. The brownie thing was good. Recap: Service 1 star. Food 2 stars. I thought the purpose of a Restaurant Week was to showcase our dishes so people will return. No thank you.
label: NEG

text: This review has been "filtered." Yelp isn't posting it in the open because it is an unfavorable review. Don't stay at the Best Western South Coast Inn! And during our prior stay at this hotel the front desk person said our file said "really nice people" and how we must have made a great impression. Now, because we were frustrated that we were in a room without a working toilet, we were told we were required to leave. It didn't make sense. We still had two nights on our reservation. This new clerk told us that last night's front desk person relayed to the owner that I had demanded to be compensated for two nights when all I did was ask as a suggestion in frustration. The desk clerk was apologetic and made excuses for the owner telling us he was under stress because of the renovations and also how the main computer system had gone down that night. We asked to talk to both the hotel manager and the hotel owner but we were told neither could be reached and the situation wouldn't change even if they could be reached. There was apparently no way to get this miscommunication undone. He was sympathetic and he did comp us $30 which we appreciated, but there was no way we could connect to the two decision makers, the hotel manager and the hotel owner to get the situation fixed. This is not the way you treat a customer. No one talked to us except the front desk person who was accusing us of demanding something we only asked for in frustration and as a suggestion. Plus, shouldn't a hotel do something more when your toilet doesn't work? The broken toilet wasn't the only problem. The cold water at the faucet only turned off at a precise point that took a while to find. The shower had very low water pressure. And, the next morning, the toilet wouldn't flush again. Plus, we heard another customer complain about how a hotel staff person walked in on them in their room really early in the morning. In the end, the owner did us a favor. We found Pacifica Suites. It is closer to our Goleta destination. The toilets work and work and work!! The rooms are much cleaner. The breakfast is better. The people are nicer. text: I visited Silver Sage last week seeking some pain control for chronic pain in my back that i have been experiencing for nearly a decade. The office staff was very courteous and friendly, however I have a problem with Dr. Pasternak. I have given myself about 5 days to cool off before writing this, so understand that this is not an angry, reactionary response. Dr. Pasternak's attitude seemed dismissive and his examination cursory, at best. As soon as I brought up the issue of pain control, he immediatly shut down and started focusing on my weight. I know i am overweight. This fact does not make any pain I feel any less real or debilitating. The message i got from his attitude and behavior was, 'You can deal with the pain, fatass.' Dr. Pasternak has been my primary care physician for a long time. And under his care i am prescribed Naproxin (NSAID), and cyclobenzaprine (muscle relaxant). The former i take on a daily basis, the latter i only take as needed for the extremely painful spasms that occur sometimes. I fail to understand why the Dr. was reluctant to prescribe me some stronger pain controll, and honestly I felt a little discriminated agaist for my weight. Sure I am over-weight, and my BP is a little high, but i take a precription strength NSAID and Prozac, both known to increase blood pressure. My total cholesterol is less than 90. I have spent my life doing heavy-duty work which (suprise!) has left me with a chonic bad back. Needless to say, i will not be returning to Silver Sage Sports Perfomance for any reason.

I would have never thought to add lemon to that overly salty mix of cured italian meats (bresaola, hot coppa, melted taleggio) but the contrast blended amazingly well to please the palette. The Pappardelle with Lamb Ragu was unbelievable. I never cared much for lamb, but the braised shredded lamb that arrived with the perfectly cooked handmade pasta was unreal. It melted in my mouth and was euphoric. The cous de gras was the Cannelle's which are the most underestimated desserts for their lack of flair. It was like eating air, which this subtle deluge of banana flavor. It was worth every penny, and would return any day.

Another thing I loved about this place is that it is 100 percent smoke free! Even in the courtyard! I am not a smoker SO this was definitely a perk for me... Our balcony overlooked the pool and neighboring suites, but still maintained a private feel. The complimentary breakfast in the morning was perfect. Typical continental breakfast offering freshly squeeze orange juice, grapefruit halves, cereal, cold milk, specialty coffee drinks, bagels and quiche. In the evenings, the hotel offers fine wine in a romantic setting. This is a place you want to go to to get away from reality and get lost in the bed sheets with that special someone. text: I grew up in Boston and lived in NYC for some time and I have definitely tried more than 100 different pizza joints over the years - I consider myself to be a pizza lover. So I just moved to Reno and set myself the mission of finding the best pizza in the city - because I have to have my pizza fix at least once a week. I actually drove past Nu Yalk a couple of times and finally stopped in one day with my wife. Now, I understand the whole New York attitude thing, and I did live there for years, but I'm sorry - being rude is not a NY attitude. It's just poor service. I am a respectful friendly person and I don't like being mistreated - maybe I'm oversensitive but I HATE rude service. These guys acted like they were doing me a favor. It was my first time there and I found the menu board confusing, and was pressured to order. They weren't busy so I took my time and finally ordered from the unsmiling guy who makes the pizza. He handed me a piece of paper and didn't say a word. I moved over to the cashier guy (there was a young girl standing there who watched me without saying a word) who rang me up while staring me down. Ummmm .....no tip for you tough guy. I waited for our slices and figured the pizza guy was yelling at me when my slices came up - and then we ate. Well, the pizza is good. Overpriced without a doubt but at least it wasn't crap. A cheese slice after tax is $2.32. - add a topping and its almost $3. A 15 inch pie with 3 toppings is close to $25. Living in NYC I could get slices like this on every corner (usually cheaper too), so it was nothing amazing, but not bad for this area. The sauce is tasty - the crust was thin and the toppings good. So my final verdict - I might go there once in a while to get a pizza to go. The jerk at the cash register will never get a tip from me, and although I might enjoy eating their pizza once in a while, I will never enjoy overpaying for it, while being glared at by the staff. Honestly, I will keep looking for better service and value, hopefully without sacrificing taste and pizza quality. I think I better start making my own pizza because 80% of the places I try do not measure up to my standards! Yeah I expect a lot - but when I ran a restaurant, I set the bar for service and food quality, and expected all my employees to measure up.

text: I waffled between 3 and 4 stars... but the food and the menu saved the day. We just had brunch here after remembering that I'd heard some good things. "Brunch" is a tricky beast, as meals in a restaurant go. It's breakfast for people who are more discriminating than just wanting bacon and eggs, for people who have the money to spend something like $10 on a waffle with no sides, for people who have nothing to do for the rest of the day and can laze off their mimosas and bloody marys. It's tricky for a restaurant staff, too. You can get creative, but not too too creative, because you have to appeal to the geriatrics and screaming children who inevitably come out. Your night-owl 2-jobs-holding hung over cooks have to come in early and make muffins. You have to make a good enough impression on diners that they'll come back again for dinner some day. Tupelo Junction impressed me as a person who cooks for a living and who's chief hobby in life is eating out. Their menu is really fun and I can't wait to go back and try the other brunch offerings. I had the beignets (against my better dietary judgment) and they were pretty tasty. They weren't particularly sweet, and neither was the creme anglaise, but they were soothingly warm out there on the cold patio. Then came the smoked salmon bagel sandwich scramble (unfortunately underseasoned, but I'll accept that as a one-time fluke. It's brunch and the egg station dude probably was still filtering a head full of liquor, and who wants to think about salt at a time like that?) which came with slightly cold but delicious looking house potatoes, and my asparagus, mushroom and truffle scramble. Scrambles are ubiquitous, yes, and so is truffle, but fellow yelper lemonjelly l. talked it up and I'm her biggest fan. It was delish. It came with a salad with a default dressing i had no choice in that was disturbingly sweet. I still don't know what this dressing was; it doesn't say on the menu and nobody told me. It came with a choice of bread too, and I went for the baguette (yum!). It also came with a plastic tub of raspberry jam, which was a little tacky, but I didn't use it anyway, so at least it was easier to dispose of, I guess. Other good grace notes: Peet's coffee! I actually first had Peet's coffee EVER just this morning at the Peet's shop and loved it, so I had to get more for brunch. I liked the hostess too. No fake nicey-nice brunch smiles, this woman had half of Santa Barbara to seat with no reservations and was a MACHINE at it! A hostess like that is the difference between a $1000 day and a $3000 day for a restaurant. When we got there, there were about 6 or 7 groups to be seated ahead of us. She told us 15 minutes; I didn't believe her, but there we were, seated and happy after 15 minutes. Good job, lady. BAD grace notes: The busser was really weird and rude in ways I don't think he intended. When we sat down he asked if we wanted mimosas. We were still kind of getting situated at his sticky, freshly wiped table, so it took a whopping 4 seconds to process what he'd asked. When we didn't respond for that 4 seconds, he started to leave, saying "oh ok i guess so no" in a rude, short tempered tone. That left a bad taste in my mouth. When he brought our food out and other tables' food he sounded really sarcastic when responding to things. "Oh, fantastic, that's great, huh..." AND I couldn't understand what he was saying when he pronounced my order. I hope he didn't MEAN to have such rude inflection, but he sure did seem testy. But yes, I'll definitely be back again some day. Thanks for shaking up my brunch routine, TJC.

text: Morimoto is everything a restaurant should be: you get a unique food experience with great service in a trendy setting that feels posh but still accessible. I came here last night with several co-workers on a business trip, which was nice because I got to sample a large swath of the menu. We ordered 4-5 appetizers, the highlights of which were an excellent Octopus Carpaccio and the 10-hour Pork Kakuni, the latter so tender it literally melted in your mouth. The tuna pizza was pretty good too; and I also had a piece of fatty tuna sashimi, tiny but yummy. My main dish, the "Tai Shioyaki", was the coup de grace. It was a large white fish called sea bream, which had light and flaky flesh in a gently crispy skin. The dish came with the chef's instructions to sprinkle smoked sea salt over it, then cover in hot white butter sauce, and lastly, dip in spicy ponzu (a tart, citrus sauce). The result was divine--the best fish dish I've ever had. There wasn't a single thing I tried that was not at least very good. I sampled the popular "duck duck duck" entree featured a terrific roast duck that was moist and crispy. My dessert of chocolate pot de creme was a good finish. If I had a complaint at all, the only one would be that Morimoto's cocktails really ought to be larger or stronger given the price. But the drinks were still good; the cilantro gimlet was especially popular among a few of my colleagues. Dinner came to a little over $100 per person but felt well worth it. This was among my favorite restaurant meals ever. If you're in Philly, check out Morimoto!

text: Great with dogs... not so much with people. It's all about the money. If I could break it down, it would be 5 stars for the dogs, 0 star for customer service. This is the only facility of its kind in Reno, and the owners take that as an opportunity to deliver customer service that would be absolutely intolerable in any other business. We have lived in a number of places, and used different "doggie day care" services, and without exception, the first time I have brought my pet in, I was invited to tour the facilities, so that I would be comfortable leaving my 'fur kid' with them. Not at Pet Play House. As a matter of fact, there are curtains preventing owners from looking into the outdoor areas from the lobby, and requests for information are handled rudely and defensively. Before you can board or leave for daycare, you must bring your dog in for evaluation - an absolutely standard practice in the industry. But I have NEVER been asked to PAY for a full day daycare for that. And that was in facilities of equal or better quality, and in cities with MUCH higher overhead. I have also never done business with someone who has less concern for their clients' needs - you want to board? You MUST bring in your dog before noon. Why? It's what is convenient for Pet Play House. Can you make an exception? No. As long as you're booking a family vacation that won't change, you won't have many issues - but heaven help you if you're traveling on business and need ANY flexibility with dates or times. If you're late, you can't pick up your dog, or will be charged extra. If you cancel less than 10 days in advance, you'll still be charged for the booking. If you come home early, you'll still be charged - even if you call in advance (even a few DAYS in advance). If you make changes less than 10 days in advance, you'll be charged - and if you call to ask - the money is the FIRST thing out of the owner's mouth. When I called to cancel an extra day I had booked the day before, I was told "You can leave him if you want - since it's less than 10 days before (the booking) you'll have to pay for the day anyway". My jaw hit the floor when the owner said that. Our dog was healthy and exhausted when he came home. Will we go back? I sincerely doubt it. I am probably going to cancel our future booking (and eat the 50% booking deposit), just because I don't believe in supporting a business that provides bad customer service - I own my own business, and would NEVER treat customers the way they do.

text: The supposed mecca of the Russian food stores celebrated its fifth year in Philly this year. Starting in New York and working its way to our neck of the woods, this cornucopia of Slavic wonder was clearly, since its inception, intended to be the one stop shopping powerhouse among the Eastern Europen community of Philadelphia. Has it achieved that goal? Is it the place to shop for all your Eastern Europian goodies, be they kielbasa, shishlik, Keifer, Kvas or mildly confusing food description translations in form of deli counter signs? Or is this just another Russian food mart in what is sometimes affectionately, and sometimes not so affectionately, called the Kiev village? Well, the simple answer to these questions is this: When you try to be everything to everybody something gets lost in the translation, shall we say. Though the store sells ethnic food, the trend it has followed over the years is all too akin to American supermarkets. That is to say, the effort and ingredient quality has suffered in attempts to maximize profit to such a degree that, in my humble opinion, the end product is at times not worth the asking price when taking into account places such as Bell's Market. Its important to note that this criticism is squarely directed at the the prepared foods section in the store, and though I feel this section is the center of such a stores appeal for most folks, it in no way reflects upon the rest of the stores many other offers. There are many items that are quite good scattered throughout the store; The smoked duck breast, for example, which can be found in the vacuum sealed meats freezer area. Though rich, it is a can't miss if you enjoy smoked meats and are not opposed to treating yourself. Another nice item is the 100% not from concentrate pomegranate juice which NetCost carries. A very good value, especially when compared to something like POM, a from concentrate juice which is still more expensive. Furthermore, this is not to say that the store's prepared food is terrible, but rather, over time has gotten less diverse and complex while , in efforts to stay competitive, allowing cheaper ingredient occasionally creep in. (i.e using more flour and less cheese when making sweeten cheese paddies ) As Zanna H. summarized " Some other little Russian markets in the area have better prepared food but Net Cost's are still pretty good." So,on the whole, an excursion here is worthwhile, but if your making the trip from someplace other then the northeast then you might as well go to the comparability sized, previously mentioned, Bell's Market.

It used to be that Whole Foods did a great job of keeping their shelves stocked, whereas lately, I can find nothing that I need there. It is incredibly frustrating, especially since I only buy a few specific things at Whole Foods and I don't use it as my main grocery store. It puts me in a real tizzy when I take a few hours out of my day to make a Whole Foods shopping trip, only to find nothing that I need. Last night was a great example of this. All I needed was some extra firm 365 brand tofu and they were fresh out. How can you be a "health food" store and totally run out of tofu? Sure, they had the more expensive brand there but I refuse to pay over $2 for a brick of soy. The prices there also kill me, which is why I don't use it as my main food shopping hub, and the craptastic economy hasn't made the affordability any easier. For produce and meat, I will continue to stick with Reading Terminal Market. I have found fresh fruit, veggies, and cuts of meat that are just as fresh as what Whole Foods sells. Sure, it may not be organic, but it's still good for me AND my bank account.

As an entree, I got the butternut squash risotto and she got the yellowfin tuna. text: Hi Corbett Field is a prime example of how NOT to build a Spring Training stadium. The original tenants, the Cleveland Indians, were right to move to Florida after playing here all of those years. The greatest thing about this park is that the movie Major League was filmed, in part, here. To begin, it is in Tucson. This makes the place unbearable right out of the gun. Then, you have to drive through Tucson to get there. There is no freeway close by. The stadium is in the middle of a neighborhood/golf course/zoo. While that makes for a nice day of activities, it does not make for a fun day for me. To get there, get off on Prince (because the freeway is all torn up) and go down to Country Club. Take Country Club south to Broadway, turn left, then turn right on Randolf. Don't mind the El Convict Mall on your left. Hope that either no one is there or that you are early enough, otherwise, you might as well hand your keys over now because you'll be parking at that mall. Parking is free but takes forever when it is busy. Come early, leave early - that's my motto. Once you get there, you can either do your best Willy Mays Hayes impression outside or you can go in. Don't say you weren't warned. Once you get in you find a stadium that is perfectly reflective of Tucson - looks like Mexico but dirtier. Section numbers are strange so plan on walking around to find your seats. You won't be able to see the field until you are in the stands so don't plan on watching the game while you get food or drinks. There is no grass at Hi Corbett. The wooden walls and metal scoreboard make up the extent of the outfield. Why a stadium in the middle of a park doesn't have grass is beyond me. They do have what is known as the "Sandpile". That, of course, is not sand either. It is metal bleachers. The Rockies try to bring a bit of that Coors Field 'Rock Pile' action to Tucson by dressing up the name of the bleachers which, as it turns out, seem to make up about half of this stadium's seats. The regular seats are small, crammed, and unshaded with the exception of the highest row behind home plate. They are, however, close to the field. The biggest problem is that the stadium faces south, drenching every seat in sunlight and making the bleachers feel like they are 100 degrees. The temperature gauge on the scoreboard is at least 10 degrees cooler than it is in the stands. The food options are uninspired. There are only a couple independent vendors which is too bad because there is a ton of space down the left field line for more. The BBQ we had was okay but not worth the calories. The biggest plus about Hi Corbett was the $3.25 Coors draft. That is a price that is unbeatable in baseball (except for those AAA dollar beer nights). I'd say get there early, get some food, steak out a picnic table with an umbrella near left field, stay for 5 innings, then drive over to Kon Tiki and order a Scorpion. It is the best thing Tucson has going for it.

text: St. Louis sucks for getting good shows and the Pageant is slightly a step above some of the corporate venues like the House of Blues, so I will give them that. The Pageant, once you actually get in and sit down, is not a bad place to see a large show. It's a good atmosphere when there's a packed house and in general the seating is comfortable. I don't really care to see shows in this way, but it is what it is and the sound system ain't bad. I've definitely heard better in theaters this size, but it's okay, definitely not a liability. Now, I don't mind some security, but getting into the Pageant is like getting into the airport. It's incredibly ridiculous, unnecessary, and over the top when it comes to security. I went there a couple weeks ago for the Explosions in the Sky show and you'd think it was Gangbanger Jamboree or something from the level of security at the place. I'm sure there's a LOT of kids going to the Explosions show packing, guys. After getting patted down, I was placed into one of two lines, the one for over 21's. Check the ID, get the special over 21 stamp. Okay, fine. But when I try to go upstairs, which is an over 21 area, I get ID'ed again!!! WTF, man, you just checked behind my ballsack and went over my ID with your special light to give me a SPECIAL STAMP which said I was over 21, why the hell are you ID'ing me again? To add insult to injury, they ID'ed me ONE MORE TIME when I tried to get an overpriced beer at the bar upstairs (yes, the bar in the restricted area). What the hell, guys, that is insane. And don't try and tell me you are just doing your job, you have to get by 15 dudes just to by a brew and that is too much work. Just make the venue 21 and over only if that's how ridiculous it has to be. Or don't sell alcohol at all ages shows, whatever. Just don't make it like trying to pass customs to get a drink. The upside is that the actual security guards and bouncers once you get past all the nonsense are actually quite pleasant most nights and pretty lenient for a hoity-toity venue like this. HOB bouncers are like Gestapo compared to these guys, so I don't really understand what people are complaining about there. What can I say, I moved up here from more of an industry town, but the calendar at the Pageant is below average at best. They have the same bands come through every few months and rarely get the killer tours to come through town. They need some better promoters, probably. If they would ease up on security (or at least streamline it) and get a better calendar, this could be a 4 star venue, but as is, it's pretty much a huge disappointment. text: Thank you, O'Grady's, for ruining one of my most dear childhood memories. You see, O'Grady's now occupies the same building that formerly was home to a Ponderosa Steakhouse. As a child, my grandmother would often take us to Ponderosa for dinner where we'd get our favorite: chicken strips with french fries and the salad bar buffet. We'd start at the salad bar because grandma said we couldn't have any ice cream unless we ate our salad. In actuality the salad was mostly cheese, diced ham, croutons, and dressing, with some lettuce, broccoli, and alfalfa sprouts thrown in for good measure. Often times we'd also get a delicious bowl of chicken noodle soup and some fresh fruit as well. We'd munch down our awesome chicken strips with barbecue sauce and the french fries doused in ketchup. After finishing our meal, we'd make the trip to the ice cream station for a big cup of soft serve (always the chocolate-vanilla twist) topped with a Niagara Falls of butterscotch syrup, chocolate chips, and fistfuls of rainbow sprinkles. Really, is there anything that symbolizes pure happiness better than rainbow sprinkles? Yes, going to Ponderosa with mom-mom is one of my fondest memories of childhood. And O'Grady's has tainted--nay, completely vaporized--those memories. The salad bar buffet at O'Grady's now more closely resembles a compost heap than edible food: wilted lettuce, brown broccoli, slimy cucumber, and soggy croutons. Consuming the soup is reminiscent of swallowing pool water. The "half oven-roasted chicken" was positively anemic in regard to the flavor and peeling the few pieces of dried meat from the carcass was a painstaking and completely unrewarding ordeal. That anorexic chicken was accompanied by stuffing which was probably just some of those soggy croutons from the salad bar. After being informed they were out of both green beans and stewed tomatoes, I received mushy carrots soaked in butter. But most importantly, O'Grady's doesn't even have an ice cream station. Our waitress was nice enough and I felt bad for her having to work in such a shit-hole. The boss lady (maybe Mrs. O'Grady?) stood at the front of the restaurant observing her territory and making sure her minions were all busting their butts so she could rake in more cash; a real-life Cruella de Vil if there ever were. There are very few restaurants at which I will refuse to eat. Even if someone else is picking up the tab, never again will I consume food from O'Grady's.
label: NEG

text: A friend recommended the Flying Pig Saloon to me, and after holding a happy hour there, it was obvious why she did. Our friendly, primary server (Carol) managed to handle our fairly large group (about 15 folks; most of the time). Assorted staff also served us, though one waitress seemed pretty bitchy. Bartender Mike was on the ball, making us cherry kamikazes. (Drinking enthusiasts, be sure to check out their extensive beer selection.) At one point, someone knocked down a lamp. Fred, one of the owners, came over to make sure everything was okay - what a cool guy! Yes, there are some potentially breakable items inside, but the Saloon is generally drunk-friendly[1]. Besides our group, there was a healthy crowd for a Thursday. (Yes, people were smoking, but ventilation was pretty good.) Per Carol's suggestion, I had a tasty double-layered grilled cheese sandwich with ham[2], which came with a pickle! Oh, and before I forget, order the macaroni and cheese with lobster. Trust me. [1] Please drink responsibly. [2] Oink, oink.

text: I guess I'm saving 1 star ratings for someplace that offers a truly horrific experience, but I was tempted to do it here. I wish I had seen the low Yelp ratings before I decided to try this place last night, or I would have at least come in expecting way less. We stopped by because we had a $25 Restaurant.com gift certificate and thought it might be a good meal at a new place at a pretty good price. The dinner started out promising enough, they were very friendly over the phone taking our reservation, and then we stepped in the hostess was welcoming and offered us our choice of available tables. Since date nights are few and far between, we had our toddler daughter with us, and we were provided a kid's menu, bread and water right away. (Things were still looking good). Once we got our server, however, the experience took a nose dive. We were up front about the Restaurant.com gift certificate and she said told us what we could and couldn't use it on. Apparently, *everyone* in the restaurant was eating from the Prix Fixe menu, which was a reasonable $22 per person and included a starter (soup or salad), choice of entree (Chicken Marsala, some type of Salmon, or a Crab Cake) and a slice of cheesecake. What were the non Prix Fixe options? A ton of other entrees, but ALL starting at $26. Even the portabella mushroom entree. Really? $26 for a mushroom while it's $26 for crab legs? We ordered a $7 plate of mac & cheese for the little one, $26 Crab Newburg for me and $26 Salmon with Crabmeat for the husband. The meals came with an iceburg wedge salad and the aforementioned bread, which was pretty tasty. Unfortunately we ordered an iced tea and it was forgotten, and our water glasses would remain empty all evening. We were starting to suffer with no more beverages (we did eventually re-ask for the iced tea, with a full glass of ice it was gone in 2 seconds and never refilled again), when it got much worse waiting a l-o-n-g time for our food. Not even the kid's meal (some type of sour tasting Velveeta shells) came out promptly, everything was just taking a long time. There was a party of 12 (all Prix Fixers) that got their food long before us, and our waittress exclaimed that our meals were taking a long time because of "them". After the meals arrived they were very mediocre, I felt bad for my husband as his salmon was identical to the Prix Fixe salmons all around us-- a little piece, some veggies, 4 potato wedges. My Crab Newburg was overcooked, and had too many breadcrumbs and strangely, no cheese. It was dry with a serving of dry potatoes. Boo. Our waittress then disappeared for the rest of the evening and we really thought she quit. Another waittress finally caught our desperate staring eyes, and recovered her for us. After our food was wrapped and our check was brought over we hurriedly paid and left. Of course 20% gratuity was added to our check and even after our $25 off, our meal was close to $60. Very disappointing for a small place in a Ramblewood strip mall. We will definitely never go back, $25 off or not!

text: The set-up in McConnell's is sub-optimal for the shameless sampler. Half of the flavors reside on one side of the store, and half on the other. In order to sample to her heart's content, the shameless sampler must make a full round of the parlor, procure the assistance of a server, then request that the server make a pilgrimage to the other side of the store and return with sample spoons. Nonetheless, the shameless sampler is undeterred. McConnell's may be a classic ice cream parlor, but the flavors are thoughtful and somewhat out of the ordinary. I requested five samples of my friendly, patient server, and she obliged. I passed on the macadamia nut and strawberry bordeaux, even though both of these flavors were quite nice. I could only justify getting three scoops, and I went with the Vermont blueberry, cherry burgundy, and lemon zest. All three flavors tasted just as they were supposed to - pure and fruity and not very sweet. I had had the lemon zest ice cream once before in a phenomenal dessert at Bouchon, and was happy to taste that consummate blend of sour and creamy again. Matt B. had coffee with chocolate chip, and I stole some. That was also lovely, though I prefer the fruit flavors. My only complaint about McConnell's is that the texture of the ice cream was slightly icy. It wasn't off-putting at all, but I do think a more velvety mouthfeel would have made the ice cream even better. No matter. The ice cream hit my sweet tooth right at the sweet spot, and I want more of it. Preferably now.

text: First of all, had I Yelped this place 3 years ago it would be receiving 5 very deserving stars. Unfortunately, Garduno's just got my last dollar last night. When we first tried Garduno's back in 2006 it seemed like a real family affair. What really shone through during each subsequent visit was the obvious pride of the owners. Last night when we agreed we had a craving for Mexican, I suggested giving Garduno's another try, despite our last bad memory. The decision was largely based on very positive recent reviews here. When we walked in the door at 6 p.m. sharp we should have just turned around and left. The place was empty, save for 2 employees (both having their supper). As usual, the service was quick and welcoming, but it was the actual food that has been lacking, in my opionion, for the past 2 years (I had a theory that their cook had either been stolen by Tower Taco or had been snared by immigration). No surprise, but the food was just meh. I ordered my previously favorite dish, the carne asada chimichanga, and my lady had her previous favorite, the shrimp chimi. Plenty on our plates, just no discernible flavor to anything. My steak was primarily gristle...the shrimp had no zing whatsoever. Even the free chips and salsa were kind of yuck. Moreover, the place just looked tired and dumpy. The same bold colors that made the place charming and real 3 or 4 years ago now seemed grimey. The booths all could use a good wipe down and the green painter's tape that adorned our tabletop (a plan to paint abandoned?) was peeling up and kind of gross. I guess in a pinch, with freezing temps and a growling gut, Garduno's could soothe your hunger pangs, but keep walking if you're not on your last breath. Most Cherokee St visitors will find any restaurant in the district to be authentic compared to the more well-known joints featured in the RFT, if for no other reason than the genuine Mexican patrons usually in abundance, but by settling for this kind of mediocrity we're just asking for more of the same. Adios Garduno's...I hope you find your way...
label: NEG

text: The first thing that you should realize is that the BBB is funded by the very people they are supposed to be rating. Think about this: If someone pays for your salary, your office and that new computer, are you going to give them anything other than a good rating? I thought not. They also claim to have a complaint procedure that's really there to stand behind the guy who's paying their shot, not help the customer who has a complaint. In other words, don't check out a business using the BBB rating. Those ratings are bought and paid for. Look at ratings such as the ones on this website. The customer who's been there and experienced their service or products first hand are the best ones to rate the business.
label: NEG

text: I've been to Daughters on two occasions and although I will go back, it is for the food not the service. The first time I went was pretty great, the waitress was overly enthusiastic which I loved and the menu is incredibly interesting and delicious! I ordered a salad of the day with a crusty roll and interesting cheese (which turned out to be brie, YUM!). I also ordered a mimosa and while I expected a small champagne glass I received a large glass tumbler of orange juice and champagne that was delicious. My friend who came with me ordered a raspberry beer with berries and cheese appetizer and begniets (I'm probably spelling that word wrong). She got the same sized beer as I did mimosa and we were very pleased, but there were no berries or cheese. When our food was dropped off by another woman (who I think is the mother) we asked about the berries and cheese and she remarked that we were given the wrong sized beer, it was too big. We were of course excited to get an extra amount of something at no extra charge but it was a little unprofessional to point out something like that in front of us, we would have never noticed the difference. No big deal though we had a great lunch. The second time I went it was with the same friend and her mother, for my friends birthday. We met her mother there and she was sitting at a table outside with no menus, water or anything. The waitress (same as last time) was over at another table talking loudly and laughing, we were the only other table out there. We waited for a while hoping the waitress would come over and at least give us menus, after about ten minutes we started to get frustrated. Finally we had to get her attention and ask for menus and waters. The wait for service was just way too long. We got two orders of begniets (for me and for my friend) and a salad for her mother. When the food came out the waitress only had one order of begniets and the salad, she sat it down in front of my friend and her mother and asked if there was anything else. I asked for my order of food and she remarked very rudely about how she only had two arms and couldn't carry three plates. This to me is why I chose 2 stars instead of 3 or 4. I'm a server. I work at a restaurant that has even bigger and heavier entrees than Daughter's Cafe and I can carry up to 4 plates at a time if need be and I have much smaller arms than the woman who served us. It isn't the fact that I didn't get my food out with everyone, it's the fact that she ASKED if we needed anything else, and then was rude when I stated I needed the food I had ordered. The food at this restaurant is just delicious and I'd probably go back more often if I hadn't had poor customer service.

text: I have been to many Ruths' Chris Steak Houses and it is still the very best I have had, when it comes to a steak house. The filet melts in your mouth and could be cut with a butter knife, the flavor is beyond compare. It is one of the few places that still make a real Bearnaise sauce and Hollandaise sauce. They are known for their wonderful lobster bisque, fresh seafood and creative salads. Each restaurant has it's own pastry chef and the desserts are heavenly, such as the bread pudding with the Bourbon sauce or the sinfully rich chocolate espresso cake. They are an upscale chain and it is meant for fine dining. All sides are Ala carte, but they each feed two or more people. Of all the upscale steak houses that I have been to, from San Diego to Texas, Boston, New York, to Philly and DC. this ranks #1 in my book. Service of course is top notch, as well as detail, cleanliness and atmosphere. The decor in this one is very open and modern. Next special occasion give them a try. Any town, any state, anywhere, Ruth's Chris is the best. Wheelchair accessible with ramp and flat entrance to enter and a small ramp inside the restaurant.

text: The server was great and the place was nicely decorated and that's about the high point of my dinner at this place. My table ordered the spinach artichoke dip for appet., I've had much better. The dip was kind of watery, can't really taste the spinach or artichoke, even though both were in the sauce. For this dish, if the dip is bad it's pretty much downhill. I ordered salmon, with rice pilaf and steamed vegetables. The entree also came with a side salad, I had the house with raspberry vinaigrette. Side salad: Flavor of the dressing wasn't really there. It's raspberry, suppose to be a little sweet, I couldn't taste it. It was mostly sour and water down. The water down taste probably came from the lettuce itself. It tasted like they just washed it and didn't dry it so lot of water was still in the salad. Salmon with rice pilaf and steamed vegetables: The salmon was grilled nicely but was very bland. The "steamed vegetables" should've been called raw vegetables on the side. It wasn't cooked all the way. It had zucchini, cauliflower and broccoli. All 3 were undercooked. For the zucchini I wasn't able to eat the whole thing, only ate the middle and left rest because it was so hard. Cauliflower and broccoli made me felt like I was eating a salad again. The rice was probably the best thing on my plate. I also ordered iced tea. I had it sweet first, but it was way too sweet, felt like I was drinking sugar water. The server was very nice and switched it for me to unsweet, which wasn't much better but at least I wasn't going on a sugar high. I might come back here again after a long long long time, at least long enough for me to forget this time. So enter at your own risk and good luck.

text: I never say this about a place, but I love everything about this place. The first time I came here on White Linen Night, the hostess said there was an hour wait. My date and I turned to walk away and we hear the hostess chasing us down the street. "Actually, I can seat you right now, since you only have two." The second time I came we were seated immediately at a corner booth. The atmosphere is great for first dates or hundredth dates. The lights are kept dimmed. The music is everything I like-- White Stripes, Black Keys. The waiters are dressed in black covetable concert tees and look like they haven't seen a razor in 6 months. Ok with me, I dig hipster beards. It just adds to the whole rocker-chic ambiance. Even the wallpaper is bad ass. From a distance it resembles french provencal toile-- but look closer and it's a burgundy pattern of tattoo pinups. The first and last time I came, I shared truffle Mac and cheese and a hangar steak frites. The steak was a tender, perfect medium rare and was served up with sauteed shrooms and crispy frites-- perfect for slopping up the steak juices! Truffle Mac and cheese is now on my list of dishes to replicate. The shells are covered in creamy, white cheese, sprinkled generously with green peas and pancetta(?) or tasso(?). The hangar is also served on a salad if you don't want frites. Jack Daniels Blackberry lemonade was also delicious and I usually don't like sweet drinks. Speaking of sweets, three words: peanut butter pie. At three bucks, it is a must have. In fact, everything at Capdeville is reasonably priced. On my last visit-- two entrees, two adult beverages, dessert and on point, noninvasive service was about $50. You can't beat it. Capdeville is a hip, nonpretentious fantastic establishment. Go and it'll sure to become you're new favorite as well.

text: Fatty's is a great local sports bar in Wyndmoor. They have TV's squeezed into every corner place and even stuck a couple outside on the patio just for good measure. Like any good sports bar they have the NFL Sunday ticket. The staff are all die-hard Philly sports fans but they're still accommodating and friendly, as opposed to the Santa Booing, fight starting, retarded asshole Philly fans you can't avoid at most sports bars within spitting distance of the city line. So when this NY boy walks in with my Yankee hat or Giant jersey on to catch the game, I catch a ration of shit and hear the taunts from all of them, but it's all good natured. If you're an out of town fan Fatty's is a great place to go catch the game in an enjoyable fashion. On top of that Fatty's has a great selection of beers on tap including an ever rotating selection of micro-brews to try out. The prices are pretty reasonable making it a great place to go with the guys and throw back beers. The food at Fatty's is your standard pub menu but it is all pretty good. I'm especially fond of their cheese fries (especially when they have waffle fries in) and their cheesesteaks are pretty good too. My personal favorite of their sandwiches however is the Buffalo Chicken Cheesesteak, I have a tendency to get it more often than not and it's excellent. That leads me to Fatty's wings. In my opinion you just can't call yourself a sports bar and not have good Buffalo Wings. Fatty's doesn't disappoint. The wings at Fatty's are easily the best that I have found in the area. The wings are large and smothered in sauce. The "hot" sauce has a very good balance of flavor & heat which is what really sets them apart. To top it off they know to give a side of rich, chunky bleu cheese and celery. The last tip I can give about Fatty's Menu is to make sure you check the specials board on the rear wall of the pub. It's a whiteboard right between the kitchen window and the hallway to the bathrooms. See, Fatty's sometimes decides to pretend they're actually a restaurant, trapped in a pub's body. They use that little board to supplement their menu and they do it extremely well. In conclusion Fatty's is hands down the best Pub in the area and without a doubt my favorite pub around Philly.

text: Oh, Fresh Grocer. I have finally gotten to you. Let's get everything everyone says off my chest first, and then progress to personal rants. Your staff blows, with the exception of checkout staff. They are either down on life but you can get them to smile, or they're surprisingly pleasant compared to the rest of the store. But lord forbid something rings up wrong because they do not have an efficient way of dealing with voids or price checks. It's horrible. You feel like such a douche making everyone wait behind you. And self-checkout has been so inconsistent since it opened. Store organization? WHAT STORE ORGANIZATION. Mollie E once described it as "I think the Fresh Grocer was organized by a little kid with ADHD." I'd like to add that he works for an interior design company on TV that always make changes you just don't agree with. Right when you know where the GOYA juice is, it's gone. Is it discontinued? Is it in the other juice aisle? Or the OTHER other juice aisle? Or the OTHER OTHER other juice aisle? Same goes with cheese. And baked goods. And snacks. And hot sauce. Do they have the international foods section? Does it have everything international in the store? I DON'T KNOW ANYMORE. And how will I get there? Because they like to put displays right in the way of something else, especially at checkout. This place is a labrynth, and I like to spend hours on my grocery excursions but here, you have to, because everything is somewhere random and new. AND DON'T BUY THE MCCORMICK OR WHATEVER SPICES THAT ARE IN THE CANISTERS IN THE BAKING NEEDS AISLE. I KNOW IT'S PUMPKIN PIE AND SPICED CIDER SEASON SO YOU MIGHT BE TEMPTED. Fresh Grocer has its own, things like whole cloves and all spice and dried herbs, in baggies at the front with the nuts and stuff, sort of near the fruit. OKAY, that's only the last time I checked. But it's like a 5 dollar price difference, so I'd say it's worth the 40 minute search. How much does it cost? The world may never know. Chances are, if it's a fresh herb, it's too much. You'll find yourself paying 2.50 for 2 sprigs of mint (which grows like wildfire and just won't die, btw, so plant your own and have it free for life and then franchise it) and 495739487 dollars for a tube of basil. You know the ones I'm talking about. They don't have a price on them but it's absurd. Don't do it. This applies to almost everything you actually want but need to weigh the cost into your decision (like cotton candy, ice cream, and queso dip.) Milk and eggs are good to go, though, so it's not always panic city. On the topic of pricing, sometimes Fresh Grocer is fantastic, from half-priced yogurt to 2 for $5 Country Crock, and their wing bar or vegetables on sale. But the next time you come, they vegetables will be double regular price, and I'd steer clear of the organics section. Seriously, I don't think you want to pay 4 dollars for two apples. Go to Trader Joes. The new "bars" are great, if you play your cards right. I mean, it's a good way to get real food to go. Don't get the stuffed grape leaves, they taste like the tin can they came in (and this applies to every place that sells them in the city. Go to the International Food Store near Shop n Bag and 7-11 and for up to 8 dollars, you can get a never ending supply that tastes equally or less tinny.) Finally, Fro Gro sushi. I used to come to Fresh Grocer exclusively for Specialty Bakery Lady Fingers and Sushi, if I had anything to say about it. Well, the sushi is a little more expensive than it used to be (I mean the standard crunchy rolls, salmon, etc.) by abount 50 cents to a dollar, but that's enough to make it the same price as everywhere else you go, meaning it's no longer a value. They also offer more elaborate options now, for significantly more. They must not know Mizu sushi is across the street. But, I suppose for more elbaroate options, they cost less than most sit-down sushi restaurants. Still, I don't think I'll be buying sushi there for a while, I liked it under 6 dollars. Fresher (okay, that's easy to type, it's happened like four times now) offers customer parking and a RedBox location, and also sells septa tokens.
label: NEG

text: The aquarium sits on the banks of the Mississippi River which dumps out into the Gulf of Mexico (little geography lesson on the side there for ya) while wading through swamp land. So I was expecting a solid aquarium with lots of diversity and cool exhibits. What I got was an aquarium not to much different then the one I have down the street from me in ARIZONA! Come on NOLA you can do better than this! The price tag is a heft $18.50 and I was able to walk the entire aquarium in one hour and fifteen minutes before catching an IMAX. There are highlights to the place I guess, but not that warrant the price of admission. I like that the place had a flow and wasn't just free wandering. The kids 'Break" room was simple and their Moray Eel tank was pretty cool. If there was a 'WoW" exhibit for me it was the White Alligator in the picture who was as big as any gator I've seen, though I hear the gator at the zoo (and the Zoo for that matter is worth it, wish I had gone there) has a feeding time and is even better. I know there isn't much you can do with an aquarium that isn't the same as every other aquarium but one of the very best I've EVER been to is the one in Chattanooga, TN and who would have thought that!

text: I love our little library. It's East Nashville and our Library kind of fits our neighborhood vibe, eclectic and unassuming. It' s obviously an older building and much of the original finish work is well in tact which I really enjoy. I also love that it's small and quaint. I love our big library too but when I take the kids, it's a little less overwhelming for them to peruse the shelves and find specific books they are interested in. The kids section really is pretty small but it's well stocked and I think really ideal for kids getting to know the library. As for me, well the adult fiction section is a pittance compared to most of the other branches. However, you can go on line and with the # on your library card, you can order up books that may not be carried at this branch and they will deliver and hold them for you. Sooooooo, I get whatever books I want and i never leave the hood. I pretty much stick to going to the shows at the downtown library because I never know when I might get back downtown and it makes it easier to manage returns from this branch. If you go directly between 2 and 4 on weekdays, it is full of teenagers from the high school. I can't say that i have ever run in to a problem with any of them but if you are looking for the typical whisper in the library experience, it ain't going to happen.

text: Alright... Sen Thai. Location was easy to find and I got a parking spot right in front (story to follow about this spot) and my friend and I were sat right away. He came back over a few minutes later with my hot... wait. Nope, my iced Thai coffee. All good though, it still had caffeine, so I accepted. My girlfriend ordered the fire rice which she loves and it looked pretty tasty... it's probably what I'll order if I ever go back. I got the chicken kabobs with peanut sauce and a side of white rice which was alright but nothing too exciting. For me, this review isn't as much about the food as it is what happened to my poor, innocent, and unsuspecting car. Towards the end of our meal I heard a car alarm blaring and looked outside to find that it was mine! First time that's ever happened. That's when I saw... someone stole my tags and tried to basically rip off my passenger side door. Awful. I felt like such a bad car mom! I swear I am going to karate chop the next person who tries to break in. Not cool.
