text: I have been eating at the Grill for many years. In fact, it used to be Friday night dinner almost every week when my husband and I lived in Reno. It was always our go to for good affordable (not inexpensive) food. Since then we have made a concerted effort to go when we are in town visiting family. Recently, while visiting family we went for dinner. What once was a peaceful intimate environment had turned into a room full of 30 something singles playing pickup and a loud, dark atmosphere (which is why I gave it 2 stars instead of 3). We sat outside which was definitely the right choice. I still held hope that the food was to the same standards. I noticed that owner who normally makes his way from table to table to check in with the customers was nowhere to be found. This was apparent not only in the service but in the food as well. The wine list was still extensive except that they had definitely moved beyond a mix of expensive and middle of the road. They were all expensive. Sometime you just don't want to drop $40 on a mediocre bottle of wine. We settled on a Petite Syrah which actually was quite delicious. Probably the highlight of the meal. The wine prices were indicative of the entire menu. The Grill had definitely raised their prices which is fine IF you don't diminish the quality of your food. My expectations of excellence were squashed. I ordered patrole sole with lobster risotto and my husband and his father both ordered the sea bass. We all had salads to accompany our entrees. The salads were nothing to write home about. Pretty standard field greens and a vinaigrette. Something I could have gotten at any neighborhood restaurant. The sole was dusted with cornmeal and then cooked in butter a twist on sole meuniere. Pretty tasty but the fish should have been more fresh for the price. The lobster risotto was good but nothing fantastic. Not particularly creamy and only the faintest of lobster taste. In all honesty the spinach was the highlight of the dish. It was wilted to perfection and mixed with garlic and olive oil. The sea bass on the other hand was definitely over cooked and the seasonal vegetables were nothing special. At the almost $30 price tag, it should have been much better. I don't see us returning to the Grill next time we are in Reno. I think there are better restaurants to be had. Especially for the price.
label: NEG

text: "Meh. I've experienced better." Pretty much sums it up. We had a reservation for 8:30, but were not seated until about 40 minutes later. I understand that sometimes patrons refuse to leave, which is out of the restaurant's control, but that's something they should account for when booking reservations. Also, the hostess had kind of a nasty attitude when we inquired politely about our table after 30 minutes of waiting. She offered to send down the manager, who was apologetic and gave us complimentary margaritas and guacamole, so at least he was nice and the gesture was appreciated. One star for the nice manager who gave us free stuff. However, waiting 40 minutes for our table was only the beginning of a long night of waiting. Service was extremely slow and each course took forever to arrive. The waitress was pleasant enough, but didn't stop by to say something like, "I'm sorry for the wait, your food should be out shortly." The bussers did their job pretty well, though. The food itself was mediocre. The guacamole was decent, but not amazing. It was comparable to the guacamole you can buy at Trader Joe's, which is good but also costs a fraction of the price. I was excited to try the ceviche appetizer, but it was unimaginative and even tasted kind of sour (in a bad way) and funky, which is not good when it comes to raw fish. This made me sad because I love both mackerel and ceviche. The braised short rib entree was good; it was probably the only thing that impressed me (this is where the other star comes from). My dining companions were not thrilled with their scallop or pork dishes, though. The desserts were not even worth mentioning, but I will anyway. The churros were dry and hard and tasted like 3-month-old stale donut sticks sprinkled with cinnamon sugar. The tres leches was bland with a weird frosting and a "pear compote" which was more like a few pieces of canned Del Monte diced pears. Overall, it was an underwhelming experience with slow service, a hostess with an attitude problem, and average food.
label: NEG

text: Note: Istanbul Restaurant and Istanbul Cafe are the same place. I LOVE ISTANBUL. Their gyro is super addictive, and their Turkish tea is beyond compare. I probably go here once a week. There are two main guys who are always there and they make it best, which is why I would recommend dinner over lunch (tends to be a little oilier). The tables are nice and large, the prices very reasonable ($7.99 for a gyro platter that is HUGE) and it is very clean. They also have a wide selection of desserts. I've been to Kalamata's and Mediterranean Cuisine, but haven't returned to either after finding Istanbul. They are also open from 11-9 without the afternoon break that most restaurants take, so it's nice to have lunch at 3pm. text: Taqueria Monterrey is the little sister of El Taconazo (The Taco Bus). They have the same great sweet tea as Taco Bus, but the menu and atmosphere are different. Taqueria Monterrey has a small menu, but is big on flavor. Much like the Bus, they have a variety of meat and non-meat options including a new option they call "Vegan Chorizo". The "Chorizo" is well-spiced crumbles of soy protein griddled to perfection. Try it in the Gringas, a grilled flour tortilla topped with the "Chorizo," grilled pineapple and slices of avocado. They offer burritos, quesadillas, tortas and my favorite, flautas. They have beef, chicken and potato flautas. The potato ones are filled with a cheesy, creamy potato mixture reminiscent of mashed potatoes and are fried crisp. They're topped with shredded lettuce, big slices of tomato and an avocado cream sauce that I really wish they would bottle and sell. Additionally, there's a salsa bar that has 10 or so fresh salsas everyday ranging from a cool avocado salsa to a kickin' peanut butter salsa (it sounds weird, but try it!). The bar also has pickled radishes, limes and their house signature salsa, a great blend of roasted peppers, tomatoes and onions. The guacamole may seem pricey, but try it. It's made-to-order hand-smashed avocados mixed with their pico de gallo and is chunky and delicious! Service can be slow at times, because there's usually only 1 or 2 servers working both to-go and the restaurant. If you're allergic to peanuts, avoid the two orange salsas on the salsa bar; I know at least one of them has peanuts in it! Try: The Potato Flautas The Vegan Chorizo Gringas The Coconut Candy

They also have great sandwiched, side dishes, packaged entrees and more. Arnie and staff are friendly and aim to please. A regular, go to spot each week.

text: I challenge you to find a better local place with more selection of food and fresh groceries. The prices are fair, too.
label: POS

text: Worst. Race. Ever. Do not attend this event. The organizer have no idea how to hold a race and the city does not want you to actually participate in this race. Not enough water or toilets on the run. Expo was a disaster, post race festival was too many people in too small of an area with maybe 1 trashcan that was just overflowing. I will give the sponsors credit, they stepped up and gave out lots of freebies. I have traveled to several races in my time and I will never be going back to this one.

text: Few places can accomodate my strange requests... For instance, "Do you have soy milk? Oh, great. Yes, a latte... But, can you put it in a really interesting mug? I noticed bizarre tea cups over there..." Aside from indulging my proclivities, Centennial Cafe has a great selection of sandwiches (and dutifully so, breads for said sammies), salads, and coffee/tea drinks that make this a great spot for a casual lunch scenario. I had their tuna salad on multigrain baguette, and it was the perfect mushy tuna vs perfectly-toasted bread combo. My favorite part about this place is the bizarre decor... Vinyl tablecloths that sent me into a tailspin through time....Envisioning family picnics at my Grandma's house (think mayo-centric everything, "punch" hinged on lime sherbet, and ambrosia salad... yeah, we went there). Just a fun spot in general with lots of windows, and odd items to stare at during conversational lulls (see sorcerer/barbershop wind chime/whirlygig thingie if you do indeed visit). I'll definitely be back for breakfast, as the menu included some items that sounded interesting, and the latte was a huge success. Great prices, too. Lovesies, D
label: POS

text: I have gone to the Piper Pub for years - convenient downtown location and a nice patio. On my last 2 visits, the service has been so disappointing that I doubt I will ever go back. It has been the same waitress both times and I am amazed this woman keeps her job! I wrote off the first experience as someone having a bad day, but her utter disregard for her customers seems to be her norm. It was nearly impossible to get her attention even in the nearly empty restaurant and twice during our meal we had to go ask someone else for help, once for the missing portion of our meal and again for the check. I only give Piper two stars out of past loyalty and the still good food.
label: NEG

text: There's a warm, neighborhood vibe going on here. All the employees are exactly what you'd expect in Fishtown: locals with rough-around-the-edges, boisterous, but affable manners. I love it here. Sitting with friends, clinking pints underneath dimmed and flickering lights, we rattled on about future plans and experiences yet to be had. Our cherub, aka: waitress, offered up dishes she swore would "change our lives" and while I thought I'd never savor a tofu club, I found myself stealing bites off my friend's dish. That said, you should order the Smoked Coconut Club (it's as exotic and delicious as it sounds). My roast pork sammy was sloppy and savory, while my other friend's seitan steak was good, albeit a slight bit too salty. This place rules and they have Racer 5 on cask.
label: POS

text: Worst Chinese food I've ever had. I think the Chinese-food situation in Boise is dire enough that I can't really recommend any of them (my advice is to eat it when traveling to a big city on the west coast with a bigger Asian influence). If you held a gun to my head and forced me to recommend one, I'd say Yen Ching, although the hordes of white folk working there made it the least authentic Chinese experience I've ever encountered. Is the city that short on Chinese people? Such is a similar situation at the cleverly titled North End Chinese Restaurant, although I wasn't able to see who was fixing my food in the kitchen. Even if he/she was Chinese, it didn't matter. Crap is crap. And for a city where Chinese food is subpar, this takes the cake for being the worst of them. I got my food way too quickly, which caused some concern. Stale, reheated dreck. I should've known when I noticed there was a drive-thru area. Buying La Choy brand food at the store is better than what I got. Stay away.
label: NEG

text: Burger was okay. My bun was shredded so it was difficult to eat. And, I have to echo everyone else on the sodas. Absolutely ridiculous to charge $3 for a soda and then $3 for a refill. Will NOT go back there - ever.

text: Delicious, snooty, and creative. Great for a date or special occasion, but I can't ever LOVE a place where the management doesn't look you in the eye. :) I was misled by this yelp posting though-- this place is NOT vegetarian, just veg friendly. Great appetizers and one tofu entree. Excellent service. Elegant atmosphere. Great portions for fancy stuff.

text: Started with 5 stars when I walked in. Nice crowd and nice girls all over. :) - 1 Star: forgot my hot sauce several times when asked for it, bastards. - 1 Star: forgot my veggies, double bastards. - 1 Star: forgot to separate the bill as I asked in the VERY begining. WTF? - 1 star: big ass hair in my food. I didn't remember ordering that! I will not go back.

text: DIET CREAM SODA....almost heaven. If they would only start making their orange in diet I would be tempted to bump this to five...tempted, probably wouldn't, but I do love diet orange. People seem to have an attitude about this place, but it's a grill, it's not gourmet, and it's a family restaurant, so I guess I just don't expect my waiter to hover and be there constantly at this place. I like it, I always leave satisfied, and I never feel like I dropped far too much money on it. Unlike most people, I don't get a burger here. I always lean to the fish and chips. Is it as good as anything you could get in London? Well, definitely not. I mean, how could you expect that? But it satisfies my craving for it, they never look at me funny when I douse my plate in vinegar, and I didn't have to drop $700 on a plane ticket to satisfy my craving. My family all love the burgers, and from time to time, I have embarked on a salad or two at this place. I even managed fine when I was a vegetarian. Also, they never give us attitude if we bring my little niece here and she decides she's in the mood to throw her food all over the floor. Gotta love that. (and leave a big tip after).
label: POS

text: First, let's get this out of the way: NoVi was, by and large, a disappointment. Despite the decent decor and reasonably priced food, I don't think I'll find myself returning. I was the only person at the bar, with only two other tables of guests in the restaurant. There was no host at the front when I entered, but I was greeted promptly and sat myself at the bar. While I wasn't drinking this particular evening, I did browse the cocktail list, and it was standard tropical fruit or coffee liqueur based restaurant fare. The menu is a decent size but relatively uninspired, classic American Italian dishes and a wide selection of pizzas. I settled on the Tuscan Chicken Sandwich with a side salad, and was pleasantly surprised with the plump and juicy chicken breast and fresh bun. My salad was pretty much crap, but the balsamic based dressing that came with it had a nice smoky flavor that I enjoyed. Unfortunately, this is pretty much where I run out of positive things to say. The staff at NoVi, including the chef who identified himself as the manager on duty, all had a bad tendency to crowd around the bar, talk or text on their cell phones, and pass around drink samples among each other as if I didn't exist. To the bartender's credit, my water never went empty and my plate was whisked away immediately when I was finished despite the otherwise complete lack of attention or engagement. Unfortunately, when I paid with cash for my meal I was flatly informed that the bar drawer had no change, and was given two large bills back along with a vaguely expectant stare. Not being the type to stiff service staff, especially after 6 years in the industry myself, I ended up leaving a double the appropriate tip for my sandwich and water as i had no ones with me, and was gone as fast as my heels would carry me. Not a great experience, and not one I'm in any hurry to repeat.
label: NEG

text: Are you kidding me! Do you like wait staff that are so HIGH they don't remember half your order and are too cool to even communicate. text: I'm almost afraid to go back to Pi as you don't want to lose that perfect vision you have in your head of a perfect pizza. Kind of like meeting a girl at a bar, thinking she is the hottest girl ever and going on a date later and realizing she's not quite a 7. Pi, it's name descended on St. Louis like a swarm of locusts, I couldn't go anywhere without hearing about it, Obama even had them fly out to the freaking White House (over Chicago places). There was no way this place could live up to expectations. I have to admit, I was blown away by the pie here, freaking amazing. In a cute nod to my old city San Francisco (Which they say this is SF pizza, I'll touch on that later), they name a few of the pies after SF 'hoods (which is why I won't order the Western Addition, I don't want that neighborhood in my mouth) and include my old place North Beach. From the toppings to the crust the "thin" crust North Beach was awesome, perhaps the best pizza I've ever had. I do have one bone to pick with you PI. I lived in San Francisco for 4 years, I ate at Golden Boy, North Beach Pizza, Pizza Orgasmica and a bunch more places and never came across a San Francisco style pizza. I've reached out to my friends there and no one knows of this San Francisco style pizza. What gives?

text: Had lunch here on Christmas Day. Best meal we had during our entire stay. Loved the white bean spread served with the bread. The beet salad with goat cheese was simple, clean, and wonderful. I had a grilled fish with cauliflower puree. I have no idea how they could make a vegetable taste that good, but they did. They only offered 2 desserts, so my husband and I each chose one. I got the red velvet cake and he had the rice pudding. I'm not a huge fan of anything that doesn't involve chocolate, so I ordered the cake only because it was included with the meal. It was jaw dropping good. And it was an absolutely beautiful plating.

text: I have been to Pennies about a dozen times in the past 4 years for lunch, but no more. It's going downhill. Others have raved on here about it but the last two times i have been there the waitress had an attitude. These girls have to be family to get away with their rude manner. How about introducing yourself and smiling?? Yesterday I had to ask for straws after the drinks where given. Then had to ask for silverware after the food was served. All seemed to be a problem. Also lunch shouldn't take an hour. People have to get back to work!! The place is dirty. The tacky Christmas lights have dust on them as well as the ductwork on the ceiling. Glass dividers, front door, floor where disguisting as well as the bathroom. Makes one wonder what the kitchen looks like. ?? The roast beef sandwiches used to be sliced beef and where excellent. Now it's shredded like dogfood and tastes different. When I said something to the waitress , again attitude. The owner is always at the bar flirting with locals. Get more paper!!! Better yet get some paper towels and clean the damn place before the health department shuts you down.

We have friends who swear by this place, and we've tried it several times, but we just can't find much redeeming here...

text: I also didn't have such an enjoyable experience here. After a raving review from my friend, I decided to try this place out this afternoon. We made it right before lunch hour, so we didn't have to wait in line. Appearance (3-4 stars) - Nothing looked better than a row of food lined up in front of you complimented by interesting decor around you. The place felt very retro; it felt like one of those dusty abandoned stores you see in vintage flicks. Food (3 stars) - I got the baked chicken with green beans and corn. The baked chicken showed signs of having been cooked a couple hours ago, with the meat dried and lukewarm. The green beans were pretty decently done, having been cooked in chicken broth. The corn was just some creamed corn with some peppers in it, nothing too special. The saving grace of the plate was the cornbread. I loved it, and stole my friend's since he said he was full. The cornbread is super buttery but a little dry, but it goes down just right. I heard that the Mac&Cheese was the bread and butter of this establishment, but I didn't try it because I heard that after I had ordered. I guess someone can enlighten us on that if you decide to go. So what made me give this establishment 2 stars instead of 3-4 based on my review thus far? The price. One piece of (small) chicken and two sides will run you close to $10, not including a drink. For that much I could have gotten food just as good at Lee's Chicken or an All-You-Can-Eat southern style buffet. I was expecting more for less, and unfortunately Sweetie Pie's did not deliver for me.
label: NEG

text: Yes, Pub & Kitchen is on the pricier side and yes, the crowd is a bit yuppy but I still love this place. Maybe it's the outdoor seating or the delicious $3 bar snacks or the amazing fries or the nicely curated beer menu or the fact that I live across the street....Pub & Kitchen has quickly become my "go-to" place for a chill night and drinks with friends. Order a dark & stormy. During certain busy nights (like game nights) they'll open the second floor which has 3 or 4 large plasma-screen TVs and a second bar. Beware the Friday and Saturday night crowd as it does skew yuppy - and by that I mean ANNOYING. Did I mention they do brunch on the weekends?

text: Best Pizza in the City? If you like ice cold chunks of mozzarella. I went in fully expecting to like this place. My friend lives in the lofts at 640 in the same building so I was really wanting to like this place. Philadelphia magazine voted their pizza best gourmet pizza in the city. What could go wrong? The decor was incredible, the service spot on but the main reason for my visit, the best gourmet pizzas in Philadelphia left a sour taste in my mouth. We ordered the pannochia pizza on suggestion of the bartender. Sweet summer corn, truffle oil and mozzarella. The pizza came out thin and soupy in the middle (crust thinner than a cracker in the center) with ice cold 1 inch chunks of mozz on top, not even partially melted or warmed up. I inquired with the bartender and was told that some cheese is melted onto the crust but a majority of the toppings are thrown on after the pizza is removed from the oven. Now I've had this style of pizza numerous times before. A nice crispy thin crust topped with ingredients meant to subtly wilt or warm up nicely (arugula, shaved parm, etc). But these large chunks of mozz were ice cold, not even close to room temp and the pizza was soo soggy and soupy that it was impossible to eat without a fork and knife. Oh and all this for a $20 pizza that was 4 small slices. OVERRATED, OVERPRICED and BELOW AVERAGE
label: NEG

text: Warm, elegant and beautiful. Now let's talk about the atmosphere! LOL My partner and I dined here on a Thursday night and when we walked in (past the dessert cooler!) and we saw that we were the only patrons of the restaurant that night, I was concerned. When my soup arrived along with the spring rolls my partner ordered we realized we were in for a treat. The food was incredible and our server knew the right mix of attending to us and leaving us to enjoy our meal. We both ordered the crispy duck and it was fabulous. I hope that the reason the restaurant was slow that night was simply because it was an off-night. I'd hate to see a gem like this go to the wayside. It was a true dining experience! Bravo!
label: POS

text: I went in to Dudes on a whim,. From the window display, I assumed that it would be all cowboy boots, of which I am not a huge fan. Despite this, I went in for kicks and giggles. Surprisingly they has some cute boots. I was looking at one CUTE green pair and noticed the price. It was $200 something but marked down to $180. A good deal I suppose for fine knee high leather boots made in Spain. What IRKED me was that, without me inquiring about the price, a "dude" walked up to me and said, "You know. We can do specials on the boots. Like, I could give you these boots for.... $120." Shady. He didn't say, we are having a sale or anything like that. By him just walking up to me, unsolicited, and saying that send red flags off in my mind. How over priced were these boots? If he could still make a profit off of $120 boots that were originally priced at $250, how high was the mark-up and what is the quality? Good thing I was not about to shell out money for these boots anyway.
label: NEG

text: I have done ghost tours in several other cities and was looking forward to this one. As other reviews mentioned, we were broken up in groups of two. At the start, the tour guide (dressed up in a white shirt, red vest and black cape) asked us to move in closer while he spoke and made a joke about body odor. The worst part is that he reeked of sweat!!! Throughout the tour, I would be standing further back and would smell it...gross. To be fair to him, maybe the costume needed to be cleaned as there were stains on it, but seriously man, practice some hygeine! I found the stories to be okay and wished we had entered some of the places (as I have done in tours in other cities). But, I really liked going in the graveyards and loved seeing the town on foot. The other thing was he walked really fast and justified it in the beginning by saying we would hear more stories because of it. He did seem to slow down by the end, though. Overall, two stars...maybe we will try the other ghost tour but I better read the reviews first.

text: I do not shop here for everyday things, more for specialty items for dinner parties or when we are grilling out. We love their burgers and steaks. They also have a good cheese selection.

text: Hooray! Soak up the irony: a bold, forward-thinking, controversial, and Californian clothing store right in the middle of Lower Broadway! I was there today, and an old fanny pack clad tourist from Iowa walked in and loudly asked if one could drink beer on the street. The clerk did not even blink as he politely answered, "no" and completed my transaction. I like watching conservative, chunky tourists react to the ridiculous, sometimes indecent, always for skinny people bathing suits, leotards and super skinny hot pink jeans. Besides all that, however, the clothes they sell (the 70% that aren't there just to shock you) are good. I bought a very sharp polo shirt here today--their shirts are not just appropriately slim-fitting, but the designs are cool --they can make something classic like a polo shirt look really design-forward and fresh. text: I am sad that I only got to have lunch at Bayona. There are so many things on the menu that I still want to try, so I'll have to go back another time. I also had their famous cashew-peanut butter and pepper jelly sandwich featuring smoked duck. It was sticky and sweet, but balanced out nicely with the apple and celery salad. I didn't have time for dessert because I was on my way to catch my flight, so again, I will just have to go back. The one drawback was the slow service, but it was very friendly and homey.

text: Previous to the shady move that Philly Car Share decided to pull in regards to canceling the free membership option and basically playing the game Telephone with its members as a method to let everybody know, I would have given Philly Car Share 4, maybe even 5 stars. Remember the game Telephone? It's the game where one person at the end of a group of people whispers a sentence into another person's ear and when that sentence finally makes it through all of the people the message is too discombobulated to understand. I found out TWO MONTHS after this went into effect, via an OLD E-MAIL --- AT THE *BOTTOM* OF THE E-MAIL, that my free membership option had been automatically transferred to the $15/month "Philadelphia Plan". Way to kick me when I'm down in the trenches of the Great Recession, Carshare. Couldn't you have possibly done something less drastic, like maybe kept a $5 option for those who originally had the free option? That way, instead of screwing dedicated PCS members you could keep them around and STILL receive payment from customers who hadn't previously paid? Getting $5 from a bunch of people is better than nothing, but obviously you don't value your customers. Most of us already use you because we can't afford our own car, so how in the world could you be so sneaky as to pull this? I feel like every month, you steal $15 out of my wallet because that's the way the change was treated. I will still continue to use you, as I have no choice and need the service, but I am going to thoroughly research Zipcar in the very near future. text: I spent the weekend visiting a friend who lives in a surround building in the complex. Luckily her side of the building is not the side where the TV is mounted to otherwise it would have been loud but her proximity to the Piazza was welcomed. Once I saw this place I fell in love. Shops, galleries, restaurants, and bars dot the lower level and apartments rise from there. The is a mix of shop types so everyone can find something- Trickzone for kids and adults enjoying magic, Lyla has the girlies covered with cute handmade fabric pieces, Darlings has great casual food, etc. The Piazza has a welcoming feeling to it with its large TV and stage, open seating, and plenty of people relaxing with friends and their dogs. There is a weekly farmer's market on Saturday's that draws in great vendors and more people to create an active Piazza. There is a variety of products from eggs, meats, cheese, pastries, breads, and of course fruits and veggies. The Piazza is really clean and patrolled well to keep the Piazza safe. There are plenty of trash recepticals and if there is a mess it is cleaned up quickly. Adjacent free parking is a great way to draw people here. I know a food store is going to be moving in the area so I wonder how that will effect things but for now it is working.

There's nothing special about this specific location, though I have never had to wait long for a seat there, which is a nice change of pace for Outback. The servers are always friendly, and unlike a lot of places in the area, I can't ever remember being annoyed with waiters taking to long here (my biggest pet peeve is waiting for a course or the bill).

I ordered a margarita which was terrible. The crushed ice wasn't broken up enough for me to drink and I think that they skimped on the tequila. We ordered an appetizer of guacamole and chips which was delicious. I could tell that the guacamole was freshly made and it had fresh cilantro leaves in there. I then ordered steak fajitas which were terrible. The steak wasn't tender and the vegetables were overcooked. My boyfriend ordered a burrito which he liked, but he asked for no cheese and they didn't listen. Another thing I should note is that the service was poor. We were sitting upstairs and it took the waiter forever to get our drinks after we ordered them. He kept apologizing, but even if he was the only waiter there, he had no excuse because we were one of two tables. I would go back maybe for the guacamole and a corona at the bar. text: I'm fond of taking friends here for breakfast. None of them would have ever found it on their own, really, because it's practically hidden. Honestly I started coming here more when Honey's wait was too long, because it's just down the street a few blocks and the food is every bit as amazing. The place has quickly grown on me in it's own right, from the pour-it-yourself coffee, which offers variety and endless refilling to the servers who have consistently been friendly and efficient, even when it gets busy. They have a really laid back environment, and whoever picks the music has good taste. Sometimes you'll see families with kids, which normally irritates me but they have a box of toys in the corner and everyone in my experience tends to be well behaved. Another fun fact: they do food to go, and don't give you any crap whatsoever about splitting checks. They also always make it clear that even though you've finished eating, you're free to hang out and drink some more coffee, a fact I've always appreciated. And the food: so. damn. good. My last meal there was pistachio and date pancakes which were out of this world. My companion had some kind of pumpkin creme stuffed french toast, which was almost too perfect looking and tasted wonderful. I always grab a side of the homefries, too, which are well spiced and perfect with absolutely everything. I always leave feeling full and happy, and I highly recommend you try it too.

I had the huevos ranchos. The savory dish was right on the money, and unlike most of the places I have had this dish (including a few so-called authentic Mexican spots) this take actually had some welcome kick. Others in my party had equally impressive dishes. The Canolli French Toast and the Lemon Ricotta Pancakes couldnt have gotten better. I didnt believe it was possible to actually capture the taste of a South Philly canolli in french toast, but guess what? The riccotta filling, tiny chocolate chips and flaky crust did just that. As for the Lemon Ricotta pancakes- wow! Not overwhlemingly tart nor heavy with cheese, they came served with sliced strawberries and honey. Needless to say, our plates were clean. I have went to every brunch spot in greater Philadelphia. Most dont warrant a second visit. This place is a keeper.

text: The BAD.....the GOOD and the BLAH The BAD - Got there about 7:50 and was immediately seated. We counted about 18 tops to about 5 servers, 1 manager, 2 hostesses and 3 expediters, so were figured service would be great (plus what we read in the other reviews). Well we sat for about 10 minutes before anyone noticed us and brought us water. At that time the waiter stated that "the waitress that handles your table has been in the bathroom for a while". Gee thanks for that information. About 10 minutes later he came back and said he was going to help us even though this wasn't his section. We ordered drinks and heard about the specials. He came back to deliver the bread and drinks then disappeared for another 10 minutes. When he eventually came back he said "sorry but because were not in his section he forgot about us"...Gee thanks again. We placed our order and off he went. The house salad was decent and brought to our table pretty quick. We felt better until he came back as we were finishing our salad and asked what we would like to order...Huh? He said "he forgot what we ordered". We waited again - now it was becoming a joke. Since the kitchen/bar spills into the dining area we could see our food sitting....just sitting...still sitting...finally a different server asked the manager whose it was and our waiter ran over after looking at us with our bare table. He brought our food and apologized again. The GOOD - The flatbread was actually really good. If I lived in the area I would venture back to sit at the bar and try the flatbread again. The BLAH - On the first visit to any Italian restaurant I always go for the lasagna. I figure if they know how to make flavorful lasagna they know what they are doing. If not - not worth going back. While the portion was big, it was bland - almost frozen lasagna meal bland. A couple of interesting things....First in a review here they said that they bake the bread. When we mentioned that we thought the bread was a little stale from being freshly baked he said that they buy it from Provence and nothing is done in house. When we overheard the table next to us ask about the Tiramisu the waiter said they get it from a local pastry chef in Nashville. When we asked our waiter about it he said they get it from Whole Foods. Bottom line is service was terrible, food was blah at best and they need to get their facts straight about their food. The only reason for 2 stars was the flatbread.

text: The "Royal Burger" is a hot item. If you don't believe me, steer over to the write up about it on Food Network, which calls it the best burger in the state. I was hoping that my burger would be something to rave about. On paper, it sounded fantastic: bacon, caramelized onions, smoked Gouda, pickled long hot peppers, and chili mayo. The pickled long hot peppers had great taste, but they weren't strong enough to stand out with the rest of the flavors. I ordered medium rare, and it came out medium. The result was a dry burger, which wasn't even remedied by the chili mayo. I was underwhelmed by the burger. Bottom Line: Not the best burger in Philadelphia, or even South Philly. Poor service and a limited beer selection leave a lot to be desired. text: This restaurant's niche is it bills itself as a fine dining establishment that serves massive portions. What most people realize in going here is that you're basically paying for almost two platters worth of food on one plate and that the size of the appetizers and entrees is reflected in the cost. Seven Stars Inn holds an unflattering distinction as being the 2nd worst dining experience I have ever had in my life (#1 is held by a TGI Fridays). Sadly, the unbelievably bad experience had nothing to do with the food, which for the most part was pretty good, and had EVERYTHING to do with our server and the host. Just thinking about the dinner our party had here makes me angry. I should qualify this review by stating that the dining experience I'm writing about happened a while ago - before I learned about the existence of Yelp. Normally I wouldn't bother writing a review so long after the fact, but the story is so incredible and this restaurant so badly ruined what was supposed to be a special evening out (retirement celebration) that it still brings back memories for everyone that was in our dinner party. Our waitress gave our party of 8 the worst service I have ever witnessed at a "fine dining" restaurant. To start things off her demeanor was a tad cold, at least towards our table. Throughout the evening various things occurred that irked us about the service we were receiving, including receiving some drinking glasses that had large chips at the rim where you put your lips (EEK). However, nothing compares to the lack of attentiveness she gave our party. We watched during the 2+ hours we were here while she zipped around to other tables of diners refilling drinks, clearing plates, checking in to see if everything was ok. All things she was REPEATEDLY negligent in doing for our table. Not too long into our dining experience a number of us were getting annoyed at the lack of service we were receiving and we are NOT a demanding bunch. So I decided to go have a talk with the host. The host was a middle aged gentleman who sat on a stool by a podium and resembled Jesse Ventura with glasses. I told him what had happened thus far and he said that he would take care of it. About 45 minutes after my first visit to the host it was clear that nothing had changed. Our plates were not being cleared, our drinks were not being refilled, more rolls and butter were not being brought out, and all while we watched our waitress serve other tables in an efficient manner. We attempted on several occasions throughout the night to get her attention as she was walking nearby coming from other tables and unbelievably most of the time she wouldn't even look our way. On at least one ocassion she looked right at us as several of us were gesturing to get here attention and she just kept right on walking. We were dumbfouded. It was as if we were lepers. I paid my second visit to the host almost 2 hours into our dinner. Once again we had been sitting with empty dinner plates and empty drink glasses for roughly a 1/2 hour and the waitress was still ignoring our table. On this visit to the host he seemed less interested in what I was telling him and the way he responded didn't inspire confidence that anything was going to be done. A short while after my second complaint to the host the waitress finally visited our table and cleared our plates - I think this was just coincidence. She once again disappeared and now we were left sitting with no offer for coffee or a dessert menu. After 2 discreet complaints by me to the host regarding our waitress's chronic inattentiveness (among a few other things), it was clear that nothing had changed. After sitting idle for another 15 minutes we collectivley decided to just give up and end the evening early by getting the check because we didn't feel like waiting another 1/2 hour for dessert. As we walked through the foyer I paid my 3rd and final visit to the host. I told him that I wanted him to know that we got tired of waiting for our server and were so disappointed with our service that we decided to skip dessert and just leave. I also mentioned to him that my comments to him had changed nothing and that our waitress had been ignoring us all evening. His reply to me was a flippant, "we'll make it up to you next time." I was so flabbergasted at his response to me that I just walked away. My thought and what I should have said to him was "Oh really? How are you going to do that, by giving us the service we should have received tonight on our next visit?", but I was left speechless by his response. So this is the type of service you can expect from a $400 night out at a restaurant that bills itself as fine dining!?! As someone who eats out often I realize that any restaurant can have an off night but that wasn't the case here. This was blissful ignorance, lack of courtesy and blatant disregard for the customer. No one in our party of 8 has ever gone to this restaurant since.
label: NEG

text: Caves to spelunk, vines for the swinging, cliffs to jump, G.P.S. treasures to hunt, trails to trek, creeks to fish, ford, and launch your dead pet's funeral boats upon... Wissahickon has it all. Thick with lush vegetation and active with local wildlife, from Valley Green's resident flocks of fowl to Wissahickon transfer center's opening day waterfall fishery, this park is a prime destination spot year round. Whether you're horseback riding, biking through the hills (with permit), skiing down the ever prevalent slopes after a snowfall, or just ambling along on a warm spring constitutional, you'll not find a more beautiful and natural place in Philadelphia. As a Roxborough native, this was practically my personal play pen growing up, but even fresh faces will become enamored. Next time the sun is out, grab your comfy foot gear, forage for a walking/beat off the crazies stick, and get back to nature only minutes from center city, just watch out for those horse apples. There are also cool historic things back the Crick (how I've always referred to it), like an old time paper mill (still operating for touring purposes), the finger bridge and covered bridge, a statue or two, some ancient looking ranger houses, and informative plaques randomly scattered throughout. Some of the Public Parking: http://maps.google.com/maps/ms?ie=UTF&msa=0&msid=210485173569154004813.0004ab1a442bac0939b52 Some (but by no means all) spots worth checking out: http://maps.google.com/maps/ms?ie=UTF&msa=0&msid=210485173569154004813.0004aadd7a2e577157193

text: I've been eating here for twenty years, since Chef Giuseppe Rosselli hung his "Good Food" sign over the door. Those were great times for Olde City, and this restaurant literally sparked one of the greatest cultural explosions in the city. Locanda was the first restaurant on this strip of 3rd St. when it first opened. After one review in the newspaper, people caught wind of the place, and there's been a line out the door ever since. I've literally grown up with this place. My mom and dad would take my sisters and I in our teens, and I try to go as much as possible to this day. Chef Giuseppe is no longer with us, but his legacy lives on in the attention to detail in both the food and the service here. His wife and sons still run Locanda, and it's as if Giuseppe is still with us. The mushroom crepes are always great to start off with, the Fruiti di Mare never lets down, the Ricotta Gnocchis are killer, and even though these are my usual orders, the specials never let me down. Whether they have lamb chops in red wine sauce, a big juicy steak with a blueberry reduction, Chilean Sea Bass perfectly cooked and accessorized, or perfectly prepared Rabbit, the specials are beyond ordinary and beyond satisfying. The head waiter, Joe, is the most loveable guy you'll meet. Yeah, sure, he's loud and can sometimes seem pushy, but it's only because he feels as if all of the customers are his family. I don't know him very well, but I can tell that he feels this way. I've eaten here on plenty of dates, as well as plenty of large parties. I've personally booked a couple large parties, and have come away feeling as if I had received preferential treatment each time. I can say nothing bad about Locanda, and only wish I could visit more often. I've read a few reviews stating that the place is expensive, but trust me, it's not. And if you book a larger party, the prices are seriously some of the lowest you'd find in any restaurant in all of Philly. So, if you like to feel as if you're at a family gathering, and you don't want to break the bank, you will not be let down by the people and the food here.

I have a home espresso machine that get's a workout often, I was an employee of Starbucks before the sell-out when there were just five, yes five, of them in the world and set the standards for Pete's and the rest of coffee in America. More recently, I lived in coffee mad Portland, OR and watched people become obsessed with the 'art' on the foam of their cups of coffee and drink under-roasted varietal beans instead of masterfully blended full-city which I believe is the peak of the art. I have pulled 10s of thousand of shots of espresso on commercial machines, drunk 1000s of gallons of French press brew, sampled coffee on five continents and 46 states of the Union. Blah Blah Blah. Even after all of this, Raging sage is my bean purveyor of choice ANYWHERE in the world. If you drink COFFEE (no, a mint mocha soy ice coffee is not COFFEE) order it black; an Americano, esspresso, etc. and you will be very happy at the Sage. As for the cafe, I can't say I am a huge fan. It's cramped, the loo is pretty much hidden, the service is average, there's no wi-fi, parking sucks, but the pastry is above average. The outside seating is pretty cool, but really, just go there for the beans, stock up and go on your merry way.

I've never had anything there that I thought was awful (well, there are these dumpling things I thought were not so wonderful, but maybe they were having an off day). My most favorite things at Rangoon are the ginger salad and the thousand layer bread with coconut sauce. So wonderful. So good. Always. I've never had bad thousand layer bread. Furthermore, I've never had bad service, which is very important to me. I ate there last night and our server was very sweet, gracious, and attentive. I'm not wild about the remodel. The space feels a little less personal and I miss all those wonderful paintings. But the minimalist approach does give it a very clean look. All in all, the food is good, often great (but no guarantees!).. text: I was in a serious need for some hearty food yesterday and I could not think of a better hearty food than a Pi deep dish pizza. Having read many reviews on here about the door issue we navigated our way around to the correct door and find the hostess. Being the beautiful day that it was Stephanie B and I opted to sit outside and enjoy the nice weather. We were quickly seated and our server showed up just as quickly. On a whim, we ordered some wings since we knew a deep dish would take a bit longer than normal to cook. This was my only regret about my recent visit to Pi. I won't say they were bad, they just were not good. They definitely were not hot wings, the skin was left on the wings I'm assuming on purpose, but it was a big detractor for me. I love chicken wings, and I left a couple on the plate if that tells you anything. But, I didn't come to Pi for their wings, I came for their pie. None of the deep dish specialty pies on the menu really caught out eye, so we opted to make our own. We went with a peperoni, sausage, salami and roasted garlic deep dish. Man, was it tasty. The cornmeal crust is amazing, never thought I would like a cornmeal crust on a pizza, but it works really well. The pizza sauce is like none I have ever had before, sweet with just a little tang to it with chunks of tomatoes. I don't think my son would like this pizza, but I loved it. It sounds like I'm a huge fan of Pi, so why only 4 stars? Well, the wings had a little something to do with that, but the price also has something to do with it. Over $40 for a 12" deep dish and order of wings seemed a bit steep to me, but it is a pretty mean pie so I think it's probably worth it. Just not an indulgence that I will partake in too regularly.

text: WOW. My last review was for another favorite pizza place in the city. Theirs was a solid triple, but Dock Street has just knocked one out of the park. The food was unbelievable! We started with the Trio fries -- white and sweet potatoes with leeks. I love me some sweet potato fries, and the leeks just sealed the deal on this one. Then the pizza...so many delicious pies to choose from. We ordered two of their 10" individuals ($8-$9 ea.) to split: the Flammenkuche (caramelized onion, apple smoked bacon, gruyere, creme fraiche, fresh thyme) and the Florentine (creme fraiche, spinach, sliced tomato, leeks, fresh herbs, mozzarella). The crust is thin, slight char, but not TOO crunchy. Perfection. My mouth is watering just thinking about the leftover slices in my fridge. The caramelized onions were unbelievable. Vegetable candy, how can you go wrong? As for the beer: the Saison was soft, not overly hoppy. It was nice, though I prefer Victory's Saison Du Buff (a little more body). Dock Street's Hop Garden Double IPA packs a serious wallop! I'm anxious to try their Rye IPA. Our server was friendly and attentive when we arrived, and then let us linger without hovering, very nice. The place was pretty empty when we got there and took a table by the window, but a few hours later it was packed. Definitely louder at that point (big open room with high ceilings) but we didn't have any trouble carrying on a conversation. GREAT food, great price. Dock Street, I will be back!

We were first in the door and only two other tables were filled by the time we left. Not a particularly good sign for this churrascaria. There are, sadly, plenty of reasons to avoid Cafe Brasil. The fruit flies are pretty high on my list. If I'm not enjoying a picnic outside, I generally don't enjoy swatting bugs away from my food and drink throughout an entire meal. If I was dealing with four fruit flies at my table alone (and I was actively engaged in battle with them), I'd hate to see the unattended buffet. Yikes. I also wasn't really impressed by the service, which was surprisingly inattentive and slow (we were practically the only people there!). Our waiter was far more interested in strumming a little ukulele guitar thing to the piped-in music than he was in checking up on us or refilling our glasses. The atmosphere of the restaurant didn't really do anything for me and it seemed especially dreary without any other customers around. I was sort of saddened by the whole thing. The food, luckily, was not as sad and dreary as most everything else. Justin really, really enjoyed his feijoada (black beans cooked with sirloin, bacon and sausage), although he did surmise that the sausages were like, packaged breakfast links or something. Still, he liked it. I had the peixada, cod with coconut milk, palm oil and fresh herbs. The serving was large and the fish was good--not as flavorful or complex as I thought it might be, but it was good. I don't think either dish was worth the price, which averaged about $20 each, but luckily we had a buy one/get one entree coupon. Was it an off night at Cafe Brasil? I'm not sure. I'd heard some good things about the place and it IS pretty huge, so I hope for their sake they fill up somewhat regularly, but it really fell flat for me. If you do decide to give them a shot, at least heed this piece of advice: do not, under any circumstances, order the special Brazilian red wine drink mixed with condensed milk. Just don't. I don't know what I was thinking; I must've been tricked by the menu's assertion that "you will be surprised!" I was surprised, alright. Won't fall for that one again...

text: I got a Groupon for this bakery and decided to try it out. I bought 4 items on my first trip (and all within the limits of my $10 Groupon!) I got a specialty pastry called a "marjolaine," a chocolate/chocolate cupcake, a hazelnut cake slice, and a complimentary double chocolate brownie-cookie drop with vanilla glaze (because I actually came a little under the $10 and they wanted to make up for it.) Very friendly service from the one woman I dealt with on a Thursday afternoon. I ate the cookie first. Very "meh." It was dry except for the embedded chocolate chips. You can make much better at home using the Baker's Chocolate Drops recipe found on the back of their unsweetened baking chocolate, very easy to do, just add a generic confectioners glaze. Next I tried their specialty marjolaine, priced at $4.99, so I expected it to be good. This is a four layer hazelnut meringue filled with hazelnut and chocolate cream, a bit of jam, and covered with a chocolate glaze. Again, I was underwhelmed and had a hard time pinpointing why. Ultimately, I found it to be too rich and too sweet (half a slice made me sick to my stomach) but without a whole lot of actual flavor. The chocolate glaze quality was pretty good though. Next I tried the cupcake. And I found myself asking, what do the following have in common: 1. Sahara 2. Mohave 3. Death Valley 4. This cupcake You guessed it - dry dry dry! And the frosting was airy nothingness. I threw part of it away. Why do people bother to make cupcakes that aren't moist yumminess? If you want cupcakes, go to Brown Betty. End of story. Finally, the hazelnut cake square. Again, a lot of airy sweet nothingness, very unsatisfying. (In fact, the bakery box, when it held just the cupcake and cake square, weighed almost nothing. I guess a few hours passed and I started getting tired of playing games. I sat down in the Pole Position machine and took a nap. During that time, my father, the Reno police, hotel security and anybody else they could find were blanketing the property trying to find me. When they found me, it was too late. My mother already knew about it. I can only imagine what she did to my Dad when we got back from the trip. :) Since then, I have been back a few times, including once last week. The place hasn't changed. It is really an odd spot. Even the parking garage is weird. If I am going to spend any time in downtown Reno, I prefer the Silver Legacy, but I usually stop in here to reminisce for a minute about the crazy scandal that was discussed throughout my childhood.

text: All pizza suffers when forced to spend time in a cardboard box, but that mainly effects the crust, and the crust was fine. It was the toppings that didn't please. A guest commented that it was like eating cottage cheese piled on a pizza crust. The No Cheese was *loaded* with great veggies (a plus), but the seasoning -- although pronounced -- was bland. It was as if, equipped with only a limited palette of seasoning, more was added to compensate for the missing meat and cheese. This happens often with veggie alternatives created and executed by non-vegetarians. The Pepperoni/Spinach/Jalapeño was the best of the lot and the jalapeños packed a whallop. It was quite greasy, a problem I overcame by topping the meaty slice with a slice of the veggie-loaded No Cheese pizza -- creating a kind of Calzone-marriage between vegan and carnivore pizza. The solution tasted great, but need I call upon my ingenuity to eat pizza? Pizza is eaten precisely to avoid having to be clever about meal preparation! Normally I'd offer to give this place another chance, but as of this Sunday morning, I just don't feel like it.

text: The best meal I have had in New Orleans was here at Cochon. The wait time here can be considerable so do yourself a favor and make reservations. Things quickly improved as we got the fried alligator with chili garlic aioli. I had never had alligator before and it is a tough meat. Otherwise it was pretty good. Next was pork & black eyed pea gumbo which was also really good. The gumbo had a great texture and the pork was mighty tender. The food just got better and better. Next came the spicy grilled pork ribs with watermelon pickle. Oh my was this divine. Sweet, a bit spicy, a little smokey with some tangy from the watermelon pickle. At this point the server noticed I hadn't touched my pretty bad cocktail and so they offered to change it with something else. Can't remember exactly what it was. It whiskey based and an improvement, but not a great cocktail. The final dish was rabbit & dumplings. I salivate even now reminiscing about this fine dish. It is like a thick stew with biscuit like dumplings on top. It is got some great spices and hearty texture to it. Just a superb dish. Excellent service and fantastic food, I would stay away from the cocktails but you simply must have a meal here.

text: A bit of a drive from L.A. for a concert but if you live nearby or can stay with a friend to minimize the long drive home, this is the best concert venue! First, it's small but because it's an outdoor amphitheater it is at once spacious and intimate. Every seat offers an amazing view of the stage. We could see Thom Yorke playing piano even while sitting down and looking through people standing in front of us. Amazing! Also because of the size, the sound is fantastic. Not too loud -- you can still talk in between songs -- and without any echo or delay. Second, it's just lovely. Built in rustic wood and stone, it's a beautiful venue. Surrounded by towering trees and open the stars, it offers a view of downtown Santa Barbara twinkling below and beyond that, the ocean. I mean, come on! Third, it's a well-run venue. The drink lines were long but moved quickly. People were friendly. No line-cutting or toe-stepping. The gals serving were super nice and the drinks were actually a decent price: $6 for a Stella Artois and $2 for a bottle of water! A few tips: 1) There's plenty of street parking if you want to walk to/from the venue. It was actually quite nice to stroll through the quiet streets after the concert. 2) There are so many restrooms! What a god send to never have to wait. After the concert there was actually a line forming because no one realized there were a dozen empty stalls. 3) There's a tunnel underneath the stage where the restrooms are. We exited that way and it log-jammed at the other end where people were coming against the tide to get to the restrooms. Next time I would probably exit the main way but even so, it took only ten minutes to leave, easy! 4) To order drinks you need to have a wristband but that's another line to stand in -- although it moves quickly. If you clearly look old enough, I wouldn't bother with it. No one checked. 5) Make sure you leave plenty of time to get there as the 101 can easily back up after Ventura, doubling or tripling the usual drive time. I can't wait to come back. What a great night!

text: The Cannery Ballroom is the Mercy Lounge's, less cool younger sibling, the kind that can be a pretentious know it all who feels like they have something to prove because you've experienced everything before them. Although they're owned and run by the same people, and literally situated next door to each other, the Cannery lacks a lot of the atmosphere that makes the Mercy Lounge so fantastic. It is a much larger space, actually the only one if its size left in Nashville. It books bigger bands there, and a lot of times if shows at the Mercy Lounge sell out too quickly they'll transfer them over to the Cannery. The first reason the Cannery doesn't really do it for me is its layout. The stage is built kind of around a corner from the rest of the venue, so visibility to the stage isn't that great unless you're standing within 20 feet of it, which is also where everyone else wants to be. There's a huge amounted of space with everyone cramming into a small fraction of it so they can see the stage, and this makes for an evening of constantly jostling and fighting over the spot your feet are planted. The acoustics are alright, not the best sound in Nashville but not the worst. The bar is huge and it's usually pretty easy to grab a beer or a cocktail there, but it lacks the charm that the Mercy Lounge has. I tend to only visit the Cannery if it's a once in a lifetime performance going on there, or if I'd already bought a ticket to the Mercy Lounge before they transferred the show over (usually then I show up with a chip on my shoulder feeling like I've been tricked out of a good time). It's one of those places where you have to wait in long lines to get in, fight for your viewing spot, wait in longer lines for the bathroom and then fight to get out of the place when it's time to leave. If waiting and fighting don't factor into your idea of a great night out on the town then I'd skip this place.

text: With the staggering array of small, proprietor-run restaurants in Philadelphia, I've always considered Stephen Starr properties a nice convenience and diversion, but not necessarily my favorites. The theme-park quality of most Starr venues is fun, but at times lacks gravitas or authenticity. Still, the service is usually extremely pleasant and effective; I've rarely had a bad service experience in a Starr property. One night, having just about finished dinner at El Rey, our waiter asked us if we'd like to try out the new place in the back. He implied that it was somewhat exclusive and private and unusual. We had seen a party of diners exit through the kitchen earlier, and this explained the strange sighting (again, think "theme park" ). We paid our check and were escorted through the kitchen, through the back kitchen entrance and presented at a dark door. We entered and were approached by an employee. We were told that there were not seats for us at the moment, but that there may be some available soon. Then - this is incredible - the employee asked us to wait out back. He explained that they were trying to achieve a certain atmosphere and that standing was not permitted. I explained that we were invited by staff, that we would be happy to wait, but that we would not be waiting on the kitchen stairs. This intensely rude person said "I don't care where you wait, but you can't wait here." I quietly asked to see the manager. The rude employee told me that the manager would say the same thing. Now I'm annoyed. I said "OK, just get the manager now, thanks." Against my better judgment and will we waited on the kitchen stairs for the manager. I must note that the manager was extremely pleasant and apologized. She explained that we should have never been invited back by our El Rey server unless seats were available. I replied that it was irrelevant, and that you don't invite someone to your "special new bar" and then ask that person to wait on the kitchen stairs. I was offered promises of free food or drink, and I politely declined. Contriving scarcity is an old economic manipulation trick, tried and true. But do they really expect people to wait on the kitchen stairs to go to a Stephen Starr property? Spend your money wisely, and walk around the corner to any one of the many hotel bars, fine-dining establishments, tavern, cheater's bars, sports bars or dives and avoid this silly place with abysmally rude, ill-mannered, narcissistic, clueless employees. Franklin Mortgage achieves the same vibe with zero attitude.

I got to the gate and they said our little commuter jet was undergoing maintenance and it would be 10 minutes. 10 minutes later "we're sorry folks, just another 10 minutes" An hour later, we finally board the plane, but we were forced to sit at the gate because every 10 minutes they would say "10 more minutes" We switched gates 4 times and I half-heartedly tried to search for savory breakfast food that was not dripping in grease. Alas, I was unable to find anything appetizing and the only things available were too sweet pastries at Au Bon Pain. Not even a Starbucks in Terminal E, (and though I don't like Starbucks in general, the option would have been nice). The bathrooms are kind of gross (even at 6am, when they should be clean) and the numerous gate changes and lack of departure screens makes for an interesting experience. I hate airports in general, but I really saw no point in flying through here (and I probably won't in the future given my renewed hatred of US Airways) And I did all this while groggily trying to shake my Benadryl induced drowsiness. Lovely time, really.

text: Absolutely the worst restaurant steak I have ever had. I'm not even going to waste my time with saying anything more than that. I wrote the above statement a few days prior to today's date (11/26/10). Upon reflection, I've decided that the above statement is not particularly useful, although I still maintain that it is accurate. Allow me to explain further. I know that Charlie's is (inexplicably) a beloved New Orleans establishment. While this is often enough for other mediocre local establishments to maintain a client base (cf. Galatoire's), said other mediocre local establishments normally have SOMETHING worthwhile to offer in the way of cuisine. Not so with Charlie's. Let's talk about the steaks. I had the largest T-Bone that Charlie's offered...my friend had some form of gigantic steak that was, I believe, a ribeye. Having not tried his steak, I can only speak about my own. I get my steaks cooked rare, and this has never been a problem for any other steakhouse in the city. The steak was presented to me on a metal plate and I immediately noticed an inordinate amount of fat on the cut. Worse still, the meat seemed as though it were barely cooked. It was not seared in the least. My suspicions were confirmed when I cut the meat, to discover that it was cold (COLD) in the center. I do not know with certainty what grade of meat the proprietors of Charlie's purchase; however, I do know that it tasted akin to something that one might purchase at Winn-Dixie, or perhaps even Wal-Mart. Perhaps most disturbing, however, is that despite the total lack of quality inherent in my meal, I would have thought that I was actually at Ruth's Chris by virtue of the bill. And that's the thing...I do not go out of my way to bash local restaurants. However, the quality of the food was SO bad, and the cost of the food was SO high that I feel like I need to warn those who haven't been to Charlie's yet. Don't go. Just don't. If you are one of those people who (understandably) cannot bring them selves to eat at Ruth's Chris post-Katrina, that's fine. Might I recommend Dickie Brennan's, then? Or, if you want a steak, and don't necessarily need to eat one in a proper steakhouse, Lillette's hanger steak is absolutely delicious. So, that's that. Bad. Bad, bad, bad.

text: I live a block away from Hot Potato and have waited a long time to go and try them out. Today I finally made the plunge and ordered a takeout lunch for my brother and I. We got the Philly Cheesesteak baked potato, traditional baked potato and the Philly Cheesesteak spring rolls. The order was ready quickly, within 15 mins. and when my brother arrived to pick it up it was waiting for him. The Philly Cheesesteak springrolls were an original and we both liked them. They were served with ketchup and what my brother guessed was some type of thickened potato soup as a sauce. Original and tasty. Unfortunately that is basically where the good part of the experience ended. The potatoes had tough spots in them where the potato was completely cooked. The traditional potato had no butter on it and was quite dry with some bacon and cheese sprinkled on it and a small spoonful of sour cream on the side of it. I had to add butter to even be able to eat it. My brother's Philly Cheesesteak potato was also dry and while he said the cheesesteak topping was ok, he didn't care for the potato. For a restaurant that centers it's menu around the potato, it isn't doing a very good job. I understand that Gordan Ramsey was there not long ago to do a makeover. If this is a makeover, I'm certainly glad I didn't try it before. I might try the restaurant again, but only if I was to eat in, for takeout it is not good at all.
label: NEG

text: This was a delicious little number, located right inside Longwood gardens. Guess what the views were? You guessed right, flowers, trees and more flowers. The food is unusually delicious for restaurants on property like this. I had a mushroom strudel along with some of the best cream of mushroom suop I have ever had, while my hubby had a homemade chicken pot pie that was loaded with tender chicken and fresh veggies all covered with a buttery and flaky crust. They had a pumpkin filled pasta, that I may try on my next trip around. Nice wine list, including local wines and you are in mushroom country and they know how to perfect dishes using them. They also offer The Cafe, where you can pick and choose your own foods, pay for them and then sit down to enjoy.

text: Small, fast-paced and South Philly family-run. These are some damn good bagels. When I use to stop here before work to get bagels for the office, I would always grab a couple of their French toast bagels (powdered sugar and maple syrup infused!). text: I attended a convention at the Gaylord Opryland recently. It was a huge location with with large meeting areas and several private meeting rooms dispersed through out the hotel. One of the key reasons I believe the hotel was chosen is because it would contain the parties and festivities, meaning people wouldn't be hung over for the morning seminars. I have to say this seemed to work out quite well as most people were up bright and early in the morning. One of the challenges of the location was the immense size and pathways throughout the facility. Many of our party got lost throughout the week. Getting lost isn't necessarily a bad thing as most of the open atrium type areas were filled with waterfalls and healthy plant life, making great views both day and night. The spa it self was quite relaxing. I got a great massage which was perfect for relieving stress. That said it was probably one of the more expensive massages I've had. $160 after tip. I'd probably visit Opryland again for a conference, but I don't think I'd head back on my own. The majority of the dinning was good ole American food. (Think fried, heavy and saturated with fat.) Did I mention it was also over priced? The best place to eat in the facility is the Irish Pub. They actually have pretty decent food there.

text: I've been to Paradiso a few times over the past 4 or so years, but this is the first time I actually felt disappointed. It was the end of a long day, I was tired, and did not appreciate waiting that long on a transaction that should take no longer than 5 minutes. Foodwise I was a little disappointed as well. I ordered the pappardelle, which I usually find delicious- unfortunately, this time the noodles were dry and some were stuck together. Likewise, the fried zucchini blossoms, which I have enjoyed in the past, were greasy rather than crispy. There are a ton of great Italian restaurants in South Philadelphia, and so, I probably won't go back to Paradiso. It's a shame.

text: I ate at Jazz a week ago, and was pleasantly surprised. I haven't ever been to New Orleans, but this place will give you the essence of being there in a Disney Land type of way. It was clean, and still had the new car smell. I give new restaurants a lot of lee way for service and food quality, but the day we showed up everything was fine. We ordered the chicken wings ($.50 each on Wednesdays), and considering myself a connoisseur of chicken wings, I was very happy with them! You can ask them to make them extra spicy, which is a good idea, as the regular are kinda wimpy. I wasn't in love with my entree, the Louisiana shrimp; it was too saucy with out a lot of substance. My rating was based on the skill of the deep fryer; he did an amazing job on everything that was deep fried. The wings, crawfish, catfish, shrimp and oysters were all cooked to perfection! Crisp and light, while still succulent on the inside. Keep that guy around Jazz! Be warned, with all new restaurants quality will vary as the chefs learn their stations... Long story short 3 out of 4 entrees were great, the appetizers during happy hour were $4.99 and worth every penny, the wings were fantastic and a great price at $.50 each on Wednesdays... and the place was clean with a decent staff. At my age with a 20 month old daughter I prefer the Disney Land Experience to the Bourbon Street experience, but your taste may vary (sorry no flashing from coeds while I was there)! The downers were my entree (the Louisiana Shrimp) and the bread you get when you arrive (big time blah).
label: NEG

text: I wanted to write the review while everything was fresh in my head. So, i grew up in Clearwater, but i moved out of clearwater as soon as i graduated from high school. Being in my early 30s and having lived in NC, Asia, and NYC (i am a current resident of NYC), I expected this place to be a drab. Got together with my high school friends (yes after 14 years) and decided to go out. First of all, we went on a ladies night -- so there was no cover for us, but if i had to pay a cover charge, i might have been a little upset. The valet parking (and it is nearly impossible to find non-valet) was $5 - why should you have to pay for parking in CLEARWATER/St. Pete? we are not in the city. Drinks were free until midnight - but they poured barely any alcohol in mixed drinks. We got to the place right around 11pm and the place was pretty empty. Well, now to the good things or rather, positive. The bartenders were cute - they are all girls, but from the girl's perspective, they were cute and classy., Because the club is known to be a little more classy than ybor, there were more older people than not. We were all in our early 30s and we didn't feel old. There were plenty of older folks and of course younger mid-late 20s. The decor is fancy; they have big screen tvs everywhere; and the bathrooms were great - though you have to tip the attendants. If you are girl and straighten your hair - in the middle of the night you'll find your hair getting frizzy. Don't worry, the bathroom has a flat iron - for about $2 per use. Other than the facility, the music was great until 1am. at 1 am, the music turned WEIRD and techno on us. People watching is the best. From the second floor, you can see what the crowd is doing on the first floor. This is a MUST. It is hilarious. We danced, sang along, took lots of pictures, drank, and had a blast watching people. This is a place to check out if you are in clearwater/st pete and want to go out for low key fun. Not a place to seek out or for which you go out of your way.
label: NEG

text: I've been here many times and usually things go well. Usually, the food is fine. I can tell you that the walnut and roasted mushroom salad has always been outstanding! When I order a glass of wine, I appreciate it when the glass clean and free of lime residue and rinse water. text: Phenomenal drinks, terrible service. I had the "Jennings," which was a fantastic whiskey drink, and since I was in the mood, probably worth the $12 price tag. So go to this place if you want good drinks. My problem is their service. They seem to have this sense that because it's such a chic place and there's a line out the door on Saturday nights they can serve you when they feel like it. My friend and I sat down and sat there for 20 minutes (after waiting in line for at least 20 or 30) without getting served. We figured if we were going to pay almost $15 for a drink, we should get some service. So we left and came back later in the night when it was less crowded. The problem here is the house rules. Essentially, they are there to maintain this as a 'high-class' establishment, whatever that means. Among the most absurd are 1) Men aren't allowed to talk to women they do not know, 2) No standing at the bar. Now, I get it, they don't want the atmosphere to turn 'clubby.' But really, who are you kidding, Patterson House? This is Nashville we're talking about here, not New York or Chicago. Also, it really wouldn't be so bad if it weren't for the staff's rude behavior, like you are only there by their good graces. Patterson House puts the P in Pretentious. So, come to Patterson House if you want a little attitude with your delicious $12 cocktail.

text: Friends from all over the country were in town for the week, and we spent a day in New Hope soaking up some awesome weather and being tourists. One of my friends had done some insane itinerary planning from afar, and we all agreed The Landing looked like the restaurant to blow our money at in New Hope. We arrived just after noon, and an under-dressed and cold hostess (I'm a hostess and nothing irks me more than an unprofessional hostess) informed us there were no riverside tables available and seated us in the middle of the deck. The menu was sorta all over the place, a hodgepodge of cuisines. I didn't want a sandwich, but a lot of the appetizers and salads sounded appealing. We got the octopus salad, which was delicious. Simple dressing, yummy greens and nicely grilled octopus. Not nearly enough octopus for the $13 they were charging for it, but at least it was tasty. The nachos were pretty pricy, pretty small, and pretty meh. The calamari was overbreaded and overfried, no good. And the lobster ravioli in a lobster sauce, not cheap at $23, was downright awful. I couldn't make out anything in the dish that even remotely resembled lobster. The flavor of each individual component - the sauce, the filling, the pasta - was all just terrible. I'm never one to send food back, but at that price, it had to go back. Our server wasn't terribly attentive, and forgot that I'd asked to look at a dessert menu. I was fine with that, though, because as soon as the words spilled out of my mouth I realized I was ready to move on, anyhow. The wine was cheap and decent, no complaints there. And the view was gorgeous. Two stars for view, small octopus and wine. I would go back here just for wine and salad IF I could get a seat on the water. I would save the majority of my appetite for elsewhere.
label: NEG
