With the parade over and the streets re-opened, we learned, when we called for the shuttle, that we had been abandoned nearly a mile from the hotel. Because we were a large group, we decided we could walk back safely through the seedy area that surrounds the hotel. We did. This bad experience should not reflect on the concierge and shuttle services, which were good, but only on management. Did I mention the seedy area that surrounds the hotel? Hotel security advises against walking in the area after dark, despite the fact that the hotel remains a headquarters for the Louisiana National Guard, which, two or three years post-Katrina, is still patrolling the streets of the city. text: This bookstore really is amazing. I was in Olde City the other day and went to another used book store and nothing compares to this place. A House of Our Own is well organized, has a collection of both new books and used books. The interior of the store is beautiful and the collection has some amazing books. New books are on the first floor and used books are on the second floor. To follow up on what Viv C. said, this book store is not for the "regular consumer." For those people God created chain bookstores. For everyone else that is looking for inspiration or a copy of a classic that is actually a first edition or out of print, check this place out. What I found really great was the quality of the used books. Unlike many used bookstores, this place tries to avoid stocking "junk books" (e.g. Danielle Steele and her ilk) as well as all those self-help books. In addition, I didn't see many "how-to" books with really antiquated information (e.g. Windows 3.1 for Dummies). Their standards for what they shelve seems to be very high. Yes, books are grouped by academic subject matter then alphabetically by author. This is something to be excited about seeing as how most used bookstores are barely alphabetized! And the book store is on the UPENN campus, so wouldn't you expect this place would cater to its main consumer, the student? This place has been in business since 1971. When you walk through this old brownstone building, you'll truly be inspired and it will make you realize why the printed book probably will never be replaced by digital texts.

text: Who knew? We walked into a retail wine store and came out having one of the best meals of the year. Visiting Tucson, I wanted a bottle of wine...something decent. I googled "best wine shop tucson" and the result was The RumRunner. We headed over and picked up a bottle of Numanthia but also discovered a tiny little restaurant tucked inside called "The Dish." Four tables and a counter with a nice ambiance. We had a quick look a the menu and it seemed right up our alley. The next night we went back for dinner and were blown away. The chef, Martin Sindells, an Australian living in Tucson, has got something special going on here. As is frequently our preference, we sat at the bar and spoke with Doug, the wine master and our server. Great guy, very knowledgeable and friendly. We started with openers...Baked Miti Crema with marcona almond crumble, heirloom tomato confit and black olive rusks. The Miti is a sheep cheese and I've never been served warm sheep cheese. This was flat out awesome but only to be outdone by the other opener, Pulled Pork and Duck Duet with peppered gyoza, fresh sheep milk cheese, pinot noir braised red grapes and baby french radish insalata. Best opener of the year. A bottle of Numanthia Termes was opened. On a sidebar I should also note that the wine list is literally the entire retail store...grab a bottle and pay only retail price with essentially a twelve dollar corkage fee. Awesome deal. I've never seen anything like this before. Entrees arrived soon. We had a Duck Confit with forbidden rice, matchstick carrots, bok choy, shiitake eggroll and black plum and pomegranate glaze. The other entree was Sicilian Braised Beef Rib with chipotle yam fries, sauteed arugula, orange zest and jus de braiser. Both were spectacular. The yam fries came with a blue cheese aioli. I might have chosen a horseradish version but nonetheless the meal was awesome. We couldn't finish our plates so the dessert menu was just a quick, though thoroughly tempting, read. The fact that this place can flourish in the dessert with a tiny staff, no marketing and no stand-alone location says a lot. The place was packed both times we visited. The folks working here have a bright future whether in Tucson or any place they choose to work. This is restauranting at it's best. Highest recommendation.

text: Although it boasts two rooms, this shop isn't much larger than the ad they run in the St. Petersburg Times, which is how I discovered it. Still, they creatively have managed to ultilize every last square inch of space, stocking shelves, counters, nooks, and crannies with delectable Pennyslvania Dutch foodstuffs and attractive gift items. A refrigerated case is filled with a seemingly endless array of meats - a wide variety of bolognas and sausages, kielbasa and franks, and smoked baked ham - cheeses, including a rich Amish Swiss and a super-sharp white cheddar, and salads, such as pickled beets with eggs and pepper cabbage with a heady dressing. You'll find jars of apple butter, pickles and relishes, jams and preserves, candies like licorice sticks, sassafras drops, and peanut brittle, bottles of molasses and maple syrup, bags of potato chips and pretzels, and boxes filled with mixes for shoofly pie, funnel cake, and pancakes. Barrels are filled with bulk items such as pearl tapioca, noodles, spices, oats, and dried fruits. Non-edible merchandise includes cookbooks, tablecloths and napkins, tea towels, pot holders and aprons, hand-crafted dolls, rugs, and brooms, homemade soaps, and wind chimes. Tucked away on a side street and out-of-view from the main drag, they rely heavily on word-of-mouth, repeat business, and that tiny ad. Unique stock and reasonable prices have lured the crowds since 1997. If the sausage I'm preparing for dinner is as good as the cheese and slaw I had for lunch, I'll be a regular for however long I remain in the area.

text: This Home Depot is just 7 minutes from my house, so it is where I usually shop. Always clean, team members (who are also encouraged to volunteer in the community) usually ask if you need assistance, returns are easy (with receipt). Here's why I really like the place: -They offer compact florescent bulb recycling (in a display, near the returns desk) CF bulbs contain mercury, and should not be landfilled. -Garden Center items have a 1 yr warranty. Just save your receipt and bring in the plant for a merchandise credit -Sign up for the "Garden Club" for special e-mail coupons -I'm frugal, so I love to shop the clearance plant section. You can find perennials as low as $1.97. I shop often just to see what is marked down. UPDATE: Rake I bought this spring broke (don't buy a plastic leaf rake!) Looked for the receipt, couldn't find. On my last visit, I asked and thye said they could look up a receipt with the credit card. So tried that. No luck. Associate said, "Would you like a store credit instead?" I said "Sure!". And (and they apologized for rake breaking) within seconds she had finished the return. So easy returns without a receipt as well!

text: On my first trip to Nashville I never got out of the hotel. So on my most recent visit I was determined to see a little more than just a hotel room. I knew nothing about Nashville, where to go, where to eat, where to hear some good music. Fortunately one of the people that I was with had family in Nashville and told us to go to The Bluebird Cafe because a friend was playing that evening. After a long day at a trade show, busting out of the hotel for some music sounded great. No one knew what to expect. When we pulled up, the cafe was packed. It was standing room only for a while but we eventually found some seats. The Bluebird Cafe is tiny, but they cram people in there, and for good reason. Monday night was singer/songwriter night. Those trying to make their mark and those that just wanted to sing their song were singing that night...from 13 years old to 85 years old everyone was very talented. We don't have anything like this in Dallas. Once the singer/songwriter show was over the Mike Henderson Band came on and they were the best blues band I have seen...that was my church for the week. Our server was great always making sure we had everything we needed. The food was nothing special but I don't see The Bluebird Cafe as a place to go for dinner, more of a place to see some good music and just get a bite. I'd recommend The Bluebird Cafe to anyone, I just wish we had something like this in Dallas.
label: POS

text: I went here twice sometime last year. It's a great restaurant for comfort food. I always get the mac&cheese because I'm a huge fan and nobody makes it like Jones makes it. We reserved dough for 4 pies and got the margherita, spinach and tomato, and 2 regular. IT WAS SO GOOD. I burnt my mouth a few times because I am too impatient, but it was worth the pain. text: This place is AWESOME!!!!!! Once my little niece was born, it was all I could do not to spend the rest of my student loan money on the little terror....when I found this store right down the street from my house, it got even harder. They have everything you could ever want from clothes for baby, clothes for mom, car seats, books, and of course, those amazing cloth diapers that you can wash, reuse, and guess what, they aren't disgusting to handle....like Jessica said, these are NOT the rectangles of cloth with the jumbo safety pin. These are modern, and surprisingly so....super cute little diapers that you just slip a pad into, then wash the pad, and you are free to use it again. Think of the money you will save?? Think of all the landfill you won't contribute to?? Amazing! They also had a bunch of really amazing books...everything from stories to how to make your own baby food at home. Think of how much easier it could be if you can just mash up the green beans you are already eating to give to your little on instead of stocking your cupboard full of Gerber products for the next 3 years. text: Moving from San Francisco was a big deal for us. Packing up the car with all of our stuff, our two dogs and a cat, and driving across the country in the winter time is a rough experience. So I was very, VERY happy to walk into my beautiful loft for the first time. Red Brick Management has succeeded (in the last year and a half) at being a reliable, honest, and financially responsible landlord for us. They are professional, and although they put you through the ringer during the leasing process (paperwork overload!) it all ends up balancing out because of the level of trust that I felt in their professional integrity. I have dealt with both types of landlords in the past: Gigantic, corporate entities who own hundreds of buildings and treat you very much as a number in their roster of tenants and having just one guy who owned only our property only. Red Brick Management seems to fall somewhere in between. You get the benefits of having a company who is experienced, as well as fairly personal service when you need it. For instance, both spring seasons that we have lived here our air conditioner has required repair (basic stuff, just a new filter and freon). I put in the maintenance request in the morning, and someone came that same day to fix it. We also went through some financial trouble when Simon couldn't find a job, and when approached, Red Brick offered to let us move to one of their cheaper apartments without charging us anything. I am taking off one star because I do feel like our building could be more secure. We have approached them about adding real locking doors to the parking area but have not had our requests granted. Perhaps if we pushed for that more it would've happened-- but sometimes as they say, you've got to pick your battles. Overall, I say "Thank you" to Red Brick Management for really upholding your half of this deal.
label: POS

text: My most recent trip down to New Orleans almost didn't happen. Everything that went wrong did: - Didn't get a chance to pack until the morning of (my fault) - Left work late - Train left late - Airtrain was absurdly slow (c'mon! Not like there's traffic on the monorail!) - TSA shut down the security line until 5 minutes before my flight - Some guy snuck on the flight and had to be escorted off by TSA So you can imagine our unparalleled bliss when we actually made our flight, and you can probably understand our need to celebrate as soon as we landed. We reigned that impulse in only long enough to check into the hotel and drop off our luggage, and then we skipped all the way to Bourbon Street. The next few minutes were a blur, but suffice it to say that they involved hand grenades (drinks, for Bourbon Street novices) and maniacal laughter. Once the tornado died down, we found ourselves checking out the menu for La Bayou, which had all of the Creole/Cajun standbys. Factoring in the large crowd within, we decided to give it a shot and ordered some cocktails, The Ultimate Seafood Platter and the Taste of New Orleans. 1. Cocktails (~$10) - the cocktails were cleverly named and tasty, though generally on the sweet side. I particularly like the Bayou Belle, which I believe was a red bull and vodka mix with a cherry on top and some sort of fruity liquer. At the end of the meal, there was an option to transfer drinks to a to-go cup, which is definite bonus points in my book 2. The Ultimate Seafood Platter ($26.95) - HUGE! Almost overwhelming! Perhaps the largest fried seafood platter I've had in multiple trips to New Orleans! All the fried seafood you can imagine including shrimps, catfish, crawfish tails and oysters perfectly seasoned and fried to a crisp with hush puppies all over a mountain of fries. The catfish was the standout for me. It was just incredible. I mixed in a bunch of crystal hot sauce with the tartar and we had ourselves a party! 3. Taste of New Orleans ($17.95) - Three cup-size soup bowls filled with Jamabalaya, Crawfish Etouffee and Chicken & Andouille sausage gumbo.. I liked them all, but the Crawfish Etouffee was my favorite. It had an extremely generous number of crashfish tails and was nice and thick. It was great piled on the crusty bread that comes with the trio All in all, it was a dynamite start to a great vacation! Glad we randomly wandered in! PARTING THOUGHT: by the time we were done eating, the restaurant was already closing up shop. I can't help but think that it would be great to have a seafood platter after a night of drinking! There should be a shop that sells fried seafood 24 hours on Bourbon St! Is there one?
label: POS

text: Nice enough staff, great soda selection, tasty sandwiches. The owner travels a few times a year and picks up sodas from different areas, and they are all stored in a giant cooler. Glass bottle sodas ftw!! This is a true hole in the wall kinda place that has nothing corporate about it. A fun experience and has a lot of repeat potential for most who go there.

text: Okay, let's cover the news flashes first: 1) A new restaurant won't have too many people in it. 2) If a restaurant is new, and is largely empty, the owner has little to no cash flow, so he/she can be forgiven for hiring inexpensive youth as help. 3) After a long night with little do do as a result of 1) above, the help can also be forgiven for A) being a little bored, B) a little punchy (age notwithstanding), and C) anxious to get the hell out of there at closing. 4) Nothing kills a fledgling business faster than a case or two of Mad Cow Disease, and since our best minds recommend cooking ground beef well, they can also be forgiven for tending to cook on the conservative side. 5) Read the name again...It's a burger joint. No wishing for anything on the menu if it isn't made from good old-fashioned dead, cooked steer parts. My kids and I liked this place. In my son's expert estimation, the fries were as good or better than 5 Guys, and he would know; At 11, he's about 50% made of them (the rest is mac and cheese, chicken fingers, and chocolate milk, and in case you were wondering, he's all of 65#, wringing wet). I like my burgers medium, but I don't care as long as it is tasty and juicy. My burger was both, and I also liked the fries. The ONLY thing I can say about the place that I did not like, and it's something I don't like about the vast majority of restaurants, is that it was cold. Really cold. This was not a problem for us, as we ate outside on the nice tables. While I realize that it's probably hot in the cooking area, why does it have to be like a meat locker? We could save a lot of energy with more reasonable cooling habits, but that's a rant for another time. Go try this place. It's good. There are enough chain restaurants in the world. Support these little guys while they are still around. Dubya (W)

text: What a letdown! Penang served as a reminder as to why I normally shy away from chain restaurants. From a pushy server to mediocre-at-best dishes, Penang was a less than stellar dining experience. To start, the satay chicken and beef were chewy and dry. The peanut sauce was lacking in flavor but generous with grease. The entrees were equally disappointing, but at least the nasi lemak proved better than the rest. Much like the appetizers, the beef rendang were tough and next to impossible to chew. As for the "king pork buff", I think a more appropriate name for the dish would have been "king pork flop." Similar to jing du pork chops in presentation, the bbq sauce simply flopped in the piquant nature of the original dish. Dessert -- ABC shaved ice -- was aesthetically pleasing but disappointingly tasting. In fact, I couldn't find half of the ingredients listed on the menu in the bowl. True, Penang has an atmosphere to boot, but that should augment one's experience there -- not to cover for its kitchen's shortcomings.

Don and Nick on the craps tables were lightning fast. I didn't even have time to tell them to press the 6 before I had a stack of chips in front of me. text: Wow. I was impressed the first time I went to The Bridge. That is such an awesome feature, and it makes buying tickets early really worth the extra effort. That way, I don't have to show up mad early, possibly wait in a line, make a dash for the seats and have to submit myself to medieval torture by stretching over all the seats I need to reserve for my group. Only to be seated a wee bit too close to the screen for comfort. When we got to The Bridge, I was a little surprised by how nice the exterior and interior are - and that they have a bar/restaurant there too! In addition to the typical movie snacks, of course - which they also serve from a cart inside each theatre. The seats are nice and comfy, nothing special though. There was a huge line at the ticket counter when we arrived, I'm amazed anyone just shows up instead of going online but the extra fee might be the issue. text: We waited for an hour. A very long and sweaty hour. text: Friends visiting out of town or having an outing with your colleagues? Want to dine in a trendy place with delicious food? Look no further!! My co-workers and I went to Twenty Manning for dinner and drinks and were all (5 people) extremely pleased. Upon initial entry we were all excited to see the open, art-deco style space. The booth couches are all upholstered and have a really cool, old-school feel, which added a ton of character to the pretty simple space. We sat all the way in the back corner in the round booth which is great for parties of 5-6 people. The waiter immediately came over to talk about specials and get us started with drinks (fast service...always a super plus!) My Sauvignon Blanc was perfectly chilled and crisp, just the way I like it. We started with some appetizers, including: Crispy Calamari, Pot stickers, crab cakes, and scallop ceviche. Can I say....yum Yum YUm YUM!!!! Everything was very well executed and the crab cakes werent falling apart. They were that perfect combo of sticky enough to stay together but loose enough to come right apart where you can taste the chunks of crab... (mouth is watering reliving this delight!). PS: Twenty Manning gives your table awesome warm bread to share, don't over load because the meals are filling, but I recommend trying at least a small piece. For my main course, I had the Seared Candied Scallops, (clearly I was on scallop overload that night). I'm a fan of seafood and these scallops were seared to perfection, a golden crust outlining each piece and as sides came roasted pumpkin and sauteed spinach. I am a huge pumpkin lover and this was a great healthy alternative to roasted potatoes. One of my colleagues ordered the and another the salmon, everyone was raving. It was thrilling to have food that both tasted good and was good for you. Afterwards we were able to lounge around, have a few drinks and soak up the trendy dim lit atmo... would we go there again? A B S O L U T E L Y!!!

text: I went there for a birthday party of about 10 people. The night started off ok, they were pretty accomodating, but this could have been because the restaurant was empty. The evening was downhill from there. The service - the server was nice, but clueless about the menu and steaks in general. He didn't know the difference between a porterhouse, a filet, and a ribeye; he explained it completely wrong to one of the girls at the table. The food - horrendous. It got so bad, one of the guys in our group had to take his shirt off for his wife, and wore an undershirt for the rest of the dinner, and this was in the middle of August. I will never eat here again! I feel like I need to give a review for this particular restaurant just to warn others.

text: I've been here quite a few times, trying to give this place chance after chance to redeem itself, but they're hopeless. Here are 3 experiences that stand out the most, and explain why I'll never go back. -One of the times that I went for happy hour with a friend, we were barely acknowledged, and there were TWO bartenders! Thank goodness the drinks were half-priced because they were mediocre, and not worth the full-price. The empanadas are tasty, but on more than one occasion there were BONES in it! I almost choked on one. Imagine biting into a warm empanada and finding a bone, DISGUSTING. -Once again, I went back with a few friends on a Wednesday night, to check out their night scene. Music was awful, and the dance floor was empty. Place was DEAD. So my friends and I wanted to sit at a particular table near the front and order some food. When I look over, a MANAGER was sitting at the table DRINKING (and I know she's a manager because I've seen her barking orders at the staff). Very tacky and unprofessional. That just brought this place's level of class to the gutter. -A group of co-workers and I came for dinner. Our food took way too long to come out, which I don't understand because they weren't even that busy. And when it came, no one was really blown away. The only highlight was the lobster mac-n-cheese. The drinks were ok, but forgettable. And the kicker? Went to the bathroom right across from the kitchen, so you can see inside, and saw a huge roach-looking bug crawling around in there. That was the last straw for me. There's nothing special about this place. Anything they have, you can get 10 times better somewhere else. Please don't waste your time or money.

text: I've been to City Gourmet twice in the last week and have officially been converted! Here's the skinny on why you need to go here the next time you're downtown: - Free parking for customers. You pick the ingredients, put it in a bowl, pick your protein and sauce and they whip it up for you. Just like the chain, Stir Crazy, only it's not a chain. - Baked goods the size of your head for $2 or less! I picked up a sampler box of cupcakes (giant!) and brownies the other night and it cost less than $10! And all of us who sampled them agreed that they were delicious. - A majority of the products they carry are either organic or locally made. Hells yes! I'm still thinking about the delicious stir-fry I had here last week and can't wait to go back again. The BF works downtown so we'll most likely meet up here for a quick lunch date sometime soon. text: one word....YUMMY! So my husband and I were heading to Clearwater for a play that a friend was in. I have another good friend that lives in Clearwater and we asked her for suggestions on places to eat dinner. This was one of the suggestions. She told me it was awesome and that I had to try it. We headed over and got there at about 5:20. It was kind of dead, but within 15-20 minutes it was getting packed! It's not a huge place, but it is a nice place. The building seems to be well kept and has a nice italian feel. You can sit indoors or out. Neither my husband or I were that hungry due to a late lunch, but knew we had to eat something so that we weren't starving in the middle of the play - no one wants a loud growling tummy during those inevitable silent moments in a play! We decided to share a "personal" pizza. I love that a 12" pizza is considered "personal." We ordered the Margherita pizza - tomato sauce, mozzarella, oregano, and basil. Nothing too fancy, we like our pizza simple :P Now I will tell you that this place is not a normal Pizza Hut Pizza like place. It is much more like authentic Italian pizza...though I've yet to find pizza that's exactly like the pizza I had while in Italy. Oh well. They have lots of food besides pizza. They have cold or cold paninis, ravioli, pasta, appetizers, soups, salads, etc. There are a lot of options. Okay, to the pizza arrived...in what seemed like no time at all. We both started to eat...and next thing we knew, the whole thing was gone. Seriously, I wasn't that hungry...but I couldn't stop eating the pizza because it was so tasty! Then it happened....they are smart people...they gave us small samples of four of their gelato flavors! How they know me so well, I'm not sure. I LOVE Gelato. It makes me think of my short trip to Italy where I think we had gelato every day we were there because it was SO yummy! We ended up getting a small vanilla with dark chocolate chunks gelato (which has a long Italian name that I couldn't pronounce). The small was $3.50 and was probably about the size of a Cold Stone Creamery Like It size...actually probably in between that size and the Love it size. It was a nice amount. It was delicious and creamy. It was amazing...and now I want more...ugh. My husband also ordered a cannoli and he was in love! Over all we had a great experience. We are already raving about it to friends. We overheard the owner while we were there saying that he would love to open up in Tampa, but right now it's just not possible. I really wish that would change, because it would be nice to not have to drive so far to get such delicious food. I also think they would do really well in Tampa!
label: POS

text: I have had a credit card dispute pending since 9/10. A dispute that I thought had been resolved. The credit was issued. THEN I get a letter in DECEMBER asking for more data. The letter was dated 12/9, but not received until the 17th. It wants me to verify that the merchandise was returned and it wants me to contact the vendor, AGAIN. While I know that credit disputes take time, it seems that Chase went way overboard in the amount of time it gave Metro PCS to respond to the dispute. To add insult to injury, I contacted Metro PCS. They promised to call back and of course, did not. I mailed off a copy of a receipt that said 'DELIVERY INSURED" with the form Chase sent. I called Chase to let them know that I had tried to call the vendor and I had mailed more documentation to them. And what do they do? Some a-hole was so anxious to get that file off their desk, that they CLOSED the file BEFORE the date specified in their own letter! The next day I got another letter saying the matter was closed and that I would be re-billed. WHAT? I called the rep who sent me the new letter. By the time I was finished talking to her, I felt as though I was being interrogated as a criminal. She disputed everything that I said, including the USPS receipt that I sent to them saying "DELIVERY INSURED!" In fact, I became so frustrated talking to her that I could feel myself wanting to cry. And I am not a cry baby. She offered no recourse. She would not even tell me where she was sending the file. She made it sound like that was just gonna be that. OH YEAH? So this is the purpose of this review. I want people to be forewarned about how some reps behave in the credit dispute services dept. You know, the department that is supposed to be helping defend you against being taken advantage of by a sleazy company like Metro (Ghettro) PCS. Instead of help, all I got were justifications as to why they could not "make the vendor pay." Excuse me? I could not believe what I was hearing. I've never had a disputed charge encounter become adversarial with a company that is supposed to be servicing ME before. Protect yourself, people. Save every shred of paper. Document every name. Cuz you will need it to defend yourself. Don't accept anything less than what is right. Know your rights. Send follow up letters when you talk to people. It's the only way. People lie on the phone to get rid of you. If you don't get satisfaction, tell them you will contact the FTC, your congressman, alert the media and report the issue in social network forums. For the record, I rarely dispute any charges. But this taught me a lesson. The fact that credit card companies offer a dispute system is NO guarantee that any purchase issue will be resolved to your satisfaction. So caveat emptor. Buyer beware. I will never again rely upon any credit card company to be my advocate in a purchase transaction. EVER. I will not "shop with confidence" any more, no matter what any credit card company advertiser says. I feel so strongly about consumer advocacy that I will offer anyone who contacts me templates of some of the letters that I have written to resolve disputes that have worked in the past. There are no guarantees, but usually written letters get results. Do not rely upon phone calls. Document everything you do and say, ad nauseam. I will post updates to this situation as they occur. For reference about the dispute, see http://www.yelp.com/user_details_review_search?userid=OfddPlzVNLSwlOTaeBGZKA&q=Metro+PCS or find the Metro PCS review in the L.A. area.

text: Wow...I really wish I could say I like biking this trail because I'm really glad the city of St. Louis is trying...but...well...try harder??? They have put in some pathed sidewalks on the river's edge and the new footbridge across the river between Gravois and Morganford is actually really nice, but the bike path...well...it just leaves a lot to be desired. The path runs from Lindenwood St. near the Metro Link, down the side of River Des Peres down near Highway 55. The path is fairly flat which is good for less experienced bikers, but that said, the trail is NOT well maintained...which is horrible for inexperienced bikers. There are ton of cracks and rocks all over the thing. It is only 4 miles long and takes a lot of random bends and turns for no apparent reason. Also, lets remember, you riding along the side of River Des Peres. In high school my friends and I maturely referred to this thing as River Des Pew. Is a sewage run off really what you want to be inhaling when you are trying to ride or run? Not so much. On the upside, it's never crowded, and you don't have to fight your way around baby strollers, but there's a reason for this...the path is just....well...sub par... text: Regarding the star rating, it's tough because there were two things that were terribly wrong with our meals at our visit to Bardenay, but everything else was just fine. Maybe not "fine." The service was lacking. We had a seat on the nice patio during the end of the lunch hour, and everything moved particularly slowly. The patio was almost full, but the inside was nearly empty, so there wasn't much of an excuse there. And the niceties of the patio and this restaurant's immaculate interior are really its saving grace. Being on Grove Street in the Basque Block with a nice building though, I don't think, warrants a positive review in itself. The food is really what makes an experience excel over a location, regardless of the latter being a plus or not. The two things that went wrong with this meal were food-related. First, I got a chorizo sandwich with fries. The chorizo was not as good as what I had eaten at Bar Gernika the night before, but was certainly still pretty good and the bread was really nice. The fries, however, were off. When I asked, the server freely admitted that they were the frozen/Sysco variety. WTF? This is Idaho! Does any respectable restaurant really need to subject their customers to frozen french fries? And not only frozen fries, Sysco fries. I mean, I'm not looking for the Bittercreek Ale House standard of excellent housemade fries, I'm just looking for something that I can't buy in a big bag at the supermarket for $2. And the only reason I know what these fries are is because, for years in college, I ate them at Burger King until I got disgusted with them and can't eat them anymore. No, seriously, these are the same fries as you find at Burger King. There's just no reason for that. Okay, so maybe I shouldn't automatically expect fresh fries at an Idaho restaurant. I mean, it's the Gem State and not the Fresh-Cut Potato State. But the other bad part of the meal was inexcusable. My companion got an "ahi" tuna salad. Quote marks are necessary there because it was nothing like the ahi tuna you may be used to. This was, essentially, the tuna that comes out of the bag. It tasted and looked no different. This is, admittedly, one step above the Bumblebee variety, coated with brine, mayonnaise and a "lord knows" variety of chemicals, but it still sucked and rendered the salad virtually inedible because of the tuna's outright stench. So we left with finishing only about 1/2 of our meals. I would not return here, nor would I recommend it to anyone else. If you want Basque, go to Bar Gernika or the Basque Market next door.

text: I spent an incredible four years at Wash U. The name carries a lot of weight when looking for jobs or applying for grad school. The experience was truly amazing. I had caring professors (except one terrible classic professor - Rosenberg, maybe?), a wonderful advisor, several professors/mentors with whom I still regularly visit, and a supportive and open community. The students are liberal, the administration is conservative, and the climate is open and fair - not all that common in Missouri. The campus is small and contained, but you can choose to venture out into the city or the region as much as you want. I really valued the containment. The sports are actually really amazing here, contrary to another reviewer's post. The women's basketball team broke records for most consecutive wins in a row (the only NCAA team in history that has more than our 81 is John Wooten's 70's UCLA team), the men's basketball team is doing really well, and the volleyball team has won several championships as well. It's not a DI school, but that's exactly why I went here. DIII means more focus on academics, and that's why Wash U is considered as top notch (if not better than some) as the Ivy League schools. That's also why it costs so friggin much you'll never be out of debt. I had a full tuition scholarship and I still have $20k in loans because of housing and such. But the costs are on par with similar schools. I think how much money you make after graduation depends on what you go into, not what school you go to. I don't know any postdocs making all that much, so you're gonna have to work your ass off to pay back the loans if you don't go into a high salary field. That said, I went into nonprofit and think Wash U prepared me for a very successful career and an incredible life as an adult with exposure to many different fields. I'm extremely proud to be a Wash U alum, and welcome any questions from people considering Wash U as one of their choices.

text: We've been walking by Trattoria Victoria for a few years, so we decided to give it a try on Friday night. Food is very good, I started with Asparagus and Prosciutto appetizer. Prosciutto was very fresh and abundant, although it could have used some olive oil or balsamic vinegar to give it some moisture. I then followed with Sea bass in tomatoes and olive puttenesca. It was fabulous, fish was very tender and fresh, with side of roasted potatoes and spinach. Husband had side of Penne (perfectly al dente), with Branzino fish. It was beautifully prepared with crispy outer skin and tender inside, waiter expertly filleted it at the table with a touch of olive oil and parsley! YUM! As with most Italian restaurants you should always try the "Special", regular menu items get boring after a while... Décor reminds me of many family owned Italian restaurants you find on east coast, a bit cramped and loud but charming (ask for table against the wall, otherwise you are sitting in prime traffic area). Not as nice as Ca Dario, more rustic. Interesting touch - they play old movies on two TV screens over bar (no sound). Clever touch, we caught the end of an old Carey Grant movie and most of Dean Martin as Matt Helm - two very stylized art directed movies, fun to watch! Movies ad an interesting "campy hip" tone. Next time we'll sit at bar, and enjoy film during dinner. Service was very good, wait staff very attentive and nice. Price is very reasonable, I read some of other reviews about it being expensive and am a bit baffled - come on this is Santa Barbra! Some of dishes are very affordable in $10 - $15 range. Wine list was decent although they could definitely add a few more reasonable priced wines in $20 - $40 range. Bathrooms need work. While an attempt was made to cutely decorate, both women's and men's rooms could use sprucing up. Let's not forget to restock toilet paper people!!! Otherwise a very nice experience!

It seemed like instead of baking it fresh, it had been re-heated and the pastry around the brie was a little mushy. Anway, when we were seated, our waiter was perfectly friendly, so that's what's keeping me from giving this place only 1 star. I'm a vegetarian who sometimes indulges in fish (don't hate), but I opted for a completely veg dish of Pappardelle Noodles w/ wild mushrooms, asparagus, leeks & truffle oil broth. It sounded amazing. I couldn't wait to try it. Then I did. It was COMPLETELY FLAVORLESS. What a waste of homemade pasta, veggies, and truffle oil. I grabbed the waiter and told him I have never sent anything back to a kitchen because I felt like it wasn't worth eating, but I had to in this case. He was very accommodating and ask what I wanted instead. I had seen an eggplant flatbread on the appetizer menu, so I just ordered that. The waiter returned and said the chef did not use any salt or garlic in his preparation of the dish. Thanks for the info? I mean I could already tell no salt was used. And it's not like I'm into heavy salting. But anyone who cooks knows that some salt needs to be used to bring out the flavor of vegetables and certainly in broth. My flatbread came out very quickly and it was pretty gross. The flatbread seemed undercooked and the ratio of veggies on it was unbalanced. Not worth eating. Luckily I wasn't very hungry by this point. So, while the waiter seemed like he was trying (and the bad food really isn't his fault--it's the chef's) and the noodle dish was removed from the bill, I have absolutely no desire to return to this restaurant ("great" view or not). I can't believe this place is actually getting away with charging the prices it does for food that is so sub-par.

text: Lucien's Manor could also be called "Lucien's Wedding Factory" or "Lucien's Taj Mahal of Weddings," because receptions are pumped out from all angles. Friends and I walked into the lobby and were faced with a woman wearing an earpiece and holding a walkie talkie. We were instructed to use a set of stairs on the left and turn left once we reached the top. When attending a reception at a place like this, there is always a moment of panic before walking into a hall that you might accidentally walk in on some other newly married couple's first dance or something. Luckily, our directions were solid and we saw familiar faces right away. Whew! We made our way to the bar and the 'tenders seemed harried. Despite its availability, I noticed that the Grey Goose was kept hidden from plain view, unless it was specifically requested. Tsk, tsk! The pours were weak and martinis were in no danger of spilling as they only filled about half the glass. I also heard a couple people lamenting over the no shots policy. Regardless, people did not seem to have problems getting socially lubricated enough to bust some moves on the dance floor. I liked the room we were in because it offered some privacy from the other weddings taking place. It was cozy, with a fireplace in the corner behind the newlywed table. There were adjoining bathrooms, which kept us completely secluded from the other partygoers in the building. Dinner was above average as far as wedding fare goes. Italian wedding soup, Caesar salad and a choice of stuffed shrimp or filet made for a filling and flavorful meal. As others have mentioned, servers walk around with trays to offer extras. Later in the evening, a huge dessert table was unveiled, along with a flambé station and gourmet coffee station. The attendant probably thought he was doing me a favor by pouring about three ounces of Jameson into my Irish coffee, but unfortunately I had to abort mission after a sip or two so that I would be sober enough to drive home. All in all, the wedding was lovely and the staff at Lucien's did a nice job keeping the night flowing and guests happy.
label: POS

text: Went to Effie's last night with a group of 10 friends. The food was pretty good (the moussaka is insanely large and hearty) and the service during the meal was fine. Ambience is nice - I especially like the garden in the back. The reason that I left the meal rather unhappy was the sequence of events that occurred when we were paying the bill. First of all, the menu said "18% gratuity included for parties of 8 or more". When it says that on the menu, you would expect that it would be the *actual* policy. So they brought us the bill (which was basically the tape reel of a calculator) and we figured that the tip was included because IT SAID IT WOULD BE ON THE MENU (am I wrong here, people??) After we paid, the server came back all puppy-eyed with the bill and some change and asked if there was something wrong with our meal. She insinuated that our tip was insufficient and then explained that they didn't apply the policy they had clearly printed on the menu because it was a slow night or something. That pissed me off. If you have a policy printed on your menu, customers expect you to enforce it (again, please correct me if I am wrong here). Or you should tell us when you give us the bill that tip is *not* included like it says on the menu. I liked Effie's before last night, but I was left with a rather poor taste in my mouth (and pocket) and don't know if I'll be going back anytime soon.

text: I thought about docking the 2010 incarnation of Capoyunk one star, given how expensive it is. But you know what? Gelato is expensive. I'm happy to pay a couple bucks more than I would at Rita's for this experience. There've been so many improvements to this shop since last summer, I can't rave enough. But I will try: First, they've hired some super-sweet folks (especially those who work the morning shift) to replace the wave of snotty kids scooping in '09. Second, H&H BAGELS. I almost don't want to mention this because they already tend to disappear by 10:30 am, but I'll say it. H&H BAGELS. They are incredible and inexpensive. So are the morning pastries -- brioche croissants, etc. -- and La Colombe coffee. It's just as pleasant a breakfast spot as a late-night treatery. Third, ambience. OK, this isn't new, but the blue on those walls, and the black-and-white photos, and back patio I haven't yet ventured into -- as one reviewer said, it's a great place to linger. Don't go to Capoyunk expecting to hop in and out, especially if you're there late in the evening on a hot-ass day. The layout is a bit awkward and causes clusters of people maybe in line, maybe not, and patience will win you as many taste tests as you desire, but expecting to be served right away will just frustrate you. Lastly, I suggest following them on Twitter (@capoyunk) -- I was on my computer at 9:30 tonight, saw a tweet that said something about Mexican chocolate and grapefruit-Campari gelato, and I immediately left my house and ran over before closing time. Effective marketing.

text: City Museum is so amazing it will make you feel like you're 5 years old again. I think that's as good an endorsement as I can give it. It really is just a huge jungle gym strewn across an old, beautiful warehouse, designed for adults. Sure, you can bring your kids and, many, many do, but this is a place the young at heart, old(er) in body can enjoy without feeling like the creepy guy without kids at the playground. You can crawl through spaces that you feel like are the imaginary rafters in every old building across America, through imaginary tundra and deserts. You can pour down a slide many stories in lengths, roast marshmallows on open fire when it's 10 degrees outside and see how compact exactly your body can get as you attempt to squeeze into places that look ever more precarious. You can even dish out a few extra and visit a small in house zoo, filled with komodo dragons and other exotic creatures. If you have any interest in buildings, history or sculpture the top floor should not be missed. It is filled with remnants of historic St. Louis and midwestern buildings and adornments, many of which are beautiful exemplars of architectural styles past. Or, you could simply sit back and watch every scramble about in enjoyment. One tip though, try to eat before or after, as the food as the museums tends to be greasy or overpriced.
label: POS

text: Had relatives in town, one of which was my small nephew who's a notoriously picky eater. Turns out one of the things he likes is these places. Which is fine with me because the numerous times we've been to Kobe it's been fun and the food has been pretty good. We had reservations at Kobe, but since the Westport location is so far from us we decided to give Shogun a shot. How different could it be anyway? Those were my naive famous last words. First off, no reservations. I don't mean we didn't have one, I mean they don't take them! ? That's pretty rediculous for a place doing teppanyaki. You have a limited number of tables, that seat a very specific number, and a limited number of chefs. It begs for reserved seatings. The odd thing is that there were a ton of people waiting, but we walked up to the hostess who pointed to a waitress to immediately take us to a table. Go figure. While it was nice to get seated so promptly, I overheard some pretty nasty things being said about me from the crowd still waiting. The entertainment: The routine is basically the same as every other place like this. That's fine with me, the kids enjoy it and I've only fallen over in my chair twice trying to catch a shrimp in my mouth... The food: In addition to the normal meal I ordered a variety of sushi to be brought to the table so that I could gauge that as well. What a waste. The size of the rolls here are smaller than usual, but I can live with that, what I can't live with is a place serving sushi that doesn't know how to properly make sushi rice. Oh well. Live and learn. At least the rest of the food will be predictable. Ooops. It was predictable in regards to what was served, it's just that every single thing I put in my mouth was below average. Salad with ginger dressing: Check. But so thinned out and watery it might as well have been soup underneath the salad. Broth/Soup: Check. Tasteless. Meal: I just didn't figure any of the proteins would be a problem. I mean, really high heat, stainless steel, place protein on steel, make a lot of racket with your knives, place cooked protein on plate. How do you mess that up? I'm still at a loss on this one, but *everything* was not seasoned properly. Mainly though, I think it had less to do with the proteins and more to do with the dipping sauces. Let's face it, it's that damned addicting mustard sauce that we go to these places for. But here? Oh no. Couldn't they just copy everyone else? The sauces were the most noticeable thing that was different from other places. Unfortunately, that's not a good thing. They sucked. Really, really, hard. Which pretty much ruined any hopes for this meal. Want teppanyaki in St. Louis? Go to Kobe. P.S. - If you still aren't a believer and insist on trying it yourself, I would suggest going for lunch. The prices are much cheaper so at least you won't be kicking yourself as much as I was.
label: NEG

text: The best pizza place hands down. I've been to both DeLorenzo's locations, on Hudson and Hamilton streets and they are pretty similar. If you are used to getting your pizza from Dominoes or Pizza Hut and you actually think they have good pizza then I would not even recommend you go to DeLorenzo's because all you're going to do is waste precious seating room. The Hudson street location is a real dive. It's in an awful area and doesn't look like it's been changed much since it opened. The place is very small with five or so tables in the front of the store and maybe another six in the back. The service is awful and you might have to wait awhile before anyone even comes to bring you water and the lady that takes your order is a curmudgeonly old ogress that hates the world. The place doesn't have a bathroom, so make sure you go beforehand, and they do not accept credit cards, so bring cash. Their drink selection is very sparse and it all tastes like watered down Gatorade. I'd just stick with water. Also, don't try to call them on the phone, they frequently leave it off the hook. So far I've made the place sound awful, but everything I've said is true and is a must know for the DeLorenzo's tenderfoot. The ONLY reason it manages to get five stars in my book is the pizza. The pizza is otherworldly. It's not loaded with heavy toppings or gloppy, stringy cheese, instead it relies on simple ingredients and proper preparation. I could write a doctoral dissertation on their crust alone, it's so perfect. Its extremely thin and crispy with a slight charring around the edges. The sauce is a perfect compliment to the crust with its freshness and real bites of tomato chunks. Also, order more pizza than you think you'll need. You'll definitely want it. They do have toppings, but don't expect to order anything too avant garde, they might throw your ignorant ass out.

text: Frankie's place is probably the best place for Italian food done to perfection on the Main Line. Even though the name of the place is Fellini Cafe, it is not part of a chain, as stated by a previous reviewer although the name may have originally been associated. Frankie's food is nothing like the other places (which I have tried). I have probably have been there over 20 times and honestly have not had a bad meal. It's BYOB and we usually bring a red and white wine so we can choose based upon what the evening specials are. One of our off menu favorites is the roasted pork chop with broccoli rabe and roasted potatoes. The Veal Milanese with hot and sweet peppers never disappoints. Classic standbys of gnocchi and spaghetti with bolognese sauce work well every time; the meatballs are the third best I have ever had (my wife makes the best, my mother-in-law, the second best). The fish dishes are delicious and someone in the group always orders the mussels with red sauce, which is a definite pleaser. After a very satisfying dinner, be sure to enjoy one of the excellent desserts. The cannoli are hand filled when you place your order (so no getting soggy during the day) and Frankie's pizelle-ice cream sandwich with home-made gelati (three types, the pistachio is incredible) with fresh made caramel sauce (Frankie makes it himself when you order) has you licking the plate clean. Aside from the great food, the service is always personal and Frankie comes out to greet everyone - all feel like regulars and the wait staff are quick to respond to special requests. The place is tight - very much European in its nature (if you don't like people, don't come) - but everyone is friendly and ready to let you know how much they like what they are eating (my wife is always asking about something new that someone else has ordered). Unfortunately, we've had to move far enough away that getting over is a very very long drive, but whenever we are in town, we always stop in for a bite to eat.

He seated us, handed us menus and grabbed us some water, and then all but disappeared for the next 20 minutes. What was he DOING? Like I said before, the restaurant wasn't super busy. The burger bar has tons of combinations that you can use to put together your own burger. You choose your bun, the burger itself, your cheeses, toppings, etc. Of course, they also have specialty burgers where everything is chosen for you. But who wants to do that when you can play chef for a night and make your own burger? Okay, so here comes the waiter douchebag part. We asked for some suggestions on what combinations are popular among other guests, and the waiter POINTS TO THE MENU and tells us that the pre-selected options are pretty good. Gee, thanks, hun...I know how to READ. Gah! Maybe I'm weird, but that just burned me up. But anyway, the food. We ordered the trio of fries as an appetizer: zucchini fries, onion rings, and pickle fries. For my entree, I made my own burger using a ciabatta bun, buffalo burger, pepperjack cheese, avocado, and jalapeno bacon. I asked for my burger to be cooked medium. Well, guess what? Our appetizer came out at the same time as our entree. Awesome. Don't you just love when that happens? Poor timing, folks. Poor timing. The app was pretty terrible to boot. How can you go wrong with deep fried goodness? Well, let me tell you: I bit into the deep fried pickle, and the whole pickle slid out in the first bite, leaving me with a sad empty breading shell. Ew. Same thing happened with the zucchini fries. And the onion rings. I guess this was God's way of telling me not to eat things that are deep fried? It worked. I stopped after a bite of each. My burger was also lame and sad. It wasn't cooked medium. Instead, it was well-done. *sigh* If a freaking BURGER BAR can't cook my burger right, I've lost hope for all burgers out there. Sorry. Aside from the meat being overdone, it was dry and bland (probably due to being overcooked!). The toppings were decent, but they didn't add much to the burger. The ciabatta bun was hard and didn't seem fresh. All in all, this was a complete disaster. Since our meal was comped, we felt obligated to leave a decent tip to our not-so-decent waiter. I'll tell you what -- leaving that $20 tip on the table was HARD. I'll never be back. Hubert Keller, you should be ashamed of yourself for this abomination.
label: NEG

text: My experience at Cooperage was solidly 3 stars, maybe even 3.5, until the very end. We'll start with the good stuff - great decor, good crowd and great sips specials. $2 Stellas and more than decent appetizers offered at half price. Though I must say that the wings, though large and meaty, were a little gooey-er than I like and the sauce could have had a bit more of a kick to it. The pork nachos were definitely a big hit at our table. Now, I hate to bring down a review based purely on one server, but this was so over-the-top that it can't be avoided. Our server made two critical errors - first, when I communicated to him that one of the bathrooms was experiencing a problem (toilet was clogged) he shrugged and said "well, did it have an 'out of service' sign on it?" - obviously not or no one on my party would have attempted to use the bathroom. After a few moments of confusion, I repeated my statement, to which he then replied along the lines of "oh, well I'll tell whoever is in charge about that". Ohhh-K. This guy definitely had a "don't look at me" attitude. Secondly, one of our party asked for a separate bill, which he received, paid and left. When we got our bill, the waiter delivered it and said "your friend was an awful tipper". We were confused for a second, and then immediately jumped to apologize and asked what happened. The waiter then said "he left $2 on a $15 bill". Now, I start at 20% and work up or down depending, but most people consider that excessive, and start with 10% - 15% and work up or down. $2 is 13% on a $15 bill. Not to mention that we had to flag down this server for the majority of our needs and once he got an order from one person, left before asking the rest of the table - causing us to call out after him to complete the round. Regardless of how bad you think our friend tipped - don't complain about it to us - at most, ask us if we were happy with the service and our experience and let us infer from there! Barring the service issues - we enjoyed our time at Cooperage and I won't hesitate to give it another try, with the hope that the service steps up.

text: Finally made it into Bluefin today. I gotta thank Yelp for this one, as even though I've driven past the place a million times I never would have made an effort to eat here. I got here right after noon, barely got a parking spot, and then noticed a line out the door. 30 minute wait. But, since I'm cool/a loser and was all by my lonesome, I was able to get the lone empty seat at the bar. Swiftly ordered the spicy noodle soup and the Sushi "B" lunch, with a salad. Got the salad almost right away...it was ok. Yea, its just the token throw-in, but I've had better. Kinda soggy. Not a big deal, though. The soup was great. mildly spicy, but with a nice flavor. Really warmed up the ol' insides. My sushi plate was next to arrive, and the fish was fantastic...very fresh tasting and at the perfect temperature. Many places serve them far too cold. This was just right! You can get more generous portions at other places but if it isn't served right, who cares? The vibe was the best...really felt like the neighborhood bar or diner. Everyone seemed to know somebody else. Nice and cozy. Seeing some of the plates that other people ordered made me want to get a second lunch, but I'll have to wait until next time. I want to try the "sundaes", and something that looked like a wedge-shaped roll, dipped into some sort of roe/sauce dish? Not sure what that was but I want it. Price was very reasonable...not cheap, but not the most expensive sushi lunch in the burbs. I'll be back here for sure (just not for a haircut).

text: Friends from New Jersey and Pennsylvania swear that in North Carolina there are no good diners. On a recent road trip to Boston, we made "When in Rome," our mantra and decided to hit a few Jersey diners for some of the foods my friends have been homesick for. Club Diner reeks of New Jersey. Neon lights. Glass cases with pies, cakes and pastries. Family drama at a neighboring booth. A kid demanding $5000 from his crying father. Still, despite this, the food is consistent. Not extraordinary. Immense menus with everything from scrapple to sandwiches, to pot roast to gyros. My fiance went the safe route and had an omelet, hash browns and toast. After a conversation with a friend from Westchester, PA last week, I had a craving for cream chipped beef. My craving was satisfied by the Club Diner. I had delicious cream chipped beef. Our server was preoccupied. You don't go to a diner for a gourmet meal. You don't go for the atmosphere, or the service. You go, because they have EVERYTHING at a low price, with convenient hours. Based upon our food, I've gotta say this is not a best-in-class diner. However, it offered up exactly the right kind of Jersey experience that this Carolina girl was looking for.

text: Those lucky little punks at UCSB really have no idea how good they have it. Freebirds is a diamond mine nestled in the upscale ghetto that is Isla Vista. I went there for the first time about 15 years ago during one of the many road trips I made from the (818) to visit the legions of high school friends who went to school nearby. During a three-day weekend, I'd be good to eat here three times in various states of inebriation. But in all fairness, the massive burritos were good even when I was stone sober. Comparisons between Freebirds and Chiptole aren't really apt. Yes, both let you build your grub from the ground up and watch the magic take place from the other side of the counter, but Freebirds has fresher ingredients (Especially the righteous guacamole) and is much, much better. They also have a variety of very good salsas that will let you tailor your food to your heat tolerance. You can also eat at Freebirds without the guilt that comes with lining the coffers of the McDonalds evil empire that Chipotle sold its soul to several years ago. Freebirds still occupies a special place in my heart and now serves as a halfway point during one of my favorite Southern California rides: Topanga Canyon to PCH to the 101 to Santa Barbara and a fat veggie monster burrito. Then return to the madness of the (818) via Lake Casitas and the Ojai Valley. Give me some decent weather and it makes for a near-perfect day.

text: I was strolling the 2nd Street festival today and noticed a long line in front of Dmitri's. Turns out it was hummus with parsley, paprika and olive oil, served with grilled pita. And it was free. Good marketing on their part, because while munching on my free and good (not Zahav good, but definitely better than your average) hummus I realized that 1: their menu is almost entirely inexpensive seafood, 2: this is the same Dmitri's as the other two locations (I'd never put two and two together) and I've been dying to try them anyway, and 3: I was craving octopus. So a couple hours later, when my friend showed up at the festival and the skies unleashed some cold summer rain, we ducked into Dmitri's for some snacks and to wait out the rain. We sat at the cool (and cramped!) open kitchen. My friend ordered more hummus, I got my octopus. I think the head chef was training a new guy, but they still did a good job grilling the octopus, though I might have removed it just a second or two sooner. I LOVE me some seasoned grill marks on octopus, though, and this place had just the right flavor on the grill. It comes in a very simple olive oil and red wine vinegar sauce with some parsley and salt, so tasty. Some peppers and olives on the side. And for $12 the portion is gigantic. It's on the appetizer menu, but no reason to not have this as an entree. Had some simple and yummy rice pudding for dessert, and a strong little Greek coffee. My only (small) complaint is the service... it wasn't unfriendly, but ever-so awkward and rushed. They asked if we'd like anything else as I was finishing my dish. I was taken off-guard, so I probably said we were fine. A few moments later they dropped the check. Then I said we might like some dessert, and she was almost off again before I managed to squeak out I wanted coffee, too. Then they cleared my plate as I was finishing my olives! Only minor complaints, though, the rest of the service was smooth. I definitely enjoyed my food and watching others' food prepared in the open kitchen, and I'll definitely be back. Good job with the free hummus table at the 2nd St festival, Dmitri's.

It's quite long and narrow with cute metal victorian chairs that cannot fit your bum if you weigh 200+. It barely fit my 169lb bum... It was quite good - sweet, iced, and was a well brewed tea + iced coffee (3.75 yelps) ----the iced coffee was a strong black coffee, no cream and no sugar. Was good and complemented the beignets well + one order of beignets (3 are served in the order) (4.37 yelps) ----fried doughy sweet powdery messy goodness. Reminds me of eating zeppoles or doughnuts done traditionally in a paper bag (i.e. the week before @ Pike Place market in Seattle) Thoroughly satisfied and the best beignets I've ever had. I can't give it 5 yelps as I need to become a beignet expert and then realize it's in the top 2-3 beignet places ever in my experience. Then, and only then, it may get 5 yelps. go eat here and get fat

I am so glad I made the reservation as this place was packed... and on a Wednesday night! The only negative thing I can say is that it was so loud in there! I guess that is a sign that patrons are enjoying themselves! After reading through several reviews I knew I had to try the blood orange margarita. It was good, but not OMG good. I probably would of ordered another if they weren't $9 each. That's almost an order of fish tacos. And what about happy hour? When i popped in at 5 pm last night as I was passing by I asked if they had one and the hostess said no. We had the original guacamole served in the huge mortar bowl which I think they do to make it look like there is more than you think. The only improvement I would recommend is that for $13 they could make the portion larger AND prepare it at your table like another overpriced Mexican joint in DC. It was very good, BTW. Also good were the fish tacos. they are about the size of those McD's snack wraps, but instead of paying $2.79 for two, you get to pay $11!! Not quite a deal, but as I said, very good. If they started having a happy hour and charged $5 for their margaritas, then I'd say this would the place to go. Paying $5.50 for one taco would be easier to stomach, especially with discounted alcohol to wash it down.
label: POS

text: I had read some of the negative reviews about Marylinn's, but because of the limited choice of bridal shops on the Central Coast, I decided to give them a chance. Especially because their website showed a large selection of designers that I was interested in. I made an appointment and took my mom and maid of honor with me. The consultant didn't even acknowledge my mom during the entire process (who is, hello!, the one that will be purchasing the dress). She right away informed me that I would not likely be able to order a dress within six months and kept pushing me to purchase a sample dress. I have been to several other bridal shops thus far and most are able to order a dress within 4-6 months, plus, most of the sample dresses were dirty and had not been taken care of. Not to mention they are about 4 sizes too big for me. The consultant promised that their seamstress would be able to alter the dress to fit me, but I don't think the design of the dress is able to be maintained with that much of a difference in size. Also, the shop only carried a few of the designers that are on the website. They only allow you one hour to an appointment , a large part of which was wasted on being "introduced to the designers" which they could have used that time to find what I needed. They won't let you take pictures, which is very important because you can't see the how the back of the dress looks without them. The consultant and even the manager were not helpful as to what styles I should try on, even after I had shown them photos of the types of dresses I like. The consultant would only let me try on 5 dresses and she kept rushing me and pushing me to make a decision within my one hour appointment. I asked if they had any other appointments available that day (since I am from out of town and could only be there for the day) and without checking, she immediately said no. Later, when she realized that I was going to leave without purchasing, she magically had another appointment available right away. I stayed, even though I had already gotten dressed by then. During the appointment, my mom was asking about alterations on a gown I was considering and the manager made insulting comments about my measurements in front of everyone in the shop! Overall, the customer service was terrible, the staff were not knowledgeable and I left feeling completely depressed and deflated. Is it so difficult to try to make the bride and her party feel special and enjoy the experience of shopping for this very expensive and important purchase? I was thoroughly disappointed.

text: i went to sushi on oracle last night. usually very fresh and good, but last night something was off about all the sushi. the tuna smelled and tasted a little fishy, which is very uncommon for this place. my wife also got a piece of scale with her halibut, also something that has never happened to us before and not up to the high standards of this restaurant. the place was kinda hot and stuffy due to the packed house. we chalked it up to the heat and maybe our sushi chef was under the weather a bit and not having a good day. the sea urchin in particular, made me and my wife sick. my sea urchin did not taste sweet like it usually does but did not taste like it was spoiled. my wife's sea urchin looked kinda slimy and smelled bad from the beginning. from the moment she tasted it, she knew it was bad. it had a sour taste and chemical-like soapy aftertaste that made her spit it out right away. our sushi chef did apologize and give us new nigiri made with fresh sea urchin, but the damage was done. i suffered the entire night after i ate here last night.

text: Despite being run by embarrassingly stereotypical rednecks (once upon a time I applied for a job here and took a little jaunt into the back area) and not appearing to have been updated since probably 1973, Tanner's is a top notch grocery store. Their dairy products are produced on-site at the farm behind the store, and it tastes it. They produce the best milk I've ever had and the only skim milk I've had that doesn't taste like white food-colored water. Many families I know including my own go out of their way to get their milk here even if they shop at Shop n' Bag or Super Fresh for everything else, and many are angered at the notion of going back to Rosenberger's or the like if they can't get to Tanner's before they close. Their chocolate milk is unbelievably delicious and tastes like someone just melted a good chocolate milkshake into a bottle. Their ice cream is also top notch. Grocery and produce-wise, everything is of excellent quality but they aren't a full supermarket and as such don't have everything. That being said, one could easily sustain a family's common food needs here with fewer trips for stuff like cleaning products and lesser-used foods. Their prices are fair and reasonable. I don't know where this deli is that DJ M mentions, though they do have a few unsliced deli meats and cheeses packaged kept in the cold case. The store employs numerous local youths but people I've spoken to who used to work there say the management sucks to work for. But then again what job at 15/16 doesn't suck?

text: This place is cozy and quiet. I made a special trip just to try its fabled hot chocolate--thanks yelpers. I went early in the morning and ordered breakfast as well. Breakfast was good--not great but good. Didn't get the fruit that the menu mentions (though I had enough to eat) and there was no butter for my toast. No butter on it, none offered. I didn't bother to ask and just ate my eggs, potatoes, and turkey bacon. Meat lovers will be happy to know that I got three or four strips of bacon with my meal. Potatoes were seasoned, and I was pleased to find that it wasn't just seasoned salt like Lawry's. Looked like there was turmeric but they weren't salty. On to the hot cocoa. It was good and definitely homemade with solid chocolate. I was caught off-guard when they asked if I wanted sugar. I said yes, and perhaps that cut the spices in my cup, because I didn't taste any chile in mine. But it was made-to-order and tasty. And did I mention the VOLUME? I think my mug probably held about 20 ounces of milk and chocolate. I could barely drink it all. They also get fresh croissants delivered, and they look amazing. If you are a parent, you'll be pleased to know that they have a table and chairs for the kids with some toys. So you can bring the little one if you want to linger over your ginormous hot cocoa, and they'll be happy to find that Cafe Pier One has made accommodations for them.

Quality food, excellent service and nice, but not stuffy, atmosphere makes Dickie Brennan's Steakhouse a must try if you aren't on a tight budget while in New Orleans.

text: I appreciate a lot of where the (first and only) 5-star reviewer is coming from. The food - which took almost TWO HOURS to arrive at our table - was not bad. Portion size was laughably small for the price. While waiting interminably for our meals to arrive, two of our party got angry and left after paying for their appetizers. They (and we) were incensed by the owner/manager's insistence that "We have no more bread...we make only so much every day" (yet we saw bread being issued to a later table). To wait 90 minutes having only been offered a slice of bread to tide you over is ridiculous; I didn't blame them for leaving and vowing never to return to Mondo. Half of our party (four seated at a separate table next to us) was served, ate, and left more than an hour before us (six who ordered before them!). I've never heard a waiter say "I apologize" more times than this poor soul, who was at a loss to explain how the kitchen could get THAT backed up. Not because the manager offered, but because we insisted, Mondo comped us 3 desserts and one bottle of wine for our misery, which lasted over three hours total! Adding to the awful ambience was the LOUDNESS of the place. You literally must SHOUT AT FULL VOLUME to be audible to the person sitting next to you. In fact, the lack of noise-abatement became our prevailing topic of conversation! We all strove to become adept at reading lips, and all meaning and subtlety were lost, which is especially troublesome for workmates, not all of whom knew each other beforehand. I was seriously disappointed as well by the disparity between what was printed on the menu and what actually arrived. I almost laughed when I saw two tiny pieces of lamb served atop 8 (counted 'em) finger-size pieces of ravioli, for which I paid handsomely ($19). That the menu even bothered to mention "fresh mint jelly" simply added insult to injury, as the dish sported zero adornment whatsoever. I was done in 4 bites! I left Mondo hungrier than when I arrived ... and nearly deaf. Truly, reservations are for naught at this place. Best deal: The hamburger. That's right... a hamburger and fries was more substantial than anything others ordered. While the artichoke appetizer was tasty, as were the beignets and chocolate cake desserts, watching them disappear so quickly due to starvation was a turn-off. I/we won't be back. That's 11 customers who agree "It's totally not worth it."
label: NEG

text: You know that overused cliche, "you can't judge a book by it's cover?" Well, dredge up this classic saying when you try out Harvest, because you shouldn't allow yourself to judge the place by it's eyesore exterior. If you did, you would miss out on some excellent (and fresh) food choices and stellar service that's offered inside. I was visiting the fam again this weekend, and my mom always manages to find a great gem of a spot to take us out to eat. This weekend, it was Harvest. We were seated promptly (thanks to reservations made the day before), and ordered up a bottle of Merlot to start us off. For our app, we went with the charcuterie plate - it was a solid "meh." A pretty small serving (especially for three people), and the meat options were a bit funky (apparently, unless is roasted, I don't like duck). The bread was okay, but the black bean dip was a tad blah. Anywho, the main course is what really makes this place four star worthy. I ordered the barramundi (new zealand fish, sea bass-esque in texture and flavor) enhanced by a plate full of added flavors (caper-olive mashed potatoes, YUM) that made it even more savory. My only complaint was the very unappetizing curly herbs on top of the plate - I apologize in advance if I gross anyone out, but it looked like a pile of green hair. So, NOT okay. I quickly stuffed it under a bread plate, and, out of sight, out of mind, I was able to enjoy my meal. My dad had the angus market steak, and considering the man knows his steak, the glowing review he gave it must mean it's worth a try. We finished with the blueberry-peach crisp and WOW. While it's a pretty large portion, great for sharing, you may not want to. It's so deletectably awesome, save your calories by not eating an appetizer so you can have this all to yourself!
label: POS

text: I think everybody who has reviewed this before has pretty much said it all, but I HAVE to put my two cents in anyway! This place is outstanding!! Yes, it is loud and crowded and the help can be a bit aloof from time to time, but you would expect that from a place this busy that people enjoy this much!! Their beer selection is second to none in Boise. It has a great craft beer selection on tap and if you need more, check out the bottled beer selection!! I was truly impressed! The level of quality doesn't stop with the beer. They have the best pub food in town. Hands down. The last time I was there I had the best Reuben I have ever had. The food is all real food, no cisco here, (or at least you can't tell) make their own ketchup!? The clam chowder is probably better than most of what i have tasted in Seattle!!, and the hamburger was the best my friend had every had! I have to say that I think this place would do very well in Seattle. It would hang right in there with Brouwers, The Naked City ale house, The Collins Pub, etc in Seattle. While I was in the Bittercreek I actually felt more like I was in Seattle than Boise because of how well they have designed the interior, the food and the beer selection. Definitely has more of a big city feel to it. I love craft beer, Belgian style strong ales, great food and a fun authentic pub environment, and you can get that here. In Boise, Idaho! Feel lucky Boise, you've got a good one there!

text: My boyfriend surprised me with dinner out last Friday to celebrate our anniversary. He chose Oh Yumm Bistro. We are new to Indy, so when we first pulled up I was like "Are you kidding?" I started with the beet salad which was great, although I would have liked a few more beets haha. My boyfriend had the rack of lamb special with tzaziki sauce and loved it. I also had the chocolate chip bread pudding for desert and it was so tasty. Bread pudding is one of my favorite desserts and I am very picky about the texture and taste. I am frequently disappointed but this was not the case. I had to move the plate to the other side of the table to stop eating it. It was so good. I'm definitely planning to eat there again!
