text: We had my bachelor party in New Orleans and all of the guys stayed here at the Rathbone Inn. What an awesome place! We had the "Mardi Gras" suite. It was the off-season in between Jazz fest and Mardi Gras, so the price was ridiculously reasonable. They offer off-street parking, however, its a tiny lot and they ask that you leave them your keys so they will move your vehicle if it is blocking someone else in. The lady running the office is very nice and I would definitely trust leaving her the keys to my car. The room was absolutely huge. There were 2 twin size beds, a king size bed and a living room with a pull-out couch. The room offered 2 private balconies! One was absolutely huge, the whole length of one side of the building. We felt like kings sitting on the balcony, overlooking the beautiful street. The smaller balcony was a little more rickety, but safe enough for 2 people at a time. It's about a 15 minute walk to the busiest part of Bourbon Street, if that's what you're after. We didn't mind the walk, but we only stayed one night. It might get tedious if you're there for a longer period of time. I'm sure you could get a quick taxi ride to the hotel if you don't want to walk it. The breakfast was also really good. Homemade coffee cake and muffins, fresh squeezed juice and coffee. We definitely ate our fill to nurse the hangovers. This place lives up to the legend of New Orleans hospitality. Very kind and helpful owners/managers with great suggestions and a good attitude. Also, the B&B is haunted. I know that a LOT of places in NOLA claim to be haunted, but the Rathbone actually has documentation of previous hauntings in the room that you can read through. It gives an up-to-date list of things people have seen and heard in the room you're sleeping in! We didn't experience any paranormal activity while we were there, but maybe our partying scared the ghosts away! I'm pretty sure the prices are exponentially higher during the peak seasons, but if you have the money or are planning to visit during the off-season, this is the B&B for you.

text: After shopping at the Tuesday farmers market, I met up with some friends at Madisons. Now, my normal happy hour spot is Sharkeez, and I don't think that will ever change. However, Madisons wasn't half as slimy as I'd thought (which I suppose doesn't make sense given that Sharkeez is pretty damn slimy itself.) Anyway, We sat on the patio which had some cute Xmas lights and a pretty nice feel - kind of like one of the chain places, Dave and Busters and such (not that I've ever been, but I have seen commercials.) Happy hour offered half price appetizers and $4 beers (Sharkeez offers 2 beers for $5 and most of their appetizers are less than $3.) The appetizer menu selection was actually pretty good, and ended up getting the Buffalo Chicken bites and a Sierra Nevada. I don't care how many people feel like the Burger King himself while drinking out of those huge, unruly glass goblets; I don't like them. I prefer a nice pint glass - something easy to manage when you lose your sense of balance. The chicken bites were actually pretty good. They didn't skimp on the hot sauce, which is my favorite part of chicken wings/buffalo chicken bites. I tried some of my friends Artichoke & Spinach dip, which looked awesome in the mini cast iron skillet, but paled in comparison to Traders Joes version, which costs about the same. I also tried the jalapeno poppers, which I didn't love, but combined with the raspberry sauce they came with, actually surprised me! Ok, so now I justify the 2 stars: - 1 Star. Sitting the the patio in downtown SB should be like sitting on a beach in Tahiti - awesome. However, you're only steps away from the sidewalk, and sadly, can't pretend not to notice when some drunk (not always homeless) dude walks buy screaming at you for a lite. I don't smoke, but would've offered the lighter if I had it. The issue was that he kept asking, ever after we'd all told him twice that we didn't have a lighter. - 2 Stars. The whole, "this could be a chain place," thing isn't totally appealing. I suppose it has it's benefits: cheap food, kind of cheap beer. However, I expect the atmosphere at a "fun" bar to inspire the spirit in you, and being someone easily influenced by atmosphere, I was let down. - 3 Stars. As slimy as it felt (this is another place I'd expect to meet an annoying, loud-mouthed Frat boy, whom after two beers, I'd approach with the intention of humiliating) there was no charm. When I do happy hour, I'm made aware that I'm "one of those people." You know, the kind who drinks during the day. I don't have any problem with this because, one, I only do this twice a month, and two, I am indeed, drinking at 4 pm on a weekday. The normal Madisons patron gives the impression that taking shots at 4 pm in the afternoon is normal and hip. The normal Sharkeez patron looks a little run down - like there may be a reason they are drinking at 4 pm on a weekday. And you know what? More often that not, there is a reason I'm drinking at 4 pm on a weekday. In the off chance that I've decided to come out to drink just for the fun of it, I'd probably go to Sharkeez anyway. I'm cheap :) All in all, this isn't my favorite place, but I'd go again.

text: I'm not a vegetarian, but having been very disappointed by other Chinese food in the Collingswood area, I figured I had nothing to lose by trying Green House. I'm so glad I did! The sesame seitan and general tso tofu are two of my favorites. I really liked the chow mei fun, but will ask them to include a few more veggies next time. I'm excited to try some of the more adventurous options on the menu. They do have a wide selection of bubble teas and fruit slushes - which (at the time of visit) come free with a meal as part of a grand opening promotion. The dining room is nothing special, but spacious, so you'll probably never have to wait for a table. This is a BYOB, so it's a great place to share a bottle of wine with friends. I ordered takeout one night and it was very fast. While I was waiting, the hostess (owner?) was very engaging and explained different things on the menu. So nice! If you like Su Xing or Kingdom of Vegetarian in Philly, you'll be right at home in Green House. If you haven't tried veg Chinese before, give it a shot. It's not like your corner Chinese takeout place uses high grade quality meat in their dishes anyway, so why not try some seitan or tofu? It actually tastes better.

text: My wild, devil-may-care, dangerous friends somehow entangled me in their net of mischief one night in their sudden, random search to play ping pong. Yeah, these guys are the kind you don't want your daughters crossing the street for. Anyway, who figured it would be tough to get a game of ping pong. What we were faced with when we walked in was slightly different. A single room with a ambiance I would describe as "dirty" still somehow felt inviting in a cold war kind of way. Perhaps it was the lone, neck-braced woman playing pool. Or maybe it was the white suited Russian "businessman" sitting and sipping what I'm sure was vodka. Still, it could have been the 3 Pagans, proudly displaying their motorcycle patches on their denim and leather vests. No ping pong table in sight. But did that matter? I asked for a bloody mary, at the bar. Right after breaking up what could have been a pro communism conversation between bartender and some guy. The bartender said the closest he could get to a bloody mary was a screw driver. I bought a Sam Adams. For a $1. Fast forward through the rest of the evening, as their are simply too many incidents to mention. We left late night/early morning, having our fill of beer, ping pong (yes, they wheeled it out for us), and interesting people. And the night was still going, as two lady deejays were just starting to unpack their equipment. I was told RUBA stands for Russian Ukranian Boating Association. But no matter what it stands for, you're always going to have an interesting night if you go. Sure, it's private club, not usually open to the public, but the security is less than strict, and we were offered membership at the end of the evening - for an annual fee of $5. text: Always on the lookout for a good meal at a fair deal, especially when traveling, it never hurts to ask a well-fed looking local. Thus prepared, four hungry travelers rolled into the deep NOLA warehouse 'hood to sample a restaurant recommended by two area hipster types as "my favorite place to eat". With no reservations we could have been immediately seated in the back room. Instead, we asked to wait a few minute's at the bar for a table in the much livelier main dining room. The young n' hunky bartender (hunky per L. and K. the vivacious females in our party) mixed up some excellently classic cocktails while we waited. Despite my initial skepticism, the guy turned out to be one of the better bartenders I've been served by. Soon seated, we found ourselves more excited by the intricate appetizers than the more vanilla-sounding entrees. The starters were so tantalizing in description that we ordered eight (of nine, less the charcuterie plate) and skipped the entrees entirely. It turned out to be a meal not to regret. However - I would caution others NOT to repeat our folly. The starters, especially the crab and asparagus gratin dish, were a delight, but so rich that none of us could face dessert. In a nod to the staff, halfway thru our our meal the building power went out, darkening the whole neighborhood. Candles were quickly it, and glasses refilled. After fifteen minutes the lights came back on. We discovered later that the maitre'd had negotiated a reprieve (possibly involving a little lagniappe?) with a nearby utility work crew to provide power until 10 PM (closing time). Our waitress and the kitchen apparently never missed a beat, and our meal service was flawless. All told, our meal at Dick & Jenny's was a little slice of Nawlins heaven. Local food, fair prices, great flavors and service, all in a funky homestyle spot that felt like home.

text: We stayed here Labor Day weekend 2010....Sept 4th.-Sept. 6th and let me start by saying this is not a Luxury Motel as they advertise. Let me also say that NO MOTEL in the history of MOTELS can ever be considered Luxurious. Now with that issue all cleared up...let me say that the rooms are very spacious...great beds...sleeper sofa...nice huge work desk to work on...fridge...great air conditioning...ceiling fan....and a pool. Now those were the good things about a Standard Hotel room...in a Motel setting...not to bad...but now here comes the bad news: First of all there are no free complimentary items...like toothpaste...or a toothbrush...or mouthwash...or shampoo...or anything that you may have left at home by mistake and need to have for your personal hygiene. Luxury hotels do offer those items...FOR FREE. The Free Wi-fi...wow what a joke....it is the slowest free Wi-fi i have ever seen. Luxury hotels offer free High speed internet and you can believe you won't have any problems with SPEED...because your paying for luxury. The bathroom was incredibly small...the toilet is right by the door so you can barely sit down and close the door. The shower was not bad..but the sink was not in the same room as the toilet and shower and in a LUXURY hotel those areas are all together. We got only one wash cloth even though there were 2 of us...but they give you two hand towels and 2 bath towels. There was no FLAT SCREEN TV....LIKE LUXURY HOTELS HAVE....but i didn't really have any complaints about that because the TV was decent. However the carpet or rug if you call it on the floor was sticky and uncomfortable...so i had to keep my Crocs on most of the time. Luxury Hotels have nice carpert or rugs and it is keep clean . The front desk staffer was "a matter of fact" person...but not friendly and i don't really know why because considering the town and area she should be thankful to have a job. Now the hotel, while right off interstate 10, is in a great location with no traffic really because it sits at the "wrong way" end of the expressway...so that was a plus. The pool however was very small considering this "Motel" is pretty big and it even has long term tenants. So i bet your wondering why i gave this locale 4 stars...well the price of course...it cost only 73 dollars for the two nights we were there...and that includes tax....that is an unbeatable deal. So if your ever in Tucson, AZ and need a nice Motel to stay in for cheap...not a luxury hotel, and you can handle paying a buck for any personal items you may have left at home...then the best value inn is your place. Eat, Drink, and Be Merry my Friends!!!!!

text: I was honestly surprised to see this place have anything more than two stars. I have been here multiple times as a result of working in the Malvern area and not having very many other happy hour locations available. The only positive things I can say about this place is that they have a nice outdoor area and they have pool tables in the basement. I should warn you that the basement is pretty lame looking and reminds me of a basement at someone's house. If it was really at someone's house it would be amazing, but for a bar it is depressing. Now moving onto some negative attributes about McKenzie's. I guess the first thing to point out is that they are a brew house and they successfully make some of the worst beer I have ever tasted at a brew house. I have tried so many different varieties of their beer and always been disappointed. They do a great job making their beer sound good, but a terrible job delivering. I started to order just their basic lager and even that is terrible. I don't know what they do wrong, but I have tried a ton of beers and never been as consistently disappointed as I am with this place. Do yourself a favor and order a mixed drink at this place. So the beer is terrible, but the food must be good right? Wrong...The food at this place is not good at all. I wouldn't go as far as saying it is terrible, but they manage to take very simple sandwiches and make them boring and dull. The buffalo chicken sliders for example, I ordered these at a lunch and could not believe that they could make me not want to eat a buffalo chicken sandwich. It's not very hard to make, all you need is some breaded chicken, a roll, some buffalo sauce and blue cheese. McKenzie's turns this into a dried up mess on a terrible roll. As you can probably guess if the beer is bad and the food is bad the service is also probably bad. I am happy to report that the service is also terrible. I will only highlight two of my particularly bad experiences at this place. The first was a lunch experiences where we ended up waiting about 45 minutes for a food to come out and 20 minutes for our check to come out. We had scheduled two hours for lunch so it was not a huge deal, but taking that long is ridiculous. A second lovely experience I had at this place was a happy hour where a friend found broken glass in his beer. I understand this can potentially happen at a restaurant, but it is a pretty big deal and you would think a manager would realize that. When we told the manager about the glass instead of being apologetic, he acted surprised and was slightly argumentative about it (not sure what there was to argue about the glass was very obvious). He ended up giving us a free round of drinks, but didn't bother telling us that or thanking us for being understanding, he just took it off the bill after being a jerk at the table. I could go on and on about McKenzie's but I think I have given enough reasons why not to go here. If you are looking for bad food, worse beer and awful service McKenzie's is your spot. If you have 15 minutes to spare do yourself a favor and drive to King of Prussia or Phoenixville, there are plenty of good spots there.

text: My co-workers and I were in town for business and decided to try the Weber Grill out. Who can't resist a restaurant with a red Weber Grill mounted on the building?! We didn't make reservations but were able to get a table. I would recommend making reservations to be safe. We loved the display of different Weber grills in the entrance and the open kitchen. It's darkly lit and nicely decorated - their wooden chairs bear a Weber grill cut-out. A few of us ordered orange cream soda. The bottle of soda was chilled and the waiter poured it into a glass without ice. Next time, I'm going to ask for ice; I like cold soda. We ordered two combos (BBQ pork ribs/Brisket, BBQ pork ribs/pulled pork), a full slab of ribs, and a NY steak prepared medium rare. They came with a side of vineagrette coleslaw with a little kick, baked beans and moist, sweet cornbread. The ribs were succulent, full of flavor, and almost fell off the bone. They had a nice rich smokey flavor, and it's not coming from the BBQ sauce! The brisket was ok, next time I'd get the pulled pork all for myself - it was sooo delicious. The steak was perfectly cooked and a nice size. The portions were so good that we didn't even have room for dessert! The waiter told us that at some point all food hits the Weber grills during cooking. This restaurant didn't disappoint in their food and service! I would go back again when in downtown Indy.

Sure, it's a little pricey, but a good meal is like a trip to the day spa -- every now and then, you just gotta splurge and give yourself a treat. Don't worry, White Dog. text: This is a review for Gray Line's Katrina tour. My husband and I booked it based on a recommendation from the NYT Travel section (http://tinyurl.com/aeybsk), but unfortunately this was definitely our least favorite part of our New Orleans trip. If you want to do a tour, our best experience was doing the Cajun Encounters Swamp Tour, which was not only better, but cheaper to boot. First of all, the tour should have been shorter, because the tour guide repeated himself constantly instead of giving us new or interesting information. Although we did drive by levees and through the 9th Ward, too much of the tour was the guide simply pointing out "this house has been rebuilt to be elevated" or "this house is not elevated." Frankly, five years after the hurricane, this tour just isn't as powerful because there's so little to see anymore: most of the search and rescue marking have been painted over, homes rebuilt, etc. The tour bus is also not allowed to go into certain areas, such as the new modular homes that Brad Pitt invested in following Katrina. Second, the tour guide was not very professional. I sympathize with allergies, but it's not a nice experience to have your tour guide snuffling and snorting into the microphone. Worse, the guide was simply not knowledgeable. Although he gave us the information about the hurricane turning course, he really provided little to no information about FEMA or the state's response, or the aftermath of insurance, etc. This contributed to the repetitiveness of the tour, because he ran out of new things to say.

You know... the dainty toothpicks thru Club sandwiches to "hold" them together... well, 4 Club sections & 4 toothpicks is what it seems like...Oph! Wait! As it raises to jowel-level, there's another toothpick in there? Broken, splintered, like the "chef," more like a "mash up" of foods put a toothpick thru, it broke, then put another one thru but didn't take out the bad one? Que? Wha? That's that...fine... it's forgivable really... oph! Wait! No it's not because the food was that bad. D'you feel that? Just then... that was my 2 year old niece rolling over in her sleep making a better club sandwich than this. And, yeah, you heard her right she just said, "Oops I just yelped in my pants," and that's better than the veggie quesadilla they're offering here. I asked directly, "what comes in the veggie 'dilla?" So the momentum builds... cheese, peppers, tomatoes, mushrooms, thud. That's all. Then, it was even worse when it was created. Nothing to it. You want guacamole? Yes, that's like a giant veggie savior to this whole thing. Oph! Wait! You just turned mayo green & added tomatoes! WHAT!? That's a food code violation offense thing isn't it? Like... could we shut them down for that? Really... they're serving up guacamole that's not guacamole AND up charging for it. To me... that's like saying you're from Texas when you're from Kennebunkport & then running for President by saying you're from Texas & winning off of it. Hey Red Eye Cafe... Hey Mayonnaise... you can't just go and ride the coattails of the avocado and say you're an avocado. Isn't that in the Bible? Wow. Sure, you deliver food all night, but look what it is & it's not even what you say it is. Barbara Ehrenreich inspired Yelpatrol in full effect. Busted.

For a place with a pig on the sign, this was disappointing. -The fried Peanut-butter Banana pie desert was not very good--too fried, weird texture. The Pros: Most of the food was great. Souffled grits with venison? Yum-O. Warm cabbage salad with hog jowls and goat cheese? Sign me up. The Boar sausage with saurkraut was surprisingly delish. And the strawberry baked alaska was a nice way to end a meal. The service was great-- we had 2 waitresses, both keeping an eye on us, and making conversation when time allowed. We gave them a heads-up that we were hoping to get out by 11:30 or so, and they did their darnedest, and even managed to have a cab waiting for us when we were done (we couldn't even get through to a cab company on our cell phone, so this was quite a feat). Despite their efforts, we were stuck in traffic when the clock struck 12, and we missed the festivities. Too Bad-- If we had foreseen that, we would have gladly stayed at Cochon, lingered over some bubbly and enjoyed the casual, comfortable space and friendly staff into 2010.

text: I rarely write an update to my reviews unless I'm majorly changing my prior rating. But having been back a few times I have to say this is becoming one of my "go to" places in St. Louis. Personally I'd have probably found another solution (thicker cut fries, automation timers a la McDonalds, etc.) since I think this was one of the kitschy draws of the first time visitor. But they are doing a solid enough business. Speaking of business, I've noticed a distinctly younger hipper crowd making up a broader portion of the clientele over the last year. Really happy to see that. Lastly, an old college friend of mine was in town directing a video shoot a few blocks away from The Shaved Duck so it was the natural choice to take him to. But we were both left perplexed by how a minor hiccup was handled by Matt (the bartender, and also serving us). While placing my order he and I apparently had a miscommunication about the 2nd dish that I ordered. When they brought it out and I said that it wasn't what I had ordered (mind you, we were there for the long haul so this wasn't even treated as an annoyance by me, just a smile and a 'no problem' when told I'd have to wait a few minutes for the right dish to be brought out). It was at this point that Matt decided to stop by and state that I *did* order that dish, but that they'd make me the other one. He didn't say it rude or anything, but for the life of us we couldn't figure out why he would do that. Even in situations where you have a real prick who completely screwed up and blamed you for it, you simply *don't* go to the customer and try and tell them why they are wrong and you're not. There's just no benefit to it. That said, he was still very nice the rest of the night and I didn't hold it against him, it was frankly just odd.

It came with an ample serving of shrimp and several tempura vegetables, such as eggplant, sweet potato, squash and green pepper. It came with a side of rice as well. We had the clear soup , which was an excellent home made chicken broth with scallions and mushrooms. The room is elegantly simple and the tables are separated by a bamboo screen and drawn back curtains, so it makes for an intimate setting. Our waiter was extremely attentive and friendly. We will back soon to try the sushi. An excellent spot in Palm Harbor!

text: This place offers the worst of the worst of Americanized Chinese. Previously I'd been to the lunch buffet and swore I'd never return, but one of my co-workers insisted that dinner was a different matter. The dining room carpet was still repulsively grotty and the place still smelled of burned onions. I got the Special Dinner B to go. I started with the Hot and Sour Seafood soup. It didn't have any seafood in it. It was piping hot out of the styrofoam container but bland. The sourness was dull instead of tangy. There wasn't even a nibble of hottness, let alone a proper bite to offset the sour. I followed with the appetizers. Fried shrimp, BBQ Spare Ribs, Egg Roll, Paper Wrapped Chicken. The Chicken was the best of the bunch being at least inoffensively bland. Everything else was deep-fried and sodden with grease rendering it virtually indistinguishable. The shrimp was vulcanized and it's breading scorched to a dark brown. The flavor of the grease suggests that the deep fryer oil hasn't been changed this decade. The ribs were, I think, burned all to hell. It's hard to tell since they were also coated in a foul sauce that smelled of burning socks (no kidding). I didn't finish the ribs. The egg roll had a good crisp wrapper, but unfortunately the contents were best described as a slimy emulsion of grease and unidentifiable vegetal matter. For the main, I chose General Tso's Chicken. It's has a little chili beside it on the menu, signifying hot and spicy. It was not. Think instead dried out chicken remnants coated in scorched breading smothered in a slightly sweet but mostly gloppy sauce. Cornstarch is not a foundation for flavor. The fried rice tasted like scorched onions (clean your stove) and old grease. I also got some plain white rice since I figured the fried might not be all that good, and you can always pull dried white rice out of the fridge and use it to make your own fried rice. The white rice was dense (loft it when the rice cooker finishes and release some steam). I'm trying to find something positive to say about the place.The service was friendly. They included napkins and some of that awesome yellow mustard you can't hardly find in the grocery stores.

text: I'm not really the kind of person who goes to country clubs, since I've never had, and probably never will have, that kind of money. That being said, I love it when the opportunity arises to visit one. (It's nice to at least feel rich sometimes.) So when my friend asked me to substitute for him at his chapter's weekly BNI meeting for two weeks in a row, I happily obliged. Although it was challenging to overcome the Broad Street triumvirate of construction sites, the usual volume of traffic, and the assholes double-parked in the right lane, my experience at Talamore made the journey worthwhile. Its outside appearance is pretty subdued, but has some nice features, like a lovely fountain right outside the double-door entrance and tasteful shrubbery. When you enter, there's a sign pointing BNI members and visitors towards the conference hall, which is helpful for those visiting for the first time. Enter the conference room. To say it was a wide-open space would be an understatement. The high ceiling is adorned with a lovely chandelier that emits a warm light, which perfectly complements the sunlight pouring in from the large windows. It really is the perfect room to hold a conference or important meeting. Since lunch is included in BNI members' monthly dues, I had the opportunity to sample a couple of dishes. The salmon was cooked perfectly, drizzled with what I perceived to be a dill cream sauce, and accompanied by rice and a melange of steamed zucchini, yellow squash, and carrots. The Caesar salad was made with their own delectable creamy Caesar dressing and contained real lettuce (none of that iceberg crap!) and freshly baked croutons. I found both meals to my liking. Of course, Talamore also has all of the obligatory country-club amenities, such as a golf course, banquet halls, fitness center, pool, et cetera. However, I didn't have the pleasure of using any of these perks, so you'll just have to check them out for yourself (provided that you can afford their dues, of course!).

text: Wonderful service, very attentive and knowledgeable staff. A little more pricey than we normally go but the food was very well prepared and presented. I had a Cosmo to drink. Their cocktails were a little on the sweet side...but I tend to like my mixed drinks that way. I had the pan roasted Barramundi with Yukon gold potato gnocchi, fondue of sweet peppers, grilled portabellas, and spinach, tapenade. I didn't know what Barramundi was but was told it is similar to cod. It had a nice sweet, mild taste...not fishy smelling or tasting at all, it was prepared very well. It was served over the potato gnocchi and vegetable mixture, which was a little rich for my taste as the entree was served in a creamed sauce. My husband had the roast chicken entree. His chicken was very moist and flavorful. For dessert we split their famous bread pudding and a strawberry shortcake. The shortcake had a nice crisp and flaky texture with an abundance of strawberries beneath it and topped off with ice cream. The bread pudding was wonderful but very rich. It reminded me of a sweet, moist but dense pancake swimming in caramel syrup. It is definitely worth trying as well as sharing.

text: Find Ooka near Best Buy, across the street from Soundex. They're open seven days a week for both lunch and dinner, and serve Japanese cuisine. Around 2006, the restaurant underwent a makeover - maturing from an ugly duckling (a typical Japanese restaurant) and now is modern chic - every detail, from the columns, to the windows, to the menus, was affected, but luckily the prices suffered nary a bit. For years, I've come here for lunch, and at least twice for dinner. Their sushi rolls are prepared with panache and come out fresh and tasty - they've got personality, son! Unsurprisingly, their hibachi (table-side cooking) rocks here as well, thanks in no small part to their the flavorful, colorful sauces, and cuts of meat. (They also have a fried ice cream dessert which is a delight.) Service is top-notch - servers are efficient, friendly, and the hibachi chefs I've had have been talented and entertaining. With fast service, quality food, and attractive decor, what have you got to lose? Worth the drive, and it's right off the Turnpike!

text: Like all other goods and services, those who would use the Phlash trolley service are advised "buyer beware". In particular, when you board a Phlash trolley, and before you pay the fare, ask the driver if they are going to the stop you want to reach, and if the trolley will travel the complete route, as advertised. On July 4th, my wife and I boarded a Phlash trolley at 16th and Market St., with the intention of going to Penn's Landing. The driver took our money, and gave us two tickets for single rides. He said nothing at that time to indicate that the trolley would not complete its normal route, nor were there any signs posted that would indicate that the trolley was not going to Penn's Landing. However, shortly after the trolley pulled out into traffic on Market St., heading East, the driver announced on the PA system that the next stop, at 12th and Market, would be the last stop of the day, and that the trolley service was ending. When the trolley stopped at 12th and Market, we asked the driver why, at the time that we bought our tickets, he had not mentioned that service was being halted, and that the very next stop would be the last one for the day. He blustered that he had been making this announcement all along, but had to admit that he had not told us this, before he took our money. Another couple, who had bought two all day passes were similarly surprised by his announcement. He told us and the other couple that he could not give us a refund, nor issue a "rain check", to be used on another day. When we said that he had acted irresponsibly, he said that he was taking responsibility, because he had said that, "he was sorry". He may have said he was "sorry", but his behavior showed that he was anything but sorry.
label: NEG

The security guard at the gate will not allow you entry if your name isn't on their guest roster. USD 15 per person admission fee, allow at least two to three hours to walk through. There's a self audio guide available for USD 7, there's also a free guided tour available. We went for one at noon and takes about an hour or so. Once your done with the collection inside, take a walk around and notice the artwork along the top edge of the building you were just inside of, and admire the grounds, there's a pond. The atmosphere here is quite peaceful and will be different once it's relocated in Philadelphia. There's no food nor drinks sold on the grounds, best to eat before arriving at the grounds. We arrived by bus, got off where the Barnes was, backtracked to where the bus turned, found a Wendy's at 259 West City Ave for a meal first. If arriving by train, eat prior to boarding. text: As others have reported: the all you can eat sushi experience is a shit show. We arrived for our 9:30 reservation and were told it might be 20 minutes before we were seated. So, right there, you get off to a bad start. After about 30 minutes we were suddenly told that we couldn't stand where we were standing and ushered to another area. Another ten minutes passed before we were seated. It was, at one point, suggested that we buy drinks to pass the time. One key way to keep hungry, hungry people from being in foul moods when made to wait? Comp them a stinkin' beverage, don't suggest that they happily endure your unpreparedness Eventually we were seated. And our waiter promptly asked us what we wanted to drink and took our order, but the fact that one of our party was allergic to shrimp threw a new wrench into the works. While, having had limited food service experience, I understand that this sort of 'all you can eat' deal necessarily leads to a frenzied environment, it truly seems like they could have prepared for the possibility that someone with an allergy might want to participate. They hadn't...and originally told my friend that they could not guarantee that any sushi wasn't contaminated, but that she was free to order off the kitchen menu, which was, you know, not what she came and waited 40 minutes to do. The situation was positively resolved, but it wasn't without a fair amount of tension and stress. The sushi itself was fine considering the strain all the sushi chefs were under (you don't go to an all you can eat sushi experience expecting the most perfectly rolled maki of your life). I don't want to sound too grumpy, I do understand that this restuarant probably functions much better under normal circumstances...but the fact that we weren't comped a roll or drink after a 40 minute wait and a 10 minute period in which one of our party might not have been able to eat without risking her life is, well, really annoying. (All that said: our waiter was great and management did the best they could, I'm sure) The end.

I drive by the downtown branch 10x every week, but I would rather pick my materials up at the Hillcrest Branch (in the Hillcrest shopping center down by Honks) than fight the traffic and wade into the main branch during the afternoon commute. The few times I've needed to speak to either circulation or the referrence desk by phone the staff and librarians have been wonderfully helpful. Staff at the check out desk downtown AND at Hillcrest are also delightful. I espeically appreciate Sam at the Hillcrest Branch. I will state, from my own experience that parking at the downtown branch SUCKS. Pair tight spaces on a one way grid with inconsiderate drivers and cyclists who don't grant right of way when they should and children being allowed to run loose through the lot and you get my picture. text: Let me start with everything Fozzies did wrong. First of all, the indoor seating is laughable. With only 4 two-top tables in a cramped dining/ordering area, you're only reliable choices are carry out or eating outside in the unpredictable St. Louis weather. The patio doesn't even have full over-head coverage, only one of those drapey triangles that always irritate the hell out of me because they don't maximize the use of cubic inches. Secondly, they don't have french fries. Not a huge deal, they got homemade potato chips right? Well, yes they are homemade. And the flavor of the Parmesan & Herb Chips is really really good. HOWEVER, they did not give the chips ample time to drain the grease off and just chucked them into the little brown paper bags and sealed them up. This meant that the left-over grease and steam had nowhere to go which made for soggie potato chips. Out of my entire bag (about the size of a Billy Goat Chips bag) I had maybe 5 tolerable chips. It was a waste. I ordered a burger, a double patty with just ketchup because I'm a purist. And it was the GREASIEST burger I have ever had in my entire life. I even sopped up some of the grease with my napkins. Now let me tell you now, that I am not afraid of grease. I love greasy things. But when the burger is so greasy that it soaks completely through your bun, rendering the bun practically useless, I must object. It was also served medium with a little pink in it, which I like, but some people may not, and seeing as how they didn't ask me if that was my preference, I can assume that they haven't quite perfected cook times on the grill. I also got a "large" chocolate shake. The shake was a joke. At nearly FIVE DOLLARS ($4.75) I got a 16 oz (yes, really sixteen ounce) shake that was obviously made with hershey's syrup. Again, it's not like I hate hershey's syrup, but I feel like if you're going to charge that much for something that small it better be amazing. Or if its going to be that pedestrian at that price, then it better be cheap. The other little, annoying things were that a sign was prominently displayed and visible by every one that "employees must pay for their drinks. No free drinks!" Yeah, I get the policy, you're a fledgling business. But it's just tacky. Train your staff. Make sure they understand that drinks are not free and there will be consequences if they steal one. By the way, the drink selection was limited to cans of soda and jumex. Not a wide selection and I really don't like that its just served in cans. I like ice a lot, so it bums me out that it wasn't an option. But I get it, fountain soda and ice machines are expensive and take up valuable real estate... All that being said, there are still some saving graces here. First of all, despite the limited space, they decorate with punchy colors and awesome lettering. And the burger, while greasy, was incredibly flavorful, just black pepper as far as I could tell, but really tasty. And like I said, the chips had an excellent flavor. If they hadn't been soggy, I'm sure I would have enjoyed them. They are also eco-conscious with a recycling bin and veggie and herb garden in the back (my favorite part). It's nice to know that the tomatoes on my husbands sandwich probably have a carbon footprint of zero. Also, the staff was friendly and fast. I think I'm going to wait a bit and see if they improve, because if they do, I would love going here.

text: This is a must-go location in Philly if you haven't been. I wouldn't come to Philly specifically for Independence Hall but it's still a worth while stop. It's the most important building in American history as well as one of the most picturesque spots in the city. In addition to the building itself the grounds (both in front and behind) are beautifully maintained and have plenty of open space. Unfortunately you can't just walk into the building and walk around at your leisure but it's extremely easy to walk into the visitors center get a free tour ticket and go over to the building and wait for the next tour to begin. The visitors center I've found is pretty boring and consists mostly of wordy plaques with lots of reading (and very few if any historical artifacts). Make sure to also visit the famous bell in the building adjacent to the visitors center, it's a little over-rated but it's free and it's a great part of history. The tour of the hall is very short but extremely informative and brings you into the two main rooms of the hall, the court room, and the meeting room where the Declaration of Independence was written. The rooms don't have a lot of original furniture but much attention has been paid to make both rooms as authentic as possible. It's a great experience to be in the space where the nation was practically born and then leave the building and stand in the back were the Declaration was first read to the people of Philadelphia.

text: I think I am in love with Roast Pork.... I finally got a chance to try the much-talked-about Roast Pork Sandwiches... I am generally not a huge fan of pork because of that strong flavor that needs lots of spices to overpower it... but this.. this was perfect. They have it down to a science I had 2 different kinds of roast pork sandwiches - you an choose from sweet/hot peppers, sharp provolone, broccoli rabe/spinach Spicy : Hot peppers with Sharp provolone and spinach The Mild: sweet peppers and sharp provolon and broccoli rabe. I have to say, that I was a huge fan of the meat. perfectly roasted. The natural juices is incredibly balanced. The amount of fat to full on flavor is perfect. The meat is sliced thin and against the grain... I am telling you, this is my new favorite iconic philly sandwich. In the sandwiches, the sharp provolone is key in the spicy version. The pungent creaminess of the cheese works perfectly with the hot peppers. I was glad to go with the spinach on the spicy sandwich because the broccoli rabe in the milder version was far too watery and made the bread fall apart - difficult to eat.. but worth it. if you are planning on trying both spicy and mild... try the mild first becuase the spicy will overpower the flavor of the milder one. If you havent tried this.. go... GO SKIP the cheesesteaks... (you can always get that later because Reading Terminal Market is only open until 5pm.) GO stand in the long line.. it is so worth your time.

text: I've been dying to find good Italian food in St Louis. Unimpressed with the restaurants on the Hill, I decided to try Acero. Acero is exactly what I had been looking for. The server was very attentive (almost too attentive but I'm not going to complain) and when I asked if the the spaghetti alla chitarra (an amatriciana sauce) was made with pancetta and the waitress repiled that it was actually made with guanciale, I fell in love. Guanciale is the cut of meat traditionally used in Italy but rarely used in the states because it's hard to find. And luckily, the pasta did not disappoint. The home made spaghetti was cooked perfectly al dente and the sauce was phenomenal. I finished the meal with the chocolate torte which was rich and warm and wonderful. text: I went last weekend to Ikkyu, and with the black curtains on the windows, i never could gauge how nice, busy, or large the restaurant was. I noticed that almost everyone else ordered donburi (rice bowls) or ramen. I tried the salmon bento box, cold buckwheat noodles, super hiro sushi roll, and the baked scallop roll. For all this, it was about $25, so if you love sushi, this is a great affordable place. It was at least ten minutes wait, but I didn't mind. It was slightly chaotic inside, so I decided to eat outside. The first thing I tried was the cold buckwheat noodles (about $4). It was so good. If you love udon, you should try this special. Dark colored noodles but tasted like udon noodles with a soy sauce type condiment, green onions, and seaweed. If you don't like seaweed, don't get this dish. So refreshing cold. Then, I tried the salmon bento box. You get a huge piece of salmon and a bunch of side dishes - the option for brown rice or white rice, seaweed salad, squid salad, and more. What a healthy meal with a lot of flavors! Where Ikkyu really shines is their sushi rolls. Now, their sushi rolls are huge, so if you want one-bite pieces and are picky about that, this is not the place for you. I do like sushi rolls that sometimes are like a meal. The baked scallop roll was amazing - a California roll with Japanese mayonnaise with spices/baked scallops on top. Even more amazing was the Super Hiro Roll - a medley of delicious seafood! I feel like Ikkyu definitely hit all my savory tastebuds! The spices were spot on. Come to Ikkyu if you want to get your money's worth and not spend too much. Be prepared for the busyness of this restaurant to be in waves. It is a casual sit-down place.

They've never experienced any Jewish tradition, so I thought it would be a fun experience for them. This deli's website said they offered sufganiyot (jelly filled fried donuts) which were "direct from Israel". At $1.25 a donut, they'd better be. Well, they weren't. Some Jewish guy in the back fries them up and barely fills them with some tasteless jelly. When I got back to my friend's place, I opened the aluminum tray and saw 12 odd-shaped flat pucks of various shades of brown. The area of the donut where they squeezed the barely there jelly through was torn and flattened as if someone stuck a fat thumb through the donut. These 12 throw-away sufganiyot cost me over $16. For a dozen crappy donuts!!! Needless to say, I was extremely embarrassed to serve these to our friends. While at the store I was also hoping to buy some lunch and perhaps some market goods. When I looked at the prices and quantities, I was shocked to see how overpriced ALL the items were. I've bought kosher and Israeli items plenty of times before at other stores in other states, and I expect the sticker shock. However, the prices in this place seemed like they were taking advantage of their clientele. WAAAY OVERPRICED. On top of the all that, the two people working the register and counter were extremely unfriendly. There were also 3 over-dressed women customers who refused to move away from the counter to let me pay when my order came up. They were so close I swear they wanted to see what was in my wallet. The only reason I can give as to why I was given such obviously crappy donuts and was treated rudely by both the counter people and customers was because I DO NOT LOOK ISRAELI OR JEWISH. The rude customers I can overlook since I've run into their type before. However, I cannot excuse the rudeness and insult of the 2 Jewish guys who took my order and money. They intentionally gave me crappy donuts. I was dressed nicely and was pleasant during my whole encounter. I didn't even know I paid for crap until I was at my friends' home. I think the owners, employees, and patrons of this deli are not used to visitors who are obviously not Jewish or Israeli (by appearance). I find it disturbing that the owners and patrons of this deli/market portray themselves as rude and arrogant bigots. My Israeli Jewish husband says it's a "xenophobic attitude common among Jews that comes from self-preservation." Whatever the reason or stereotype, I don't believe it can justify the over-priced donut rejects I was sold and rude treatment I encountered. I hope a competitive kosher deli/market opens in Tucson since I will not be recommending this place to anyone.

text: I continue to order from here regularly because it is within walking distance from my house. Wonton soup, egg drop soup, lo mein, general tso's, beef/chicken with broccoli, fried rice are all good (and by good I mean typical, average Chinese food. no surprises in either direction) here. I tried the "Singapore Mei Fun (Rice Noodle)" and it was not rice noodle but instead regular old angel hair. I got the fried scallops and they weren't even scallops at all, but rolled up, dried up, weird pieces of surimi meat (granted, I did wonder how the heck they got away with selling scallops for only $3.25, but I've ordered those at at least 5 other chinese restaurants in the past and I've always gotten actual scallops, albeit smallish ones). So that's two dishes that are specifically advertised as being one thing and aren't that thing at all. One of my favorite Chinese dishes is Moo Shu. I got it here once and it was literally ALL cabbage plus the meat. Wtf? Worst ever! The only *good* I've noticed about this place is the "roast pork" appetizer, which I don't see many other places' menus. The small size for $4 is literally a pint of the pork slices/chunks that they use in all their pork dishes, in a juice that's "salty and bad for me" as I said the other night to my boyfriend. He pretty much orders this every time, and I just wanted to eat it all myself it's so addictive. So for the future, I'm going to stick with Hong Kong only when I'm craving my comfort foods of lo mein, wonton soup, and beef with snow peas. I'll save the experimenting for when I'm willing to drive to pick up the food.

text: If I could, I'd live at the Apple store. I began my descent into computers at an early age and on a Mac. As I grew older, I became part of the PC population out of being poor and just plain outnumbered. Well, when I started my freelance writing business two years ago, I was determined to do it "right", which meant upgrading my home computer system and rekindling my love affair with Apple. I visited my local Apple store and was hooked! I recently visited to buy an iPhone. Yes, I have the iPhone. At the Marlton, NJ store, folks were camped out on folding lawn chairs during the wee hours of the morning. But when I arrived at 2:00 p.m., when the store closed to ready for the launch, there weren't very many people there: maybe 30 or so. The staff (and security) were friendly, approachable and helpful. I remarked that I hadn't seen people camped out like that since I waited on line for New Kids on the Block tickets when I was 16 and the whole staff broke out laughing. Even John "Mayor Gadget" Street had a catbird seat at another store in the middle of the night. But I decided to shop for a few hours before the reopening (I'm much too cool to sit outside a store for a phone), got ice cream, listened to the Phillies day game on my car stereo, then, joined folks in the line, which by 5:00 p.m. was growing longer. Apple staff arranged for coffee and Panera Bread to offer us free beverages and donuts while we waited! But even with the circus atmosphere (kids scalping their spots in line while local news helicopters hovered above us taking photos) Apple staff was poised, calm and helpful. When I finally picked up my box, I had a staff member offer to check me out using a mini, portable credit card machine! How's that for service? I was talking on my new iPhone in mere minutes. At any Apple store you can peruse and play with any gadget or computer with smart support and without the frustration of the "hard sell." Leave it to Apple to create products that not only are the most usable and glitch-free, but they're also the most stylish and awe-inspiring. I can't take out my iPhone in public without being asked for a look and a tutorial. If it were a man, I'd be jealous! Visit an Apple store. There's a third area Apple location on Gulph Road at the King of Prussia Mall.

text: I can't believe this place only has an average of 3 stars so far. It's time to change that. It's up to me. And no, I'm not just giving this restaurant 5 stars because "I feel bad for it" or something like that. The food, the staff and the experience is simply always great! From the entrance, it feels like you're being welcome into someone's home. And it is, I suppose. There are comments in other reviews on the many ownership changes, but from what my co-workers tell me, the current family used to own it...then they sold it...then they realized how badly it was doing, so they bought it back. The hostess is very nice and always chatting up my bosses, and the manager Nick usually comes to say hello when my party is seated (I only go here for work luncheons- it'd probably be a different story if it was just me and a few friends, as we are much younger than their typical crowd of diners). I have never been for dinner, but I can remark on lunch. As a vegetarian, it's usually hard for me to find something. The New Tavern is a happy surprise here--- I ordered their veggie wrap twice, which comes with sauteed onions, peppers and I think cheese if you want it, on a whole wheat wrap. The wrap is the tastiest I've ever had, and seems like it's homemade. That's a nice touch. My boss always gets the Penne Vodka- and he's been coming here for a long time, which I guess says something about how good it is...or maybe some people are just not adventurous eaters, and when they find a recipe for success, why mess with it? Well, I'm a fan of messing with success. So I did it on my third time here. I ordered the Mediterranean platter (brown rice salad, hummus, pita, and a side salad with lettuce, tomatoes and eggs). And it was deeeelicious. My co-worker gave me a "what the heck are you eating, catfood?" I guess some people have never had hummus. Anyway, I've always had a great lunch here and friendly service.

text: Oh, Oceano - I really wanted to like you. I wanted to like you so much, that I was willing to overlook my, "only eat seafood in states that border oceans" rule. I had been waiting for the right time to visit, and when I recently found a $40 for $18 offer on a local foodie website, I happily pulled the trigger. Wow, was I disappointed. For starters, my girlfriend and I shared our dinner with several fruit flies. It wasn't just our table either. I noticed another table swatting flies as well. I was willing to overlook this, because minus the flies, the atmosphere in Oceano really is quite nice. Let's move on to the drinks. Our server took our drink order professionally enough. My girlfriend ordered a cranberry and Absolut. When the drink arrived it was mostly Absolut. The server knew the drink didn't look right, because when she set it down she said she could add more cranberry if it were too strong. It definitely needed it. Rather than take the drink back and try again, the server brought a second glass with cranberry juice in it. So now, we have to play bartender and mix our own drink at the table. We began our meal with two appetizers - oysters on the half shell, and marinated tomatoes and halloumi. The oysters were fine. Not much control a restaurant has over raw shellfish, just buy good quality and put it on the tray with some ice. I had no complaints. The other appetizer was an interesting dish. In addition to the halloumi and tomatoes, it contained grilled watermelon, arugala, and some aged balsamic. The dish had a lot going on. I couldn't understand why the tomatoes got top billing, when there were two giant pieces of grilled watermelon on the plate. Anyway, if there are any would be BBQ chefs out there - don't grill watermelon, it doesn't taste good. For dinner, I ordered the Sauteed Herb Crusted Sea Bass. No complaints about the emulsion or risotto, it was quite good, but the fish is where things started to go wrong. If the name of your establishment contains the word Ocean, the fish had better be stellar. Sea Bass should be a touch on the firm side - this was not. The fish was almost soggy. The flavor was OK, but the texture was way off. My sea bass was also missing its Herb Crusted jacket. My girlfriend ordered the Rainbow Trout. First, the fish was bland. Second, it was lightly pan fried. Nowhere in the menu or in the server's description of the dish was it mentioned that the trout would be pan fried. Had she known, she would have ordered something different. The flavor of the fried batter overwhelmed the already bland fish. Given our experience with the meal, we decided to skip dessert. Our server brought the bill, and this is where things really went downhill. My coupon clearly stated that it could not be combined with other coupons or offers. I understand, and it makes perfect sense. The coupon, however, didn't say anything about method of payment. I chose to pay with a gift certificate. The server came over and said that it was not allowed. I asked to see the manager, who came over and explained that a "gift certificate" is technically an "offer" and that it was the rules of the coupon - his hands were tied. I felt like I was arguing the definition of "is" with Ken Starr. When it became obvious that the manager was not going to accept the gift certificate (something which Oceano had already collected the money on when it was purchased, mind you), we paid and left. If it had just been one of the previously mentioned grievances, I could have justified a second visit. But, after mediocre service, poorly prepared food, and an argument with management, I am content letting Oceano be the big fish that got away.

text: We stayed here for a week. This is our second time staying in a Hotel Indigo - last year we stayed for a week in the West End location. I very very (very very, very very) very much prefer the downtown location (NOT West End) - we were on the 12th floor here and had no complaints about water pressure. The W.E. location had poor pressure, lukewarm water, toilets that refused to flush, sinks that drained slowly/not at all.. We had none of those issues here. The room was beautiful, modern and clean, our floor was quiet. The hotel restaurant was OK. I had a yogurt "parfait" which consisted of about a quarter cup of yogurt with two small pieces of pineapple topping .... .... .... and how much did we pay for it? argh! ..... But the drinks in the bar were tasty and they have nice desserts. The bar hosts writer's rounds nightly, which is a great Nashville touch. The staff is super friendly, attentive and quick. I did wish that we had a fridge/microwave in room, especially since we stayed for a longer period of time. No bathtub either, but I don't mind that so much. The bed was very comfortable (firm, not cushy, which is what I like) and the linens were very clean and fresh. This is a very insignificant thing to complain about, but is a pet peeve of mine: the in-room coffee came with powdered creamer. Not that the in-room coffee was that great to begin with, but powdered creamer just makes my eyeball twitch. A minor complaint, but it makes a difference to have the good liquid stuff, even if the good stuff is still fake chemical-ly milk. TV was fine, lots of channels. The parking blows, 22 bucks a day for valet or 20 for self-park. There is no street parking. They comped us on valet parking, maybe since we were staying with them for a decent length of time, but I'm not sure if that's the official policy or not. Our room was on Union Street, and traffic rarely was noisy enough to be distracting, although there were a couple of ambulances/fire trucks that would scream down the street. We had a nice view of the pretty new City Hall building. The hotel adjoins a somewhat mediocre Starbucks, but there are some decent dining options within walking distance - Varallo's and Provence are reasonably closeby, and then you have some tasties on 2nd avenue (nachos at Buffalo Billiards are my favorite on earth. Also, try the wings at Piranha's or the cozy Beer Sellar.. if you venture down to B'way, there's the BBQ at Jack's.. I could go on forever : ) We lived in Nashville for years before moving to Oregon and I miss the food more than I can communicate in words.) The walk to Broadway for touristy fun is quick and easy. Great experience at the Hotel Indigo downtown!!
label: POS

text: After visiting twice for both mother's day and father's day this year I can safely say that Keegan's is one of the Gulf beaches better casual seafood restaurants. It did end up on TV show "Diners, Drive-ins and Dives" and some people seem hung up on that fact. I've seen reviews debating it from both ways. With some saying it was deserving of being featured or others claiming the food is no good and they are guilty of resting on their laurels. I tend to think it was deserving as the ambiance, service and waitstaff, and fresh fish all scream authentic Florida beach food. Some of the reviews say the service is bad but on Father's day the place was packed and super busy but after waiting a completely reasonable 30 minutes for a table we were seated were well taken care of the rest of the night. Not once did we have to wait long for anything like our order being taken, refills, or food coming out. I've had a very solid blackened grouper sandwich here, awesome jalapeno hush puppies,and very meaty and flavorful crab cakes that aren't frozen and contain amble quantities of lump crab meat. The best dish I've had yet was off their daily specials list, and it was a blue corn tortilla crusted wahoo which was flaky, moist, and tasted as if it jumped right off the boat and on to my plate. They feature Stella and Shocktop on draft at a reasonable price, and the red or white sangria pitchers were a a big hit with my parents, who can be particular about their Sangria. One reason they liked it so much is that it is kicked-up with lots of freshly grated cinnamon which you can see floating around. Lastly, they offer vegetarian menu items to help provide options for dining companions that may not be that into seafood or meat in general. The black bean burger is solid, and they also have a vegetable pasta entree as well. I look forward to coming again and trying some she crab soup as well as their char-broiled octopus, and from my experience with the wahoo I think its a safe bet to pick off their fresh fish specials menu. Overall, not the best on the beach but definitely a solid option with ample appeal and plenty of noteworthy dishes.

text: The Belcourt Theatre is, without a doubt, the most authentic and, well, neat establishment in the Hillsboro area. Independent little artsy movie houses are an absolute staple in any community, and fortunately for Nashvillians, this one is about as unpretentious as is possible when it comes to indie cinemas. The theatre was open as a silent movie house back in the 20's, and the Belcourt's current management still keeps the dream alive with classics, foreign films and documentaries that you often can't view anywhere else in Middle Tennessee. The Belcourt's full bar and intimate atmosphere give it an air that is far more welcoming than that of most sticky, towering multiplexes. The theatre also holds art shows, film festivals, special screenings and concerts that are consistently charming and entertaining. In fact, the Belcourt is renowned for holding concerts for huge acts that like to stage occasional intimate shows--think the White Stripes, Yo La Tengo, Feist, et cetera. Prices are about the same as you'd find at a typical chain cinema: $6.25 for matines and $8.50 for evenings. The only difference here is that you'll probably see a better film and get to have yourself a cocktail while doing so! The Belcourt typically only shows two films at a time, but they maintain their website regularly and rotate films on a consistent basis. And it's perfect for first dates.

text: I had dinner here last weekend with a couple of friends. For a Saturday evening, it was surprisingly empty when we came around 7:15 PM or so. I would have appreciated the specials being told to the table a bit slower; we didn't end up ordering any, but I also had little idea of what was available after the waiter had told us. On the advice of one of our party who had previously been there, we got the gnocchi (both the spinach and the ricotta), the tacconell al porcini (my suggestion), and the pesto ravioli. All of the dishes were fantastic; the gnocchi in particular was a highlight. I'm not sure how it's made, but the gnocchi is really rich and has a dense, flavorful middle. The tacconell was also a revelation; the long, thin noodles tasted very good in the cream sauce, and the porcini mushrooms added a nice touch of flavor that allowed it to stand out against the sauce (which wasn't as rich as an alfredo). The ravioli was probably the weakest dish, but even so it tasted better than most I've had. Put together, those 3 dishes were under $20 each, so it was a very affordable dinner for the price. The atmosphere is a bit quiet, but once more parties started flowing in later on, you could speak at normal levels without feeling too out of place. My one recommendation is that this place is more towards the dressy end of casual; I felt a bit out of place in my shorts, polo shirt, and sandals. text: For our inaugural trek to Reno on what could only be described as a weekend of pure romance, my husband and I chose the Silver Legacy. These people know how to keep you entertained.....at a low price point. Once the burning sensation in my nose subsided (I attribute it to maxed out A/C and in-door smoking), I started to recognize this place for what it was. A superbly run land-based cruise ship...the kind with all-night gambling. The demographic was as expected and then some. We had the senior contingency, the rockers in their concert tees (I had a weird compulsion to rat my bangs) and the bizarro-land, cougar-esque singles scene (the place has 2 nightclub/lounges and 2 or 3 other bars. But what I didn't expect was the huge number of families. There were strollers galore...Reno ain't just for your uncle's cousin's girlfriend's aunt anymore. Maybe it's because the El Dorado, the Silver Legacy and Circus Circus are all connected via this indoor walkway that channels some bizarro-land underground city - we literally didn't go outside until we left on Sunday - but I love this place for all that it is: $5 blackjack tables all night, great service, cheap eats and some damn good people watching. It doesn't hurt that they cater to the Asians -- I had hot & sour soup one night and it was pretty damn good. Did you know that the Silver Legacy has a Head of Asian Games? Is that the best title ever? We left up over $200. Anywhere else that would be nothing, but in Reno it paid for most of our trip. Needless to say, I'll be back.. text: I visited this legendary restaurant when my friends and I recently attended the New Orleans Jazz Festival '09. Neil Young was amazing, but Jaques-Imo's still ranks up there as one of the high-lights of the trip. I honestly thought I died and went to Creole Cuisine heaven. A friend who went to Tulane wrote me up a list of restaurants to check out, and Jaque-Imo's was one of those "must trys". My friends and I took a taxi to a remote area of New Orleans which seemed a bit sketchy, but once we arrived at our destination it was like we stumbled upon some outdoor patio party. Live music, oysters a la carte served right on the street, and a gallery we checked out as we waited for a table. The wait was long, but the food is well worth it. Plus there were plenty of friendly and colorful characters outside keeping us company. Once we went inside we went straight through the kitchen to a cozy and colorful back area. We were starving, and the food looked amazing (we did get a sneak preview as we walked through the kitchen), so we ordered right away. I ordered the alligator cheesecake, fried green tomatoes, and blackened red-fish, both which were incredible dishes. Were I not such a gentleman I would have cleaned the plate with my tongue. The sauces were amazing, and the food in general was angelic. On top of the incredible food the bar up front is lively and fun. They pour stiff drinks (if that's your thing), and there seems to always be a friendly local or two to chat about Jaque-Imo legends with you. I highly recommend you search out this out-of-the-way location if you're in New Orleans. I'm no local, but after spending my brief time in New Orleans this is easily my favorite restaurant in the Big Easy so far.

I'm not much of a steak person, but I enjoyed their prime rib. Also excellent chicken ceasar salads that are less expensive than the red meat of course. They do have take out available! So if you're wishing to dine at home, you can come in and pick up a meal to go. It has a luxurious atmosphere. Dark rooms, candle-lit booths and a clean appearance to all of the waitresses/servers. It can be filled with tourists during the tourist seasons. They also have an outside bar, with tiki torches. Plenty of parking around the back of the building. text: A Restaurant Week Review: *Note: online RW menu isn't reliable* I so badly wanted to give Smokin' Betty's 5 stars! But I couldn't... As phenomenal as their BBQ was, two things kinda bugged me: 1) We were seated fairly close to the bar on the 2nd floor. It was pretty full, and quite loud. If you have the chance, ask your waitress for a table further from the bar. 2) The womens bathroom on the 2nd floor... absolutely disgusting. Not only were 1/3 of the stalls "Out of Order", the working ones were really dirty and one lacked toilet paper. Hopefully they'll clean it up soon! On the more yummy sides of things, Smokin' Betty's offered us the best Restaurant Week experience we've had yet. And possibly some of the BEST BBQ in the Center City area... Service - Our waiter was so sweet and attentive. The best service I've had in a loooong time. Thanks guys! Drinks - Good, yet selective beer selection. - Fun, refreshing cocktails (try the Raspberry Lemonade Cocktail). First Course - Cheesesteak Springroll: I was skeptical at first, but WOW. The spicy ketchup that they offer for dipping is realllly good too. Any cheesesteak buff has to try these. And the best part... they're 1/2 off during their happy hour! - BBQ Sliders: YUM. The carolina pulled pork had an amazing mesquite zest; just the best kind of "spicy." My favorite, hickory smoked beef brisket, had a sweet and tangy BBQ flavor. Then the caribbean pulled chicken, though tasty, lacked the kind of awesome flavor the other two had. But all of them were cooked to yummy, tender perfection... Second Course - Soup of the Day, Portobello Mushroom & Sage: When we walked up to Smokin' Betty's I noticed this special on their board outside. I absolutely love mushroom soup, I got so excited! Rich, creamy, loads of mushrooms :)This was, hands down, the best mushroom soup I've EVER had. For a soup of the day at a BBQ joint, I was very impressed... - Mixed Green Salad: Tasty, crisp salad. But the balsamic vinaigrette it was served with was WAY over-powering on the bitter factor! Some people like their vinaigrette that way, but definitely not me. Third Course - Hickory Smoked St. Louis Ribs: I don't even know what to say or where to begin... These BBQ ribs were jaw dropping-ly, UHmazing. Again, I got my favorite of the BBQ sauces (sweet and tangy, hickory smoked BBQ goodness). But the even better part... the juicy, tender meat pulled right off the bone *insert Homer's drool here.* I'm just gonna leave it at that. The ribs were served with two sides, like most of the entree items, we got asparagus (perfectly cooked with a nice crunch) and... MAC & CHEESE*!! Fourth Course - Triple Chocolate Layer Cake Typical chocolate mousse and ganache cake. Nothing special. If you really want a treat, go with the... - Chocolate Mousse served w/ mixed berries I prefer my mousse to be light and fluffy. But Betty's thick mousse was still insanely YUMMY. The strawberries, raspberries, and black berries were key :) Overall Smokin' Betty's Restaurant Week menu, offered an extremely tasty selection with hearty portions, for that price we all love... $35. I'm super excited to come back and try some more of their menu items!! *Mac & Cheese: But before we get too excited, I have to admit... I was kind of disappointed. So here's the scoop... I learned that Smokin' Betty's is owned by the same guy who owns Devil's Alley (I knew their mac & cheese tasted familiar... I'm not a fan of Devil's Alley's mac & cheese either). The noodles are always over cooked to me (I prefer the more al dente kind) and the cheese sauce, though nice and thick, has a kind of gritty texture. Then instead of a tomato jam on-top, there were bread crumbs with a hint of garlic flavor to them (which was the best part of this mac & cheese). Though it has potential, I wasn't a fan...
label: POS

text: This is the newest Hudson's location in Edmonton, located in the busy eating district of West Ed. Mall, known as Bourbon Street. Seeing as I've never been too crazy about the other restaurants in this area, Hudson's Tap House is a nice Canadian addition to it. I shouldn't say it's a restaurant, it's really more of a pub. A real Canadian pub, with stuffed moose-heads hanging on the walls and everything! Okay, when I put it like that, it sounds like it might take away your appetite, but really, it's not that bad. I think it adds to the atmosphere! They've got plenty of seating, an assortment of small free-standing tables, cozy booths, and of course, the bar seating. The big bar stands right in the middle of the place, and is the first thing you see when you walk in. Everything is in this rich mahogany shade, so it doesn't look like just any pub -- it's a sleek pub. The food is yummy, and they give you these huge portions of everything, so you're definitely getting your money's worth. I had wimpy taste buds that day, so I only ordered the soup and salad (now I'm thinking, what the frick?). But the cream of broccoli was oh so good! Very creamy, not too salty. And uh, the salad was very fresh. Oy, that sounds so lame. Lucky for you guys, my friends had the sense to order something real that day. My friend had the buffalo burger (huuuge), and my bf had their super-spicy beef burger (also huuuge). Both guys were stuffed at the end of it! A tip for all you spicy tongues out there: Hudson's has a helpful scale on their menu which helps you rate how spicy you want your food. My bf is always bragging how much he can take, so he ordered the hottest one. He was sweating bullets in the end. If you want to go for their Happy Hour, it's from 4-6pm weekday nights. You can get some yummy wings and mini-cheeseburgers for $7. Mm, I'm getting hungry just writing this ... Another note: if you're short like me, you might want to consider getting a booth instead. Their individual tables are really tall, so you may have an awkward time slipping and sliding off your chair. I personally like having my feet touch the floor when I'm eating. And, you know, looking like I'm not 12 when I'm in a pub ... So I hope this was helpful to anyone considering a visit to Hudson's. As for myself, I think I'll go back and have that buffalo burger give it to my wimpy taste buds.

text: What a pleasant surprise! After checking in to a hotel in Indy we asked for a recommendation of a restaurant. Rick's Cafe Boatyard was suggested. It was mere minutes from the hotel - very convenient after a long day of travel. The atmosphere was upbeat and pleasant if a bit noisy. We were seated immediately (8 pm on a Friday night). The tables felt very squished together - this is not someplace you want to come to if you are seeking a very private romantic dinner. Conversation from all the tables drifted up into the vaulted ceilings and bounced around making it difficult to hold a conversation with the person across from or next to you. However, we had a very picturesque view of the lake at sunset - who needs to talk? The menu was very extensive with items everywhere from moderately priced to really expensive. I'm a fifth generation Floridian and they had an extensive and interesting seafood selection. I really liked the fact they marked their house specialties so clearly. Service was great except for one tiny thing. Our waiter came and took our drink order (I can strongly recommend the Midnight Martini) and left. When he came back with our drinks he asked if we had any questions. We said no so he asked if we were ready to order - THEN he told us the specials! Very frustrating. My husband ordered the Atlantic Salmon Roulades - a house specialty, and I ordered one of the daily specials - grilled marinated grouper and scallops. We also ordered the goat cheese appetizer. Every piece of food served to us was exceptional! The seafood was perfectly cooked - the scallops were tender and fell apart in my mouth. The presentation of the dishes was wonderful as well. The baked goat cheese came with seasoned slices (thin) of french bread and a special home made tomato sauce. We could have used a few more pieces of bread - i wanted to lick the bowl toward the end. Both entries came with the vegetable of the day - a medley - that was perfectly cooked (still a bit crunchy). The grouper was possibly the best I've ever had!! The Salmon Romalaudes were amazing!! My dish came on a bed of rice and his came with homemade mashed potatoes both of which were fine. This food was just so amazing. I found myself really taking my time and savoring every bite. The bread served with the meal was a wonderful grainy bread served with whipped honey butter. During our meal a terrific jazz ensemble began to play in the bar area but, as with all the other sound, the music carried through the dining room. This was a good thing in this case as the ensemble was top notch and applause could be heard at the end of each number throughout the restaurant. I simply had to try a dessert since everything else had been so incredible. My husband ordered the mile high chocolate cake. I swear it was enough for four people! It was absolutley wonderful (I can hardly wait to eat my leftovers). When the waiter brought my take home containers he also brought one for the bread - with an entire loaf already inside along with a small container of the honey butter! As long as you are't hoping to hold really meaningful conversations, this is one of the best restuarants I've been to. I will be sure to dine here on my next visit to Indy as well. Well done!!

text: When we visited The Good Pie, we were expecting good pizza baked in a stone oven. What we got was mediocre pizza burnt in a stone oven. A group of three of us went on a Saturday night around 5:30. Everyone in said group has dramatically different tastes, so we knew that perhaps one or two people might like the place and the other/s would either be "meh" or hate it. It turned out we all had something in common that night- a bad experience involving pizza. The Good Pie had a fantastic ambiance and the waitress was attentive and pleasant. The menu looked enticing: basil and cherry tomatoes with buffalo mozzarella on a pizza baked in a stone oven- huzzah! But when the food got to the table, we all looked at each other as if to say, "Really?" The crust was burnt in several places, and while a stone/ brick oven adds "character" to a pizza, is there really any reason there should be blatant scorch marks and undercooked areas? And when the menu said the pizza had basil and cherry tomatoes on it, why were there only three leaves of basil on it and just as many cherry tomatoes? I realize that this is authentic pizza, the way it's made in Italy, but still, three basil leaves and cherry tomatoes, on soggy oven-scorched crust? The sauce was decent, but by no means memorable. If the goal was to serve understated food, The Good Pie has hit its mark. But good understated food it was not. And getting hit with a thirty dollar check for two pizzas that were, at the end, disintegrating into mush, was too much for all of us. Never have we ever agreed on a meal, but unfortunately we were unanimous in our disappointment.

They've got the usual suspects (Bliss, Frederic Fekkai) cult following favorites ( N.V.
