Sure, if you want the entire Kiehl's line you'll have to walk down the block, but Blue Mercury carries the 'best seller' products of each brand...and for the smaller or independent manufacturers, they cover the full line. If the cool packaging doesn't draw you in, the chic, shiny staff will. Beware! They are quite knowledgeable and sure, learning about the latest green vegan chicken friendly product line is fun, (did I mention they have some awesome up and coming brands as well?) but before you know it, 2 hours have passed and you're in credit card debt. Save the mascara purchase for Rite Aid, but get the face wash here! There's a small spa/salon which is part of the store as well...I've never tried it myself (other than a one time eyebrow wax which was, well, an eyebrow wax) but I've heard mixed opinions....if we're talking haircuts, I suppose I'll have to review House Productions next...

text: Wow, this place is outstanding!!! Mere Bulles is well known for their Sunday brunch buffet. This is not your average buffet! Here is a list of items from my visit over Labor Day weekend: --creme brulee French toast (with a side of strawberry glaze if needed) this is probably one of their most famous things and it is outstanding!! --pork tenderloin, cut to your liking by a chef --there was a fondue fountain pouring out rich chocolate that you could smother in fresh strawberries, marshmallows, chocolate wafer cookies, ect. --She-crab bisque. This is their most famous item. People will drive here just to order this soup, and you can get as much of your fill of this as you want during the brunch buffet. It is very rich, the crab is outstanding! One of the best bisques I have ever had!! --The pasta salad was oil based (not mayo) with spices and was very flavorful, chilled to perfection. Tasted home made, not made out of a box. --All of your standards such as bacon, sausage, made-to-order-waffles with a myriad of toppings such as fresh raspberries and mini chocolate chips, whipped cream. --build your own eggs Benedict!! In addition to this you can also add fried green tomatoes! These were some of the best fried green tomatoes I have had. The only better ones are the ones my Me Ma makes. --There are a few lunch type items such as wild rice, mashed potatoes and the well known rib sandwiches. Yum. --And another outstanding selection? $9 bottomless mimosas! You cannot beat the price for the quality. This buffet is very reasonably priced at $20. The quality for everything at Mere Bulles is 2nd to none. I can understand why so many famous Nashville stars come to dine here. I would love to come back and try them for dinner as I know they would serve a great meal.

text: I don't like dishonest places, nor do I like surprises in my bill at the end. We went here because a friend got a restaurant.com gift certificate, and didn't get a chance to use it, so she gave it to us to try. The certificate was $25 off if you spend $35. So basically out of pocket you should spend $10 + 18% tip. Knowing this, we tried to order $35 worth of food for 2 people for lunch. Hubby ordered the sizzling beef and scallops, I ordered an order of crabrangoon, beef chow fun, and then we needed one more dish. They had a whole peking duck for $26, and they had 1/2 a crispy duck for $10. I ordered the 1/2 crispy duck, but asked about the peking duck. The waiter checked with the kitchen, and they were willing to do 1/2 a peking duck. When I asked the price, he said it was the same price as the crispy duck. So I said "oh, nice, $10?", he said yes. The food came out and it seems like they don't have a wok there. Things aren't fried properly. The sizzling plate looked more like steamed veggies in a gravy of soy sauce and corn starch. The chow fun was HARD. It was so hard it wouldn't even break up. It was just one hard lump. I actually had to send it back, because the noodles seemed so old. I had 2 excuses to send it back though, because I asked for no bean sprouts, and when it came out, 20% of it was bean sprouts. The peking duck was horrible. The skin was not crispy, and the duck had a nasty smell to it, with a texture that was similar to liver. The buns were hard and cold. Service was great until I got the bill. They charged us $15 for the 1/2 peking duck, which would have been fine if you told me in advance. Total out of pocket for 2 people at lunch with the $25 discount was $26! Totally not worth it for the quality of food we got. I would have to say, Panda Express is 10 times better than this place. I'd never go back here, and I wouldn't tell my friends about it. If you're in the area, China Diner is cheaper and more authentic than this spot. Noon on a Sunday and we were the only table there. We should have known. :(

text: My first visit to Nashville, and the mad Platter was a great way to end my trip. My buddy and his girlfriend could not stop talking about this place, and now I can see why. Located within an older building in a historic part of town, Mad Platter blends modern with the traditional. I had the five course meal, and I would recommend ordering that. It gives you a chance to sample some cool stuff which you may not ordinarily order. One of the cool things that they brought out for us to try were some mini "salmon-melt" sandwiches, with a side of some type of bisque. Awesome. The place is relatively small, so that wait staff is extremely attentive and the service was really good. One of the chef's actually came out and talked with us for awhile. This place is a little expensive, but is a great bargain considering the quality of the food and the experience. The best way that I could describe the Mad Platter, is take the trendy LA restuarant.....mix in some some cool food ideas, a little bit of southern charm, and a staff that strives to make each diner feel at home.....NOW subtract the super high prices and pretentious staff; and you have a great place to eat. text: I'm not sure when Desi Village exploded onto the Baltimore Ave. dining scene, but I'm glad it did. I'm not a real connoisseur of Indian food. I enjoy it, but I'm never too clear on what it is that I'm eating. It seems like most Indian places in this area go with the buffet format, which is a fine way to fill up, but sometimes I crave something a little more than unidentifiable Indian cooling in a steam tray. Desi Village brings a cooked to order option to the table; they even ask for a desired spice level upon ordering. I went with my standard bearer of Indian: chicken tikki masala and a side of naan. Yawn, I know, but just as chicken and broccoli with an eggroll is to (American) Chinese, I must use this dish as a yardstick to evaluate an Indian restaurant on level ground. This was the best chicken tikki masala I've had in a long time. Heavy sauce, filled with peppers and onions and lots of meat-- it was a pleasure. I'll also note that the naan was delicious; a lot of places in West Philly seem to have rubbery naan, which is just unacceptable. I haven't canvased the city for Indian with enough thoroughness to tell you if it's worth a trip to West Philly, but if you're in the area, you should definitely check it out!

text: My boyfriend took me here for a special birthday weekend getaway, and it was the perfect retreat. The room was beautiful. We stayed in "The Overlook" room, which had a small balcony with table and chairs over looking a gazebo. Our room had a canopy bed and a fireplace. The room had a tiny tv and wireless internet access. It was exceptionally clean and absolutely perfect for relaxing. The staff was really gracious and helpful. Upon check in, the staff gave us plenty of information about activities and sights in the area. They also helped my boyfriend arrange to have flowers and chocolate covered strawberries in the room upon our arrival. Each breakfast was delicious. I can't imagine not having something there you can eat. One day there was fresh fruit salad, yogurt, homemade granola, hard boiled eggs, quiche, warm croissants and muffins, bagels, coffee, tea, and juice. In the afternoon, there was tea time, with cookies or other treats. There are two porches where you can take your meals. There are also nice areas to sit in the back lawn, including two gazebos and a hammock. We found so much to do in the area that we didn't spend much time sitting and relaxing, but it's nice to know the option is there. Most importantly, it was a very short walk from the main shopping area of New Hope and the bridge to Lambertville. You can park at the Inn and not have to worry about the street and meter parking. Throughout our stay, the staff was incredibly kind and helpful. I think the Inn is also pet-friendly, but of course you should double check. Overall, I can't think of anything to criticize at all and I hope to make it back there someday when I need another break from reality.

text: Similar to Symeon, I did not have a good experience at Wayne's Garage. We took our 2006 Camry here for the state inspection, and failed because they told us we had to replace all our struts and 3 of our tires. (We replaced all the tires in 2008, and have put only 23,000 miles on them, then got a new one after a flat this spring.) The service estimate was enough to make us get a second opinion. Guess what? Tires are well within the parameters for safety (see details in this PDF of equipment standards: http://www.dmv.state.pa.us/pdotforms/pub_45/section_e.pdf), and the struts don't leak and don't need replacement. We saved ourselves about $2000 of unnecessary repairs, and passed the inspection with flying colors. I'm currently going through the process of filing a complaint with the bureau of safety inspection. If you feel that you've been scammed in an inspection, call the complaint hotline at 1-800-265-0921. Have your VIN and the inspection station's # ready (usually on their sign outside). Wayne's is fine for oil changes and basic repairs, but I won't go here for an inspection again. Go to Garrison's Garage at 2335 E. Gordon, in Fishtown, instead.

text: I ran out to this market over my lunch break to grab some lunch with a friend. She had been to this cute little grocery store and was kind enough to show me this place. Rumor has it the multigrain (yes, I was surprised too!) is a good flavor. I made the mistake of going to this store slightly hungry, so please do not judge me harshly when I tell you I got a shrimp tempura roll box and a roast beef, roasted red pepper, tomato, brie and champagne mustard panini. The shrimp tempura was pretty good. I will admit, I am not a sushi connoisseur, so I am not sure how much my opinion on the matter counts. The panini looked to be a good deal at approximately $8. Unfortunately, it is only a good deal if the sandwich is good, and it was not. The brie was very good, but the mustard (at least that is what I think it was) was too sweet. The extreme sweetness just did not work with the rest of the sandwich. My friend was also disappointed in her sandwich, so we switched halves of our paninis. She went so far as to suggest that perhaps they mistakenly put honey mustard on the sandwich instead of champagne mustard. I have never tasted champagne mustard, so I can not really comment except to say, whatever it was, it was much, much too sweet. My friend ordered the prosciutto, mozzarella, basil and tomato panini. text: This Target is easy to get to using the bike trail, and the prices are amazing. I just purchased three beautiful light fleece jackets for $12 a pop (their regular price was only $15), their clothing dept. was fun to shop in, and I bought several boxes of luna, cliff and power bars for $4 each (that's like 70- 80 cents each). Anyhow, I was also impressed with the level of help - everyone was above and beyond friendly, and a lot of people asked me if I needed help. They called into the warehouse to see if they had my size in a floor item they were out of. Even the cashier was friendly and helped me when I asked for separate receipts. They have a well-stocked "tis-the-season" area, and a full grocery store in there. Pretty neat. Big boxes of crackers for super-low prices, and when they have sales it's nearly half-off of what I've been paying at neighborhood pharmacies. Also, although their costume jewelry prices are really cheap, I noticed their lovely real jewelry - I have my eye on a few pairs of earrings, and can't wait for the sale! Plus points for bike racks right outside. Minus a few points for being completely out of stock of good Bike head and tail lights.

text: God, where do I begin to list the problems? I believe I'll go with a modified bullet-point system. - Complimentary salsa, but no chips?! What the hell is this?! text: Excellent Mediterranean fare. Solid menu with a good albeit Greek wine list. We had our second birthday dinner here and were delighted again. We sat in a side room with a single large table for ten, which set us aside from the loud dinner room which made for a great night of conversation and let us enjoy our meal even more. Appetizers included a fried cheese plate (which I loved), grilled octopus (which was tender, delicious, and awesome too), squid stuffed with cheese something over greens (yummy), feta and olives, pita and hummus. Dinners included lamb chops (marinated for 3 days with lemon and olive oil - yum), lamb shank (so tender - wow), langoustine (so sweet - so much better than lobster), and Black Bass baked in a salt crust (pretty presentation and quite delicious). The wine list was very limited to almost entirely Greek wines, but we had three bottles of one from Nemea that had "velvety tannins" - cuz it was great and only $55. Desserts were also very good. They were generally variations of phyllo dough, honey, nuts, and custard. Mine was a tall custardy version that was great along with a very respectable cup of cappuccino. Our waitress was also very good. Thumbs up all around.

text: We just recently celebrated the 1st birthday of our baby daughter at the Oystercatchers Restaurant. I decided to pick this location for the event as it happens to be just 9 minutes from our residence. it happens to be one of my favourite places for really good sea food especially for their crab cakes and it was my default choice. The Oystercatchers Restaurant branch is very conveniently located for just anyone to reach and is much easier to go to.Booking was easy and hassle free. Just a phone call couple of days prior to the big day had been enough. We were all together nine of us and they had arranged a table and seating accordingly. I really liked that knowing that it was a birthday celebration they had reserved for us the raised sitting area with comfy seats and decorative lightings and nice paintings on the wall which make the videos and photos extra special. All of our guests arrived on time as they had no difficulty locating the place. Everything was nice the wood chairs, the glossy floor and the neatly attired ever present attendants. Even though we had not made any special requests it was really nice that the staff played the birthday song when I had my daughter cut the cake and that made her the special person for the evening. The restaurant was quite full even though it was not a weekend which I felt was a good sign and also it added to the event. After the candle was blown and the cake was cut and everyone had their slices, the attendants were quick to get us a container to pack the remaining cake to take home. And all this without even making a request and it really made us feel pampered and special. Overall the service was excellent, the glasses were always filled up with chilled water without ever asking for and the meat dishes were to die for and that pretty much makes up for the not so great vegetarian dishes.I highly recommend the Oystercatchers Restaurant to anyone who would like to enjoy a wonderful seafood at a convenient location without having to pay a lot.

The portions are small enough and cheap enough to try many dishes...and the menu could definitely be approached in a small plates/tapas way if you wanted. The restaurant itself was very crowded and the wait significant on a friday night, but the atmosphere is generally festive and everyone is offered free sambuca shots before leaving. Especially since their menu changes frequently, it's definitely a place worth going back to.

text: We visited New Orleans right at about the 2 year anniversary of Katrina. It also only took us about 15 minutes to walk to the French Quarter from St. Vincent's. The staff was wonderful... very helpful and caring. The price was right (40 bucks a night for 2 people and a king size bed!) Our room was also very clean upon our arrival which is a plus. St. Vincent's used to be an old girl's orphanage or something so it was kind of eerie but still added to its charm. There is a coffee shop across the street from the hotel (I think it was called Mojo?)... you can get Wi-Fi there or at the hotel. I believe Katrina volunteers were also staying at the hotel while we were there. All around it was a great experience while in New Orleans. If I come again for more than 2 days I will definitely stay here again.

text: Delicious, classy, hip and just plain cool all around. I just got back from a weekend trip to Philly with my bf and I was thrilled when I came across Morimoto's restaurant in my guide book (I'm not very familiar with Philly, haven't been in over ten years, so I had no idea it was even there). We started with an eel & avocado roll which was good but not mind-blowing. The ingredients were very fresh and the eel melted in your mouth but still was not the best sushi I've ever had. (I would say 4 stars for the roll). The rest of the meal, however, was 5 stars all the way! Next we got a cold sesame chicken appetizer to share and this blew me away. The chicken was cooked perfectly and the sweetness of the sesame sauce mixed with the spicy oil that was drizzled on it made for a wonderful combination. We both got the same main course, cold green-tea soba noodles with dashi-shoyu dipping sauce (we got several small things rather than one main dish each so we could create our own tasting menu of sorts) and this was also extremely good. The portion was quite large considering it was listed on the appetizer page of the menu; it was more than enough for an entree. We also shared a plate of the wasabi fried rice which is probably one of the best fried rice dishes I have ever eaten. (I have to point out that the wasabi used was very distinct in both texture and flavour...it must have been either real wasabi, and not the common tubed variety, or a VERY good quality immitation). Atmosphere was hip and trendy but yet not too outrageous that it will look dated in a couple of years. Waitstaff was very friendly and easily accomodated us in a packed restaurant without reservations. **$92 including tax, tip, all of the above mentioned food, 1 beer and 1 cocktail = a great place out for an elegant but not TOO expensive date with great food and beautiful surroundings. (skip the drinks, as beer is beer and the cocktail was not overly unique for the $12 price, and get another delicious course instead!)
label: POS

text: After three generations of serving Louisiana's finest seafood cuisine, Anthony and Gail Uglesich sadly hang up their hats and decide to close this lunch-only cash-only culinary mecca in the Garden District. When i had lived in New Orleans i was fortunate to make it to U's twice and each time was in sheer heaven! The first time I indulged here I was with my brother who is a total foodie, we launched ourselves head first into the fresh live oysters that still had their siphon reflex in-tact and could squirt seawater at you if poked appropriately. Making sure we were well hydrated with their specialty bloody Mary's; we followed up with the barbecued shrimp and barbecued oysters. Uglesich's is a place where Cajun-creole staples like jambalaya; shrimp and grits in a creamy sauce; crawfish maque choux (crawfish smothered with white corn, tomato and seasonings; blow the competition out of the water! I still dream of being served the BBQ shrimp followed by the deeply flavored and fried green tomatoes topped with shrimp and remoulade sauce. It's no surprise why limos regularly pull-up outside this divey and decrepit seafood shack and the wait for a spot in their 12 capacity establishment. Although they may not have reopened i hear since the release of their newest cookbook they have been doing some catering events for special occasions. "The Uglesich's Restaurant Cookbook," from Pelican publishers has 19 restaurant recipes that weren't in the first book, 41 recipes made in the Uglesich family home and a handful of desserts. The new book also has a nostalgic sections of photos of locals dining.
label: POS

text: Thank you, Arturo!!! After being snubbed by some other Indy restaurants when trying to make a reservation, my stepfather advised me of this place Indy should be incredibly thankful for. From the decor to the food to the staff, everything was PERFECTION. We initially had a reservation for 6 that turned into 9, and we had no issue; they were incredibly accommodating to our every need. We started with a few bottles of presecco, this was a bachelorette party after all! For starters, while sipping on the presecco and decorating the bachelorette in her tiara for the evening, we had the calamari and artichoke. The calamari was lightly breaded with a marinara, very basic and simple but well done. The calamari wasn't drenched in batter so as to lose its taste but more of a light pan fry. The artichoke was the only average part of the meal--anywhere else it may have been a highlight. The orders for the table of 9 were a variety of main dishes, all of which received superb reviews--even from my younger sister who never finishes a meal ate every morsel of her penne pasta. I had the spaghetti and meatballs because I couldn't resist the description of homemade veal meatballs AND homemade pasta. I try to avoid ordering pasta at a restaurant but it was well worth it. The table also shared a couple of great, moderately priced wines. They had a nice selection. Before ordering our desserts, our waiter--who was one of the best serves I've ever had--leaned in to me and asked if we wanted a little time after the table cleared so the bride to be could finish opening her gifts. He knew when to come and refill glasses and be around when something was needed and disappear without notice when the table had everything it needed. Perfection. BRAVO!

text: All this time living in Indianapolis, and I had no idea that my favorite steamed bagel place in Oxford, OH had made its way to me! The menu is expansive - make that enormous. It's thankfully divided up into sections - roast beef, turkey, vegetarian, etc - because the names of the sandwiches rarely give any indication of what's actually on them. Take, for instance, my favorite - the China Cat Sunflower. While it does come on a sunflower bagel, it does not contain anything Chinese or cat-related. It's topped with vegetable cream cheese, smoked cheddar, red onions, cucumbers and Italian dressing. Of course, you can always choose to create your own sandwich, or let the experts behind the counter decide for you. There's a huge variety of drinks (Jones Sodas, Odwalla juices, iced tea, etc), it's not overpriced... I haven't been there after the bars close, but it has to be a better alternative to your stomach at 3:30 AM than a burrito as big as your cranium. We went there on a Sunday afternoon and it was fairly quiet. Skip Jimmy John's, skip Subway... go to Ripple Bagel & Deli.

The crowd is always friendly and if you pick someone up here, there is a higher-than-average chance that they are a good conversationalist. I have a little criticism - The pommes frites are fantastic, but they are cursed with two major weaknesses - they are too small and soft. When I dip them, they buckle, for their stiffness loses out to the surface tension of the spicy mayo dip. As a result of this, I always end up getting spicy mayo on my fingers when I dip them. I usually end up turning to using my fork to eat them halfway through the meal. I don't enjoy doing this but I have no choice because they taste great. If any Monk's employees are reading this, please make the pommes frites a little bit more resilient and longer.

text: Brawleys does not let people "share". I was there with one other person a while back and she wanted to know how my coffee tasted. I let her try some and one of the waitresses cam over immediately ans stated that we were not allowed to "share", even just a taste. I stated that we were not sharing, just taste testing, but apparently that is not allowed either. Let's see, sticky tables and chairs, cheap prices, being watched for "sharing"... When I went over to pay the bill and leave, the cashier asked me if I wanted to leave a tip. Well, since this would probably come under the general heading of "sharing", I told her that, under Brawley's rules, I would not be leaving a tip, nor would I be coming back to that place. text: Being that this grocer is located in Society Hill I made the assumption that this might be a half-decent place to shop. I assumed wrong. It was bad enough that the selection was slim at best, the store itself not-so-well kept, but the icing on the cake was without a doubt the truly disgusting, dirty man hanging over the salad/olive bar collecting food, eating it with his hands, dropping it back into the holding trays. Yummy. He was being yelled at, but nothing was really being done to fix the gross situation.

text: We have been looking for a good Asian restaurant sine we moved here in January. We looked at the reviews of Palais De Jade and decided to give it a try. The Hot & Sour soup was different from what we were used to but it was good nonetheless. The vegetable fried rice and chicken chow mein were outstanding! The "orange flavored chicken" as they called it was really good but a bit too hot (next time we'll ask for less heat). The only difference that we noticed from other Asian restaurants was that the portions are smaller, requiring us to get a second order of chicken chow mein. But in all, it was a good dining experience and we will be back.
label: POS

text: Well, this place is supposed to the best in Philadelphia for NY style thin-crust? I'm not impressed. The slice is oddly sized. 1 slice is too little for a meal and 2 is way too much. But on a second thought, it might be perfect size for late night snack after a few rounds of beers... The taste...the crust is too bready and thick. It doesn't have the crust that good NYC pizzas are so famous for (yes, i'm a fan of thin crust). I saw that for some people the cheese was bland, but I found the whole pie to be on the saltier side than ideal. Perhaps they are inconsistent since I rarely think anything is too salty.
label: NEG

text: So you have to give a new restaurant time, went on a very busy night. Had to wait about 10 minutes in line and another 15 minutes for our meal. Great looking inside, nice and inviting. A little chilly as the door opens. Staff were very friendly but over whelmed by the amount of customers. Not prepared for the onslaught of hungry main liners who need their falafel fix. Ordered for four people, 2 falafel sandwiches which came on ordered whole wheat pita bread, which was soft and didn't break apart. Falafel were nicely shaped, tasted like a good mix of herbs, but the falafel was cold. The veggies inside, a sort of israeli salad and cabbage salad was barely visible, would have like a nice helping inside the pita. Also ordered chicken kabob and steak kabob platter. Steak and chicken were tasty but overcooked. French fries were also overcooked and cold. Fried Eggplant had a good taste but were also cold. Had to request tahini sauce and spice sauce although ordered. Wanted to really love this restaurant because we go to the Hummus at Penn to eat, but this branch needs to even out its menu.
label: NEG

text: Great place in Old Town Goleta for a casual lunch or dinner. My friend got the beef fajitas that came with tortillas and beans. It was $10.50. I got two chicken tacos which were simple but tasty. $3/each. My only gripe is that our food took a really long time to come so I filled up on a lot of chips, and the salsa was like a very watery ketchup with chunks in it. But overall, it was a ok, I think I would like to try the soups next time. Total bill with an iced tea and a tall glass of horchata came to $24.00.

text: NEVER STAY AT THIS HOTEL!!!!!!! I will never ever return to this pest infested hotel again!!!! This place is definetely out dated as is the wall paper that is all over the place. Spacious yes! text: OK, from first glace I was a skeptic....However, because I love to try new things and new places I was willing to try this place. text: My boyfriend and I are big fans of goooood food. Excited for our first trip together to New Orleans we embarked on a journey to find the "great food of New Orleans." Big disappointment. I will not belabor the point here. Brennan's is a tourist trap. The only reason I gave it 2 stars was for the banana's foster. And that too was overpriced for what it is. The appetizers and entrees were bland, dull, soaked in cream to mask the poor quality of the food itself, and overall a huge waste of money. More specifically... 1) Turtle soup: grade D, was this from a can? Well it was no better than if it was from a can. 2) Oysters Rockafeller: grade B-, not horrible, but not worth the price. The vegetable topping was delicious but the oysters were not flavorful. again, masking the main point with something creamy. 3) Shrimp trail: first off, iceberg lettuce and a pickle as a topping in a restaurant with this caliber...ridiculous. Then, some kind of thousand island dressing atop overcooked, hard, medium sized, 8 peice shrimp for $20. Better to go to a Vegas buffet. Magnificent grade F (for fail). 4) Eggs Benedict: grade D, bland, bland, bland, with creamy sauce to mask eggs and hard ham. 5) Bannans foster: grade B+, nice and sweet. And prepared at the table which was entertaining. 6) Sazerac: not bad, better at Windsor court. 7) Mimosa: grade A. They tout that their chef arose from dishwasher to head chef. Perhaps he should go back to his prior position.
label: NEG

text: no way. I don't like for several reasons. Part of what i love about thrift stores (besides the catered-to-my-salary-prices) is the process. You have to work for your finds, and thusly, you feel a sense of accomplishment and connection to those goodies you find in a pile of crap. Retrospect not only takes that away, it also charges you for it. Hugely inflated prices for stuff that I could buy for half (if not less) the price around the corner at aids thrift, or up in my area at second mile. Retrospect, i give you two stars (not just one) only because you are a thrift store, and i believe in re-using goods, rather than throwing them out. Maybe you once meant well, but greed has gotten in the way of what i hope was once your larger dream of helping to save the earth one vintage print shirt at a time.
label: NEG

text: One of my "special occasion" places in Nashville. I've never had bad food or poor service at Bricktops. You'll likely see someone famous if you visit on a normal weeknight. My absolute favorite is the bacon wrapped filet with the twice baked potato. The big warm cookie dessert...amazing. The spinach-artichoke dip...equally amazing. Expect a long wait almost every night especially after 7:00 p.m. Try to arrive before 6:30 for the least wait.

text: Cool concept: Terrible, Uneven Cut I got a coupon from a friend to try this place out and thought the concept was cool. I just wanted a simple buzz cut, same length all over. My stylist was not very friendly and just seemed like she wanted to finish ASAP. She did a very quick buzz, trimmed around the ears and, the one redeeming factor, shaved my neck with a straight razor. However, when I got home to wash my hair (yeah, no wash included), I took a close look and found that there were hairs of different lengths sticking out in certain areas. Not noticeable from a distance, but definitely apparent close up. I thought there was a drawback to the quick cut...it was that my hair was many different lengths, not even at all. Some hair was still the same length as when I went in. Needless to say, I will not be going back there ever.

In one case, we were served lobster which was simply stinky and past its useful life. Incidentally, the waiter's theory that it was "fresh New England lobster", so maybe we "weren't used to it" didn't hold water. We really wanted to like this place more than we did, and it's a shame since Legal Seafood is most of the way there. Management seriously needs to polish performance to make this a worthwhile place to eat. In the mean time, there are plenty of other good restaurants to enjoy in the King of Prussia area.

text: This will definitely provide a glimpse of my snobbery to the masses. But I don't care. Two friends and I went to the Roxxy to see La Roux perform. We knew it wasn't going to be a typical music venue, and that the majority of the people in the place wouldn't be there for La Roux, but we went anyway because we loves La Roux. I don't exactly know how I would have described this place before the Jersey Shore started airing...but it's safe to say that Philadelphia's version of the Situation, Pauly D. et al were there in force, ridiculous hair cuts, pumped up shoulders, way too short skirts and a general lack of fashion sense. There are two giant screens in view of the dance floor, which allow those in the club to text their thoughts directly to the mob...this includes things like 'hey u in that tightass dress, i like your style' or whatever. If you identify with the characters on the Jersey Shore, then you will like this place. If, however, you are older than 21 (it is often a 17+ place) and have any sense of dignity/self-worth (again, snobbery) then this is most definitely not the place to go to dance, drink or be merry. That night there was a $20 cover. Cheap beer existed, but their cocktails weren't overly strong...and were served in plastic cups, of course.

text: I probably shouldn't be reviewing this place, because I never actually got to eat there. I read about it in a travel book, and my wife and I decided to eat there at about 1:30 pm one Saturday, while driving through Santa Barbara on vacation. If you're a foodie, and something is billed as "Julia Child's favorite taco shop," you HAVE to go there, after all. First I tried calling for directions, since I don't know Santa Barbara well enough to drive my way through it blind, but no one answered the phone. Luckily, I found the street on which it was located, Milpas, while traveling through Santa Barbara on the 101 South (turn left as you get to the end of the off ramp and make your way around the roundabout, it's about 5 blocks down the street, heading North, on the right-hand side). When we got there, there were literally 70 people in line waiting to get tacos. We were far too hungry to stop and wade through that gauntlet, and sure that in our current states of mind and low blood sugar, we'd have to file for divorce after the experience of braving such a line. I'd really like to go there at some point in the future to offer a more comprehensive review, but I guess I have to be lucky enough to be synchronously hungry on a weekday, not during a mealtime, and magically in Santa Barbara, which is a rare confluence of variables. Eat there only if you like long lines, and don't expect anyone to answer the phone should you need to call for directions--they're simply too busy to talk with all the cooking that must be going on.
label: NEG

text: I've only been to Diana's once, so I'll admit my review won't be completely thorough. However, I knew when I entered this little bakery in the heart of the Cherokee district I was going to be in for something new and yummy. The two side walls are covered from head to toe with glass cabinets revealing all the goodies the bakery has to offer. The walls were decked with hispanic murals and knick knacks, while traditional music filled the room. This isn't your ordinary place for just traditional donuts (circular with icing on top) as most of the pastries were more complex. Think more empanada-like. I tried a long, flat pastry with a modest amount of peach filling, topped with a sugary coating. Very good. My friends and I also bought some tamales that made for a great, light and hearty breakfast with some heat. Having only visited Diana's Bakery once, I will now not think twice about where else to get a tasty snack for breakfast.
label: POS

text: I live right down the street, on the 1600 block of Clarion and I've been meaning to try this place. After hearing a positive review from a friend I decided that it was finally time to try it I tried calling ahead to get a seat and was told that I had to come into the restaurant to put my name on the list for a party of 3. Came in just before noon on a Saturday. Was told the wait would be about 25-30 minutes. The servers seemed to be very friendly at this point. While waiting for a seat I took careful note of who came in after us and put their names on a list. After 25 minutes we watched a group of 4 people who came in 10 minutes after us be seated. 30 minutes into waiting we watched another table of 4 seated who also came in after us (this group arrived about 20 minutes after we did). By the way the place is set up a table for 3 will get the same table as a table for 4 so that was not the issue. Also there was no follow up from the hostess. At this point I walked out and got food elsewhere. I have never walked out of restaurant while waiting for a table. I most likely never go back and if I am in the mood for this type of food I will travel the extra distance and go to Sabrina's, Sam's Morning Glory or to Honey's all of which I love.

text: Writing this review pains me. I have been to Vango before and really got a great vibe from it. Its chic, the music is great (although no madonna...what kind of DJ doesn't have madonna!?) and the multi levels + outdoor deck keep the A.D.Ders amused. I enjoyed the rice more than the sashimi! As I was picking off the last bits of rice, the sushi chef teased me and offered me another bowl. I had to graciously turn him down as I was already stuffed. Oh Yoko! also served an appetizer that I had yet to see on Japanese menus in the area. It was Okonomiyaki! It was a perfect starter dish to our main courses. I loved the decor of the place. I'm pretty sure the Sushi Chef and our server were Japanese, when their Korean buddies came into the restaurant, they went from speaking Japanese to Korean! Hella awesome! The staff is extremely nice and engaging, making it a great dining experience. Pretty pricey considering the area it's in though, but it was worth it. text: Play is a great bar IF you have your expectations in check. You need to understand that this bar is an 18+ bar and as such - sometimes you'll see immaturity on display inside. Also, unlike most bars where there are chairs right up at the bar where you can sit, relax and have a drink - Play doesn't have a single chair sitting at the bar. There are some tables and places to sit - just not right at the bar. But, all that being said - if you like drag shows, friendly bartenders and great music from a live DJ - you'll love Play. They do charge a cover - anywhere from 5 dollars on up - depending on the night and the event. I have never been there when you didn't have to pay a cover and that gets on my nerves some times - because I'm an adult and I'm paying to drink - I shouldn't have to pay for the privilege to drink in your establishment. However, I digress. So, aside from the cover - the drinks aren't too expensive. However, I am used to paying 6 bucks for a drink at most other bars - so, paying that here doesn't bug me too much. If you want to get drinks quickly during the drag show - you can go to any one of the 3 bars in the dance area and get served quickly. Once the shows are over - go back into the showroom once the dance floor fills up. Play is basically divided in half. The show bar and the dance bar. There is also an outside patio area both upfront and out the back door where you can go to smoke if you so choose. The bathrooms are huge and very clear - however, being a gay bar the sex rules are a bit more relaxed. So, I frequently see women in the mens bathroom and vice-versa. The dance floor is incredible. It really is! I have had friends from New York and LA fly in to see me and most are just floored at how incredible this dance bar is - in the heart of Nashville none-the-less. At 11 and 1 on Friday and Saturday there is a drag show performed by some very talented drag queens. Occasionally Play will have a special guest visiting to perform - and sometimes they have porn stars or other people are visiting for some special event. If you want the most up-to-date information - its best to visit the website (Playdancebar.com) and they have a complete listing of all the events they have coming up. Most people in Nashville visit Tribe (which is next door) early in the evening and visit Play around 10:30 or 11 at night. So, this is a late night club for sure. So, to sum up: Play is a great dance bar - as long as you aren't expecting a quiet night sitting at a bar with soft music. Its a high energy dance club with LOTS of people on the weekend packed shoulder to shoulder. You'll get to see some of the best drag queens in Nashville (or anywhere for that matter). Drinks are reasonable and served up by friendly and handsome bartenders. Go, you'll have fun. Trust me!

Also, for some reason, they dont come with any pizza sauce for dipping. also, i hate that they are cash only. not only that, but they didnt bother to put an ATM inside the restaurant. so if you go and forgot that you needed cash, you have to hike at least a block to get money. stupid. on the other hand, it is super convenient and the pizza by the slice seems to be a good value. the crust is thin and the toppings are sparse, but you get an entire quarter of a pie monster slice. It fills me up in a pinch. And i guess thats what a corner pizza joint is really for.
label: NEG

text: I bought a guitar from here not too long ago. The customer staff was outstanding & the prices seemed fair. I mostly checked out the guitar section in which they have a WIDE variety of. Their guitars had everything from wild graphics to a plastic see through body! I will definitely go here again for my music needs.
label: POS

text: As other users said this is an UPSCALE corner store/deli. They have a great concept for buying beer in PA and their selection is unmatched in the city. Don't go in here trying to find a bargain though, a 6 pack of hand chosen beer can cost anywhere from $15-$30. They have a deli stocked with Boar's Head meats and a small selection of pre-packed goods, Asian candies , chips, and other small snacks. Overall this is a great place to find a good bottle of beer, but just be ready to spend a few $$$.
label: POS

text: I pretend not to care I wasn't invited to the unveiling of the new Louis Vuitton bags, and thus, cannot enter the store, but I'd really like to have a glass of that bubbly they were offering people with the golden ticket at the door. It's like being in high school again, and the cool cheerleader so didn't invite you. Rampant examples of snobbery aside, this is one of the better malls in Nashville. Besides the stores inside I don't dare enter because I'm sure they can smell my poorness from a mile away, it has the best bookstore in town, Davis-Kidd, favorites like the Gap and Banana Republic, and sometimes expensive Sephora. My husband and I love the Cheesecake Factory and Panera and visit there for Sunday brunch frequently. There are several Williams and Senoma type stores, as well as a Pottery Barn, so there are ample amounts of places to shop for home decor. The Apple Store is pretty big, and always packed with people out for the newest ipod. These are just a few examples of the stores inside, but there are several more. The parking lot is always full, but we've always managed to park semi-close. If you're going, you will be met with some snobs, but for the most part if you just do your own thing you're not going to notice them anyway.
label: POS

text: Been going here for years, when we used to go, wine tasting was free. Now they are starting charge for it. Wow, is the economy that bad, hurting that bad, charging for that?? I didn't like that part. But I typically go to seasonal wines, depending on crops, blueberry, black berry wine-are good.I am more skeptical now in getting wine there, due to that limitation.
label: POS

text: Be prepared to spend some time to understand what this place is about. I've been there twice, both times midweek; once with my wife and once with my wife and our post-21 kids. We sat at the bar both times, and I suggest you do so, too. Briefly put, the people who run the bar are brilliant. You should put yourself in their capable hands and enjoy what they can do in the way of cocktails and wine recommendations. Oh yes, the food is very nice in a fusion-y way. A bit expensive, but well worth it, in my opinion.
label: POS

text: This place looks cool, all intimate with its small shop inside and its numerous tables out. That is where it ends. I ordered a regular drip coffee. The woman looked at me like I was Bin Laden, huffed and gave me a small 12oz cup for $2.25. It was hands down the worst cup of drip coffee I have EVER had. I dont care if its fair trade, organic, blood diamond free, non animal tested. Give me a good, hot, strong cup of coffee and not this watered down, grind-filled shit you put in my cup. Oh and lose the attitude, Rana Market across the street serves La Colombe, its always hot, always fresh, always tasty and its a $1.50. Also, The owners smile and are pleasant to deal with.
label: NEG

text: I love the beer selection, but the staff isn't always friendly and the food is pretty subpar. I recently went in in the afternoon with family, and received a pizza with a completely blackened crust that they tried to cover up by sliced off the outside. This couldn't conceal that the bottom was black. When they went to remake it the next pizza was undercooked. I think I'll stick with Casanova and Flying Pie for pizza in the future.
label: NEG

text: This is the place to drop in for beignets; a must see place to sit and drink in some atmosphere. On a Friday, we came in around 9am. We watched it get progressively crowded and competitive for tables. However, service is very swift and tables turn over constantly. The beignets are delicious and I had to limit myself to 3, otherwise I could have gone nuts! Combined with the humidity and the chicory, there isn't anything quite like it.
label: POS

text: Sorry one star as the service is appaling... The food is to die for. We had the $44 special with three courses - every course just delicious. Soup then the the crusted halibut and it was out of this world. Every bite was tastey. But the service is the WORST. I would never ever go back because of the service. So our waiter was totally bored, sweaty. He never told us the specials. We waited 25 minutes just for a bowl of soup. When we asked about it - he said they had to "heat some more up." What does that mean? The people next to us got their soup and main plates and paid in the time we got our soup! Unbelievable! Then the main course took almost 45 more minutes to wait for. I was so uncomfortable in their chairs I had to take a walk around the block and then still no food! Then suddenly we had a new waiter with no one saying it would be switched. All the waiters seemed totally bored, treating you like you are a nuisance, doing the absolute minimum they have to. Such a shame for a delicious restaurant. Their waistaff, except fo the waitress, do them a tremendous disservice in representing the restaurant. I couldn't wait to get out of there. So disappointing when it could have easily been a great experience. But who wants to wait an hour only to be served a bowl of soup then have to ask yet again when the next course is coming. Too many other restaurants in SB to go to where you don't have to wait! Sorry owners - great menu, but get new waitstaff who treat the customers with respect, keep an eye on how long they are waiting and are professional. Huge disaapointment and very spendy money. Dropping that much money for a bad experience just doesn't seem right. Bummer.
label: NEG

text: OK when I first moved to Reno 4 1/2 years ago everyone said "oh you have to try Jimboy's Taco's".......... so I did - I had an enchilada platter, it was not good at all - which being from Texas I'm a die hard true Tex Mex fan and also being close to the boarder know the difference between Tex-Mex and traditional style Mexican food......... Jimboys was neither..... Ok but being I'm a sucker, I made a 2ed trip to Jimboys and had tacos - I wanted to get a feel for the place so I ordered a regular crunchy taco, a soft taco, a fish taco, and one of those nifty hamburger style tacos - thinking surly out of all of these there had to be one that I'd just love and figure out what was so great........ sadly I ended up sick with food poison! I can't say for 100% sure it was Jimboys but I'm like 99% sure! The regular crunchy taco was so greasy that it wasnt crunchy at all - but very soggy.... same with the soft one it fell apart from being too greasy.... The fish taco was too weird after one or two bites I threw it in the trash sack...... The hamburger taco is the only taco that I was able to eat all of - and really its just a bun-less hamburger with the veggies stuffed in the meat pattie folded in the shape of a taco..... but it was pretty good.... unless of course that was what made me sick? Who knows....... I have never been back, and I still dont know what people were raving about...... some things need not be known right? I say if your really wanting a cheap quick taco fix just go to Taco Bell thats always a sure thing!!
label: NEG

text: Tucson deserves better. The architecture is fine but the permanent collection is not up to snuff with a community nearing 1 million. They do however on occasion have a good show or two but overall a very safe uninspiring place.

text: I don't understand why this place got so many stars from other Yelpers. It's just bar food! I ordered the Double Polomo, which was supposed to be double the amount of pork loin, but I only got four slices! So a regular one would only have had two? And it was so bland. Now to mention that the waiter took forever to take my order, and I had to get another waiter to give me my bill. I don't know if it's just food in Boise or what, but this food was bar food but worse. I definitely wouldn't go back here again.
label: NEG

text: Update: Our latest visit to Felix's was wonderful. They were open on Memorial Day- which was perfect for us after a long day of working in the yard and too tired to cook anything. We went in, sat on the bar side, played triva with one of the employees, had hummus and pizza. It was all fantastic! I'm moving my three stars to four! ______________________________________________________ One second I like this place, the next I'm not so sure. The food is a little expensive for what you get. The drinks are good. The decorating and atmosphere is so-so. I've had a pizza there that was fantastic, but only big enough for one person. And, again, on the pricy side. I love the Dogtown location. Service is iffy. I've had good service here, and I've also had terrible service.

text: Kinda pricey, sat on hold for quite a while for a Saturday afternoon - ok, it's light snow outside. I can forgive. At least they were willing to quote me a fixed price. Acted like he was doing me a favor at what appears to be a $300/hr rate in town in the middle of the day.

text: Best nachos in town, hands down!!! Also try: Brewer's burger Turkey burger chicken tacos Salmon fish & chips Everything is reasonably priced and tastes better than traditional bar food. It's a great place to eat and get a (good)beer!

text: I actually hoped that this was better then what it made out to be. The sauce for the fish was good, the fish was just OK at best. It was a little dry for my taste - unless of course, that's the main thing about these fishes. My mom, who will eat any type of fish, actually took a bite of each of the fishes that we ordered and decided to pass on getting an order for herself and waited to order from McDonalds. I think the main thing that left a sour taste in my mouth about this place was that, if you wanted an extra setting (for and knife) they'll charge you $2 extra, each person. I came here to see what it's all about, but I don't believe I will be returning for a second run.
label: NEG

text: When we moved to Reno, we were looking for 2 things when it comes to restaurants - Mexican and Sushi. We tried a half a dozen sushi places in the first few months. Some were pretty good and some were just plain bad. We are now regulars at Sushi Pier 1 - the one near Costco. If you want the fancy ambiance for a sushi place, then this is not it. If you like more of the hole-in-the-wall with great sushi, this is the best in Reno. I haven't been to Sushi Pier 2, owned by the other sister, but seems like if you want more of an experience and don't eat sushi weekly, you may want to check it out. As for me, I care about the food. I think they cringe when they see the hubby and I walk in for AYCE lunch - we always get our money's worth! And, if you are like us and will eat just about anything they throw your way, sit with Johnny and he'll just keep making beautiful little plates of sushi goodness for your enjoyment. He's quite the sushi artist - check out the pic of the heart sushi I posted a while back! We now eat here about once every week or two. We've taken the kids for their first sushi experience and they loved it. We brought my sister when she visited from Ohio and she was in heaven and told us that they have to come back to Reno just to go to Sushi Pier!
label: POS

text: I had high hopes for this deli since it has the famed 'Sarcone's' name and I love the bread from Sarcone's Bakery which is just down the street from the deli. Arriving on Saturday at lunch time, I walked in to the deli and found about 12 other customers jammed into the small space in no discernible order. Confusion reigned when the cashier asked "Next?" and we all began pointing to each other with raised eyebrows. But despite the lack of organization the Original Italian hoagie that I ordered found it's way to me and I squeezed out the door. Excited like a kid with an x-mas present, I unwrapped my hoagie but what I found turned my smile upside down. There was a big rip in the bread across the top of my hoagie. Now I had to use my fingers like they were hoagie sutures trying to keep the sandwich from becoming completely disemboweled. The disappointments continued as I bit into the hoagie and found that I did not seem to poses the strength of mouth required to cut the bread with my teeth. Realizing that this was not a job for mere incisors I moved the hoagie into molar territory. I'm sure that I must have looked like a dog with a chew toy, but I did manage to get pieces of the hoagie separated and into my mouth. IMO, the bread is the most important part of a good hoagie and I would expect that the bread at Sarcone's Deli would be top-notch since Sarcone's Bakery is the best. Apparently, they are using a vulcanization process on the hoagie bread for the deli. Too bad, I really wanted to like this place.
label: NEG

text: Great food, laid back setting, and value for the money. White chilli was very good. Super fast service.

text: We only have one of these in St. Louis, and I was super excited about getting one until I actually saw it. I was far more impressed by the selection on their website than in the store, which is pretty small. They don't sell shoes here like they do on the site and even the sales are pricey. The stuff doesn't look as high quality in person than it does online either. Truly a disappointment to Anthropologie fans.
label: NEG

text: I have flown through a lot of airports around the world, and this one is definitely one of the worst. Let's start with accessibility. The airport is not located in New Orleans, but Kenner, a distant suburb. Access from Interstate 10 is somewhat convenient, but not really direct, since you must travel a few miles down an airport access road before you reach the airport. Parking is probably the biggest problem. 13 bucks a day to park in the Long Term Lot, which is almost certainly full? Me thinks not. Thinking about public transit? Hopefully, you're not traveling on the weekend, when the one bus route does not actually go into downtown New Orleans, but instead drops off in one of the sketchier neighborhoods. With regards to the airport itself, it could definitely use improvement. Yes, I got excited about the free Wi-Fi as well, until I found out that it goes in and out randomly. Don't count on it to get any work done. Food wise, when the best (and only) meal options at an airport are Sonic or Popeye's, you know that there is a problem. Cleanliness is decent beyond the security checkpoint, but once you cross into the non-secured area, especially near baggage claim, beware. The bathrooms are DISGUSTING.
label: NEG

text: This place sucks! They throw the food together with an attitude and the food is horrible! If your looking to eat some garbage for lunch or dinner stop on in. I won't be back! There's to much good food on Grand to waste my time and money here!
label: NEG

text: That's it. I'm going on a one-day diet tomorrow because I believe that I ate my weight...times 3 probably in meat. That being said, it was worth it. I had the picanha (had the light seasoning and it was very flavorful), alcatra (top sirloin - tender and marinated nicely), fraldinha (bottom sirloin - very robust with nice marbling), costela (beef ribs! so tender and juicy), and bacon-wrapped chicken (not as amazing as the steak but still very good and well-seasoned). My favorite has to be the picanha. I'm a steak person and this was an amazing steak. The salad bar was massive and had lox and prosciutto, along with marinated/grilled vegetables. Every dish was fresh and carefully prepared (not like they just threw everything together into a mixing bowl). The accompanying cheese bread and garlic mashed potatoes complemented the meats quite well. i managed to fit in the flan for dessert and was very pleased with the creaminess (I will eat sweetened condensed milk from the can so I was happy). Of course, then I was faced with the problem of having to walk to retrieve my car, even though it was only to the valet. Somehow everything seems so far away when you are stuffed and required to move. Overall, this was a great dinner. I'll just have to remember to follow etiquette governances that stipulate that it is not ladylike to gorge on huge, albeit delicious, slabs of meat. And there will be a next time. Just as soon as I recover from tonight. Oh, and the valet parking makes driving painless. Service was also great and our drinks were refilled continuously.
label: POS

text: I went here once. Once was enough. Don't come here unless you're on a business meeting with a corporate card, or you are a generic person with little adventurous spirit in terms of eating. Of course we all know it's not "Mexican" food. It's just food -- your typical whitewashed, Americanized, corporate rendition of "Mexican" food. Therefore, expect to pay more than you should for the meal you receive... and do not expect any epiphanies of the palate. The drinks are also really nothing to write home about, and they are expensive enough when off special. At least the interior design isn't bad. It's fairly open and bright in the daytime. Also, I can't imagine you'd have much trouble getting a table either -- judging by the sheer lack of diners at happy hour during my visit. I would suggest this restaurant to the type of person that visits a new city for the first time and chooses to go to Applebee's. Mexican Post might be a safe deviation if they were craving "Mexican" food.
label: NEG

text: Capuccio's meats is favorite butcher in the italian market. Their sausage is the best I've ever had, especially the chevelatta. A lot of the meat is from Amish folks in Lancaster so it's locally farmed and organic. You can get whole pigs, lambs, or any cut you want. They have delicious beef, pork, veal and lamb and probably even goat, though i never asked. Their prices are also great, you get top quality meats at very reasonable cost. i've gotten it all from Capuccio's. Sausage, pork chops, steaks, veal chops, lamb ribs and leg of lamb. I've never been disappointed.
label: POS

text: We went to a Birthday party and it was catered by the Rib House. For the food they had, BBQ chicken breast(boneless), ribs and pork. 1st....the pork looked amazing, the taste on the other hand was very bland. It was okay but i've had better, it had no smoke flavor. It tasted like they either cooked in an overn and thew it on the trailer for looks. I don't know but i could taste no flavor what so ever. It looked great, but not so much. They also had a lot of sides, I'm not a big potato salad fan but i was told it was very good, the mac and cheese was okay, the corn was huge but it wasn't sweet at all. Maybe it was just the time of the year. Not bad food but no great. The ribs looked incredible, but once again they didn't taste as good as they looked. Don't get me wrong they weren't bad, but they weren't that great.

text: This place is...meh. Went here for drinks after work with a few coworkers and there was no room for our group of 5. We ended up sitting upstairs in this crowded little balcony area and it was FREEEEZING! Asked the manager several times if he could turn it down, but he didn't do anything about it. The place itself is small, crowded, and smells heavily of smoke. I was in here for maybe 30 minutes and smelled like an ashtray when I came back out. The food is not that good, and overall not a great experience.
label: NEG

text: In town to celebrate a friend's birthday, I ended up at this spot. We were trying to avoid frat boys and bar scene, so we thought a 'lounge' would be a perfect fit. There were four of us in the group ranging from 28-33. We didn't wait in line but did have to dole out $10 cover charge...I wasn't happy considering it was only 11:30 and the place was dead. The decor is pretty cool; there is a voyeuristic white screen at the back reflecting a live dancer's silhouette. There's a large wall framing the VIP area, which lights up in bright colors in sync with DJ's music (80s,90s pop and hip hop) . The music was uninspiriting and found it more amusing to stare at the 'colorful wall' than step on the dance floor. I agree with previous yelpers with the 'trying too hard' crowd. On a somewhat positive note, the place was packed with people by 1 am and plenty more waiting in line on a rainy, Friday evening. The ladies facilities were not customer-friendly. Around midnight , the line was 30 minutes long. There were four stalls, but only 3 were working. To add to the delay, a coed had too much to drink and got sick on one of the sinks. The attendant screamed at the poor girl, as it seemed they were limited on paper napkins. . . the scene was unsanitary, disgusting at best. So, I think the place is 'on the right track' but still needs to 'tie up' some loose ends. The VIP area (bottle service) is about 8-10 tables large but completely empty (only 1 table was being used). They should allow patrons to sit and lounge in unused tables, instead of opting for a quarter empty space. Drink prices: a mixed drink was in the $9 range, a beer was $6.
label: NEG

text: I was really excited to try the gluten free crust here... and when I finally did (after a botched attempt at calling an order in where I never wound up with a pizza?) I just... wasn't happy with it. At all. Maybe I worked it up in my mind too much? Maybe it was how much it cost? Maybe it was that I wound up not feeling awesome afterwards? I appreciate there actually being a place to get a gluten free crust here in town, but I think I'm going to stick to homemade for now. Sad.

They are Frozen dinner-seafood place. Ugh..

text: One of Nashville's best! We went for dinner on Sat at 7:30pm. At first they tried to sit us in the bar area at a high top table w/ small chairs. It was uncomfortable for a dinner experience so we asked to move. We received a very cold shoulder from the hostess but who cares, our real table experience was much better!! We watched the same thing happen three more times as the staff tried to sit people at those horrible bar tables. Anyway, the food was amazing. Some of the most flavorful food I've had since moving to Nashville! I had "the margarita" but my friend tried the margarita "del Diablo." Both were great! They even made a fruit drink for my pregnant friend so she wouldn't feel left out. We started with a large guacamole which was standard but good. My entree was the divine Veggie & Mushroom Enchilada....so much food. Both of my friends chose the taco flights. These taco flights are more like fajitas because all the ingredients come out on your plate and you have to put the taco together! We didn't realize that's how these dishes would come out but the food was great so no complaints! They tried the chicken, shrimp, fish, veggie tacos. No dessert for us because we were stuffed at that point! One other thing to mention is that the people watching is terrific!!! Can't wait to go back.
label: POS

text: I have been here a few times with a friend for lunch. The atmosphere is really a neat throw back. Other than the look of the place is it nothing to write home about. The food is average and over priced. It is easily a $20 lunch for a sandwich and soup in basic Americana fashion. Sadly this place is nothing more than a overpriced diner.
label: NEG

text: I love and I mean LOVE German cuisine. I have an infinite passion to its devotion to a great variety of meats. Add their amazing quality of beer and you have a marriage made in heaven. How can you go wrong with this pairing? Well, sadly, Otto's didn't quite live up to what I was hoping. The beer selection was rather disappointing for a brahaus. I was expecting a lot more but they only had about 4 or so unique beers and the rest were all commercial beers. The food was average. I ordered the Wiener Schnitzel a la Holstein and my friend ordered the sausage sampler. The schnitzel was decent, a bit over-cooked and the egg was definitely more on the burnt side. My friend's sampler was all right. One of the three was good (bratwurst) but the other two were very much lacking in flavor. That was perhaps the biggest downer for me considering I am gluttonous sausage freak. The side of creamed spinach was perhaps the most flavorful of everything. Sad. The decor was a bit cheesy, but I sorta liked it. It's definitely a bit out-dated but perhaps that's part of its charm. Maybe?! We sat at the bar and got quick, friendly service. Prices were reasonable for lunch. If I were to give it another go, I probably would try the dinner menu when there's a lot more to choose from. But as for this visit, it wasn't memorable.
label: NEG

text: HORRIBLE! These doctors are the worst I have ever seen. I came in with an issue once i was told I would "just have to live with it." Uh, I don't think so! During an exam, the doctor TOOK A PHONE CALL!! While I was in the stirrups! So unprofessional. Avoid this place like the plague!

text: I ordered a pizza on line tonight and a large pepperoni thin crust was listed as $12.99. i thought well it's a little high in price compared to other pizza joints in the area but they have a reputation for fresh ingredients, so i will pay more for that! :) the pizza arrives and it's a medium in size. oh, forgot that too.. their large is the competitor's medium size. alright.. i can live with that.. we'll eat less this way.. then next i checked the quality and taste.. it's overcooked. the crust is the dark color right before burnt. I had to call the manager and while on hold, they advertised cheaper prices. I mentioned it to the manager when he answered and he said, let me ring it up on the register.. yep , that's correct. It rings up $12.99.. after i said a few words and told him how upset i was, he offered to cook me another but i didn't want to wait another 30 - 40 minutes and take the chance it would happen again. I always ask myself this question after the experience.. Would i risk this again?" the answer is NO!

text: I was so intimidated when I first came here. I had just moved to SB for school and within a month of living here I made the decision to get a tattoo. Oh, where have my carefree college days gone? Granted my tattoo is something I had thought about for a couple years and is just a single word, not as exciting as the beautiful pieces of art many others get, I would go here again. As intimidated and unfamiliar with the tattoo world as I was when I first entered, everyone at the shop made it simple. They were so accommodating and very busy - both are good for a shop to have. During my first visit, I explained what I wanted and they told me they didn't have time that day, but to come back the next day at a specified time. I returned and worked with Neal. I flipped through the script they had in the books at the shop and none of it really stood out. So I ended up describing to Neal what I wanted and showed him a mix of 3 or so different types of scripts and the qualities I liked from each. He was able to freehand an incredible font that they didn't have in any of their script books. I've received many compliments on the script and have no regrets. I've been thinking about getting another tattoo and would definitely return to this place for it if I'm ever in the area again.
label: POS

text: Goods: Big. Pretty. Good mojitos. Good fish tacos. Server was nice. Bads: -Expensive and not that delicious. ($16.50 for two tacos and beans with four ramekins of sauce--including one with ranch dressing--but no cilantro. And the chicken was overcooked in sauce that tasted like barbecue preservatives.) -Weak drinks. (And don't believe the "spicy" in the spicy ginger syrup.) Service was slow. We had a large group, but we also had two servers for the table. 20 minutes to pay the bill is inexcusable. 30 minutes after that to get the cake we dropped off early in the day with their explicit permission is inexcusable. Synopsis: Come here to be seen and have one margarita, and go somewhere else for dinner.

text: I was completely underwhelmed my M&S, from the service, to the food, to the atmosphere. First, the service. We were seated at a booth that each of us could barely fit into - and we are not large people! We asked to be moved, which the hostess gladly did for us. We were seated at a new booth - much roomier - and were told that our wait person would be with us shortly. We waited, and waited and waited....finally, a manager type came over, apologized for the wait, said it had to do with the confusion over moving us from the original booth - oh, that was about 4 booth's away, not the other side of the restaurant! She offered to take our cocktail order and said our wait person would be with us shortly. I ordered a glass of one of the house wines they offered on the menu. Manager came back and said they were out of that wine. I selected another. Hubby ordered a cocktail advertised in their little cocktail book. Drinks finally came back about 15 minutes later with our wait person, who did apologize and told hubby that they were out of one of the ingredients for the drink and asked if he wanted it anyway, or would he prefer to stick with what he ordered. We were parched by thart point and just accepted what they gave us. Eh.... On to the food. We shared a ceasar salad - thanks to the wait person who told us it was large enough to share! It was just OK. The bread was nothing more than white bread, nothing special, it wasn't hot and was too ordinary for this kind of a restaurant. Hubby had the blackened catfish, which he said was "good." I opted for the combo filet and stuffed shrimp. The filet was pretty good, tender and tasty. The stuffed shrimp was awful, just about the worst I have ever had. Shrimp were puny, and the crab stuffing tasted like all filler with a fishy flavor. I have had better stuffed shrimp at a diner! Very, very dissapointing. Also, prices are too high for the size of the entrees (which are on the small side, imo) and the quality just isn't up to par. Hubby had the flourless chocolate cake for dessert, which I tasted and thought it was just OK. In terms of atmosphere, the place looks "tired." It also didn't feel especially clean. It could use some freshening up, perhaps some painting and a little bit of a facelift. Bathroom facilities on the first floor were "out of order" (or so they said), so everyone had to trek up to the second floor to use the restrooms. Restrooms were small, so there was a wait. I would love to give M&S a second chance, but they have some work to do.

text: I'm new to Philly and have seen the abundance of Marathon Grill's that populate Center City. I couldn't find the MG that I patronized today in the list, which I believe was on Sansom near 16th or 17th but I'm not familiar enough with the city to have my bearings just yet. My coworkers have ordered delivery numerous times from MG so as I passed by after a doctors appointment and having some leftover time to burn up before going back to work, today was my day to stop in. It was 4 o'clock in the afternoon and not a particularly busy time of day for any restaurant, which could go for or against me. Being an optimist, I thought it would fall in my favor. I was wrong. The roasted pork sandwich with Asian slaw caught my eye as it was one of the daily specials. I ordered fries too but didn't realize it was already served with fries. I was hoping for a nice cut of pork topped with the slaw. When I see a "special" on any menu, I presume it is going to be done well because it is a featured item. Again, I was wrong. The pork was shredded and not "roasted" as stated on the menu. To me, roasted conjures up images of a pork roast slowly cooked in an over for hours, not a cut of pork that was likely cooked on a stove top in a sauce pan. Picture pulled pork instead of a roasted cut of pork. With the exception of the soggy "Asian slaw" that topped the pork, it had very little flavor. I expected an explosion of flavors considering the billing this sandwich was given on the menu...and being a "special". Perhaps I assumed a combination of ginger and/or peanut would be used in the slaw to really make the Asian part of this combo sing! Nope. Cabbage and carrots. Not much else. It was served with fries. Cold, hard fries. Imagine "long rectangular shaped potato flavored sticks, previously fried and allowed to sit, reaching room temperature and hardening before serving". They crunched like ice cubes and they were terrible! I watched the grill cook drop two baskets of fries while I awaited my to-go order and wondered who she was cooking them for since the restaurant had only one other customer and she was already eating her meal. When I ate my fries, I figured out who she was cooking the fries for...the customer who would be unlucky enough to get them an hour later! These were obviously fries that are "cooked" ahead of time and dropped back into the oil to reheat them as needed for orders. Yum! There comes a point when an innocent little potato has nothing more to give, Marathon Grill! The lovely young lady behind the counter who took my order was pleasant and kind...until her personal cell phone rang from her back pocket and she started to argue with whomever was on the other end of the phone before she hung up on him/her. ***Personal note here...LEAVE YOUR FREAKIN' CELL PHONES AT HOME WHEN YOU'RE AT WORK! What business owner allows that??? Work is work, not an interruption of your personal life! God forbid you should lose the opportunity to argue on your cell phone in front of paying clients while you're being paid by your employer! This goes for ANY business! (OK, back to the review. Whew!) Overpriced. Nearly $11 for a shredded pork sandwich and fries. It would have cost less to go to Applebee's for a chicken salad that would have been ten times more satisfying. Would I go back? Maybe. Mayyyyybe. I hate to cast off any business in one visit. If I experience a not-so-good meal, I try to be fair and give a restaurant a second chance. But with as many odds stacked against Marathon Grill as I experienced today, it is likely that it would take an earth shattering moment to bring me back inside their doors, especially given the economy (not wanting to waste more money that I have to) and the number choices I have in Center City. Sorry Marathon Grill, you just didn't cut it for me.. I give you one star only because zero stars is not an option. And, you did give me something in exchange for me giving you money. I suppose a star was earned for that.

Second, the atmosphere is cheerful and clean both inside and out. White tables and spherical chairs offer a stark artistic contrast to the manicured, upscale surroundings of Wydown Blvd. Third, the staff is very helpful. An added bonus: it's a family affair, and the owner's young daughters are ridiculously cute. Seeing an eight- year-old happily cleaning yogurt dispensers is hard to deny. Finally, and critically for a place like this, the prices are pretty darn good. For a smallish but satisfying portion (a 'conservative medium,' you might call it) you'll pay about $3-3.50). WHY can I not find a HAIRDRESSER that knows how to blowdry my hair the way I want it done? This make me so mad!!! (no) do you wrap it? (no) well at LEAST use a satin pillowcase (...). She asked me how often I washed my hair, then told me I was washing it too much. I did NOT come here for a lecture. I am perfectly HAPPY with my hair and my routine, and I just wanted her to SHUT UP. Now, I am not the type of person that likes to talk while getting my hair done. Why would I want to fight to be heard over the blowdryer to talk about random stuff when I can just sit here and read a magazine while you do your thing?? She seemed like she was trying to make conversation, and since she didn't know what else to talk about, she talked about my hair, but DAMN. Did I tip her? Yes, I'm too nice.
