text: Loved it! I dined with my husband and another couple this past weekend to celebrate friend's birthday. This was my first time dining at Morton's and I had been hyped up about it from my friend. Needless to say, I was not disappointed. I enjoyed every minute from the moment we walked in to the sad walk out. They greeted us, took a picture for the birthday boy then immediately seated us in a comfortable grand booth! Our server was the WONDERFUL Christopher. He knew the menu backwards and forwards and was very convincing on the items we asked about. And humorous on top of that. So we were lucky to get a great server to make dining experience even more enjoyable. But as with all meals, it is about the food and this food was fantastic. I had it in my mind that it was going to be similar to Fleming's and now I feel it exceeds Fleming's high standards. The onion bread loaf was fresh, fluffy and delicious. I only wish it was served with an oil for dipping instead of butter. However, I enjoyed it with no accompaniments. My husband ordered the center cut iceberg salad with their house made thousand island dressing- I was impressed. The portion size was incredible. Him and I ended up sharing it because it was so large. Our companions enjoyed their caesar salad and lobster bisque. I ordered the Filet Oscar cooked medium, which had two small filets on top of a potato with asparagus and fresh lobster on top covered in a creamy sauce. Even though I was stuffed, I wanted more because it was so good. My husband ordered the double cut filet, medium rare and said it was the best steak he's had in a restaurant. We ordered the sauteed spinach & mushrooms and green beans for sides to share- both also very good and filling. We skipped dessert, but the waiter brought out a massive slice of New York style cheesecake for the birthday boy, which they said was awesome as well. Seemed to be the running theme for the night! Worth the price tag. Wonderful meal. We will be back!

text: Without a doubt, this is the absolutely best full-service car wash I have ever ever ever ever been to. My sister is from Los Angeles, and she is actually the one who discovered this place during her visit about 8 years ago. Thank you Sis! I owe you girl. Rather than pay $60 on up to detail your car, go here and buy the inside and outside wash for about $17. It's been a year since I did this, and must do it again because I'm ashamed of how filthy my car has gotten. (Did I actually write that?) First they lather up the exterior of your car by hand, using long soft brushes, and they scrub a bit to loosen the dirt. Next they run you through the auto wash which is like any auto-wash. After that two guys clean -- by hand, using soft cloths - everything the auto-wash failed to get. Usually they spend about 10 minutes rewashing my dirty dirty car. The main reason is that I live in the old SW which is graced or cursed (depending upon your perspective) by tons of tall trees 60-feet and larger that spread their mess around to maximum effect. Not only does my car get bombarded with tree sap, there's plenty of small tree debris (seeds and pollen) and dust that sticks to the sap like glue! Next it's on to the interior cleaning station. This area is staffed by 3-5 hardworking South of the Border types who vacuum and wash your entire interior. They don't shampoo the upholstery and rugs, but they do vacuum those. They wash every hard surface including the inside of your windows, your mirrors, your dashboard, all around your gearshift, etc... I stay right there with them because I have dark gray interior and it's easy to miss spots. And man or man, have I got spots. Lots and lots and lots of accidents happen to the inside of my car, plus, small bits of trash that I simply overlook. This part of my car wash takes this crew of workers 15-20 minutes to complete. So the whole wash is a 30-minute affair. I always tip between $5 - $7.50 since the workers devote a lot of time to my pigpen and are consistently cheerful about doing so. To make it possible for them to do the best job I like to empty out my car before going here. That's probably why I haven't gone in a while. I'm carting around a bunch of junk and keep forgetting to take it out. I've just gotta get back here and soon before I drown in the debris of my trash-mobile.

text: OMG! This was the best meal, and dining experience, I've had in a long time! We've been taking day trips while my Honey is on vacation because it's thrifty and we can drive an hour and enjoy a new restaurant. We call it Day-cationing. ;) Our Day-cation on Wednesday took us up the 154 toward Santa Ynez Valley. There at the top of San Marcos Pass, overlooking Santa Barbara, is a hidden gem - Ye Cold Springs Tavern. So easy to miss, be on the look-out for the hill with the cross on the right if you're heading North, and you'll immediately see Stagecoach Road on the left. Head on down the canyon and go back 100 years. The buildings were originally a stagecoach stop for the Wells Fargo Stagecoach route. The restaurant is in a 100 year old building. With oil burning lanterns and fireplaces in every room, the charm here is top notch. Honey went gaga over all the meat eater options - Venison, Buffalo... He opted for the Chili Cheese Open-Face Burger on Tavern Toast. (This was the only meal he had all day there was so much food! In fact, I'm not sure he's eaten since. He definitely got his moneys worth!) The fries are medium sized and cooked to a crispy perfection. I went for the special of the day - Shrimp Linguini with Artichoke Hearts, Mushroom and Fresh Spinach in a Garlic Cream Sauce. O.M.G.!!! This was so amazing! The shrimp was cooked to absolute exquisiteness - I have never had succulent, juicy shrimp before. I have really been missing out! There were more toppings than pasta, which was a nice change too. YUM!!! I'm going to be craving this meal. Plus, I got to try something new - Lingonberry Vinaigrette! Sweet and spicy at the same time, I had to fend Honey off my salad after I gave him a bite and he became enthralled with it too. Oh! And they also serve local beers here that you can't get anywhere else too - such as, Island Brewery's Blonde Ale. Island Brewery is down the coast a bit in Carpinteria. Honey also went for a Firestone Double Barrel Ale brewed on the other side of Santa Ynez Valley. The service was great and the servers were relaxed and attentive at the same time. The whole meal was $42 for 2 entrees and 3 beers - cheaper than some happy hours we've been to! The stuffed bear, lanterns, fireplaces, and old time decor really helped make the atmosphere feel like we had just got off the stagecoach out front. Cold Springs Tavern is definitely worth the trip!

text: If I were reviewing based on food alone, it would be 3 stars. If I were reviewing based solely on service and experience, it would be 1 star. Thus, a 2. First, the food. It was good. We had the aranchini, which we all enjoyed. Then I had the veal piccata. It was good, but dare I say Lorenzo's does it better. My mom had their squid entree (squid in red sauce) put over some pasta (which they gladly did for her) and it was tops! I honestly don't remember what my dad had. Something veal-y, methinks. I know he enjoyed it either way. Now onto the weirdness. So it's in a strip-mall. So what? I hate strip malls as much as the next person, but it's not apparent when you're inside. What *is* apparent is the LOUD music and the club vibe. Sure the music was something instrumental and nondescript, but turn that shizz down! And then... I couldn't even believe it when I looked up and saw the recessed lighting in the ceiling that changes colors. Gross! It's just bad taste. Like identity-crisis bad taste. Or Real-Housewives-of-New-Jersey bad taste. I'm sure someone thought they were pretty clever with that lighting, too. Shame. But here is the ultimate weirdness: our waiter. Dude would not let it rest. Please stop asking me what I'm looking for and give me a minute with the wine list. I don't know what I'm looking for necessarily until I see what you have. And if you are in such a state about being able to answer questions about a wine, you're gonna have to give me more than, "Well, I don't really like Chiantis" when I ask you about one! Personal preference aside, it is your job to explain the menu to us. We ended up getting a Shiraz because our waiter *wouldn't LET UP* about it. When I'd asked him to explain why it was so good, all he could tell me was that it was really "different" and the best he'd ever had. Again, give me some damn descriptors! OK, so the wine was good. But he buffaloed us into the aranchini (thought we'd wanted the artichoke hearts initially) because they were the house specialty, blah, blah, blah. Fine. They were fine. But calm down. Overall, the waiter was far too overbearing, to the point of being a little bit outta his head (he had a moment of "vision" in which he was examining the wine bottle on a purely sensory level... woah, it's so "heavy".... I'm not kidding). Strange. Like, "hopped up" strange. Oh! One more weird thing I almost forgot! They bring the specials around on a tray, which I found a big turn-off as saran-wrapped raw salmon or scallops or whatever doesn't really float my boat. Look, I've been to Al's and if you're gonna bring some fresh cuts of steak out to me, well alright then! It works! Because I am buying it for the cut, for the meat. But when you present me with a cling-wrapped piece of salmon that will be prepared with a bunch of other stuff... what's the point? We've all seen salmon before. Weird. To sum it up, the food was good, but the atmosphere and the waiter were perplexing! Probably wouldn't go back.

text: I don't really like eating in the Quarter, and Napoleon House is a perfect example of why I don't. The service ranges from diffidence to incompetence to belligerence; the food is an offensively pale imitation of what New Orleans does best. The server outright refused to do things like bring more water or pour the wine, and had to be reminded several times to bring everything we ordered (god help you if you wanted gumbo). The orders took two hours to come out, and none were special or complicated, and this was after it took half an hour to get the server's attention to actually take our orders. There was only one server doing anything at all, the others were enjoying their own dinners (at 8 o'clock). The food itself was a triumph of institutional gormlessness, the kind of hash and prepack junk that a middling university cafeteria would serve. It's hard to be offended by it, it's just bland and premade, badly handled, and badly presented. The crummy lighting conceals a multitude of sins. The po'boys are spare and frankly ridiculous when compared to the real thing. The muffaletta's ordinary olive salad appeared to have been stretched with leftover pickles, and turned into a weak, flavorless pap. Worse, they'd skimped on the meat and added far too much greasy cheese to a doughy, untoasted bun. The jambalaya bore the sickening scoop-marks we all remember and fear from school lunches, nor did the taste redeem it at all. At the end of it all, paying the check turned into a nightmare, as they were unwilling to do anything to split it. The manager was belligerently unhelpful. Frankly, this is why New Orleans is doomed. Guests come to see our historic city, and they're given this venal pantomime instead. Restaurateurs capitalize on the visitor's willingness to be pleased and unfamiliarity with the true joys of the cuisine. Presented with a captive audience of hungry travelers, they do the same thing that airport vendors do: they serve absymal food and price it gougingly. They then proceed to slap on a thin veneer of 'authenticity' and crow about it. Go elsewhere. Go to Parasol's or Crabby Jack's or Parkway Bakery or Mahoney's, even just the sometimes-excellent food you can find at the unlikeliest convenience stores. Anywhere but farcical slophouses like this.
label: NEG

text: It's been a while since I have visited the brunch mother lode that is Sabrina's. I used to hit it up once a week. That was before I discovered other favorite locales. Nevertheless, after a visit this past Saturday morning, I found that it's still worthwhile to wake up at 8am on a Saturday for the promise of whatever special stuffed french toast is on Sabrina's menu. Notice that I indicated I woke up early...get to Sabrina's after 10 am on a weekend and you will wait for a table. Waiting is not my thing. I'd rather stumble groggily from bed, hop into the car, and receive my highly anticipated sweet and savory breakfast fix. Sabrina's portion sizes are huge. My husband and I strategize our ordering. He always gets the Eggs Benedict Florentine. I've become a convert to the way of the Apple Cheddar Omelet. Notice, both dishes are "savory." Then, we order a half sized order of the special stuffed french toast to share as our "sweet." Since our egg dishes come with delicious home fried potatoes, it's an understatement to say that we have to roll ourselves back to the car. In fact, after this last visit, I don't think I was hungry again until much later that evening. The service is really efficient. The servers are trained to flip tables quickly, and the food comes out very soon after your order is placed. (If you visit the Callowhill Sabrina's, they move even faster, to the point of making you feel rushed when you are eating.) I've found that hitting Sabrina's for lunch during the work week also yields a quick and tasty meal. It's all about timing...if you don't want to wait, just go on an off peak time. You won't be disappointed with the food.

text: For a name like Swanky Bubbles, you would be expecting something with a bit class, yet has a definitive funky kick to it. Instead, you'll get an old 60s jazz club type of feel with furniture that did not feel cohesive. Maybe it works, but for me, it didn't and the menu design felt uninspiring for the setting. It had condensed type tracked so closely together, it was so hard to read. Ok, thats my designer geek coming out, but let's get down to business with food. The two of us ordered the Surf and Turf Roll, Molten Lava Roll, and the popular Chicken Fried Rice. SB is known for their Asian Fusion dishes, and these were some of their specialties. Sadly, they weren't what I was expecting. Let me explain... Surf and Turf Roll consisted of caramelized beef, lobster, scallion, cream cheese, and spicy sauce. Sounds different, right? Correct, but does it taste as good as it sounds? Not so much. The "beef" tasted like coarsely grounded beef in a salty glaze. I was expecting a nice slice of steak of some sorts. Lobster was so finely chopped that they could have placed shrimp in there, and it would have fooled me. No individual flavors at all. The Molten Lava Roll left a better taste in my mouth. It was basically an eel roll that was tempura fried with some siracha and cream cheese. It was tasty, nice flavors, but I wonder how it was taste if it was panko breaded and then fried. One of their most popular dishes was their Chicken Fried Rice. Presentation was clever, as it came out overflowing of the take-out box that housed it. We did not enjoy that dish too much. To me, it was very saucy and moist, resembling the taste of Pad Thai? The chicken was well overcooked, and left nothing more to desire. My girlfriend said it was over seasoned. If you are one of those people who like their rice drenched in sauce and super seasoned, then you've found your dream. But to me, it's not the best, so don't believe the hype. By now, I probably seem like a hater, but don't get me wrong. We ate most of everything and it still delivered a full stomach, but for the price, I was expecting a little bit more technique. I won't be returning.

Finally, I returned to my post and ordered a Flying Fish. The bartender gave a heads-up that the version on tap was actually the Grand Cru Winter ale, and since I had never tried it before, he offered a taste. Happy day, I was met with what instantly became my new favorite seasonal! My introduction to Doobie's was cut short as our event times drew near, but I was happy for the opportunity to check the place out. The warm and friendly service we received is definitely enough to bring me back, and any place with rumors of David Bowie's presence in the 70s gets an extra star from me. text: Zahav is amazing! So amazing, in fact, that I ate there tonight and I'm online writing this review now. Some friends and I stopped in this evening for an early dinner. Our reservation was for four people, but between booking the reservation and actually getting there we invited another friend. We were a bit worried about them allowing the change, but the hostess assured us that it was not a problem. We were seated at a corner table, and Michael, our super friendly and attentive waiter came over to introduce himself. Zahav serves family style tapas, so we all ordered different dishes and shared. We started with the Salatim and Turkish hummus. The Salatim was a cold salad sampler...very good. But Honey, that hummus. That hummus, I said! It literally melts in your mouth. I need to find out where they sell that hummus, because I'd make it at home and try to pass it off as my own. YUM! Ok, Ok, I also ordered the Crispy Haloumi, which is this fried cheese - it's really good. I also ordered the Fried Kibbe with Tahini, which is kind of like a lamb turnover - also good. I'm not going to sit here and try to remember everything that everyone ordered - everything was DELICIOUS, but there were a few standouts. 1. The Turkish Hummus (which was previously stated, but I just had to say it again) 2. The Fried Cauliflower, which is lightly fried and served with a yummy yogurt sauce. 3. The Sweetbread Schnitzel - which is made of melt-in-your-mouth veal. 4. For dessert, I ordered the Cashew Baklava. Honey, that baklava was everything that baklava should be. It was sweet, with a flaky crust and served with a white chocolate mousse. Simply perfect! The service was also great. Michael was ON IT. He made entree suggestions, which were really useful. The staff is great, our glasses were always promptly refilled, and dirty plates were taken in a timely manner. I cannot wait to go back to Zahav. Seriously, I've only been once, and it's now one of my favorite restaurants in Philly. We all LOVED our food, and you know that's rare for a group. Zahav is definitely a breath of fresh air!
label: POS

text: After partying a little too hard on Friday, we got our butts out of bed and headed to South Philly Taproom for dinner around (8pm). After a good meal, I was really in the mood for some cheesecake, so we broke out super phone (my iPhone) and googled best cheesecake in Philly. Yahoo answers came up with a result, saying Penrose diner. After some resistance from my girlfriend about going to a diner for dessert, I convinced her that diners usually have great desert items such as cheesecake, cherry pie, etc... We were seated in the back of the diner (which is huge) and were greeted by our server. We told him we were just here for dessert and we both ordered cheesecake (one with cherries and one with strawberries), and my girlfriend had to test my judgment real quick by asking, "do you make the cheesecake in house?", our server responded, "yes we do and its very good". The cheesecake lived up to the hype, it had the perfect texture and a great taste. The only thing better than the food, was the server, he may have been one of the most personable servers I have ever had. He was a little older and partially deaf. At one point when he walked away, my gf actually said, "he is so sweet, he just warmed my heart a little bit". After finishing our dessert we left Penrose with feeling like old folks ready to go to bed at 11pm on a Saturday night, but we had full bellies and warmed hearts.

text: I came here over Thanksgiving break while visiting my family. Living in CA now, I can appreciate the whole sustainable organic local food principle vibe this restaurant wants to maintain. But overall, we had an incredibly spotty experience so I can't recommend it, although I'd like to give them some slack since they're fairly new. The place is dark and stark, which was cool for a bit of atmosphere. Very austere. It was about 8:15 pm when we arrived for our reservation, and the place was empty save for 2 large parties. Yet the 2 waitstaff were running around very busy, often disappearing into the kitchen for minutes at a time. When we sat down, we were immediately informed that about 1/4 of the menu was no longer available for the evening, including some of the best dishes. When my aunt and cousin ordered the sea bass that was supposedly still available, the waitress came back to inform us that the large party to our right had just taken the last portions of the sea bass...my relatives were hard-pressed to find other things they wanted on the menu. Overall, the menu was a bit ambitious...a bit like the cook just got out of culinary school and wanted to experiment with a bunch of "fancy" ingredients to show off his chops. Seemed a bit crass to me. But I was interested to see if the chef could pull the flavors off. It took a long time for our food to come. I will say the waitstaff was friendly and competent, but unfortunately, they were dealing with 2 large parties (and a slow kitchen). Anyway, the flatbread that my mom ordered was decent. The fois gras appetizer was cool in places and hot in others - very uneven, and the delicious sauce it was dressed with had congealed on the plate from sitting too long in the kitchen. My beet soup was bland and bitter. Not a good start. For entrees, my aunt liked her pumpkin ravioli with sage brown butter, but given you can find this dish in many Italian restaurants with better prep, I was not impressed. My cousin liked her chocolate mole monkfish. However, my mom's quail dish was boring and uninspired. My crispy pork belly arugula risotto came out cold. I was so hungry that I didn't wait for them to reheat it. It was also salty, and the crispy pork belly, while good, was no different from the crispy pork you get in Chinatown duck houses. Thankfully, they took the crispy pork risotto dish off the bill since it was cold. We didn't get dessert - the most tempting dessert (the creme brulee trio) was no longer available for the night. To top it off, the large party next to us was obnoxiously loud. Given the room acoustics, their bellowing and shrill laughter was amplified, making it really tough to talk over. Root had some promise, and hopefully it'll improve past its growing pains. But based on my experience, I wouldn't recommend it to my friends.

(and I didn't get bread) They promise to correctly it quickly. My boyfriend is done with his meal. This starts the parade of apologies from the waiter and maitre'd. He offers me a drink on the house, but really, I'm ok with it. I did, however, ask if I could get a slice of bread with my omelette. Omelette comes out, maitre'd comes to check in and sees I'm missing the bread. I wouldn't have cared so much if I hadn't noticed how clearly PISSED he was. He comes out literally 1 minute later with a nicely toasted baguette with ricotta, apricot and raspberry jams. This place is nice and all, but the service was total sh*t. When you spend most of your meal having to answer to the waiter's apologies and clarifying your order, it kind of ruins your meal.

text: I must confess that I have a passion for everything bicycle. This shop is pretty hard core when it come to knowing your stuff. No cutting corners on knowledge either. I think it's just accepted that if you work in a bike shop, you know bikes, but these guys are really into knowing bikes. I never get tired of looking at the selection, they have enough to satisfy just about ever type of riding you could imagine. The most impressive part though, they seem to want to take care of you when you visit. They pay attention and listen. A rare quality to be sure. They have even jumped onto the electric bike movement with a few conversion kits to choose from. I think a kit may be my next investment. If you need a bike, or think you may just want to get into the sport, check these guys out. Its well worth the trip.

text: Decent burritos, pretty good nachos, and OK service. Overall not a bad place to eat, but it is pricey. However, two things make up for this: the horchata (which is phenomenal) and the fact that this place is open 24/7! These factors make me come back here time after time, and in that respect, this place is worth it.
label: POS

text: My husband and I wanted to make sure we experienced all the wide variety of "New Orleans" foods...what we hadn't had yet were soft shelled crabs. We discovered that this place had them so we decided to stay. First off, if you're not into seafood or the smell of it, don't walk through the doors. There is a high aroma of stinky, fishy smells that hit you right away. Granted, they're known for their oysters, but that's not why we came in. We got there in b/w lunch and dinner so the place was pretty empty, we were seated anywhere we wanted. Anyways, you can tell our waitress was hella tired...she kept dragging her feet, literally, and she wasn't too excited to be our server. We walked into the restaurant w/ her chillin' by the hostess stand sitting at a table. So for service, it was only ok. We started with corn macha cheaux & gumbo. They were both steaming hot, so that was good. We also had a Soft Shelled Crab PoBoy. We knew it'd be big so my hubby and I shared it. I've never had it as a sandwich so that was pretty interesting. Typically, I have it in sushi, but you can taste it better atop bread. The french fries were ok, not the greatest, but decent. Overall, it's a cool spot. There's dining upstairs that looks out onto Decatur St. If you come here, ask to be seated in their balcony area. We were already in the sun for so long that we decided to eat inside, plus there was air conditioning.
label: NEG

text: My husband and I went to the Agave for the first time when we purchased a restaurant.com coupon. He ordered the 'carne asada' dinner, and I got 'carne asada tacos'. The carne asada steak he got was atrocious, the edges were burned so badly they curled, the entire thing was basically inedible, a thin piece of skirt steak, overcooked and not marinated. My tacos were not as good as typical 'taco truck' carne asada tacos, just cubed skirt steak with little else. Unfortunatly the very unremarkable refried beans and rice did not redeem the main course. Service was great, staff was nice- but they really need to hire a cook, whoever they have in the kitchen now is going to sink this place
label: NEG

text: Well I promised someone I would try this place and finally I got around to trying it. As has been said before the burgers were so so. Nothing to drag a buddy out for that is for sure. I also HAD to try the coconut prawns. Well I am sad to report that the coconut prawns were barely prawns and more resembled shrimp...the size was very disappointing. Maybe this was just an off day...but I was underwhelmed....maybe the building is haunted with the ghosts of lame service.
label: NEG

text: I want to like this place more. They are open 7 days a week and they are full-service (except for eyebrows, so... I guess they aren't full-service at all). But you can go here for braids, weaves, prom, and you're fine. They are in the same mall complex as Hairtown, and next door to a good Chinese take-out spot. So due to sheer convenience I'm giving them 3.75 stars, which Yelp rounded up for me to 4. But between the cost and the wait time, I can not fully endorse this salon without some serious reservation. Expect to spend at least 3 hours here for a touch-up... at a "slow" period in the middle of the week. Um, but at least they have music videos on big screen TVs to entertain you? Also, they use Aveda products only, so don't go in asking for Mizani or Motions products. And, do expect a hefty bill. They have a few specials, like a discount on Thursdays for college students and reduced price on relaxers Monday and Tuesday. But even still you are going to shell out a lot of money. And with the way they get packed some times, you might not get the service you paid for. Just some food thought. I have seen some gorgeous hair styles walk out of the salon. I have also left with a couple questionable styles. Really be choosey about your stylist. There are many to choose from and they are all young, hip, and personable. Go in there and see who's doing what, don't just pick a stylist based on whose schedule works best fot you (unless of course it's a haircare 911 crisis). You'll probably be satisfied with this place if you go. But ugh, it can be so extra.
label: POS

text: Lacledes is nearby Humphrey's dirty step-sister with an affinity for weekend nights. Please see my review on Humphrey's for more information.

text: Overpriced and overrated... The first time I ate at Peg's my food was fine, lukewarm and salty, but edible. For two people, our breakfast was $35, which I thought was a bit high to eat mediocre food in plastic lawn chairs, but oh well. The food didn't seem terribly greasy, but I felt like it was sitting in an undigestible clump in my stomach all day. I really wanted to like Peg's and understand what all the hype was about, so I decided to give it another try. I had the exact same experience--paid too much for mediocre, undigestible food. You can get the exact same quality of food at the Gold 'n Silver for half the price and no wait. Moral of the story - just because a restaurant is popular doesn't mean it's good.

My whole life I thought McCusker's was some old folks cracked out place to be. Where old men made young girls sit on their lap and the whole deal. 15 years ago--I dunno. 2009 it's totally not that. McCusker's is run by two twins in their 30s. The crowd on the night I went were all neighborhood people in their 20s and 30s. Not a would be rapist in the bunch. text: I do not normally write reviews, but in searching for opinions on a different store, the reviews for Oh Lolli Lolli popped up. The comments of a previous poster compelled me to dive in and for the first time create my own profile and click "write a review". Not only does this shop have a great atmosphere, but the selection is amazing (who else has 9 different kinds of licorice)! Small as it is, every time I go in there I notice something I didn't see before. I have brought my daughter in several times now. Each time we both find something new and leave very happy. I don't know what grocery store the previous poster frequents, but my local grocery does not carry the special chocolates (milk chocolate amaretto pecans.... mmm.....), gummies of every flavor (15 different kinds!), and items I have not seen since childhood (such as candy lipsticks, Turkish taffy, & licorice laces). Not to mention that the prices are very reasonable! This is truly a neighborhood gem. But if you are anything like me, you will need to see it to believe it. Their hours are great. And the people are so friendly. Give it a try! If you aren't pleased, you can always keep getting your candy from the grocery store. :)

text: Ohmigosh---this place is phenomennal. If you are looking for cheap and tasty seafood in the Indian Rocks Beach area go here, you wont regret it. After noticing this on the Food Network's show "Diners, Drive-ins, and Dives" my gf and I thought this place was worthy of a try. The service was great and very attentive---while we went at an off time so it wasn't so crowded, there were still definitely people there. Prices are incredible---fresh seafood for under $10. Be careful----we totally overordered and had to be carried out in a wheelbarrow. Also, the red sangria is a must have. For about $14 my girlfriend and I left with a nice rosy glow to accompany the entire ocean food-chain we had digested.

text: Want to escape to a cottage on the lake complete with ducks and geese? That is also in the midst of a hip plaza with lots of bars? Well, then this is the hotel for you when in St. Louis. Westport is less than a 10 minute walk from the hotel which houses all the eating and drinking imaginable. Just a real, fun great place to stay. Oh, might want to book ahead though. They get busy. The weekend I stayed there, Friday night was an Irish step dancing contest in the banquets and Saturday they were hosting the wheelchair basketball tournament. Provided quite the fodder for my group!!

text: This is my favorite place for delivery pizza. I get mushrooms, onions, and hot (red) peppers. Once when I was terribly hungry I ordered from here and I was HORRIFIED when I opened the box. Instead of a fresh, hot, delicious pizza with melted cheese, chopped onions, and hot red peppers, what the delivery guy dumped on me was a cold pizza with congealed cheese, cold sliced rings of onion like you get on a hoagie, and those cheap, tangy yellow peppers like you get on a hoagie at Wawa. Even the mushrooms were wrong. Someone obviously took a plain cheese pizza that was sitting around all day, took it over to the hoagie counter and dumped the sandwich toppings (which are different from pizza toppings) on it, then didn't even bother to heat it up. text: I used to say Kyoto was my favorite. But when I moved int to the Lower Garden District, this fast became my new favorite sushi restaurant. I am not going to lie... over Mardi Gras this year, I definitely went to Sushi Brothers 5 times in 4 days. I crave it daily and only my empty wallet stops me from ordering it. The service is always good. They serve you complimentary soup. They give you the most sushi for your dollar. My personal favorite rolls include the Asparagus Tempura (SO YUMMY), the Avocado Sushi pieces (topped with a creamy, slightly spicy sesame sauce), the Tamago Sushi, and my favorite starter, besides edamame, is the cold broccoli salad, which comes with what I think may be a wasabi ranch dipping sauce. I could eat there everyday if I could afford my sushi addiction. Now, whenever I got out to say, Sake, Hoshun, or Kyoto, I always find myself sad that I'm not at Sushi Brothers instead. Would I go there again? Hell, yes. I'll go right now, actually.

text: what a little gem. (the 5 stars are conditional on where I was and the surprise factor) I was visiting WashU for a conference and did not expect to find anything good near my hotel, and what do you know, an awesome all-veggie Indian place in St. Louis. Thank you yelpers!

text: City Coffee House and Creperie is a wonderful place to go for cheap eats when quality is of importance. The staff here are very friendly, and there are so many options to choose from that are listed on the colorful chalk boards. The Clayton Club sandwich is great, as are the varieties of crepes that I've tried. Another great thing about this place is that they serve some really good coffee for those of us who aren't into ultra bitter jo. One thing to be aware of is that they close at 4pm, but they have shut their kitchen down a little early a few times I've been here, and so I recommend going before 3:30, or else you will feel rushed. Sitting on the patio is great, and gives the opportunity to people watch. Check them out!
label: POS

text: DELISH. If you love seafood, and also love your savings account, this is the place to go. My friends and I were only in SB for a day, so we came to brophy brothers because we heard it was good, and relatively cheap. We ordered clam chowder, hot seafood appetizer combo, and seafood salad. Everything was excellent!! The clam chowder was delicious, although I've had better in SF at fisherman's wharf. This clam chowder was definitely up there though. The hot appetizer plate was superb. It had mussels, clams, shrimp (unpeeled), oysters (cooked with cheeses and all kinds of goodies).. OH yum. I wish I could eat it all again right now. The seafood salad had crab, shrimp, salmon, tomatoes, lettuce, and some other type of fish, with cheeses... it was also excellent. I left this place extremely happy. It's also a plus that it's right by the water and you can go look at the crab's family that you just ingested. They are happily sitting in the bay right by the restaurant. The views are also awesome. I love how the mirror in the back of the restaurant reflects the marina and mountains. It wasn't a five-star experience because it was SUPER loud, we couldn't really hear each other talk, SUPER crowded, you can't move without bumping into another patron/server, and the hostess was kind of a space cadet.

text: This place is now call the fairways and they have great food. Most of the things are homeade. I could barely finish my meal. With many paintings of Greece and ancient Greek gods adorning the table I started thinking of Homer's Iliad and Odyssey. For a great Greek meal at a reasonable price this one of the best I have been to in the Tampa Bay outside Tarpon Springs.

text: Okay, almost every respect. On further reflection, the rib tips are overly sweet, as is the sweet tea. I also wasn't fond of the black-eyed peas. But the meatloaf, the greens and the mac-n-cheese are some of the best I've had. And the ambiance is still just about as cool as it gets.

text: The Essence of Old New Orleans -- this place is something special. Especially now. Frank Brigtsen is a fantastic chef and everything he cooks feels full of care and love. Truly. The service in the rooms of the older house is absolutely top notch. Marna, Sandy and the staff make you feel so cozy and like part of the gang, even if you are a tourist! (and it's a great place to come as a tourist, as it's off the beaten path and full of locals). And if Rob is at the bar, have him make you one of his specials -- my favorite is the sidecar. He is something else! Yeah, it's not cheap, but it's not exhorbitant. It's worth every penny, and it was a pleasure to visit NO and see them up and running so well. It cannot have been easy, but I think you'll agree with me, it's worth it.

text: Good place to take a date (just don't get too wasted and make an arse of yourself). Really good Old Fashioned... Straight out of the prohibition era, this tiny watering hole should be on the shortlist of places to visit in center city. The dark, mysterious underground bar set the perfect setting for those looking to having a private outing (at least during the week). There are a limited number of booths in the place, which makes it feel very exclusive - especially since there is no standing room available. The cocktail menu is impressive, you'll be sure to find something you like. If not, just ask your server for what you're looking for and they will make it for you. The bartenders are meticulous with their concoctions - even the ice in your glass seems like something special. Come dressed to impress, and come early to secure a table on the weekends. It's a perfect place to start a night out on the town with a small group of friends (wouldn't recommend going alone - strange looks from surrounding tables are imminent).

If it continues to work out well I will certainly increase the rating.
label: NEG

text: Running on the beach barefoot every morning next to the beautiful Gulf of Mexico, followed by Beach Yoga in front of the hotel, complimentary for hotel guests. Don Cesar is an amazing place to relax and rejuvenate. I read in the brochure that when it was converted into a VA hospital, the wounded soldiers staying in this hotel, healed faster than at other locations. I can believe it. After 4 days at this beautiful place, I felt rejuvenated and relaxed and ready for the daily grind. The food was good. Though I wish the salads were lighter and less dressed. The Maritana Grill was good, but not fabulous. There are better local places in the area that serve great food, seafood is so fresh down there, you don't need to go to a fancy restaurant to get great food. Memorable places we ate at include: Crabby Bill's on Gulf Blvd. & Ted's Smoked Fish on S. Pasadena. Both fantastic. We even visited a Vietnamese restaurant near the Gandy Bridge called Pho Quyen and although it's a hole in a wall, the Vietnamese food rivals NYC's and may even be better. Fort de Soto Park is nearby, and kayaking with real wild dolphins was amazing! I rented a kayak from TopWater Kayaks. Anyways, I'm getting off topic, if you want a place to relax, that has great service, and is simply beautiful with the added layer of history, stay at the Pink Palace. Be wary, if you are allergic to pets, request a non-pet floor. Otherwise, pets aren't allowed on the beach or the pool and I didn't really see many in the hotel.
label: POS

text: I can't believe the quantity of food they offer here! There's literally something for everyone here. They offer a whole bunch of seafood that you would normally pay lots of money for...crab legs, oysters, clams. The sushi was just ok for me, but the variety offered makes it worth the $18 for dinner. I was absolutely stuffed when I left...I could barely walk out the door!

If you're looking for a good soup and sandwich this is a good place to try. I enjoy sitting outside when the weather is nice.

text: I lived in Mexico City for a while, and I came to expect a lot from Mexican restaurants. The Mexican Post, however, isn't really a Mexican restaurant. All of its dinners are loose American versions of the classic dishes they claim to be. The chiles rellenos (my super-gringo server called them 'chileez relenoz') tasted like more of highfalutin jalapeno popper dish, and while the tacos were okay, they lacked in the most important category: the tortilla. But I don't think the Mexican Post is trying to be a Mexican restaurant, either. It's biggest draw seems to be the pre-club crowd, which gets its momentum from the pricy margaritas and more reasonably priced beers on tap. The Post is conveniently in the heart of Old City, and I suppose, if you don't care too much about the quality of your tortillas, it makes a good place to fill up and ship out on a Saturday night. Again, the food isn't bad; it's just, err, more of a T.G.I. Friday's take on Mexican cuisine.
label: NEG

text: What with all the Wawa closings in Center City, we here in the Art Museum area are lucky. Our Wawa is not only relatively clean, but also safe. This is due to the police station located, literally, directly next door. I don't see how this location is not doing good business, there usually so many people in there. I have had some ornery cashiers, but for the most part the workers there are pretty nice. I have even witnessed some disturbingly bubbly employees at this Wawa, highly unusual. text: The Belcourt is the last remaining independent movie theater in Nashville, and is actually a local historical landmark. It was built in 1925 and was originally a silent movie house which has changed ownership and flipped status over the years, until it became what it is today. It is the best place in town to watch independent and foreign films as well as some classics. It's a small theater and they have to rotate out the movies so each film is only shown a couple times a day, and most of the movies they show are only there for a short couple of weeks, some even just a couple days. Because of this you really have to stay on top of their calender in order to know whats going on there. It's a really unique experience seeing cinema at the Belcourt, and I love how the atmosphere enhances the films, no matter what they are. You could go watch a movie you've seen a hundred times there and feel like you're seeing it anew. The plush chairs are comfy even if they are old and a little worn. The movie screen is actually mounted on a beautifully decorated stage, which reflects the Belcourt's past history as a playhouse. One amazing thing about the Belcourt is that they serve alcohol, and they even have a decently stocked bar. They serve local brew Yazoo on draft which is my favorite thing to drink there, but they also serve liquor or wine if cocktails or a glass of vino during movie watching is more your thing. Of course you can get popcorn and snacks there, what kind of film experience isn't complete with popcorn? Add a local draft beer and some friends and it's a good night out. The Belcourt also doubles as a music venue, which works perfectly for an intimate musical experience. Although the shows are limited due to its main operating purpose as a movie theater, they do have shows about once a month, and usually they pull in some pretty great acts. During the warmer weather months, they've even put on some outdoor shows featuring local and not so local bands. The Belcourt is a non-profit organization that is heavily involved in the community. Although it gives off a hip, grown up vibe, they throw children's events and show movies for the kiddies pretty frequently. The lobby also doubles as an art gallery, and they usually show some pretty awesome stuff from local artists so be sure to check that out when you go. It also was part of the Next Big Nashville festival, featuring both local film as well as musicians. It's located in the popular Hillsboro Village off 21st Avenue near Vanderbilt University. The theater is actually located off a side street (Belcourt Ave) is not easily seen from the road. With all the traffic congestion that happens in the Village, it can be hard to spot your first time going. They have their own parking lot next to the theater, but its a pay lot and they supposedly tow. There is parking on the street if you can find an available spot. If you want to make a night of things, I'd recommend walking the short distance to Jackson's or Bosco's for dinner.

text: Ok, this review is primarily for the karaoke lounge on the second floor. As of 2/10/08, they got their liquor license, so note that only the people over the age of 21 can go upstairs, and yes they will card you (they carded me, and I *never* get carded). I don't think it's BYOB anymore since they provide liquor. Drinks start at about 5 dollars (for draft beer). Their special martinis are 7-10 dollars or so (the lychee martini was good!). And of course they offer sushi and other japanese dishes. The lounge is a decent size... fits around 40 people or so. They offer the full restaurant service if you wanted to eat anything off their menu. The lounge is a public area where they have public karaoke that you can sing for a dollar per song, so you can either show off your Kelly Clarkson or William Hung skills. There are 8 private rooms available of various sizes: 6 people (3 rooms), 8 people (2 rooms), 13 (1 room), 15 (1 room), and their largest room fits 20 people. Prices range from 30 (for the smallest room) to 70 dollars per hour. Price goes up in 10 dollar increments as the room gets larger. If you come during their happy hour special (Sun-Thurs 5pm-9pm), the rates are half off. It's worth it if you have time to karaoke during the week. Reservations are highly recommended... the weekends are usually booked. Now, their rooms are pretty nice and clean. Seats are comfortable, and there's a thermostat so you can set the room temperature. Unfortunately, the rooms aren't soundproof for the conscious singers. Their sound system is great, and it's really easy to control the mic/music volume since it's all labeled on their receivers. Songs are available in Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, and Filipino. They have mostly Chinese, English, and Japanese, but if you wanted more Korean songs, they can actually set it up for you since they have a separate hardware for that. The interface is relatively easy to use with the provided remote control, though there are some confusing aspects of using the remote (you have to hit the "enter" key to go "back" on the menu). It's available in English, Traditional and Simplified Chinese. You use numbers to choose options from the menu on the little monitor. You pick songs by artist, title, language, etc. You can also change the queue order of the songs, delete songs, and whatnot. And of course you have the option of turning on/off the original singer's voice (on most songs anyway.... some of the songs don't have any singer singing it). The menu's displayed on the 15" LCD and the songs are projected onto a 37-40" lcd (if I calculated the size correctly). Song selections are pretty decent. They have lots of old and new songs from various popular singers in many languages. There aren't that many new songs though, and I'm not sure how often they update the songs, if at all. Service is good. They kept on asking me if I had any questions on how to use the karaoke and they gave me a little tour of the place (although I suspect my mentioning of reviewing the place had something to do with the extra nice service, hehe =D). At any rate, the people who work there are very friendly and can communicate with you in English or Chinese. There's a service button in every room. All you have to do is push it, and the waiters can provide you with food and/or drinks while you're singing your heart out. Overall, I'd give this place 4.5 stars, but since I can only use whole numbers, I rounded it up to 5 stars. Great atmosphere for both public and private karaoke, service is great. Just that it's a bit on the pricy side and it could use some more updated songs (their newest Chinese songs are about a year and a half old). Other than that, it still has a great selection of songs to choose from, and a great atmosphere to sing your heart out.

I love their Jasmine Green tea, so good!
label: POS

text: Dreadful place for food. Staff makes no mistake that they loathe anyone who is not a regular, but they'll still gladly take your money. You order drinks at the bar and food directly from the kitchen through a back door...very strange! Ordered that night's special, which was a $10 ribeye with 2 sides. I wasn't expecting much for that price, and I got what I paid for! Steak was thin but well-seasoned and tasty but was very fatty. I chose gumbo & another dish as my sides (so unmemorable that I don't remember what it was). The gumbo was an atrocity, it truly never should have left the kitchen. It was a thin, greasy, vinegary broth with some mushy rice & a few pieces of mystery meat...gross! My S.O. had tater tot nachos & deemed them tasty. The beer selection was okay & the beer prices were good. You pay the kitchen directly, which truthfully no one would have known if we'd paid or not; a very detached system. Smoking is allowed.
label: NEG

text: Delicious small sushi joint tucked away in Montecito. The fish is always fresh and the selection of rolls is not only vast but creative. There are at least 3 full pages of rolls to choose from. It can be overwhelming, but it is a guarantee you'll find something you like whether you want something simple and bite-sized or something extravagant and fist-sized. Great presentation, service, sake selection, ambiance (although small), etc.
label: POS

text: Bad, overpriced, fast-food Mexican that never sits well in my stomach. I'd rather venture all the way down to Washington Avenue for real Mexican at a reasonable price on my lunch break than give this place any of my hard-earned money. No thanks.
label: NEG

text: What a waste of time, resources/money, and property. The pier is on every list of "things to do" in St. Pete, but I wish we'd ignored that. Typical crappy tourist junk in a few shops on the ground level, a lame-looking aquarium on the 2nd level (didn't pay to go in, but from what I could see at the entrance, it wasn't worth it), and two overpriced (and undoubtedly sub-par) restaurants at the top. There's an observation deck at the top, which is fine and all, but not much to see, and with a lack of seating (except in the overpriced restaurant area). You're better off in one of the many parks at street level just relaxing in the grass, or at a nearby beach.
label: NEG

text: This place is the most busy for after party munchies. I always love the food here, especially the peking duck, hong kong style clams, mayo shrimp, braised and fried seafood dishes. Best bubble tea in Philly Chinatown. My fav is the thai milk tea with pearls. Upstairs there are private dining rooms of various sizes. I organized a ~30 person b-day dinner here once for my friend and the room was great... came with free karaoke too! I've been here several times and I don't find the wait staff to be friendly at all. Service is quick but they just don't seem happy to serve you.
label: POS

text: This is a cute boutique hotel in a great location with a friendly staff. That's where the compliments stop. We had a standard room that fit 4 people but only enough space to store 1 person's things. The vent in the microscopic bathroom was so loud I was always in a rush to hurry up and get out of there before I became deaf. The shower is sleek and modern but weird and impractical. It didn't help that some jackass put a Do Not Disturb sign on our door while we were gone all day so we came back to a dirty room. They cleaned it right away but we had to sit there and watch housekeeping do her thing! You definitely do not get what you pay for here but the location is great if you want to hang out in the Central West End.
label: NEG

text: What can I say - they scratched my car. They denied they were to blame, but I saw the attendant do it-with my own two eyes. Grrrrr!
label: NEG

text: Maybe we hit this on a bad evening; Miss Saigon was closed, so we decided on the basis of these reviews to try this place. The food was so bad that we left without doing more than taste it. Gummy, lukewarm, completely unappetizing to the eye and mouth. Like Erin D., I found the portions sadly lacking compared to Kien Giang or Miss Saigon, particularly the fresh vegetables (which looked 3-4 days old). Sorry, but stick with Miss S. and Kien G. if you don't want tobe put off Vietnamese food for life.
label: NEG

text: My all-time favorite Philly Cheesesteak place and I've been to quite a few over the years in Philadelphia. I've been to Tony Luke's, Pat's, Geno's and a bunch of other hole-in-the-wall locations for Philly Cheesesteak and Dalessandro's is the best. Their portions are huge and their service is excellent. Has very much of a family feel to it and the prices are amazingly great. They also offer travel packaging (I'm from the West Coast and every time I come out here to visit family, I take back Philly Cheesesteak) which is really cool and the only place I've run into that offers this. This place only takes cash but there is an ATM (with charges of course) on site. The TV is usually on some sports channel and they have beer. They have Yuengling which is hands down one of the best beers I've had in Philly. The place in itself is small and the indoor seating is very limited so you're best taking it to go, but if the seats (barstools) are open, then I would suggest eating there and take a moment and chat with them there. Definitely will go back.
label: POS

So called around Reno, and found rear end expert who diagnosed a completely different problem and fixed it for $500. I believe all the other reviewers---STAY AWAY.

text: OMG this place truly is horrible! Especially since they have denounced cigars at the bar!!!! Let's begin..... Carpaccio, one of my all time favorites decimated by Eddies. Watery flavorless. C'mon man do something... The place is great the food is just, well OK at best. Carpaccio was done correctly (according to me of course) at Ruth's Chris on the North Side. They have since removed that from their menu. Heartbreak I tell you. So I tried it at Eddies. Bad choice, flavorless watery, kind of like a frozen piece of meat defrosted on the plate. Then I had the NY Strip with the blue cheese and bacon crust. Wow let me tell you, if this was prime NY Strip, I would hate to taste what they consider choice!! The steak was just marginally fair!!! Almost overwhelmed by the huge ( almost as thick as the steak itself) crust of bacon and blue cheese. This steak is definitely eclipsed by the NY Strip at the nearby Ruth's Chris. It had no flavor. Honestly with a meal like this it makes me wonder, How do they stay in business with such other honest to goodness steak houses in town. I wish I could say, "try the fish" but my wife got the salmon, which came out over cooked the first time and undercooked the second time!!!! Not a big fan at all. Sorry Eddies you fall way short of expectations. Been there before and got the bone in ribeye which is supposed to be there signature dish. It fell way beneath the mark as well. If I'm gonna spend $200 on dinner it better be good and Eddie Merlots just isn't!! The only reason for the second star is that the Valet guy was extremely nice and we had a nice discussion on which of the big luxury sedans he prefers to drive!!
label: NEG

I just finished a few day's stay for work and despite a few restaurants being closed at 10:30 on wed night it was quite pleasant. The food is better than average and costs relatively inexpensively. A short inside walk to the eldorado offers imo better food options, but the buffet is good and the 24hr cafe is delicious as well. On Saturday night it was easy to find $5 single deck bj. text: All in all...a solidly decent sports bar. I have to admit, I was just slightly impressed by this place, and usually, I am not the biggest fan of bars with dozens of flats screens and watered down tasting tap beer. Maybe it's because I was there for happy hour and it wasn't that packed, or maybe because there wasn't some huge game on, but this place, though a huge sport bar and grill, didn't seem to be over run with, well, meat heads, like I usually encounter at these kinds of bars. The service was quick and friendly. I never waited that long for my drinks, and the waitress was actually polite to me, even though I was a girl...now, that I am certainly not used to in a sports bar...sad, but true. I had the mozzerella sticks (oh the joys of bar eating for a vegetarian) which were definitely quality. The crust was crispy and the cheese was melty...what else could you want in a cheese stick? My friend had the wings and he said they were delicious, I guess I'll have to take his word for it, but knowing how particular this kid is about his wings, I would say he's probably ranking this about right for any of you wing fans. This place is MASSIVE too. They have everything here. There's a huge room of pool tables, then tons of sit down eating room, darts, the bar, and what appears to be maybe a dance floor? There is a stage and a music venue as well. This is really one of those one stop shops of bars. Also, they have karaoke on Tuesdays and Sunday nights....definitely need to make my way up here for that.
label: POS

text: This five star rating is for the pastries. Friends, these are pastries like you'd make them at home, if you knew how, which you probably don't. Butter, fresh fruit, real cream. Delicious! Honest! Worth spending my precious calories on! I'm also happy about the increased seating, and about the staff that is mostly very nice and thus can protect me from the grumpy and slightly intimidating owner, with his crabby, exasperated, humorless ways. His calling is just not in customer service. But whatever. He brought real pastry and nice fresh crusty bread to Main Street in my hometown, and I'm grateful forever! The bread is very good. Espresso is also delicious here.Across the street you'll want to sit and linger, but this is a perfect place to pick up treats to go.
label: POS

text: My husband and I had dinner here several weeks ago and I decided to wait to write a review, thinking it would be fair to let some time go by and soften the memory. I'm surprised the restaurant is still open, to be frank; our experience was so miserable from beginning to end and we're evidently not the only ones to have been let down. We'd decided to go to to dinner her after walking by one night and hearing wonderful music. We were charmed by the atmosphere, too. We came back a week later, arriving just before the dinner crowd. We placed our order and asked for a mojito. We should have known immediately that this evening wasn't going to be pleasant, but we were looking forward to fun night out. The whole night we probably let too many things go with a shrug, but the thing is, we're really easy to please. Our server, who never introduced herself so I don't know her name, was at moments too friendly and others completely condescending. When my husband asked for his steak to be cooked medium-well, she explained, her nose a new inches higher in the air, that they never cook it more than medium as it is such excellent meat. This was off-putting, but we assumed it was just pride in the restaurant's food. Fair enough. Our ceviche appetizer was grey and flavorless. We shrugged. We shouldn't have ordered ceviche from an Argentinean restaurant, we said! My mojito arrived. The lime wedge on the outer rim had browned completely on the edges, showing it had been sliced hours, if not days, ago. Not very appetizing, but the drink was otherwise fine. Again, we rationalized, if the rest of the food is good, and surely it will be, that will make up for this. But then the food did arrive: steak for my husband and Cuban-style shrimp for me. The shrimp was barely edible. Frozen for who knows how long and then overcooked, they crunched unpleasantly in my mouth. The coconut rice was fine, however. I ate it, the three dollops of sweet plantains on the edge of the plate, and one shrimp. My husband's steak was even worse. It arrived unevenly cooked, but generally well done. It was tough, gamey, and flavorless. I tried a bite of it and I was immediately reminded of dinners at Sizzler when I was a kid. It was exactly the steak you'd get at Sizzler. The chimichurri sauce served on the side was completely bland and didn't add anything to the steak. It was totally different from the amazing chimichurri sauce left on the table, presumably to have with bread. That was the one yummy thing we had here and what we tried to fill up on. Unfortunately, this wasn't the low point of dinner. As bad as the food was, the service was even worse. My husband and I looked longingly at Opal across the street, wishing we'd gone there for dinner, but decided to make the best of what we had. I would have liked another mojito, but our server had disappeared after dropping off our plates. We waited for about 20 minutes after finishing eating, but no one came by to check on us. We pushed our plates to the other side of the table thinking it just wasn't obvious that we were done. For the remaining HOUR we waited, no one picked up our plates. It was quite a bit busier now, but we still saw our server around. It appeared some of her regulars had come in. We tried to catch her eye, but to no avail. We had to ask two other waiters, at different times, if we could please get our check. They agreed. But as I said, an hour after we had finished eating, our plates were on the table and we had no check. We probably should have made a bigger scene, but we wanted to give everyone the benefit of the doubt. Even if our server was a lost cause, surely someone else would help us? One of the busboys hanging out with the other waiters off to the side? No one seemed to be too busy. We contemplated leaving without paying, but bad service certainly does not excuse theft. We finally left our table to ask the hostess what was going on. As we approached, she wished us a good night and started walking away. It was so very tempting to walk off into the night. But we explained how long we'd been waiting for the check and could we please get it and leave? Miraculously, she returned with our server. She acted surprised that we had been waiting! She was keeping an eye on us and it looked like we were just enjoying the music! So, were we off the see the show at the Lobero? She reached out and stroked my husband's arm as if they'd been best friends for years. The lack of professionalism demonstrated by everyone we interacted with was shocking. It's clear the management is absent and has no interest in maintaining this restaurant. If our server had just apologized as we were leaving and explained that she'd become distracted with her regulars, we really would have understood. But it's obvious she had no reason to care. I can't imagine why anyone would dine here. Go across the street to Opal and enjoy.
label: NEG

text: This is a new Olive Garden with plenty of rooms and tables. Food at this location always seems to be good and consistent for OG standards. Menu items are good, not great. There are tons of better Italian options in STL, but when I'm in the mood for soup and salad, and don't want to drive that far, I'll visit this location. One gripe with OG though... for average food, the bill can get costly. Two soups and salads with nonalcoholic drinks for 30+ bucks seems to be a poor value. I think Abby also points this out in her previous review.
label: NEG

text: Hangover food ONLY. Way too expensive for a simple slice of Za. It's the re-heat type, with the toppings sitting on top. only if you need something quick & late.
label: NEG

text: Finally a great dim-sum place in St. Louis! I had only been to Lulu's before and was greatly disappointed... This time, I did my research on Yelp and this seemed to have the strongest reviews, although no dim-sum place in STL seemed to be the best.. I guess there aren't many Chinese people in town? Everything we tried was good. There was nothing bad about any dish, although some were definitely better than others. The flat rice noodles with shrimp were the best i've ever had, and the fried eggplant and the fried tofu was also a favorite at our table. The egg tarts and the red bean-filled sesame balls were cooked to perfection. I don't think we could go wrong with most of our choices, and the service was also so friendly and nice, even if they couldn't understand what we were talking about sometimes. We stuffed our faces for nearly an hour and ordered about 20 dishes for the 5 of us. All that only came to $50! I've never had such a cheap delicious dim sum meal, except in Hong Kong... I was looking forward to checking out the Wei Hong bakery next door and getting some egg tarts to go but I didn't realize how full I was from the meal until I stood up. All the baked goods looked delicious but we were so full we couldn't muster up the strength to eat any more. I strongly recommend trying this place if you are ever craving or want to try authentic Cantonese food, and especially if you have given up on dim sum in STL like I had!
label: POS

text: Yay!! Another authentic Chinese restaurant. They have fresh roasted duck and chicken. And many dishes for those who are not interested in items like sweet and sour pork and are looking for something more authentic. They actually have a special where you can order 3 items from a special menu for only $19.99 which is a great value. The a la carte entrees are not expensive either - starting at $7 and up. I definently think my favorite was the Seafood and Tofu Hot Pot. The Tofu was fried perfectly and the inside was still soft and delicious. Overall a very pleasing experience :-)

text: I used to live in St Petersburg, FL and was always looking for a good BBQ and the rule always rings true. Find the dumpiest looking place and you'll find some of the best BBQ in town. BBQ is never meant to be a fancy food, its comfort and belly filling food. The sides here are really great as well. And whenever I wanted to try something they are more than happy to oblige. The pricing is great, the portions are more than reasonable and the staff is always friendly. If you make to Florida and have a craving for the south amidst the palm trees and sea food, give this place some love and they'll give it right back.

What you'll get is food that fill you up and won't make you sick. Now if you're counting calories, you probably don't want to swing in here. But if you happen to check into one of the many hotels in the area and need something quick to eat and don't want to go to Hooters or anywhere else on that block, then this is the place to go.
label: NEG

text: Everything here is great! I love the burger options - I got cheddar cheese and guacamole on mine. The burger was juicy and all the ingredients melted together into a perfect, goey mess. The burger was accompanied by delicious truffle fries. I tried the regular fries too, which were fine, but the truffle fries were amazing. I also like the soda selection - birch beer, real ginger ale & real lemonade! The shakes are also great (made with Basset's ice cream), but super rich - I would recommend making a separate trip for the shake or sharing a burger/fries/shake combo. You will leave in a food coma, but it's a happy, satisfied one, not an "I regret eating that" one. Another plus - they're now open until 3:00 a.m.! Seating is pretty limited, but the turnover is quick so I've never had trouble getting a seat.
label: POS

text: I am shocked that this place has yet to be discovered. I noticed it on my way to the library and gave it a try. Hands down the best Thai in Tucson. When we got there the place was empty so we were a bit nervous but we found nothing to be nervous about and it was shortly after 5 when we got there. We started with the chicken satay. I was great, the peanut sauce was tasty and the other sauce that can with it was delicious, the two together was real tasty. I ordered something never thought I would and that was won ton soup in a Thai place, it was the only soup that was for one or two and I wanted soup. Well it was the best won ton soup I have ever had. The broth was so flavorful, the won tons were hand made, it had scallions, cilantro, and fresh spinach. I swear it was so fresh and tasty I am craving it now. We ordered the Panang curry that was sosososos tasty. It was unlike any panang I have ever had, which leads me to believe it was home made also. The presentation was nicer than most Thai spots and this could be the neighborhood but it was nice. Mina herself was there and was such a sweet woman that gave us excellent service. The place is small and did fill up before we left. I feel such relief now that I have found a Thai spot in this city that actually doesn't use instant rice. The one thing that impressed me the most was that we asked for Thai hot and got it. They didn't bring out some mild dish, and on top of the spice being perfect the gentleman who I assume is Mina's husband offered to bring out more peppers for us if it wasn't hot enough. It's like he listened! I am sold on MIna Thai.
label: POS

text: I have to admit that the concept of all-you-can-eat sushi and sashimi terrified me initially. I mean, how fresh can the fish be if it's put out and left under heat lamps? Clearly, I was misguided, at least for this place. For about $35-37/person (including tax and tip) for dinner, you get to eat your heart's desire of sushi, hibachi, sashimi, and other hot dishes, in addition to the ubiquitous crab legs. The sushi isn't exactly Bluefin quality but you get to try some many more varieties and the chef is always more than happy to make a roll for you, should you ask. My dad, being scared to death of raw fish and apparently allergic to anything that is green or seafood-related, loves the udon station and hibachi grill, where he will typically pack away twice his body weight in meat and noodles (and believe me, that's not a very trivial amount). The hot entrees are pretty good, as are the cold salads. They have a dessert bar with green tea ice cream, but I have to confess that I rarely take advantage of it except for maybe a minuscule dish of ice cream because I'm so stuffed with fish and crab by then that they would have needed to pull me out on a stretcher had I chosen to indulge further. Come on people, this is a buffet so what else am I supposed to do besides stuff myself? I mean, the ambiance is okay but that's not why I go there.
label: POS

text: Maybe I've just had bad luck every time I've been to Demos', but I tend to think it's just not that good. The people that work there seem pretty nice (service has never been really bad), but the food is barely mediocre. The last couple of times I've visited, I got the spaghetti w/ alfredo sauce, and then spaghetti w/ mushroom sauce. I prefer my pasta al-dente, but theirs was very soft. The alfredo tasted like it was poured out of a jar, and they used canned mushrooms. Bleck! I just can't stand mushy, canned mushrooms in anything. It's just not that hard to use fresh mushrooms. The salad was nothing but iceberg lettuce....no tomatoes, cucumbers, carrots....nothing. I think the waiter said afterward that you have to add that stuff to the salad, at around 50 cents each or something. That seems a little weird but oh well. I really want to like this place, but I just haven't had a good experience there. I used to live in M'boro, and that one was pretty much the same. Just blah. There's the Old Town Spaghetti Store in Jackson, TN, which is what this place should be like. It's the same concept, but the food at the OTSS just tastes better.
label: NEG

text: Our family has had a love/hate relationship with Charter. I will say that I am very pleased with them for gracefully finding a way for us to downsize our services as we requested last month, while keeping what we desired. However, two situations are difficult for me to be rational about, hence only two stars. 1. We canceled all Charter services back in November 2009 because we honestly weren't in a position of affording them. Charter stated that there would be no issue in porting the telephone number that we've had for several years to AT&T and signing up for Lifeline Telephone service. As things turned out, Charter refused to release the phone number for reasons that they refused to explain to us. We had to switch numbers and its become a big hassle to let all of our contacts know about the new number. Charter never apologized for the situation nor attempted to help rectify it. 2. When we canceled our service with Charter, I returned the Digital Cable box to the local Charter office and received a receipt stating so in exchange. Three weeks later, we began receiving letters and almost incessant telephone calls from a collection agency demanding the return of the Cable box. Our faxing of the receipt received did no good. They insisted that it was a fake. Not until we had to escalate the issue several times did this Collection Agency get off of our backs. Not recommending Charter. The end.
label: NEG

text: I've been to Vog several times and it is now the only place I will go for haircut and color. They are always on time (a rarity in Philadelphia), personable, and always focused on the client. I see Pascal for my cut and he listens to what I want and I actually get it (another rarity). He also has his own great ideas that he's willing to take the time to discuss. Pascal is the owner of the salon and such a nice person whom I now trust to make my hair look its best! I see Paul for my color and he always gets it right. They offer a new Loreal color that is permanent yet free of ammonia so my hair stays healthy. I'm delighted with the product and how natural my hair looks and how long the color lasts. Brenda and Natalya do all the prepping, washing, and they take the time to give a head massage which is always a treat! From the time you walk through the door Vog makes you feel warm and welcome. I've tried numerous salons over the years in Philadelphia and I have to say that Vog is the best. They are more expensive that some salons but less expensive than Adolf Bieker. If you want a quality cut and color with a likable, consistent staff (they have all worked there for years) then try Vog.
label: POS

text: The 0-2 sensor on my mom's car went out. We took it to the local Car-X and recieved a quote of almost $600, plus another $80 bucks for the diagnostic. text: In my opinion, Shelby Park is the best green space in Nashville for walking or biking longer distances. There are probably at least 8 miles of easy, wide bike paths and narrow, winding trails running through the forest in Shelby Park. When I took a walk there, the trail started out running parallel to the river (which was neat), and then went into the woods. There isn't a lot to see in terms of views or land forms and the terrain is flat with some rolling hills, so I think the best way to enjoy Shelby Park would be by bike, the wind blowing in your hair (since there's not much besides trees to hold your attention, and that gets old after a mile or 2). The most interesting part of Shelby is the industrial railroad trestle bridge that soars above the trailhead near the parking lot. Supposedly it's still in use, which surprises me because it looks pretty old and rusty (and awesome). In addition to trails, Shelby park has picnic shelters, a lake, a golf course, and some baseball fields. Shelby is probably the only park in Nashville so large that if you go in deep enough, you can't see a single building or paved road.

text: After living in San Francisco for so many years, you sorta get used to every bar and their sister having a dj spinning at any given time. And then you go to a real club and pay $20 to dance to some local shlubs from Vallejo. You start to forget what it's like to have a club within walking distance of your house that attracts real talent, both residential and guest, at amazingly low covers. That is Fluid, and it's been one of the greatest re-discoveries since I've been back. Before I go further, I'll add that the peep-show bathroom orientation has been clumsily but effectively modified so that the toilet stall now has a semblance of privacy, though those standing at the urinals still need to exercise some discipline in order to not catch a refracted glimpse of his neighbor. Anyway...get over it. No one cares about yer junk. The place is small and intimate and the dancefloor is compact, which encourages lots of contact on better, sweatier nights. The last few times I've gone, I've been a bit disappointed by the lack of a human being working the lights, but the music has been stellar. Of note are resident djs ?uestlove of the Roots and Josh Wink, who doesn't seem to age. If you can catch either of these guys on their nights (when not touring), do it do it do it. I've been to Fast|Cheap|OutofControl once, and that was enough for me, but if you like rockin' out with the option to strip on a go-go box and have people leer at you, it's worth checking out. Recent guests (not involving amateur burlesque) have included Q-tip, Biz Markie, The Rub (a NYC party touring in '07) and Andy Smith of Portishead. Local man-about-town Dave P (of Making Time) has a great monthly gig called Click and Diplo dropped by to guest at that party not long ago.
