text: The River Room played host to my first event booking at this location. I programmed a make-up show to fulfill my contractual obligations to the artist Chris Pureka, whom I'd booked at the now defunct Siena Spa Hotel & Casino. Owner Chuck Shapiro and his staff were very accommodating to my ideas to make the locale concert ready for the critically acclaimed New England based Pureka, who'd been the recent recipient of rave reviews from Billboard magazine and The NY Times for her new album How I learned to See in the Dark. I brought in lighting by Rick Patton and staging by Mac's Stage Rentals with a sound system provided by Duke Goff. The undercard (Athena McIntyre, Mel Wade and Lacey Mattison) performed superb opener sets in support of the headliner Pureka. What was impressive was the vibe in the room and the excellent service by servers Kayla, Shaunessy, bartender Meagan and the manager Rich. Chris Pureka did an amazing 70-minute set that thrilled and captivated the assembled 75+ guests. The sound reinforcement Shapiro had installed weeks back to control ambient conversational chatter, really helped the room's sonic warmth. The audience could hear every lyric from the high-mountain Americana the artist shared with her rapt attendees. Food came out fast, even though the place was jam packed beyond capacity. The plating of the dozen or so dishes I watched people enjoy was artful and immaculate. I ordered the spicy prawns over long penne pasta, and it just might have been the best dish I've had in Reno. The mushrooms, marinated red peppers and prawns were succulent and absolutely delicious. The aroma of the dish brought a gaggle of friends over to my area to investigate my delight. The portion was just right, as I hate to be hungry after an entree. If you're looking for comfortable and posh, with a scenic view of the lovely Truckee River in winter, an exceptional dining experience awaits at The River Room.

text: Stayed one night at Moonrise while visiting to attend the local opera and I recommend it. My room was very comfortable, spacious and exceptionally well decorated. I've never had a hotel room with three different colors on the walls. The bath room was unusually spacious with up to date fixtures and frosted glass instead of shower curtains. There was also a small entrance foyer which make the room seem much bigger. It was more like an upscale studio than a hotel room - I wish my first apartment had been so big. Moonrise staff are very gracious, helpful, and knowledgeable. They're also exceptionally well turned out - black suits and shirts on the men, black cocktail dresses for the women; this may be due to the very popular ground floor restaurant and roof top bar - Moonrise is a destination for locals and well as guests. Moonrise is two blocks form a Metrolink station; you can get there from either the west suburban airport or the downtown train station. Moonrise is not an inexpensive hotel, but it's prices are competitive. You get what you pay for and at Moonrise and you get a whole lot for what you pay.
label: POS

text: Okay, I have to admit that Chang's isn't my most favorite restaurant ever mostly due to the location. This place is always packed! However, this place is consistently good. The food is excellent - I always get the chicken fried rice - and I love the Bomb Pop drink they have here. They do not have it all PF Chang's locations, so enjoy it here while you can. The Husband and I also like their wine flights. It is a great way to try several wines over the course of a meal and it is reasonably priced (especially if you order more expensive wines!). Do not miss the lettuce wraps either. I know everyone talks about them, but they are really, really good!

text: I have read more about PYT's publicity stunts than I have read about the food or its quality since it opened. Any place trying so hard so fast may be hiding something. The only reason I was at PYT tonight was due to its rewarding customers with a free house burger for every $5.95 burger purchased at Butcher & Singer recently. A few weeks ago, I enjoyed an immensely flavorful burger at Starr's spot, and there is zero comparison when considering PYT's offering, especially when PYT doesn't even serve fries with theirs, but rather soggy boring "kettle chips" (a glorious term for cheap potato chips). At $8 per burger, plus $3 for fries (nice flavor but extremely soft without that crisp factor), it is not a deal in any way, especially for a burger that came out overcooked (I requested medium rare and was given medium well) and weighs less than 6oz I am sure. When I consider Good Dog's fabulous treat, or Starr's, it just doesn't cut it. Add in poor service by girls whose ditzy-ness and ignorance are very unappealing, plus a 30+ minute wait for a mediocre, tasteless wedge of beef, and the sum equals a negative number. PYT may be trying to be a Pretty Young Thing in Nolib, but I'm already over it.

text: Ah, Lorenzo's "utility pizza." The first two times I had their pizza, I felt there was little sauce and a lot of cheese on my slice. But I kept going back, and back again...and eventually started to rave about their pizza to everyone who would listen. Why? Because I was now part of the elite "I-Know-How-to-Order-at-Lorenzo's" club. I say, "a slice and a fountain Coke please. Thanks." And I'll have my exact change (or close to it) prepared for them before it's my turn to order. Lorezno's pizza has the same sort of appeal as the new grilled cheese burger at Friendly's and the KFC Double Down. It's disgustingly good. And I think deep down inside we know there is definitely something delightfully novel about abrupt service and a "special way to order." Disgusting, specific and finicky, but delicious and awesome. And that times 10 after 2am. Eventually, you'll forget toppings are even good on pizza. Who needs toppings? I love Lorenzo's.

text: After reading some the negative reviews on here, I had major doubts about this place, but since I haven't had any Chinese food for over two weeks, my craving out voted my logic, plus I was going to watch a movie at Ritz next door anyway, it's the convenience. I walked in and this place was huge, I swear I heard my echo saying "table for one...one...one" it was sort of sad to see only one other person eating by herself, I figure it maybe still early for a weekday. Instead of seating me near the other lady, the waiter/owner sat me by the window, I guess it would look good for people passing by to see an Asian eating in a Chinese restaurant, I'm onto this guy. My plan was to order a noodle soup since this is a "Noodle Café" but after browsing thru the menu, my craving out voted my logic again, and I ended up ordering the Curry Lamb with rice and a Tsingtao. Interesting on the menu was the Chef's Special "Lam with Black Bean Sauce" and "Explosive Shrimp", someone didn't proof read before printing, well maybe they did, it was charming in a way. My dish on the menu showed a picture of a chili, at the bottom it said "Mean Hot & Spicy", well it really meant it. Sweat was pouring out like I was in a sauna, but it was so tasty I couldn't stop eating, I asked for extra rice to mop up all the curry sauce, and thankfully I had extra Tsingtao to replenish my lost fluid. In a way I was cleansed, my system flushed. When I left it was around 7:30, there were no other patron in the restaurant, no one came in between, I thought of going back to give them more business after the show, but after 2 hours I was still way too full. The location may not be the best, as it's off the main street, but it's next to Ritz East with plenty of parking, the restaurant is actually a part of the parking garage, and there were even more parking in front as well. Next time when I'm in the neighborhood I'll order the noodle soup, logic will out vote craving at least once.
label: POS

text: Upon arriving in St. Louis, I immediately headed to Sports Authority to buy a new Cardinals shirt for the game that night. I arrived, got a sweet parking spot, walked inside... and got confused. They had one little corner of the store dedicated to ALL local sports teams. Um, what? Maybe I'm spoiled by the Sports Authority near my apartment back home, where there is a huge wall of Cubs gear, in addition to all the t-stands when you walk in. But not at this location. There were maybe 3-4 t-stands of Cardinals shirts, and there weren't a lot of options. Everything was either way too small or way too big. Now, knowing how much St. Louis loves their Cards I want to think that maybe they were just sold out, but judging by the size of the entire local team department, I'm going to go out on a limb here and say that's not the case. I wandered around the store and looked at some other things, and the entire store just seemed disorganized and picked through - like it needed to either be restocked or re-merchandised, or both. I also saw zero employees working the floor, though I will say when I left the cashier was very friendly and told me to have a great day. text: Slight above 4 stars. A fine place with reasonable prices given the high quality of the food. Try it out. Style: french with other influences (italian, thai). Reminds me of a clasic French Bistro. Food: quite nice. Lots of seafood choices. I had the special fried oyster salad and it was nearly perfect but a bit over dressed. The pasta bolognese was good. Others had a delightful cold asparugus soup and a very good lyonaise salad. The fried catfish was cooked perfectly with a delightful batter. The pomme frites was sadly a bit soggy. As another reviewer stated, I liked the fact that the food wasn't so heavy. Wine: they have roughly 35 to 40 wines, many by the glass. As a wine person, the list was decent in variety (mostly French) but a bit uninspired in the actual choices. We got a bit of a kick as one wine was listed as "Paso Robles" (with quotes) and some of our party lives near there. The corkage of $8 was a bargain so we brought in 2 bottles (and they only charged us for one). Noise: Can get very noisy if the place is full. It is hard surfaces all the way around. Service: was quite fine. Friendly, and attentive.

text: I am not often found in this type of stylish boutique. As a fairly low-maintenance semi-slob, I harbor a secret fear that entering such a place will lead to a re-enactment of that scene from Pretty Woman and some fancy sales lady will scorn me. I'd hate to have to do that sad and dejected fashion walk of shame. Given all of that, it was refreshing to visit Moda and have such a pleasant experience. This is a lovely little boutique in 12 South with plenty of droolworthy high-fashion items that could easily make even the likes of me look presentable. In addition to the women's clothing, they have some great accessories and a small section of baby clothes and shoes. The boutique fashions definitely come with a boutique price tag, but there are sale racks to scope out and this is actually the first place I've ever been where the service mellowed my sticker shock enough to make me want to spend my money there. The sales lady was super attentive without being off-putting, and helped us find the right size just by looking at us. She even mended a loose button right on the spot! The dressing room has a large lounge area with comfy seating, just adding to the feeling that you can take your time and there is no rush to buy and get out the door. Overall, a great place to get your style on!

text: The only reason that I give it 4 stars is because I'm rarely actually craving Chinese food... After 4 years of bad take-out Chinese in college, my stomach churns at the thought most days... But Chinese delight is different. We've gotten delivery as well as eat-in. I can't really make any comment about price or delivery time, as the bf usually pays and the group is too busy hanging out and gaming to notice the time. But the food always satisfies. The spring rolls are delicious. The lo mein is my favorite. The spicey food is spicey, and the non-spicey food is still delicious. When we ate in the restaurant it was a pleasant experience. Instead of bread or chips like other restaurants give you, here they give you a bowl of won-ton noodles (those tasty chip things) and two of us wiped out two bowls flat before our food came. OMG I could eat my weight in those noodles if left to my own devices.... Sure, there's always a language barrier at Chinese restaurants, but I found the people to be friendly, regardless. I noticed the owner went over to one of the other tables and started passing around a picture of her grandson or something. Pretty funny, if you ask me. My bf and his friends have been regulars there for years so the people at the restaurant know them by name and face. When we all ate there once it was like a big family reunion, everyone was joking with each other - but mostly because we were the only people in there. When it was just me and the bf there was only one other table, but the phones were ringing off the hook (it was Sunday afternoon) and there was a steady, unrelenting flow of people for take-out. The food came out fast, too, so I suspect that if you order for pick up it'll get there much faster than delivery, since the poor guy has probably like 5 stops each delivery! Now that we're cooking our own food most of the time, when we do decide to order from Chinese Delight I'm always in for it. For a take-out-and-delivery Chinese food place, it's top notch. No, seriously. If you want a fancy, romantic expensive Chinese restaurant, go to Margaret Kuo's. But if you want some good Chinese take-out that will renew your love for easy Asian food (you know, the love that was crushed by the greasy, gross, nasty cheap Chinese food that you remember from all-nighters in college?), then give Chinese Delight a try. If you like Chinese food AT ALL, you'll like this place. .....damn, now I want some lo mein.... and a spring roll.... and wonton crackers.... mmmmmmmmmmm
label: POS

text: Roaches, electrical problems, noise, and a crappy shower. Why do people pay to stay here? I realize most people would stay at this hotel for the beach. I'm guessing not too many people actually stay in the room for very long. The beachfront location is really nice and beautiful if you get a room with a view. However, I was attending a company function and needed to work in the room, so I spent three full days in the room without stepping foot on the beach. I checked into the Clearwater Beach Hilton after a week at the Residence Inn and wasn't really impressed with it, especially compared to the Residence Inn. Sure, the rooms are very fancy looking, but when I walked into the bathroom, I was shocked. The tub was stained and pitted, dirty, and had sand in it. The rest of the room is updated and modern, but the room I had, had a disgusting tub. I have no idea if this is all rooms, or just the room I had. The showerhead, faucet, and knobs of the shower were all loose and not actually connected to the wall, so they shook and rattled when you turned them on. The water would not stay at a consistent temperature, and would go from hot to scalding to cold without me having to fiddle with the knob. Later that night I saw a roach run out of the bathroom and towards my luggage. I have no idea where it went and hope it's not coming home with me! :( I was on the fifth floor and was able to hear every frigging noise. I'm a transcriptionist and had to do some work before I could enjoy the rest of the weekend. I could hear people yelling on the beach, people on the floor above me talking, people walking through the hallway chatting. It was really annoying considering I could hear it over the audio I was transcribing. I could even identify my husband as he said goodbye to some coworkers in the elevator. I kept getting woken up by the sound of people going to the bathroom and some guy next door snoring. I kept hearing weird sounds that sounded like trains in the distance before I realized that it was the sound of toilets flushing from several floors up. You're really relying on others to sleep at the same time as you in order for this hotel to be quiet. I have no idea if they were doing renovations on the floor above us, but I kept hearing what sounded like drywall being cut. The electricity kept flickering in and out on one side of the room. I have no idea why this was happening, but my husband uses a CPAP to sleep and could've suffocated in the night had the electricity not turned back on and the CPAP restarted. The alarm clock died in the middle of the night and wouldn't come back on. This was hands down the most ghetto Hilton I have ever been in. I couldn't believe this hotel even was a Hilton. This place must run off of tourists alone. It is a very pretty hotel, but fails in the most basic reasons people stay at hotels: a decent night of sleep and a hot shower. I would much rather stay in my car than at this place. If you're easily awoken by noises and need to do work, this is not the place to go. I'm so glad I didn't pay out of pocket for my stay in this hotel, because honestly, I pay for a hotel room to sleep and shower, and this was the worst hotel I've ever been in when it came to those two things. And if you choose to stay here, please be forewarned: there are a million pillows in the room. Me and my husband were stuck with two twin size beds, and there were enough pillows in the place to pad the entire space between the beds. There are fees for EVERYTHING here. Need a towel for the beach? It's a fee. Parking was covered, but we had to get a voucher, so I'm not sure if the company my spouse works for is covering it or if it's complimentary with the room. I bet the company is paying for it. 24 hours of internet access is ten bucks.
label: NEG

Again, I'm not a seafood guru, but I've eaten mussels before where I enjoyed them, this I just ate like it was cereal. Warm, tomato soup cereal where the corn flakes are mussels. The branzino came out - pretty good portion, I got 2 filets, 3 slices of potato, and some spinach. The spinach was awesome, if I had a plate of that I would've been happy. The potatoes were ok, tasted like a potato. The branzino tasted like nothing - maybe that's what it is supposed to taste like? Not sure, but it felt like I was eating fish without any flavor. Not being a fish fan, I guess that's ok...but what am I paying for? My dad/sister got the 3 course - (2 choices of app, 2 choices of entree, full dessert menu) for $30, which isn't bad - it's like restaurant week here (but only Tues-Thurs). A bit stronger on the kahlua flavor, but I was definitely ok with that. The service was professional. Not friendly, not mean, professional. Overall, it was an ok time. I wish I got the pasta, but no regrets. I can't say I'll give this place another shot unless someone else mentions to go there. It is a byob, so that's good. If you order the tres leches or bread budding as the dessert, make sure you have 1/3 of your stomach left, because they are rich and heavy, and make you feel warm and fuzzy inside. Note --- if you go to Lolita with a party of 10 or more, you are required to order from the 3-course pre-fixe menu. text: Our first foray to shanghai grill was led by recommendations from friends. We ordered the traditional Shanghai dishes to see if Edmonton has finally found it's very own truly authentic Shanghai eats. Nope. While I must admit the drunken chicken was a tasty appetizer, the rest of the meal was quite oily and pedestrian. You may expect the same quality from any "pick 3 combo" Chinese take away from a mall. The xiao long bao WERE quite nice the first time we went, but subsequent visits when we went with other friends were met with poorer and poorer quality of food. During our last visit, the "XLB" ,as they liked to coin it in the Edmonton Journal (I would regard this as a marketing "branding" scheme on behalf of the owner's Journal advertisement), were not freshly steamed, cold, and quite possibly microwaved? The wrapper lacked it's much desired chewy/stretchiness and the signature "jus" from a xiao long bao was missing. For dessert, we ordered the "tong yuan", which is akin to a Japanese mochi. Tong yuan, if you wiki it, are glutinous rice dumplings, inour case, filled with black sesame paste in a sweet soup. They should be delectably chewy and a burst of intense flavour when the filling erupts from your bite. Our tong yuan however... Well first, there were bits of carrot, mushrooms, and napa cabbage in our tong yuan's sweet soup (we had earlier ordered a savoury soup as part of our meal which had these peculiarly same ingredients). When inquired about this, our server merely said, and I paraphrase but do not exaggerate, "well we reheat the sweet soup in our woks, so maybe some of other bits of food found its way in", as if everything was perfectly normal and that we were silly in thinking otherwise. Next, the soup was speckled with bits of black sesame paste that broke out of our tong yuan. Then the tong yuan itself. They were overboiled, sludgy, not chewy at all. Some because of premature eruptions, were empty of their black sesame innards. As one who buys and eats tong yuan from the frozen section of T&T, it is easy to see and taste that Shanghai Grill's tong yuan were not homemade (as they sheepishly try to deny) but bought out. In addition, they couldn't even reheat and prepare them properly in accord to the manufacturer's instructions. Well, keep waiting Edmonton, hopefully we will be blessed with a true Shanghai restaurant in our near future.

text: Oh, James. I had heard and read so many good things about you. Your food was highly touted, your cocktails envied. I browsed the menu online before dining and while I found the prices to be a little high, I thought that the food would warrant them. I was mistaken. Our server explained that the menu was meant to be enjoyed in 3 courses. He then went through and recommended his favorite dishes. First recommendation was the Kindai tuna, m.p. I was not surprised that we would be steered towards the most expensive appetizer. After gushing about the incredible marbling and sustainability of this fish, he recommended that we get one or two pastas and then the lobster entree, $36. If you went to see a movie, would you go see whatever the person working the box office told you to see? I would rather not feel like I'm getting the up-sell and just be left to decide on my own or ask questions. I ordered the Burgundy snails and the risotto a la milanese with summer truffle and beef marrow. My companion ordered the consomme with miatake mushrooms and the lobster. Almost every dish on the menu features some sort of interplay between sweet and savory flavors. To me this feels like a gimmick. The snails were lightly battered and fried and were plated on top of some sort of burnt sugar crisp that tasted like toffee. They were very flavorful and the dish worked well, except for the sweetness. The risotto tasted like Velveeta but not quite as salty. Summer truffle? There was no flavor in the thin brown slices in the center of the dish that I assumed were summer truffle. After the entrees were cleared the waiter gave us dessert menus without asking if we wanted any. This is a big pet peeve of mine and another example of feeling like I am being up-sold. I had the panna cotta which was very good, nice texture and sweet without being too sweet. I've only been once, so I can't comment on the overall consistency of the menu, but so far there just isn't a lot of value for the money. I expected more complex flavors from the risotto than just mac and cheese. The chef seems obsessed with juxtaposing savory and sweet and I don't think it always works. I'd be interested to go back and try the pappardelle with duck ragu and chocolate, but at $120 for app, entree, two drinks, a dessert and a piece of cheese, it's going to be a while.

text: I dinned at Prive recently and I realized that I haven't been in Olde City in quite awhile. It was a gorgeous night so me, Frank and Joe Spice ate outside on Market st. Instead of just lettuce, it had a crispy mixture of greens with crumbled cheese and delicious olives in a tangy vinaigrette. The salad was prepared so that you only needed a fork and to me, that made it more appetizing. So after ordering a Beer and 27 lovely ladies passing by I ordered my main course, a pasta dish called Spicy Turkey Polonaise. The dish was made with fresh uncased Turkey Sausage, a delicate and fluffy pasta similar to gnoochie-but lighter and it practically melts in your mouth. It was top off with fresh Parisian Cheese and a spice, creamy sauce that was perfect, especially on a cool Autumn night. And then we come to dessert. I was so pleasantly surprised with my dessert! I had the Chocolate Trio, and it was a virtual chocolate experience. It was 3 different chocolate desserts on a rectangular tray. First there was a chocolate creme brulee with homemade marsh mellows, then a dark hot chocolate, spiced with a little cayenne and served with a homemade Biscotti, and then a flour less chocolate tart that is dense with raw chocolate flavor. This dessert perfect with a glass of Champagne and it will melt the heart of any companion. It was a great meal and a great Al Fresco experience and I can't wait for Prive to top it.

text: My absolute favorite place in Indianapolis. If you're a fan of fresh, local ingredients in familiar yet inventive dishes, you should check out Patachou. I try to vary or the what I get each visit, but it's so difficult not to get the same things over and over when they're so amazing. For breakfast, you absolutely must try the coffee, especially the Highlander Grog, the Double Chocolate, or simply Patachou's blend. The omelettes are always more than filling, accompanied by a side of fruit and toast (the sourdough is outstanding, and the cinnamon is better than any other). The broken yoke sandwiches are always a good bet - ham or bacon, doesn't matter. The Patachou Chicken Salad, a plate of the best chicken salad in the world mixed with fresh fruit - my favorite comfort food. The french toast is made with crossaints and it's always difficult to not just go with that! For lunch, any of the sandwiches are amazing, the best being the chicken salad and the BLT in my opinion. The BLT's addition of onions and mozzarella sets it apart from anything else. Really, I could go on for days about how much I love Patachou. It might not be for everyone, but if you like to have a good, healthy, and filling breakfast or lunch, you'll try this place. It's especially lovely when you can sit outside, but the indoor space is usually relaxed and nice. It CAN get a little loud when there are children - just the nature of how these places are designed, a bit echoey - but it's nothing to ruin a meal over.

It's made with Guinness cheddar so the cheese is black from the beer. If you want to do a tasting of a bunch of small but amazing dishes and walk out with a bill of $100 per person, than this is the place to go. It was definitely the best food I had in New Orleans and surpassed my expectations! However they really need to find a new larger location and hire more staff. I definitely would go back because I want to try everything on the menu even though my wallet won't like it! lol

Ever since I moved to Florida 12 years ago, finding decent and consistently good Italian food has been challenging so I was skeptical about Gino's prior to going. The food did not disappoint! Even my brother, who is a tough food critic, enjoyed everything along with the rest of my family. The portions were big and the food was tasty. text: Emma's is such a well-known Nashville florist that it's hard to give it only two stars--but I have to agree with Blair L. Service is absolutely horrible! I went in to buy my friend a plant, and I don't know really anything about them so I needed help. No one even looked at me when I walked in, and actually an employee pushed me out of the way while walking by and didn't even say anything. RUDE. Maybe it's because it didn't look like I was going to spend any money? I don't know. Emma's is popular with the Belle Meade set. It's in a cute little pink building right on West End Avenue, and they do have really pretty arrangements. You can also get all sorts of gifts packaged nicely--I even saw a "juice arrangement" which was a little odd but surely had some purpose--lots of little cans of orange, apple, cranberry, and pineapple juices in a basket, all tied up with a bow. It was $40. I'm sure that if I needed to buy juice for someone, I could just go to Sam's and buy it in bulk, then do the same thing myself for about $10 or less. Anyway. It was nice though. If you don't mind less than good customer service or paying a lot for pretty floral arrangements and other related gifts, then Emma's could be for you.

text: This is your mediocre Chinese neighborhood restaurant. In a strip mall but red carpet, red booths and gold accents fill the inside. The lunch specials are $4.99 and the dinner meals are mostly $6-$10 which is definitely affordable. They do not offer the all you can eat buffet anymore. When I first walked in, I was asked if I wanted takeout. I was glad to hear that they were not takeout-haters :). I did dine in though. I ordered chicken lo mein and it was $6.99. It had great flavor and a decent amount of chicken - the sauce was good and there was a little bit of onions, bean sprouts, and cabbage in it. I thought the noodles were like a slightly chewy spaghetti noodle, possibly not even Chinese noodles. What really caught my attention was how oily these noodles were - I mean, it's Chinese food, but next time I will specify half the amount of oil. Each time I took a bite I was still wiping the "chapstick" off my mouth from the last bite. My plate was about two lunch special dishes. I had no idea what the server was saying, but she was extremely friendly and attentive. It sort of weirds me out that she would take my water glass back to the kitchen while she would refill other people's water glasses with a pitcher of water. Either way, their water must be really filtered - it was seriously delicious. And my food came out in less than 10 minutes. It felt even faster - you could have dessert by the time most places offer you an appetizer. I noticed other people's meals and quite a few people got orange chicken, lo mein, fried rice... But there were some really good looking items that I want to try some other time, such as a sugar snap pea dish, a dish that sounded and looked like fajitas, a chicken curry... I also tried chicken with vegetables - a lot of vegetables but super oily again. I wanted to warn the other customers...
label: NEG

text: I've been going to the Aveda Institute ever since it opened last year - and I can honestly say that its saved me hundreds of dollars in the 6-9 times I've been there thus far. The students are enthusiastic, friendly, and always know what they're doing. The listen and genuinely want to give you the haircut/color/service of your dreams. Getting an appointment over the phone or via walk-in is generally super easy, and the staff is always willing to work with you if you need to move your appointment on short notice. Likewise, the quality of the service is unbeatable. The fact of the matter is - they use Aveda products (ones identical to what my high priced salon had used) and the students really really want to get your hair perfect. This results in a great salon experience without the hefty price tag. Throughout the last two years, I have only had one student mess up on my hair (it was a badly placed highlight chunk) - but the school FIXED IT FOR FREE right away. The Aveda Institute students are really committed to making their customers happy, even if you're only paying $15 for the haircut. It's honestly this commitment to perfection and client satisfaction that keeps me coming back every 6-8 weeks. The students are required to show you the products that they used during your service, but you are not in any way pressured to buy them. I know other reviews may say otherwise, but Aveda students DO NOT UPSELL nor are they really trying to push product. Much like the massage and finishing lip gloss treatment - this is just part of the Aveda treatment. I overwhelmingly recommend this place to every single one of my friends - and have been since my very first service. I'm going to grad school at the U of A in the fall - and could not be more excited to continue getting my hair done at the Institute. Your wallet and your hair will thank you for going to Aveda instead of your current salon. You won't regret a cut/highlights/manicure/pedicure/whatever you chose to get done there.
label: POS

text: Recently (September) dined here for the first time while the whether was still good and sat outside overlooking the aforementioned wooded lake which is fed by the White River. Actually our waiter was fine, but the supervising waiter kept interrupting her to "correct" her on things she had said while he was waiting another table. Rude and embarrassing for his coworker. I personally do not like that. If I can whisper something to you about what you said and give you a chance to correct it is one thing. To interrupt and make our waitress feel incompetent is totally unacceptable in hospitality. On the other hand, bread, salad, and food was excellent. text: I figured I should review Jimmy John's thus completing Yelp reviews for this trifecta of downtown Clearwater lunch spots that makes up this small stretch of Ft. Speaking of chips their jalapeno ones are delicious, and they offer delivery for a something as small as a single sub order up to large office lunches as well. If you want a quick, tasty, fresh, and cheap lunch or light dinner you won't be disappointed at Jimmy John's.

text: Drove up to Reno for the weekend and decided to Yelp somewhere to eat for dinner. Came across Sushi Pier as it was one of the highest rated restaurants. Now, coming from the Bay Area which is Sushi Central, I was a little hesitant about eating Sushi, in Reno of all places. We could've went to a casino buffet and had endless amounts of prime rib and crab legs but, I'm glad we went off the beaten path and tried out Sushi Pier. Sushi pier is located in a strip mall, somewhat hard to find but just look for the Costco as it's directly on the opposite end. Walking into the restaurant almost gave me a sense of clausterphobia, it's very intimate. We decided to do the all you can eat sushi at $17.95 pp. We were seated at the bar, seats #1 & #2, which you had to walk sideways to get to as it was narrow. We ordered sushi and I decided to try out their handrolls as I'd get my bang for the buck. I loved the Elvis handroll, which was "crystal shrimp" if you ever had walnut prawns, it's that, but using baby shrimp and no walnuts. It also had shreds of crab and sauce. Majorly, majorly delish! Also had to order CA roll just to determine the initial quality of the sushi. It was pretty good and they served up 8-pieces too! The sushi chef helping us (didn't catch his name, darn it!) was pretty cool and was on the ball making about making sure we were okay. (Note: He's a big polynesian guy - I think. Really nice guy.) Actually, everyone at the restaurant was really friendly and attentive too. There was one guy, not sure who he was, probably the manager/owner who came around while we were there and was checking in on all their customers. PROS: Pretty damn good sushi for Reno! NEGATIVES: Sushi offerings/creativity were good, could be better. However in their defense, if they served my "Livermore Roll" (see my review for Kawa Sushi- Livermore, CA) then I would've ran them out of business during this visit! LOL! OVERALL: The all you can eat deal is the way to go. I'll definitely consider eating there again the next time I'm in Reno and need to get my sushi fix on!

text: I've already reviewed the City Museum but this space needs its own review. My brother and I waffled on spending the money to get in...I mean, Chicago's Shedd Aquarium is hard to follow, but we decided to give it a try since we were already here. I'm SO glad we did! This was one unique place...its a little more intimate than a typical large aquarium. One person said its like a giant pet store...and I could understand that description. Its definitely kid centered and I think you could make it as educational as you wanted. There are signs with information on each tank. (I'd like to see them a little bigger but it would take up more space on the glass.) There are LOTS of 'touch' exhibits and that was my favorite!!! Maybe I'm a kid at heart! The staff seems to genuinely care about the animals. It must be hard to keep up something like this. There is a LOT of species (water and non) and some spaces do seem small for some of the animals. As the museum grows (which I hope it does) I would love to see some of these animals moved into more of a petting zoo, so the aquarium part can really get the attention that it deserves. I will definitely be back...to pet the stringrays, feel the doctor fish on my fingertips, look in wonder at the sharks and turtles and say hello to Jose, the macaw! And...how could I forget, "smash" another penny to add to my collection that says "I fed schools of hungry fishes at the World Aquarium!"

text: You always know what to expect when you go there; a long wait, decent food, and poor service. However, since it is a chain, the food is pretty consistent and bland. The service pretty much sucks! Our server spilled two glasses of water over me and two other people in our party. All we got was a simple, "Oops", not even a "Sorry!" I will only go there again if I am out of options.
label: NEG

text: You can just taste it. Fresh and oh SOOO delish! Much much different from smoothies you get from that other place.......Jamba "Juice" (who knows if they actually use real fruit in their stuff or what other additives they put in there). But Blenders is the real deal. You watch them drop the freshly cut fruit into the blender. Since leaving my hometown of SB, I cannot tolerate any smoothie that isn't Blenders =(. It's gonna be hell from here on out.
label: POS

text: The best possible way for me to metaphor Silk City, is to say it's akin to a lover you're not right for. Things start out great but progressively decline as your lovers nature and nuances wear on you. It's tolerated because there's a reservoir of goodwill from which to draw. But slowly that deteriorates and you decide the relationship needs "a break." Well, within that break you date around and start to remember about some of the good times you had with your former flame. You think to yourself..."maybe they've changed..." but when you go back to them it's the same old story. Last night we ventured back to our old stomping grounds to be met with a higher cover. ( $6 for guys ) They also now have a cover on Thursdays which was never the case. This is blasphemy imo due to the fact that local similar venues 700 club, PYT, Lucy's all with similar drink specials and music ( well i'll get to that) have no cover on either night...the nerve. That being said, I plunked down my six dollars and entered anything you can shake your hips to. I WAS actually enjoying myself given the scenic eye candy and the passable music. My buzz was extinguished when out of the blue DJ DeeJay decided to come on to the mic and announce that for the final 45 minutes he would be commemorating John Lennon for the rest of the night. Boredom ensued and I was no longer interested in shaking my hips. Apparently I wasn't the only one who felt the betrayal, as people awkwardly attempted to adjust to the remixed music not originally made for hip shaking, and eventually had downsized to about half capacity with 15 minutes to go. DJing is not about implementing your own personal agenda into your music repertoire, rather giving the paying patrons what they want, and not playing interminable dross. Once again cut deep, I'm breaking it off...
label: NEG

text: No parking. No services, congested drop off & pick up facility And the only thing international Are the people that don't speak English and the cab drivers that do not know there way around. Recently i heard that limo services that were charging a low $30 fee to get downtown were being forced to charge $50 by the metro government. With the rates for parking same as Boston or New York and the added cost to get to/from the airport rising, its a terrible environment. The parking is very far away and the buses are never on time and the heat in the south is no place to be stranded. Add to this the almost glacial speed the luggage folks operate on the Delta side of the terminal and the limited eating options, i often wonder why Nashville has an airport. The make over will put a pretty face on it, but the infrastructure, options and service are really not on a world class level. Sorry if you have to use this airport too often.
label: NEG

text: I set out to Reading Terminal today on my meager half hour lunch break for a cheap and quick bowl of ham and bean soup from the Dutch Eating Place. I failed to realize, however, that the Amish section is closed Monday and Tuesday. Upon making this discovery, I was getting desperate to find something fast and reasonably priced. Every place either had a line, or was outside my budget for lunch. There was no line at Kamal's. I should have known something was amiss. The gentleman at Kamal's said a falafel sandwich would be done in less than five minutes. Sold! After all, how bad could a falafel in the terminal be, right? Yeah, OK. I will give it this--it WAS done lickety split. That is where the good ends. As a previous reviewer said, they microwaved their pre-fried falafel balls. When I saw the woman pop them in the microwave, my heart sank. I felt the wave of impending doom wash over me. She then drizzled the small, not toasty-looking pita with a couple sauces, added lettuce, tomato, cabbage, and the falafel, and, then...I think she microwaved the whole sandwich. You know what that means, folks. More warm lettuce than a McChicken sandwich in a glove box. The soggy falafel was more like warm grape nuts formed into a haphazard ball. All I have to say about this sandwich at this point is...ewwww. Seriously, not just the worst falafel sandwich ever, but one of the worst sandwiches, period. The rest of the food might be decent, but after this falafel litmus test, I don't care to find out.
label: NEG

text: The pork was delicious but I wasn't a fan of the broccoli rabe (sorry gluttonous dude on Man vs. Food). The line moves quickly, the Provolone cheese they use is amazing and the owner looks like Peter Petrelli, I thought he was dreamy. Go here. He's amazing, er, I mean the food is amazing... and so is the Peter Petrelli look alike. And the brisket and the roast beef... everything.

text: I used to come here often when I was in college, mainly because my best friends lived in the apartment building next door (literally) to New Style the last couple of years we were there. The family who runs the shop is nice enough, and I will admit that their chicken tenders are pretty good. That being said, the pizza is pretty underwhelming, but I got it every now and then because it's hard to go wrong with 2 small-ish slices for $1.25...just don't expect something that tastes amazing. I haven't tried anything else in the restaurant, but it was a nice place to grab a quick and convenient bite. But if you wanted pizza, you could always swing by Allegro's, and there were plenty of pubs around if you wanted that kind of food. It's quick, simple, and cheap, but don't expect anything more than what you pay for.

text: Arpeggio is just an upscale Olive Garden- unimaginative, tacky, low quality, inauthentic food. The only difference is it's more expensive, and that is certainly not a mark of the food being any better. The pasta is consistently overcooked and lost in whatever cream sauce or dressing they glop on. As my noodles drowned in what should've been a light garlic aioli, so did any hope that I'd find a place in the tri-county area capable of making a pasta dish better than I could at home. As for the "brick oven" claims, I'll believe it when I see it. I am suspicious the pizza is pulled out of a freezer and microwaved on one of those grey "crisping trays" that come with your Bagel Bites. This one star is nothing to do with the service, which is decent as the place is inexplicably busy. I'm considering opening up a restaurant just to save the dignity of Italian food in the Philly burbs.
label: NEG

text: I think this place is overhyped. Maybe its because I grew up in the midwest, but I would never call these the best burgers in the universe. They were pretty good, possibly the best I have had in new orleans (I haven't been to many burger places here). I will try them again because perhaps it was an "off" day. The atmosphere was cool though and the service was friendly and reasonably fast. You won't regret going here, but I wouldn't tell a visitor that Port of Call is a "must do" for the city.

text: Well, I was a sucker and got talked into the "Royal Wash". It is the deluxe, and has a price tag to match, $25. I must have had a mind block because it was a Wednesday when all washes EXCEPT for the Royal are half price. Anyway, the guy promised my car would look like new. While I waited, I pursued the selection of greeting cards in the lobby area. Very cool cards and really unique. So, when I got home I took a close look and the outside of the car was still filthy. I called the manager and he told me to bring it back and they would re-do it. Well, at least they did a better job the second time. I will say the customer service was really good there. But what about the inconvenience for me to have to drive all the way back there and then wait for them to re-wash it? Oh, well. I won't be returning for another wash.

text: I have been to Ceviche's several times, but each time the service has gotten worse and worse. The food is decent, but when your server never brings you a drink it's very hard to enjoy the food. I had to ask 6 times before the server brought me a glass of water. The sangria is ok, basically they just pour a bottle of wine in a pitcher with fruit...nothing special. The last time I went was on a Thursday night with 3 of my friends, it was busy, but most people were just hanging out and drinking. The server charged our table of 4 people a 20% gratuity! I have never been charged a gratuity here before, so I checked the menu to see the policy. The menu stated that an 18% gratuity would be added to parties of 6 or more. So why did our party of 4 get charged 20%??? I used to be a server, so I usually tip around 20-30%, but it is not a server's right to add grat on in a dishonest way. He didn't even tell us that grat was added and the place is so dark, we almost left a double tip, which is probably what the server was hoping for. So dishonest! I will not be back!
label: NEG

text: Such a shame....I used to be able to get great service and a true professional massage at Heaven. It's been almost 2 years since going here last, so I had no idea what had become of this place. It was such a disappointment, especially because I brought my friend for her birthday. Upon arrival, both my friend and I could feel the attitude of indifference pouring of the male at the check-in counter - believe he's the manager. Tried to shake it off thinking at least the massage will be good. When we entered the locker room we were overwhelmed by the strong odor of artificial scents, which I can only imagine was an attempt to replicate the natural scents that are in the air of a proper spa as a result of using good products. There was actually a bowl of those cheap potpourri crystals on the counter, along with plastic flowers & plastic gold doilies. Tacky. I've never been a fan of the lounge at Heaven, and the new owners have done nothing to improve on it. Decor is the same, just in worse shape. The oppressive odors were heavy in this room as well. My friend and I actually had a discussion about what we would do if the treatment rooms smelled the same. We were prepared to leave if that was the case. Thankfully, they weren't. The massage staff were nice enough, but did not seem well-trained. Both of our massages were awkward, staff didn't follow instructions and the oil used was low-grade. I had bought a gift-certificate for my cousin's birthday when I made my own appointment. Now I am going to buy one for another spa for her and have her give the Heaven certificate back to me. If I can't get my money back, I would rather use it myself (definitely for a different service) than have my cousin experience this place.
label: NEG

The gelato was still great, but the 20th St spot has worse AC and a more crowded feel than the University City location, so I would really only give it 4.5 stars, which got rounded down. I got the Salted Bitter Almond, which was incredible despite the disturbing name ("The Landlady", by Roald Dahl anyone?). I also got the Banana and Dark Rum, which was much better at 20th St than University City - it tasted like real bananas and was delicious.

Fuji Mountain was definitely a welcome change and we loved being in the room with the bar. In comparison to YB, I think FM has a slightly smaller selection of songs, but we did a 4 hour party there and everyone was still finding stuff to sing. text: just came back from my second trip. Unfortunately for the review, I ordered the exact same item as last trip so there isn't too much news to report. Fortunately for me, it was still really delicious. But it was missing several key ingredients that I love about burritos. Namely, avocado which is an essential for me. Also, there was just a hint of beans and lettuce and tomatoes, and zero sour cream. Still, the meat and rice were plentiful and delicious. Also wanted to say that this time when I went in, I encountered a counter lady/probably server lady who was very friendly and smiley, but who also had the same disappearing act as the previous counter lady down to a science. However, this time I dug up some courage to use some spanish and say hi and ask how she was, etc. When I opened up my box of burrito heaven, I saw homemade tortilla chips and salsa! No soggy american fries. And the salsa, while runny, was spicy! Imagine a tomatilla salsa consistency, but red. So maybe if you want french fries, you say hello. And if you want chips/salsa, you say hola?

text: Visited on a Saturday night for a birthday celebration with friends. 8 person party. We were seated promptly even tho our party was not complete...a plus. The decor is outstanding! A very cool Mediterranean atmosphere lends to the upscale vibe they are going for. After being at another event all day I was not super hungry so I ordered the Antipasti appetizer. Note: it does not come on a bed of lettuce or with greens. The waitress did attempt to up sell me a $6.00 plate of lettuce. Served on what looked like a cutting board the meats and cheeses were quite good. However, some of the cheese was very strong and could have used some lettuce to cut it. We did not see our waitress during our entire meal. Not once. No "how is everything" No refills of water ( my empty glass was not hiding). I often think that parties are neglected since servers are guaranteed an 18% tip. No need to be attentive and it showed throughout our entire meal. Perhaps this place is better suited for a couple or a party of four when the servers are actually working for the tip.

text: Ok, these guys have lots of products they offer but we recently purchased the gutter protection system. -The company is based in St. Louis but they cover the KC area as well. It was a great start when the saleslady showed up to give us a quote. She was on time and the first thing she said was that our gutters were in good shape so they wouldn't have to replace them. She gave us a quote for the GutterMonster system and a schedule for the installation. The crews started a day or two earlier than scheduled and they did a great job. (I didn't find a mess after they left, they didn't damage anything and overall the system looks great!) I will definitely consider using this company for other projects.

text: We stopped by before a movie based on the reviews here. Either other folks have much lower standards or something has changed tremendously at this restaurant. We had a lunch special of chicken tacos along with chips and salsa and a side order of fries. The service was friendly, although the staff seemed to be sitting in the restaurant having lunch themselves. Let's start with the fries. I know you shouldn't expect much in a Mexican restaurant, but they were almost without any taste at all. They were a bit underdone although very hot. Moving onto the chicken tacos. The shredded chicken was excellent as were the taco shells. However, the rice and beans lacked any real flavor and tasted like they'd come out of a can and been quickly reheated. The portions were also somewhat small. The chips and salsa were equally unimpressive. The chips were served cold and the salsa tasted like someone had dumped the salt shaker in it. This was a shame as the underlying flavor notes were quite interesting and had it been prepared with care could have been very good. We decided to forgo a dessert after the lackluster main courses. In short, this was some of the worst Mexican food overall we've had in Tucson. Perhaps there has been a change in the restaurant since the other reviews, but our experience will not make us a repeat customer.
label: NEG

text: If you don't like sashimi and fresh authentic sushi, this is not the place for you. For all of you avid consumers of raw delicious fish, going here is a must. My mom and I went on a Wednesday night (in fact, I am just getting back from the restaurant now) and the restaurant was quiet, lit from the outside by it's neon sign. We sat at the sushi bar and ordered Chirashi and cajun edamame. Food came quickly and was fantastic - I couldn't stop shoveling sashimi into my mouth. The cajun edmame had a great spice to it, and their ginger is great because they don't use the food coloring so it maintains its zip. Another little secret: try the Plum Wine. If you haven't had it before, it's a pleasantly sweet refreshing surprise. If you have had it before, it holds up true to form. Wonderful little spot, recommended for any sushi aficionado.
label: POS

text: This place is lame and is just a waste of concrete. I am giving it two stars for the possibility that I just missed something, apart that I walked out of my way to see and there was nothing but a crappy view.

text: I love Tony Romas ribs, but I will never return to this location. My last experience here was horrible for more than one reason. We sat down in a very packed Tony Romas on a Saturday afternoon and we waited and waited for a server to come by. The place was really busy so we sort of understood, but it got to the point where we almost got up and left. Finally, a very angry server stomped up and asked what we wanted to drink. No hello, no sorry, no eye contact. It was super uncomfortable. She pretty much forced us to make a decision on the spot about what we wanted to eat and after we ordered, she avoided us like the plague. She had one large table half filled with kids and one of them asked for another milkshake. She was holding a bunch of dirty dishes and as he asked for the refill, she stormed over to the drink area right behind our table and THREW the dishes into the sink. It was so loud and it startled me. I can't imagine how the kids felt. How embarrassing. After a mediocre meal and continued empty glasses we asked for the cheque- and the manager. All of a sudden, she was nice and said she would be happy to grab the manager for us. Another server came up to the table and said that the manager was just on a phone call and she was a senior server and could talk to us. I was not buying it. I had seen the two servers chatting at some point during our horrible meal and assumed they were friends and she was now covering her friends butt. Nevertheless, I told the problem to her in detail and she apologized. That was about it. No discount, no "please come back", no accountability. The worst part about it was when we were walking to our car, we saw the manager standing outside with a group of servers smoking. "On a phone call"? Right. This place definitely lost our business.
label: NEG

text: Ever since Longs turned traitor and sold out to CVS, things are not the same around here Alice! In the beginning, CVS put on a very smart promotion. The store sent excellent discount coupons to everyone in the neighborhood and I shopped here a bunch using the promotional discounts. However, I was paying attention to their operation all the while, and noting a general sense of disorganization along with what seems to be a low employee count. Managers are rarely visible and whenever I did see them, they mostly stood around schmoozing with other managers in a self-congratulatory manner -- presumably pleased because they were busy due to all the discount retailing -- but they shouldn't have rested on their laurels. During this break-in period, the store's newly hired employees were friendly and accommodating enough. But after the honeymoon period, the employees became the typical hassled discount drug store employees -- and the customer count quickly dropped. CVS has a stupid policy that punishes the customer for a cashier's ineptitude. Recently, armed with a couple of coupons, I brought a purchase of multiple items to the register and gave the cashier my phone number because I use that instead of carrying a store card. She forgot to input the phone number, and didn't scan in my coupons, so the total was about $6.50 more than it ought to have been. It's a good thing I looked over my receipt when the total seemed too high, before leaving the register. After I caught the mistake, the cashier agreed that this was her screw-up, but it was only my life that was to become more difficult due to CVS's erroneous policy. I was compelled to drag all of my items to the register in photography because my purchase needed to be refunded and re-rung. What a hassle, and what a giant time waster. Overall prices seem a little higher than when this was a Long's store, but between the coupons and the sales, there are items worth purchasing here. CVS closed the store's neighborhood contract postal counter when they took over, so I will never shop here unless I'm getting a fantastic deal, or am so pushed for time that I can't go anywhere else. See, I've got a long memory Alice.
label: NEG

text: For a restaurant/lounge trying to be upscale the service was extremely poor. We arrived on-time with reservations and after waiting at the bar for 20 minutes WE went up and asked the hostess what the deal was. They had given our table away. After another 15 minutes we were seated. After being seated for 15-20 minutes WE had to ask for a server to come take our order and bring us water. Even after that our food took forever to come out and our drinks sat empty for 5-10 minutes multiple times. The whole experience took 2 hours and 1.5 of that was waiting for our entree. Pros: The mints were good

text: Prohibition Taproom is a wonderfully hidden happy hour location. Gotta love the neon "BAR" sign outside. There aren't really many other places around the taproom, so you really have to go there to go ONLY there. Don't plan on leaving and bar hopping, unless you walk up to broad street or a little deeper into the Fairmount neighborhood. The beer battered green beans are great, as are their vast selection of beers. The last time I went there, I didn't see the special drinks menu, but when I asked for a drink I knew was on it, they made it for me. I seriously recommend it - it's called the prohibition punch! It's a heck of a rum drink, and tastes nice and smooth going down. The taproom is great for large groups, and there is a TON of parking around if you are planning on driving in. I'm a big fan.
label: POS

text: I have started going to Su Xing on a regular basis and am not vegetarian. The hot and sour soup is a favorite, as is the General Tso's Vegetable. The General Tso's Vegetable and not Tofu was recommended by the waitress as her favorite dish. I have tried Kingdom of Vegetarians near Chinatown before, and Su Xing is better. Su Xing stays true to Chinese recipes so that even if you aren't vegetarian, the food is recognizable and just as delicious. The textures of the "meat" dishes are not far off from the real deal for those who like meat. The service is wonderful and they try hard to accommodate requests. (We asked for warm bubble tea, as it was cold out. They heated up the bubble tea despite their confusion since no one had asked for it like that before.) Su Xing is also very comfortable inside with booths and tables and lots of space. :)
label: POS

text: I went for brunch at the Atrium Cafe this weekend (located in the Radisson Hotel). I have always held the Atrium Cafe as the best of the best when it comes to brunches in the city (I've been there once before but it was years ago). I was wrong. And I was very disappointed. There was a lot of food but the food wasn't very good - the waffles were soggy, the ribs were cold, the crab wasn't fresh, and it was apparent that the food had been sitting out for a very long time. We had just sat down with our first plate of food and a server came and dropped off our bill. She kept coming back - not to check on us - to see if we'd paid yet. It was awful! It was rude! It was uncomfortable! Do not waste your time. Don't go for brunch here. It is not a pleasant experience.
label: NEG

text: I can't even begin to tell you how many times I have stayed here. My parents are big fans of this place and I can see why. The rooms are all newly redecorated and beautiful. They always have chocolates on your bed and the housekeeping staff do a wonderful job of maintaining the cleanliness of your room. The hotel serves complimentary wine and cheese from 5-7 pm and a complimentary breakfast in the morning. Now of course these are not five course spreads with top notch food and wine but they are free and still delicious. This place is surely a nice place to stay when in Santa Barbara and has easy access to the beach/ State street/ and many outstanding restaurants.

text: I have eaten at my share of sushi restaurants, but this one is by far the best I've had in quite awhile. Went here for lunch with some coworkers originally- the service was quick enough to get us back to work on time. They also have a small sidewalk patio outside that was in the shade- perfect for a nice day. The gyoza was a little overdone, but still tasty. I got the Maki B combo- colleagues got the Maki A and ordered a few rolls to share. they were all so amazing! It is melt in your mouth sushi! I will definitely be going back. The place was fairly busy, but looked like they had another bar seating place that could hold more people if need be. It can be difficult to find a parking spot- try going around back and parking by the dog park.

text: If you like guys who bathe in cologne, pop their collars, and obsess over themselves than you'll have a great time at Mandarin. I'm not from St. Louis, but I've noticed that a lot of people here are completely obsessed with "status"... even when it comes to the high school they went to. It's kind of a joke, and the last time I was dragged to Mandarin that's all I heard about. Other than the lame clientele, the bar itself is a joke. If you want a good rooftop bar, go to the one at the Moonrise hotel on Delmar. Definitely don't come here on a week night - you can hear crickets, and if you come on a weekend, prepare yourself for a throng of self-involved douchebags.

text: I can't speak for the Texas side of the menu, but I was suspicious of a place that tries to do Mexican and Texas BBQ. Turns out I was right. I had the machaca burrito which was too hot to even taste, but when I took the peppers off, tasted like a steak-um from high school lunch. The side of corn was mediocre, it was in some odd state between grilled and boiled, drizzled with way too much sauce. The beer wasn't even right, the Kensinger I ordered tasted strangely like a PBR. The outdoor seating seemed to be the one saving grace, but you can get that at Bar Ferdinand.

text: This particular location gives me the willies. The last time I went into this store, I heard the following quote from the cashier at the photo department: "Shit! Everything was wonderful from the appetizers (we split the Caesar Salad and a Crab/Smoked Salmon/Avocado special) to the dessert (lovely Tahitian Vanilla Creme Brulee) Their menu is truly eclectic and inventive. With pizza, pasta, steak, seafood... there really is something for everyone. I had the Chicken Scaloppini with GOAT cheese (!!), pesto, tomatoes, and avocado. It was fabulous! The salad was a perfect light balance to the perfectly prepared chicken and powerful cheese. My mom had the filet mignon with a green chile-mushroom sauce. A very interesting combo. It was served with truffle whipped potatoes and a HUGE green chili pepper stuffed with cheese and herbs! I've never seen a chili pepper prepared this way, and it was damn good. On top of everything else, Opal's *WINE LIST* is fantastic! I'm talking pages and pages of vino. Since you ARE in Santa Barbara, you've gotta have some great wine with your meal! :) Also, I have to comment on the attentiveness of Opal's staff. The hostess, manager and servers were SO warm and complimentary. The manager personally greeted us and seemed genuinely happy to hear about our time in Santa Barbara thus far. I was very prepared to encounter a high snob-factor since SB is such a posh little town, but I was pleasantly surprised. No matter where we went, everyone was so friendly! Anyway, I'll wrap this up by advising you to definitely bop into Opal if you are looking for a fabulous meal on State Street.

text: My wife and I stopped there for an early dinner on 7/8/2010 after dropping my son off for his first quarter at AIPH. Not being a beer person like I am, she was a bit hesitant at going there. Overall the brew selection is slanted towards the higher alcohol styles. The food - We had the Charcouterie Platter as a starter. The rabbit terrine was wonderful as well as the grilled sausages and the mix of Belgian and English cheeses. The coarse mustard included on the platter was one of the best that we have ever had. She had a small pot of the Ghent style mussels (leeks, bleu cheese and bacon in a DuPont Saison) while I had the grilled duck salad. She said that the mussels were great (I can't eat them, as I sometimes become violently ill while eating mussels - something to do with whatever they were feeding on rather than the mussles themselves, so I avoid eating them altogether). I had a vew of the pomme frites that were served with the mussels, and was not impressed with them. The cut of the potatoes was all wrong, limp skinny shoestrings rather than thick cut & chunky, the included burbon mayo was quite good however. The duck salad included a perfectly cooked half breast, and a nice slice of fresh goat cheese but the mesclun green salad was rather average. The included spiced walnuts were good, but nothing to shout about. When I get back there again, I will probably just have a burger. Overall, I would give it a 6/5 (yes I know the scale only goes to 5 but the list was well above average) for the beer and a 3/5 for the food - call it a 4 overall.

The place is quite large with a dining area with a sushi bar, a full bar and an outdoor patio. The menu consists of all things seafood battered and fried. text: Last weekend Jonny and I were in the suburban sprawl of New Jersey and pretty hungry. I had heard about a place with a mean grilled cheese, so we made our way over to The Pop Shop in Collingswood. The place was kind of wild inside; I can only assume that at 4pm on each Saturday every seven year old girl in the tri-county area is having their birthday party at the Pop Shop. The place was pretty packed and crazy, like an elementary cafeteria with moms. The decor/theme they're going for is a 1950s diner, and by looks alone, they do an okay job. We didn't have to wait at all for a table, which was a plus. The host and our server were both really nice, but seemed overworked. I don't fault them; the Pop Shop seems to suffer from poor management. The menu is another problem. We were given mock newspapers made for the restaurant that were the menus. It's a cool idea, it's just a shame that it's about as long as the Inquirer. There are hundreds of items on the menu, and it's overwhelming. The grilled cheese menu alone offers more than thirty choices. Jonny and I ordered a two sandwiches, the 5 Bs: Brie, goat cheese, applewood smoked bacon and tomato. The other was the East Zane: brie with grilled asparagus and pesto mayo on a baguette. Both sandwiches were disappointing. The goat cheese of the 5 Bs overpowered everything else, which was sad because it sounds so good. For the East Zane, the bread was too hard and the pesto mayo was the only good part. A condiment should not be the best you have to offer. He had a root beer float, which was sadly made with soft serve. I had a malted milkshake which was good, but nothing special. Bottom Line: The Pop Shop doesn't seem to try at all. They are offering the very lowest quality food that won't cause people to complain. The food could be better made in my own kitchen, and the prices aren't great either. I have no idea why this place has a good reputation.

text: Some of these reviews are clearly for The Summit at Grand Sierra Resort rooms, not the standard Grand Sierra Resort rooms. This distinction is important! I'm not sure how this compares to other Reno rooms, but in general that's a pretty good rate for a decent room. 2. Pretty Clean - For a cheap casino stay, the room was pretty clean. 3. Fairly Quiet - Walls weren't as paper thin as other casino hotels I've stayed in. Also, I don't know if it was just considerate people or the way the doors are designed, but I heard way less door slamming as compared to other hotels I've stayed in. 4. Customer Service - When we complained about our room we were relocated to a new room without much fuss. Once reaching the registration counter at check-in and check-out, staff was friendly. CONS: 1. AWFUL Beds - Our mattress was seriously horrible. We were first put in a room with a king bed. The bed had a huge lump in the middle and sloped down to one side. I spent the majority of the first night trying to get comfortable, only to roll into the nightstand on my side of the bed. I have the bruise on my arm to show for it. We asked for a new room and got one. The mattress lacked the lump and slope, but was still very uncomfortable. 2. Tacky Decor - Our first room had this disgusting vine-patterned wallpaper in the bathroom that made you dizzy if you looked at it for too long, which was difficult to avoid seeing as most of the walls in the bathroom were covered in mirrors. Our second room was cowboy-themed right down to the fabric with cowboys roping steer on the loveseat in the room. The hallways (I can only speak to floors 7 and 11, though I'm sure they're all the same in the GSR part of the hotel) are this weird mix of Bavarian and Southwest motifs and the patterns they painted on the elevator doors seriously makes you think you're looking at one of those bad 3D posters. 3. Long Waits at Registration - We waited a good 30 minutes to check in and I waited another 20 minutes to try and switch my room and get new keys. If you're going to have 15 check-in stations, maybe try staffing at least 1/3 of them? 4. Blah Casino and Shops Area - The casino was kinda blah and the "Arcade Level" left a lot to be desired. I was foiled multiple times when trying to call down to both the resort's spa and another salon on that level to try and make an appointment for a simple manicure. I can't speak to the pool or most of the restaurants as we didn't really eat or hang out at the hotel very much. We did eat at the Sierra Grill. The food was decent, but a bit on the pricey side. I only ended up there because I'd gone out for Sunday lunch with a bunch of friends, and when we discovered Yianni's wasn't open Sunday for lunch this was the next closest option. We were one of maybe 3 or 4 tables with people in the place, and usually restaurants are pretty good when they're not busy. Unless of course the reason they are not busy is because they are TERRIBLE. All 5 of us ordered different stuff and not one of us enjoyed our meal. Lots of leftovers, and no one requested a doggie bag. That about says it all. I won't ever be back. Additionally, the seating was wobbly, high and uncomfortable with no where to hook your purse over the chair. All three of the women on this outing noticed this and were miffed by it. Since eating there I've moved to Texas where we have GOOD Tex-Mex, but even in Edmonton I've had better examples of this cuisine. text: MUST READ! I cannot believe the reviews people have left on this thing. Whatever happened to honesty? I'll tell you my story and let you find out for yourself how TERRIBLE this place REALLY is! text: If you're not eating at the newly owned and much improved Seasons, get there now! I have eaten here twice now - once for late lunch and another for Christmas Eve dinner with my family. I will definitely be returning many times over. New owner and chef, Kevin Smith, is focused on providing a truly delicious experience for his guests. After visiting our table on both occassions, we could tell that he was passionate about his food and sharing only the very best with his guests. The atmosphere at Seasons is very nice. Don't be fooled by the strip mall exterior. The lighting is perfectly dimmed at dinner time, and my husband, who is a total music snob, gives two thumbs up on the jazz selection. This restaurant would be great for anything from a family dinner to a romantic date. Now...the important part...the FOOD! When my husband and I stopped in for lunch, we started with a ridiculous amuse bouche - a smoked bacon and sundried tomato risotto topped with a seared bay scallop. If I could have ordered a bowl of that for lunch I would have! Luckily, since we had dinner here again a little more than 24 hours later, we did get to have another bite! Still not enough though! I want more! Next, we were in for a special treat - another amuse bouche. We were given a sample of what was in store for an upcoming dinner special - a honey-miso glazed sushi grade bluefin tuna (see photo) on soba noodles. Holy crap it was good! Perfectly cooked, totally flavorful. For our lunch entrees, my husband ordered a special - cornbeef hash with egg your way (also pictured). My husband called it "breakfast on steroids". I did manage to sneak a bite from him, and I have to agree that it was yum. However, I was completely happy with my selection - the chicken salad croissant (pictured - forgive me on screwing up the presentation. I cut into it before thinking to take a pictue.) The salad is nice a chunky - big hunks of chicken, halved grapes, whole cashews and bites of celery in a honey-tarragon mayonnaise. The salad was fantastic and the croissant perfectly buttery and fresh. Our meal was finished up with truffles - mmmmmmm! Unexpected and delightful! Upon returning for Christmas Eve dinner with my family, my husband couldn't resist the entree portion of the tuna we had the luck to try the day before, and it was just as delicious as our amuse bouche the night before. He, along with 3 others that ordered it, were more than satisfied. I ordered the filet mignon - oh baby! It was cooked perfectly to my order, the sauce was fabulous, and the vegetables of the day (asparagus, mashed potatoes and turnips, and spaghetti squash) were fantastic. I also had a couple cocktails throughout the night - a Fire Brush and a Bailey's Heart. I can't remember all the detail of them, but they were both delicious. My husband and I also stuffed ourselves with a dessert that I couldn't resist - Warm Pear Spice Cake with rum raisin ice cream and dark caramel sauce. It was probably one of the best desserts I've ordered from a restaurant. The ice cream was fab, the caramel sauce to die for, and the cake was super yummy - very similar to a bread pudding. I think there are some things left to be wanted in the wait staff while others in the staff are fab. I think these kinks will eventually be worked out, as the restaurant has been open for just under a month. Like I said before, if you haven't gone, get there and support this great up and coming restaurant. If you get there by New Years, try the egg nog - holy crap it's awesome!!! Chef does have a great event coming up on Tuesday evening (12/28/10). $10 gets all the delicious food that you want (you pay for drinks), and the proceeds go to a local charity (the exact charity name escapes my mind at the moment) - a great opportunity to try a bunch of what is offered by the chef.

text: Founded by a grieving father who could not find his young daughters grave in a church graveyard in Old City, Laurel Hill is built on the site of the Laurel Hill Estate. It opened around 1840 and is recognized as one of the most beautiful, and inviting, cemetaries in the country. Members of every old and noteworthy Philadelphia family are buried here as well as forty Civil War generals and other notables. And though Paris' Cimetiere du Pere Lachaise may have Balzac and Jim Morrison, Philadelphia's Laurel Hill has Adrienne Balboa. Reason to go while you're still alive? There is no better spot, not even Rittenhouse Square to lunch on a beautiful sunny day than here. And it isn't being disrespectful, it is encouraged. The old and some magnificent gravestones, markers and family mausoleums make fascinating sight seeing and not at all macabre. Forget that you think that this recommendation may have been written by Crispin Glover or other slightly off center character, its a good tip.

First came the mussels pernod, which was probably the best part of the meal, and was served with spinach. The mussels were fresh and tender and the sauce they were served in was quite tasty. I chose the salad for my meal, and my boyfriend chose the pasta. It was served with garlic bread that was delicious and we asked for a refill of that we never received. My boyfriend ordered the pasta with his chicken parm and was not informed that the actual meal comes with a side of pasta as well. One would think that the server would comment on this and recommend the salad instead, because really who can eat 2 sides of pasta? The sauce was flavorful and a bit spicy, however undercooked. His side of pasta as well as his entire chicken parm dish was filled with WATER due to how undercooked it was. My veal ocean was TOUGH and overfried and the seafood on top of it was overly fishy tasting. I had about 5 bites of it. We should have ordered the lamb, someone else had it served in the interim and it looked pretty delicious. Total was $70, Adolfo's takes cash only. text: Let me start off by saying I did not come to Sandrina's to drink. We came because it was late and we were hungry and someone recommended this place.
